## 0. Why this exists (product context — read this)

The primary persona is a DevOps engineer managing **hundreds of servers**. A customer sends a renewed SSL certificate (e.g. `*.example.com`) and they must find **which subdomains exist, what IPs they resolve to, and which of their own servers need the new cert installed** (e.g. 10 of 300 servers). Existing online tools disagree (5 vs 8 vs 9 subdomains) and **Cloudflare's orange cloud (proxy) hides origin IPs**. It is also meant to be a general **DNS toolbox**: global DNS (multi-resolver + geo view), full record lookup, bulk resolve, IP intel, domain health — "everything useful on the DNS side".

Deliverable: an **open-source static web app hosted on GitHub Pages** (no backend; everything runs in the visitor's browser against CORS-enabled public APIs) **plus** a companion stdlib-only Python CLI (`cli/ssl_origin_scan.py`) that is run *inside the user's network* to TLS-probe their server IPs with SNI — the only reliable way to find origins behind Cloudflare.

UI languages: Turkish + English (default by `navigator.language`, toggle). Turkish is first-class; the project is for everyone.

## 1. Hard constraints

- **No dependencies, no build step, no CDN.** Vanilla ES modules (`<script type="module">`), plain CSS. Pure libs must run in both browsers and Node 22 (`package.json` has `"type": "module"`). The Pages deploy only copies files: `tools/assemble-site.mjs` puts `assets/` under `v/<commit>/` (`v/dev-<content digest>/` when assembled without a commit) and points `index.html` there, so every deploy has new module URLs (GitHub Pages caches every file for 10 minutes and views load lazily). Hence every URL inside `assets/` is relative to its module (imports, stylesheets a view injects, and data files through `import.meta.url`); only `index.html`, `sw.js`, `favicon.svg`, the two web app manifests, `icons/` and `cli/` stay at the site root. `sw.js` is the one file written rather than copied: the deploy's precache list goes into it (§5.35). `tests/js/assemble-site.test.js` checks all of it.
- **Libraries in `assets/js/lib/` are DOM-free** (no `document`, `window`, `localStorage`). Use `globalThis.fetch`, `globalThis.crypto` only via injectable options where noted. UI code lives in `assets/js/ui/` and `assets/js/views/`.
- **Dependency injection for I/O:** every network function accepts `{ fetchImpl = globalThis.fetch, signal }` (and DNS-dependent functions accept a `dns` client object). This makes them unit-testable with mocks.
- **Every async network op supports `AbortSignal`** and timeouts.
- **Security:** Untrusted data (subdomains from CT logs, TXT records, RDAP, API responses) must **never** reach `innerHTML`. Build DOM with `textContent`/`createElement` only. `index.html` has a CSP meta: `default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self' https:; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'; manifest-src 'self'`. No inline `<script>`/`<style>`/`style=""` attributes in HTML (setting `el.style.x` from JS is OK). The service worker needs no CSP change: without `worker-src` / `child-src` the registration falls back to `script-src 'self'`, and `manifest-src 'self'` covers the web app manifests; a view's stylesheets are `<link rel="stylesheet">` elements (`style-src 'self'`), never inline.
- **Privacy:** certificate files and server inventory never leave the browser (an address from the inventory is sent only when the user looks it up: Verify's opt-in origin check, IP Intel's "My servers' IPs" and Look up). The private key must never be needed; if a PEM contains a private key, warn and ignore it (never display it). A PKCS#12 (.pfx / .p12) bundle is opened with its password in the tab (§5.47): the password lives in the dialog's field and the one open call, is never stored, logged or sent, and the field is emptied when the dialog closes; the bundle's private keys are never returned, shown or exported — only the opt-in key check decrypts one, in memory, imports it into WebCrypto as a non-extractable key to sign a fixed challenge the certificate's public key verifies, and drops it. A missing intermediate is looked up in the site's own copy of the CCADB list (§5.49): the page reads the dataset's manifest and roots table and, for a chain that stops short of a root, the shards named by the first two hex digits of the key identifiers of the issuers it looks for (for a certificate that names no key identifier, first the DN index shard named by the first hex digit of its issuer DN's hash; usually one or two in all) — files of the site itself; the certificate is never sent anywhere, and no AIA URL is fetched. Seven features send user-chosen data to a third party, all through Globalping and all only after a click and a per-page-session consent (`ui/globalping-gate.js`, one consent per feature): SSL Targets › Verify sends only (public IP, host name, port) pairs — never a private address, the certificate or an inventory server name (§3 Globalping, §5.19) —, Domain Health's MTA-STS **Check the policy** sends the host name `mta-sts.<domain>` and the policy path for one probe (§5.24 `lib/mtasts.js`), and Renewal readiness's HTTP-01 test sends the host names it tests and a made-up `/.well-known/acme-challenge/<token>` path for three probes per address family (§5.44 `lib/renewal.js`), Zone File's New name servers comparison sends the names and types of the zone's record sets — never a value, an origin address, a proxied record's hidden target or (unless its switch is off) an internal-looking name — with the new name servers' host names as the resolvers, at most 100 probes a check (§5.52 `lib/nsparity.js`; its DS question goes to the DoH resolvers), Retire an IP's old / new server comparison sends one host name, one path and two public addresses for two probes (§5.53 `lib/origincompare.js`), Global DNS › ISP resolvers sends the checked name, its record type and the places typed — never an internal name — for at most 50 probes, each asking its own resolver, so those ISPs' resolvers receive the question too (§5.86 `lib/ispdns.js`), and Servers › Exposure audit's direct origin probe sends the proxied names and their public origin addresses as pairs of HTTPS GETs — never a private or reserved address, nor an inventory server name — the origin probe pinned to the proxied one's vantage (§5.87 `lib/exposure.js`); the results are public by measurement ID for about six months, and all spend the same hourly quota. Domain Health's Web category adds one send outside Globalping (§5.78 `lib/observatory.js`): **Check HTTP security** posts the host name to Mozilla's HTTP Observatory once per click, which loads the site from Mozilla's own servers and grades its HTTP response headers; an IP, a single-label name, an internal-suffix name or a host whose addresses are all private is never sent, and the HSTS preload list is a link to hstspreload.org, never fetched (it has no CORS). The Renewal readiness check itself sends only DNS queries (names and types) to the DoH resolvers, four named ones for the CAA comparison, and only after a click or on a shared link (§5.44). An imported zone file never leaves the browser and is never persisted; the Zone File live check sends only record names and types to the DoH resolvers, and only after a click (§5.23). The second zone a Zone File comparison reads (§5.66) is held like the first — the view's module memory only, never a URL, the page session or storage; Forget, another workspace or "Delete all local data" drop both — and Compare and Convert (§5.67) send nothing; a comparison's exports hide the origin addresses of either zone's proxied records unless the user opts in, and its Copy summary names record sets, never a value. The DMARC & TLS reports view (§5.58–§5.60) reads the dropped report files in the browser and keeps them in its module's memory only — never stored, never in a URL; Forget, another workspace or "Delete all local data" drops them —; after a drop it sends the SPF lookups of the reported domains (names and types: the domain's TXT, what its record includes, its `mx` hosts' addresses) to the DoH resolvers, and an address's reverse DNS and network (lib/ipintel.js) only on a click, at most 25 addresses per click, never a private one. A network-owner lookup sends one network address to RIPEstat, only on a click (§5.13). IP Intel's **Check routing** in a row's details (§5.72) sends the public address, its announced prefix and origin AS to RIPEstat (RPKI validation, routing status, abuse contact) and the AS number to PeeringDB, only on that click and never for a private, reserved or documentation address; its CIDR breadcrumb matches the server inventory in the browser. A reverse DNS sweep (Reverse DNS view, §5.28) sends the reverse names of the swept addresses and the PTR names it finds (PTR, then A / AAAA queries) to the DoH resolvers, only on a click, and never a private address; listing an AS's prefixes sends only the AS number to RIPEstat, only on a click; Domain Health adds the PTR and forward queries of the MX addresses to its DNS lookups (§5.15). The DANE / TLSA check sends MX and TLSA queries (names and types, never the certificate) to the DoH resolvers, only on a click (§5.25). Retire an IP (§5.45) compares the addresses in the browser; its check sends the names it looks up (each domain's own records, the host names the page session knows, the imported zone's records that reach the address, a wildcard one through a random name under it — never a host name the imported zone marks as internal, whatever the Zone File hand-off toggle says, and the zone's own domain is not filled in when its name looks internal; a domain typed into the box is checked as typed) to the DoH resolvers, only on a click; its passive lookup sends each public address to HackerTarget and ip.thc.org, and its discovery sends Small-wordlist guesses as DNS lookups, each only on its own click. The page session (§5.30: the current target and each tool's last result) lives in the tab's memory only; a carried target goes into the hash of the tool the user opens and is filled in there, and nothing is sent until that tool's button is pressed. What the app stores lives with the origin: the customer workspaces (§5.39: inventory text, learned names, custom wordlist, expected CAs, notes, recent domains, the opt-in origin map §5.70) in its IndexedDB (database `ssds.workspaces`), the settings, remembered view options and a pointer to the active workspace in its `localStorage`. Every page of that origin can read both: a GitHub Pages project site (`<user>.github.io/<repo>/`) shares its origin with every other Pages site of the same user, so a deployment that keeps inventories should have an origin of its own (a custom domain, or a user / organisation site holding only this app). A workspace leaves the browser only as a hand-over file the user exports (§5.41), sealed with a password if one is given (§5.40; the password is never stored). The DNS change request (§5.50, §5.51) sends nothing while its form is filled in, and a Zone File fix offers no check link (the imported zone never reaches a URL); "Read the current records" sends the names and record types of the change (and, for a new SPF record, its includes' TXT lookups) to the DoH resolvers, only on a click; its check link holds only the zone and the expected records (the new values, and the old ones where they were read) — no server stores it, and whoever opens it asks four public resolvers (names and types) from their own browser. "Show the fix" of Domain Health and Zone File is built in the browser from the report or the file and sends nothing (a missing CAA record offers one Cert Spotter request, crt.sh as fallback, only on its own click). The service worker of the Pages bundle (§5.35) keeps only the app's own files and the wordlist tiers a scan used in Cache Storage: never a third-party response, a URL with a query string, or anything the user typed, imported or looked up. Every request the page makes is counted for the page session (§5.54: the fetch calls it starts and the browser's Resource Timing entries, as request signatures without values) and shown under About › What this page sent with what each service received (§5.55, the registry every endpoint must be declared in); nothing of it is stored or sent. The Certificate view's key continuity check (§5.57) sends only the SHA-256 of the certificate's public key to crt.sh, only on a click; the Subdomains view's related domains (§5.56) are read from the Certificate Transparency answers a scan already has and send nothing. Its Takeover risks card (§5.73) sends nothing before its button; then the scanned hosts' names (their CNAME chains asked again) and the scanned domains' NS / MX / TXT questions go to the DoH resolvers, each registrable domain those records name outside the scanned domains goes to its registry over RDAP (rdap.org only as the fallback) — a reference under a special-use or private suffix (`.test`, `.example`, `.invalid`, `.localhost`, `.local`, `.onion`, `.internal`, all of `.arpa`, the private TLDs `.corp` / `.home` / `.lan` …) is never sent anywhere and never called registrable —, and only the optional page check sends host names (ten at most) to Globalping, with the gate's consent. IP Intel › Domains on this IP (§5.71) sends a public address, only on a click, to HackerTarget, ip.thc.org, AlienVault OTX, Robtex and Shodan InternetDB (and with a key the user types there to the Shodan API or WhoisXML: the key in that one service's request only, never stored, logged, put in a link, a snapshot or an export), and its reverse name and the names found to the DoH resolvers; a private or reserved address is never sent (the workspace alone answers), nor is a name that looks internal or that only the workspace knows (the origin map, the server list). The Domain overview's Lookalike domains (§5.76) makes its candidate names in the browser and, only on its Check, sends an NS question for each to the DoH resolvers (A, AAAA and MX for the ones in DNS) and the registrable domains in DNS to their registry's RDAP server; its certificate lookup sends at most ten of those names to crt.sh, one search each, only on its own button; the workspace's own domains (its recent domains and the inventory's host names) are never sent.
- Code style: 2-space indent, semicolons, single quotes, `const`/`let`, JSDoc on every export, small focused functions. Python: PEP 8, type hints, stdlib only, Python ≥ 3.8 compatible.
- Tests: `node --test "tests/js/*.test.js"` (= `npm test`, what CI runs; node:test + node:assert/strict; each file in its own process), `python -m unittest discover -s tests/python -v`. `node --test tests/js/` runs the same files through `tests/js/index.js`, which starts one `node --test` process per file so results never depend on file order. Tests must not hit the network (mock `fetchImpl`). Live/manual checks go in `tests/live/*.mjs` (not run in CI).
- Test data is generic: reserved names (`example.com/.net/.org`, `example-test.com.tr`) and documentation IPs (`192.0.2.0/24`, `198.51.100.0/24`, `203.0.113.0/24`). `tests/js/repo-hygiene.test.js` fails on any other IPv4 literal that is not well-known public infrastructure, and (locally) on anything matching the gitignored `.private-denylist`.

## 2. Repository layout

```
index.html                    # SPA shell (CSP meta, the global stylesheet only, web app manifest link, <script type=module src=assets/js/app.js>)
favicon.svg
sw.js                         # the service worker (classic script, scope = the site); BUILD = null here, the deploy's manifest in the bundle (§5.35)
manifest.webmanifest          # web app manifest, English (start_url / scope ./, icons, shortcuts); manifest.tr.webmanifest: the same in Turkish
icons/                        # PNG app icons drawn from favicon.svg by tools/build-icons.mjs (192, 512, maskable 512, apple-touch 180)
.nojekyll
package.json                  # {"name":"domainscope","private":true,"type":"module","scripts":{"test":"node --test \"tests/js/*.test.js\"","test:py":"python3 -m unittest discover -s tests/python -v","test:e2e:offline":"node tests/e2e/run-all.mjs --only shell,subdomains,zone,scan,verify,renewal,dane,pfx,chainfix,renew,estate,global,ptr,retire,carry,ip,lookup,health,workspaces,origins,domain,change,cutover,privacy,reports,portfolio,secscore,locales,explain,revocation,takeover,waivers,regwatch,dmarchistory,monitor --offline --no-shots","serve":"node tests/e2e/serve.mjs 8080"}}
```

## 3. Verified external endpoints (probed 2026-09-23 with `Origin: https://example.github.io`)

Only these are browser-usable (return `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`). Do not add endpoints that were not verified to send ACAO. The sources of `cli/ip_intel.py`, which runs outside the browser and needs no CORS (mnemonic sends none), are listed in §7.2.

### Passive subdomain sources
| id | URL | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `crtsh` | `https://crt.sh/?q=%25.{domain}&output=json&deduplicate=Y` (+`&exclude=expired`) | CT logs; slow (up to 60s+) and flaky (502/503, and a backend 404 page while it flaps). Retry plan (code: `sources.js`): the main `%.domain` form up to 4 attempts with 4 / 8 / 16 s backoff (±25 %; a 429 `Retry-After` over 60 s ends the retries), then a 32 s wait and ONE lighter `q=domain` identity search as the fallback (`queryForm: 'identity'`, result `partial`); gives up once another attempt would start after 180 s. Rows: `{issuer_ca_id, issuer_name, common_name, name_value ("a\nb" newline-separated SANs), id, entry_timestamp, not_before, not_after, serial_number, result_count}`. Dates are `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS` UTC without Z. Duplicate rows per cert (precert+leaf) → dedupe by serial+issuer. |
| `certspotter` | `https://api.certspotter.com/v1/issuances?domain={d}&include_subdomains=true&expand=dns_names` | JSON array `{id, tbs_sha256, cert_sha256, dns_names[], pubkey_sha256, not_before, not_after, revoked}`; paginate with `&after={last id}` (max 5 pages; a non-empty 5th page sets `truncated`: more may be left); unauthenticated quota: about 10 full-domain (`include_subdomains=true`) queries per hour per IP (100/h for single-hostname queries, which the scan never sends); 429 → rate-limit error and later pages are skipped. |
| `hackertarget` | `https://api.hackertarget.com/hostsearch/?q={d}` | text lines `host,ip`. Errors come as 200 text like `API count exceeded - Increase Quota with Membership` or `error ...` → treat as error. Free: ~50 req/day per IP (shared with reverseiplookup). Provides IP hints. |
| `anubis` | `https://anubisdb.com/anubis/subdomains/{d}` | JSON array of names (may contain `*.x`). (`jldc.me` is dead — do not use.) |
| `otx` | `https://otx.alienvault.com/api/v1/indicators/domain/{d}/passive_dns` | JSON `{passive_dns:[{hostname,address,record_type,first,last}]}`. Historical A records = great origin hints (pre-Cloudflare IPs). Anonymous → often 429 `{"detail":"Anonymous access ... limited"}` → rate-limit error, non-fatal. |
| `thc` | `POST https://ip.thc.org/api/v1/lookup/subdomains` body `{domain, limit: 100, page_state}` (sent as `text/plain` → no preflight) | ACAO `*`. JSON `{domains:[{domain, last_seen_on, …}], next_page_state, matching_records}`; 100 names per page, paginate by sending `next_page_state` back as `page_state` (`''` on the last page), max 10 pages (1,000 names) per domain, pages 2 s apart. Anonymous token bucket of about 250 requests per IP refilling 1 every 2 s. Provides `lastSeen` per name; `truncated` / `available` when more records exist. |

NOT usable from browser (no CORS): urlscan.io, subdomain.center, Wayback CDX, threatminer, api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/ips, jldc.me.

### Build time only: the CCADB reports (verified 2026-09-28; no ACAO — tools/build-intermediates.mjs, never the page)
| Report | URL | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Mozilla: public intermediates with PEM | `https://ccadb.my.salesforce-sites.com/mozilla/PublicAllIntermediateCertsWithPEMCSV` | ≈ 5.9 MB CSV, ≈ 2,550 rows: `CA Owner`, `SHA-256 Fingerprint`, `Extended Key Usage`, `PEM Info` (prefixed with `'`), … — the non-revoked, unexpired intermediates whose CCADB parent is a root Mozilla includes for websites. It misses the hierarchies browsers reach through a cross-signed root (Let's Encrypt's YE1–YE3 / YR1–YR3 under Root YE / Root YR, Microsoft TLS G2 …) and the ones under a root only other stores keep: the records below add them. |
| Mozilla: included roots with PEM | `https://ccadb.my.salesforce-sites.com/mozilla/IncludedCACertificateReportPEMCSV` | 172 roots: `Trust Bits` (`Websites`, `Email`), `Distrust for TLS After Date` (`2024.11.30`), `PEM Info`. |
| CCADB: all certificate records v4 | `https://ccadb.my.salesforce-sites.com/ccadb/AllCertificateRecordsCSVFormatv4` | ≈ 10 MB: roots and intermediates, `Apple` / `Chrome` / `Microsoft` / `Mozilla Status` (roots: `Included`, `Removed`, `Blocked`, `Disabled`, `NotBefore`, `Not Included`; intermediates: `Trusted` / `Not Trusted`), `Revocation Status` (`Not Revoked`, `Revoked`, `Parent Cert Revoked`), `Subject Key Identifier` (base64), `TLS Capable`, `Valid From` / `Valid To (GMT)` (`2035.06.04`); no PEM. ≈ 275 current, trusted, TLS-capable intermediates are not in Mozilla's report. |
| CCADB: all certificate PEMs | `https://ccadb.my.salesforce-sites.com/ccadb/AllCertificatePEMsCSVFormat?NotBeforeYear=<year>` | 1–2 MB per year: `SHA-256 Fingerprint`, `X.509 Certificate (PEM)` of every certificate CCADB holds with that notBefore year (2025 holds YE2). Only the years of the records above are read. |

Licence: CDLA-Permissive-2.0 with attribution to the CCADB (CCADB Data Usage Terms). The AIA caIssuers URLs stay unusable from the page (plain http, mixed content; ROADMAP, rejected).

### Build time only: parsedmarc's reverse-DNS map (checked 2026-10-08; tools/build-senders.mjs, never the page)
| File | URL | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| The map | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/domainaware/parsedmarc/<commit>/parsedmarc/resources/maps/base_reverse_dns_map.csv` | `base_reverse_dns,name,type`; at the pinned commit `6effd80` (2026-04-20) 3,133 rows and 50 type spellings (47 types without case), 1,349 of the ten mail-relevant types and 950 ISP rows, 23 names with a quoted comma. The newest commit (2026-07-16) has 38,628 rows and 46 types, but is CC BY-SA 4.0. |
| Its licence words | the same commit's `LICENSE` and `parsedmarc/resources/maps/README.md` | Apache License 2.0; from commit `ec2db72` (2026-04-26) the README distributes the CSV under CC BY-SA 4.0 (rows from IPinfo Lite): the build refuses such a commit. |

The page asks nothing new at runtime: the lists are this site's own files (§5.93), the reverse DNS goes to the DoH resolvers and the network to RIPEstat as before. dmarc.io is not used: its API sends no ACAO and its data is CC BY-SA 4.0.

What a certificate names (probed 2026-09-28; Subdomains › Sources › Related domains, `lib/ctrelated.js`): Cert Spotter's `dns_names` is the certificate's whole name list (a 41-name certificate came back with all 41), while crt.sh's `name_value` lists only the names that matched the search, plus the row's `common_name` (the same certificate searched as `%.wikiquote.org` gave its 3 matching names and the common name `*.wikipedia.org`). Other registrable domains of a certificate are therefore complete from Cert Spotter only.

What a released resource answers (probed 2026-10-08 from Node, one request each; Subdomains › Takeover risks, `lib/takeover.js`, which adds no endpoint: DoH, RDAP and Globalping as above): Verisign's RDAP server answers 404 for an unregistered random `.com` name (`rdapDomain` → `notFound`, rdapServer `https://rdap.verisign.com/com/v1/`) while DoH answers NXDOMAIN for its NS, and RDAP statuses arrive lower-case with spaces (`client delete prohibited`); plain HTTP GETs of a random name under `s3.amazonaws.com`, `github.io` and `herokuapp.com` answer 404 with `NoSuchBucket` / `The specified bucket does not exist`, `There isn't a GitHub Pages site here.` and `no-such-app` (title `No such app`) in the body. A Globalping HTTP GET (`httpGetRequest`, port 80, one probe, 1 credit) of a random bucket host finished with `statusCode` 404, `truncated` false and that XML in `rawBody` (`results[0].result` keys: status, resolvedAddress, headers, rawHeaders, rawBody, rawOutput, truncated, statusCode, statusCodeName, timings, tls).

### One host name's certificate (verified 2026-09-27; Certificate view and SSL Targets step 1, `lib/ctcert.js`)
| Service | URL | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Cert Spotter | `https://api.certspotter.com/v1/issuances?domain={host}&match_wildcards=true&expand=dns_names&expand=cert_der` (`*.x` queries leave out `match_wildcards`) | ACAO `*`. `cert_der` is the base64 DER of the final certificate, or of the precertificate while only that one is logged (the CT poison extension tells them apart). Unexpired issuances only, ascending id, 100 per page; `&after={last id}` pages on and an empty page ends the list (the `Link: rel="next"` header is not CORS-exposed). A single-host query counts against the **100 per hour** allowance per IP (`X-Ratelimit-Limit: 100`), not the 10 per hour full-domain one of the scan's source. The rate-limit headers are not CORS-exposed: a browser sees only the 429. |
| Cert Spotter, issuers (verified 2026-09-28; Domain overview, `lib/passport.js`) | `https://api.certspotter.com/v1/issuances?domain={domain}&match_wildcards=true&expand=issuer&expand=issuer.caa_domains&expand=issuer.operator` | ACAO `*` (a preflight is allowed too). Each issuance carries `issuer: { friendly_name, name /* DN */, caa_domains[], operator: { name, website }, pubkey_sha256 }`. One single-host request (the 100-per-hour allowance) returns the first page of current issuances in ascending id order (11 for one busy apex, a `Link: rel="next"` a browser cannot read behind it), so the view says it read one page. |
| crt.sh | `https://crt.sh/?q={name}&output=json&exclude=expired` (the name, plus `*.{parent}`: identity searches match literally) | ACAO `*` on the JSON search, but the download `https://crt.sh/?d={id}` sends **no** ACAO: a page cannot read the certificate. The precertificate and the final certificate are two rows with the same serial that nothing in the JSON tells apart. Used only to *find* the certificate when Cert Spotter cannot answer; the user downloads the file and drops it. |

### A portfolio's certificates (verified 2026-10-08; Domain portfolio › Certificates (CT), `lib/ctwatch.js`)
| Service | URL | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Cert Spotter | `https://api.certspotter.com/v1/issuances?domain={domain}&include_subdomains=true&expand=dns_names&expand=issuer&expand=cert_der&expand=revocation&expand=problem_reporting` (`&after={last id}` pages on) | ACAO `*` (probed with `Origin: https://halilibrahimd27.github.io`, the last two expansions again on 2026-10-08). The unexpired issuances of the domain and every name under it, ascending id; an empty page ends the list and a short one does not (`Link: rel="next"` came with 34 rows). Rows `{ id, tbs_sha256, cert_sha256, dns_names[], pubkey_sha256, issuer: { friendly_name, pubkey_sha256, name /* DN */ }, not_before, not_after, revoked, revocation: { time, reason /* an RFC 5280 CRLReason code */, checked_at }, problem_reporting, cert_der }` (`time` and `reason` null unless revoked; `checked_at`: when Cert Spotter last read the CA's CRL; `problem_reporting`: the CA's contact for a revocation or misissuance report, free text from the CA); 34 rows with their DER were 84 KB. A subdomain search counts against **10 requests an hour per IP** (`X-Ratelimit-Limit: 10`, not CORS-exposed), so a domain costs two at least. |
| crt.sh | `https://crt.sh/?q=%.{domain}&output=json&exclude=expired&deduplicate=Y` (lib/sources.js, §5.11: its retries, backoff and identity-search fallback) | ACAO `*` on the JSON search (§3 above); it answered 502 throughout the 2026-10-08 probes, which is why it is the fallback. One row per certificate with `deduplicate=Y`; nothing in the JSON says whether a row is the precertificate, nor whether it was revoked. |

### Is a certificate revoked? (verified 2026-10-08; Certificate › CT logs › Is it revoked?, `lib/revocation.js`)
| Service | URL | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Cert Spotter | `https://api.certspotter.com/v1/issuances?domain={one of its names}&expand=revocation&expand=problem_reporting` (`&after={last id}`: another page only while the certificate was not on the one before, at most 3) | ACAO `*`, a simple GET. Sent on a click only, with the certificate's first DNS name that is no wildcard (else its wildcard); the single-name allowance (**100 an hour per IP**), whose 429 cool-down it shares with Load from CT (lib/ctcert.js `ctCooldown`). Rows as above without `dns_names`, `issuer` and `cert_der`. The certificate is matched in the page by its SHA-256 (`cert_sha256`), or — only the precertificate logged — by `pubkey_sha256` and the exact validity; neither hash nor the certificate is sent. Unexpired issuances only: an expired certificate or one without a DNS name is not asked about. |

### Server side only: the CAs' renewal information and revocation lists (never the page; the runner's `tls`, §9, the CLI's `--ari` / `--revocation`, §7)
| What | URL | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| ACME directory (read 2026-10-09) | Let's Encrypt `https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory`, Google Trust Services `https://dv.acme-v02.api.pki.goog/directory`, ZeroSSL `https://acme.zerossl.com/v2/DV90`, Sectigo `https://acme.sectigo.com/v2/DV`, SSL.com `https://acme.ssl.com/sslcom-dv-rsa` (RSA) / `https://acme.ssl.com/sslcom-dv-ecc` (EC) | Its `renewalInfo` URL, read once a run and used only on the CA's own ARI host (`acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org`, `dv.acme-v02.api.pki.goog`, `ari.trust-provider.com`, `ari.sectigo.com`, `acme.ssl.com`). A certificate's CA comes from its issuer (lib/renewal.js `caForIssuer`, the CLI's `ari_ca_for_issuer`); DigiCert, GlobalSign and private CAs have none (`unsupported`). Only Let's Encrypt's answers carry ACAO (the page's Renewal readiness › Plan asks it, lib/renewalplan.js): the table is `tools/ds/ari.mjs` `ARI_SERVER_DIRECTORIES` and the CLI's `ARI_DIRECTORIES`, kept equal by `tests/js/ds-tls.test.js`. |
| ARI (RFC 9773) | `GET {renewalInfo}/{base64url(AKI keyIdentifier)}.{base64url(serial)}` | `{ suggestedWindow: { start, end }, explanationURL? }` and `Retry-After` (kept in the report as `retryAfter`, at most 7 days ahead: the certificate is not asked about again before it, its last answer is carried). 404 is `not-found` (the CA does not know the certificate), not a failure; 429, or 503 with Retry-After, and that CA is not asked again in the run. SSL.com's renewalInfo answered 403 `Missing Authentication Token` on 2026-10-09: reported as it is. What is sent: the CertID (the issuer's key identifier and the serial number, both public). |
| CRL (RFC 5280) | the certificate's CRL distribution points (`http://`, `https://`) | A DER CRL of at most 20 MB in 15 s, each URL read once a run; parsed with the serials asked only. A CRL of another issuer (its name differs, or its authority key id when both carry one), a delta CRL, one with a critical extension the tools do not read and one whose issuing distribution point scopes it to other certificates tell nothing (`unknown`, and the next distribution point is tried); one for some reasons only, or past its nextUpdate, still tells that a certificate it lists is revoked, never that one is not. The runner verifies the CRL's signature with the issuer's key from the handshake's chain (node:crypto: ECDSA, RSA PKCS#1, RSA-PSS, Ed25519 / Ed448); the CLI cannot and says "CRL signature not verified". OCSP is never asked. |

### A certificate's public key (verified 2026-09-28; Certificate › CT logs › Key continuity, `lib/keycontinuity.js`)
| Service | URL | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| crt.sh | `https://crt.sh/?spkisha256={64 hex}&output=json` | ACAO `*`, a simple GET (no preflight). Every logged certificate whose SubjectPublicKeyInfo has this SHA-256, expired ones included: rows `{ issuer_ca_id, issuer_name, name_value /* the hash itself */, id, not_before, not_after, serial_number, result_count }`, no `common_name` and no host names; the precertificate and the final certificate are two rows with the same serial (`deduplicate=Y` does not fold them in this search). Under load it answers 429 or 502 without ACAO (a browser sees a network error). |

Cert Spotter reports `pubkey_sha256` for each issuance but has no search by it: crt.sh is the only keyless source.

Verified ACAO `*`:
| id | URL | location / notes |
|---|---|---|
| `cloudflare` | `https://cloudflare-dns.com/dns-query` | anycast; validates DNSSEC (AD); no ECS |
| `cloudflare-family` | `https://family.cloudflare-dns.com/dns-query` | anycast; malware+adult filtering |
| `google` | `https://dns.google/dns-query` | anycast; validates DNSSEC; **honours ECS** |
| `quad9` | `https://dns.quad9.net/dns-query` | anycast; malware filtering; validates DNSSEC; needs HTTP/2. **Not readable from browsers**: its HTTP/3 answers lack ACAO and Chrome/Edge use h3 from the first request (HTTPS RR alpn=h3); no endpoint/form workaround (measured 2026-09-23, `tests/live/browser-doh-matrix.mjs`) → `browserReliable:false`, not in DEFAULT_CHAIN / balance pool |
| `quad9-ecs` | `https://dns11.quad9.net/dns-query` | anycast; **ECS-enabled** variant; same HTTP/3-without-CORS limitation as `quad9` |
| `controld` | `https://freedns.controld.com/p0` | unfiltered; unreachable (TCP timeout) from at least one ISP network on 2026-09-23 → not in DEFAULT_CHAIN / balance pool |
| `dnssb` | `https://doh.dns.sb/dns-query` | |
| `iij` | `https://public.dns.iij.jp/dns-query` | Japan |
| `cleanbrowsing` | `https://doh.cleanbrowsing.org/doh/security-filter/` | security filter |
| `tiar` | `https://doh.tiar.app/dns-query` | Singapore |
| `seby` | `https://doh.seby.io/dns-query` | Australia |
| `cznic` | `https://odvr.nic.cz/doh` | Czechia (CZ.NIC ODVR) |
NOT usable (no ACAO): AdGuard, OpenDNS, NextDNS, Mullvad, AliDNS's RFC 8484 endpoint (`/dns-query`), DNSPod, Wikimedia, dns.sb json, CIRA, HE, SWITCH, LibreDNS, Yandex, 360, etc.
Also verified: Google JSON API `https://dns.google/resolve?name=..&type=..&edns_client_subnet={a.b.c.0/24}` (ACAO *), Cloudflare JSON `https://cloudflare-dns.com/dns-query?name=..&type=..` with `accept: application/dns-json`. Prefer wire format everywhere (one code path, all resolvers).
The one exception — a location only a JSON API can serve (re-verified 2026-10-02; [RESEARCH › Mainland China and zone fetch](RESEARCH.md#mainland-china-vantage-and-zone-fetch-verified-2026-10-02)):
| id | URL | location / notes |
|---|---|---|
| `alidns` (`ECS_RESOLVERS`, `format: 'json'`) | `https://dns.alidns.com/resolve?name=..&type=<number>&edns_client_subnet={a.b.c.0/24}` + `accept: application/dns-json` (safelisted, no preflight) | ACAO `*` (its `/dns-query` sends none), over HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 (real Chrome, 2026-10-03). Applies the subnet (the mainland China ISPs' /24s get their own edges) and echoes it as `edns_client_subnet`, without a scope; no DNSSEC validation (dnssec-failed.org resolves). Cuts a large answer short without TC (TXT: 15–17 of 59 records), so it is asked only for A, AAAA, CNAME and HTTPS. Asked only for Global DNS's mainland China locations — plus once per check on behalf of a subnet outside China, the control —, never in a chain or the bulk pool |

### A zone from the DNS provider's API (verified 2026-10-02; Zone File › Fetch, `lib/zonefetch.js`)
Preflighted GETs with the user's token in `Authorization`; real Chrome reads a made-up token's 401 body. Neither API sends `Access-Control-Expose-Headers`: a page reads `content-type` / `content-length` only, never `Link`, `Retry-After` or `ratelimit-*`.
| Provider | URL | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| deSEC | `https://desec.io/api/v1/domains/{zone}/rrsets/` (`?type=`, `?cursor=`), `Authorization: Token …` | preflight: ACAO `*`, Allow-Headers include `authorization`. Over 500 RRsets a 400 "Pagination required … (N total)"; the cursor is in `Link` (unreadable), so the zone is read type by type. 429 text "Expected available in N seconds". 401 `{"detail":"Invalid token."}` |
| DigitalOcean | `https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/domains/{zone}/records?per_page=200&page=N`, `Authorization: Bearer …` | preflight: ACAO `*`, Allow-Headers `Authorization`; `meta.total` and `links.pages.next` in the body. 401 `{"id":"Unauthorized",…}`, 403 without the `domain:read` scope |
Not usable: Cloudflare's API (`api.cloudflare.com/client/v4`: no ACAO, 400 to the preflight); the old Hetzner DNS API (`dns.hetzner.com/api/v1`: 301 to its console). The new Hetzner Cloud API (`api.hetzner.cloud/v1/zones`) sends ACAO and exposes `Link` — a candidate, not built.

### A nightly repository's results (verified 2026-10-08 and 2026-10-09 with `Origin: https://halilibrahimd27.github.io`; Monitoring › GitHub, `lib/monitorfetch.js`)
`GET https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/results` (the listing: `{ name, type, size }` per entry), `…/contents/results/history` and `…/contents/results/{path}` with `Accept: application/vnd.github.raw+json` (the file itself, up to 100 MB), and — only when asked — `GET …/issues?labels=domainscope&state=open&per_page=5` (pull requests among them left out): `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`; the preflight allows `Authorization` and `X-GitHub-Api-Version` (`Access-Control-Max-Age: 86400`); `X-RateLimit-Remaining` / `-Reset` and `Retry-After` are exposed; `Accept` is CORS-safelisted. A fine-grained token with Repository access to that one repository and Contents read-only (Issues read-only for the issue) is enough; 5,000 requests an hour per token, 403 with `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0` (or 429) when spent. A private repository the token cannot see answers 404 like a missing one; a token without the permission 403 "Resource not accessible by personal access token". The page sends the token in the Authorization header only, no cookies, no referrer, no redirects.

### IP intelligence / RDAP (all ACAO verified)
- RIPEstat (global data, not just RIPE region; add `&sourceapp=subdomain-scanner`): `https://stat.ripe.net/data/prefix-overview/data.json?resource={ip}` (ASN, holder, prefix), `.../maxmind-geo-lite/data.json?resource={ip}` (country/city), `.../reverse-dns-ip/data.json?resource={ip}`, `.../whois/data.json?resource={ip}`.
- RIPEstat announced-prefixes (re-verified 2026-09-27, ACAO `*` on 200 and on 400): `https://stat.ripe.net/data/announced-prefixes/data.json?resource=AS{asn}&sourceapp=domainscope` → `{ status: 'ok', data: { prefixes: [{ prefix, timelines: [{ starttime, endtime }] }], query_starttime, query_endtime, resource } }` over the last two weeks (a prefix whose last timeline ends before `query_endtime` is no longer announced); IPv4 and IPv6 mixed, unsorted. An unknown AS is `prefixes: []`; `ASxyz` is a 400 with `status: 'error'`. A large national ISP answers about 50 KB (≈ 480 prefixes, most of them /17s) in ~3 s.
- RIPEstat's routing calls of IP Intel › Check routing (verified 2026-10-08 with an Origin header, ACAO `*`; `&sourceapp=domainscope` on each, §5.72): `https://stat.ripe.net/data/network-info/data.json?resource={ip}` → `data: { asns: ['15169'], prefix: '8.8.8.0/24' }`; `.../rpki-validation/data.json?resource=AS{asn}&prefix={pfx}` → `data: { status: 'valid' | 'invalid_asn' | 'invalid_length' | 'unknown', validating_roas: [{ origin, prefix, validity, max_length }], validator: 'routinator' }` (a wrong origin and a too-long prefix checked live too); `.../routing-status/data.json?resource={pfx}` → `data: { origins: [{ origin, route_objects }], more_specifics, less_specifics: [{ prefix, origin }], visibility: { v4 | v6: { ris_peers_seeing, total_ris_peers } }, first_seen, last_seen: { prefix, origin, time } }`; `.../abuse-contact-finder/data.json?resource={ip}` → `data: { abuse_contacts: ['…'], authoritative_rir: 'arin' }`.
- PeeringDB (verified 2026-10-08; ACAO echoes the request's Origin, `Cache-Control: s-maxage=10`): `https://www.peeringdb.com/api/net?asn={asn}` → `{ data: [{ id, name, aka, website, asn, info_type, info_types: ['Content'], info_scope, policy_general, irr_as_set, … }], meta: {} }`; an AS it has no record of answers **HTTP 404** `{ data: [], meta: { error: 'Entity not found' } }`. Anonymous use is throttled after about 16 quick calls (429 with `Retry-After: 10`, a header CORS does not expose): the page asks one AS every 4 s at most, and each AS once (§5.72).
- `https://ipwho.is/{ip}` (ACAO *) — fallback geo/ASN. `https://ipinfo.io/{ip}/json` (ACAO *; tokenless quota). `https://ipapi.co/{ip}/json/` (reflects origin; strict daily quota).
- `https://api.hackertarget.com/reverseiplookup/?q={ip}` (ACAO *) — domains on same IP (quota shared with hostsearch).
- ip.thc.org reverse IP (verified 2026-09-28, ACAO `*`, preflight allows any method and header): `POST https://ip.thc.org/api/v1/lookup` with a `text/plain` JSON body `{ ip_address, limit }` (no preflight) → `{ matching_records, domains: [{ domain, apex_domain, asn, organization, ip_address, … }], next_page_state }` (`''` on the last page; `limit` pages it); `count_unavailable: true` (with `matching_records: 0`) when it has no count; `{ status: 'error', error: 'invalid ip' }` for a bad address. Same token bucket as its subdomain lookup (~250 requests per IP, 1 every 2 s; the `X-Ratelimit-*` headers are not CORS-exposed). A documentation address answers too (it lists junk hosts for it).
- Domains on this IP (§5.71), one request each on 2026-10-08 with `Origin: https://halilibrahimd27.github.io`: AlienVault OTX `https://otx.alienvault.com/api/v1/indicators/IPv4/{ip}/passive_dns` (`IPv6/{ip}` for IPv6; ACAO reflects the origin) → `{ passive_dns: [{ address, hostname, first, last, record_type, asn, … }], count }` (times in UTC without a zone; `count` counts records, duplicates included; a busy address answers slowly: 1.1.1.1 took over 25 s, 9.9.9.10 a few); Robtex `https://freeapi.robtex.com/pdns/reverse/{ip}` (ACAO reflects the origin) → `application/x-ndjson` lines `{ rrname, rrdata, rrtype, time_first, time_last, count }` (Unix seconds); Shodan InternetDB `https://internetdb.shodan.io/{ip}` (ACAO `*`) → `{ cpes, hostnames, ip, ports, tags, vulns }`, HTTP 404 `{ detail: 'No information available' }` for an address it does not know (free for non-commercial use; a burst locks a client out for about an hour); Shodan API `https://api.shodan.io/shodan/host/{ip}?key=…` (ACAO `*`; a bad key: HTTP 401 `text/plain`) and WhoisXML `https://reverse-ip.whoisxmlapi.com/api/v1?apiKey=…&ip={ip}` (ACAO `*`; a bad key or no credits: HTTP 403 `{ code, messages }`) — checked without a key, so their error answers are verified and their success shapes (`{ hostnames, domains, ports, … }`; `{ current_page, size, result: [{ name, first_seen, last_visit }] }`) follow the providers' documentation, read tolerantly.
- RDAP: IANA bootstrap `https://data.iana.org/rdap/dns.json` (ACAO *), registry servers e.g. `https://rdap.verisign.com/com/v1/domain/{d}` (ACAO *), fallback `https://rdap.org/domain/{d}` (ACAO *, redirects). IP RDAP e.g. `https://rdap.db.ripe.net/ip/{ip}`. `.tr` has no RDAP in bootstrap → report `unsupportedTld`. Verified 2026-10-02: `.io`, `.sh`, `.ac` and `.me` are still missing from the bootstrap, but their registry operator's server answers them, `https://rdap.identitydigital.services/rdap/domain/{d}` (ACAO *; §5.14 `RDAP_OVERRIDES`). rdap.org's 429 carries no CORS header, so a browser sees a network error: the page asks rdap.org at most once a second and leaves it alone for a minute after such an answer.

### Globalping (verified 2026-09-24; the SSL Targets › Verify tab, Domain Health's MTA-STS policy check and Renewal readiness's HTTP-01 test)
Anonymous use of `https://api.globalping.io/v1` only (never configurable from a URL or a setting). Facts the client and the verdicts rely on (raw evidence in `tests/fixtures/globalping/`, summary in [RESEARCH › Globalping facts](RESEARCH.md#globalping-facts-for-the-verify-tab-verified-2026-09-24)):
- **Endpoints:** `POST /measurements` (202 `{id, probesCount}`), `GET /measurements/{id}` (the whole measurement; `status` goes `in-progress` → `finished`), `GET /limits` (free). Measurement ids are alphanumeric; the client puts nothing else into a request path.
- **Body:** `{type:'http', target:<public IP>, limit:1, timeout:10, measurementOptions:{protocol:'HTTPS', port:443, request:{method:'HEAD', host:<name>, path:'/'}}}`. `request.host` sets both the SNI and the Host header; an IPv6 literal target works (the API picks a v6-capable probe). Always send `port` (the API default is 80) and never `ipVersion` with an IP target (400).
- **JSON only:** `content-type: application/json` is required — a `text/plain` body is ignored (`400 "type" is required`) — so every POST is preflighted (allowed, `Max-Age 600`). GETs send no custom header (simple requests, `cache: 'no-store'`, no ETag).
- **Quota:** `/v1/limits` carries it in the **body only** (`rateLimit.measurements.create {type, limit, remaining, reset}`; `reset` is 0 until the first spend, then a fixed 1-hour window). The POST 202 carries `X-RateLimit-{Limit,Consumed,Remaining,Reset}` and `X-Request-Cost` (= probes allocated), readable under the app CSP. **Remaining is not monotonic across concurrent POSTs** (220, 216, 215, 219, 217, 218 in one window; later 241, 240), so the client keeps the minimum per window. Anonymous: 250 probes per hour, **shared by everyone behind the same egress IP**. A POST 429 (`rate_limit_exceeded` / `insufficient_credits`) was not triggered live.
- **Free errors** (no quota spent): 400 for a private or reserved target (RFC 1918, 127/8, 100.64/10, 169.254/16, 192.0.0/24, TEST-NET-1/2/3, 198.18/15, 224/4, 240/4, 255.255.255.255, 0.0.0.0, `::`, `::1`, fc00::/7, fe80::/10, ff00::/8, 100::/64, 2001:db8::/32, mapped v4), for a host that is an IP, contains `_` or `*`, carries `:port` or a trailing dot, for `timeout` outside 5–30, and for a global `limit` together with `locations[i].limit`; 401 for a bad token (an anonymous retry works); 422 for a location without probes (also a v6 target plus a country without v6 probes).
- **Charged although useless:** port `0` (accepted, charged, treated as 443) and the IPv6 documentation prefix `3fff::/20` (accepted, charged, fails with `connect ENETUNREACH`). The client refuses both itself; `isGloballyRoutable` is an allowlist for IPv6.
- **Polling:** the limit is **per measurement id** (8 parallel GETs on one id gave 3 × `429 too_many_requests` with a readable `Retry-After: 5`; 12 different ids in parallel all got 200). Wait ≥ 500 ms before the first GET and after each response. Client deadline = `(timeout ?? 30) + 10` s; `timeout: 10` makes a filtered target finish in about 11 s; a success finishes in about 0.8 s (median).
- **`result.tls`:** `authorized`, `error` (only when unauthorized; **one** code — chain errors mask name errors), `createdAt`, `expiresAt`, `issuer{C,O,CN}`, `subject{CN, alt}` (Node's `subjectaltname` string, IPv6 SANs uncompressed), `keyType`, `keyBits`, `serialNumber` (colon hex, byte-aligned, no sign byte), `fingerprint256`, `publicKey` (RSA: the full SPKI; EC: the raw point), `protocol`, `cipherName`. Leaf only: no chain and no revocation (revoked.badssl.com is `authorized:true`). Any HTTP status (403, 421, 301) still carries `tls`. A failed test has no `tls`; its cause is in the `rawOutput` text only.
- **Payload:** a finished body is 2–35 KB (the headers appear three times); only a trimmed summary is kept (no headers or body, `rawOutput` for failures ≤ 300 chars, `publicKey` in memory only).
- **Privacy:** results — target IP, host name and the server's response headers — are readable by anyone with the measurement id for about six months. Probes are run by jsDelivr and volunteers (a `u-…` tag marks a probe adopted by a registered user) and send `User-Agent: globalping probe (https://github.com/jsdelivr/globalping)`.
- **HTTPS GET of a path (Domain Health › MTA-STS, verified 2026-09-27, fixtures `m26`, `m27`):** `{type:'http', target:<host name>, limit:1, timeout:10, measurementOptions:{protocol:'HTTPS', port:443, request:{method:'GET', path:'/.well-known/mta-sts.txt'}}}` — a host-name target (no `request.host`): the probe resolves it itself and uses it as SNI and Host header. A finished result carries `statusCode`, `headers` (lowercase names; values may be arrays), `rawBody` **already decoded** (a `content-encoding: br` body arrives as text, CRLF kept), `truncated` (bodies are cut at 10 KB) and the same `tls` object as a HEAD check. A host without an address fails with `rawOutput` `queryA ENODATA <host>` (charged, one probe). The results — the policy included — are public by id like any other.
- **Plain-HTTP GET from chosen continents (Renewal readiness › HTTP-01 test, verified 2026-09-28, fixtures `m28`–`m30`):** `{type:'http', target:<host name>, locations:[{continent:'EU',limit:1},{continent:'NA',limit:1},{continent:'AS',limit:1}], timeout:10, measurementOptions:{protocol:'HTTP', port:80, request:{method:'GET', path:'/.well-known/acme-challenge/<token>'}}}` — three probes, charged three. `measurementOptions.ipVersion: 6` (allowed with a host-name target only) makes the probes resolve AAAA and connect over IPv6 (`resolvedAddress` is then IPv6). **Redirects are not followed:** a 3xx result carries `statusCode` and `headers.location` (lowercase names), so the client judges the redirect itself. A finished result also repeats the response head and body in `rawOutput`; the client reads only `status`, `statusCode`, `headers.location`, `resolvedAddress` and, for a failed test, `rawOutput`.
- **DNS at a chosen name server (Zone File › New name servers, verified 2026-09-28, fixtures `d01`–`d14`, `v-dns-cases.json`):** `{type:'dns', target:<name>, limit:1, timeout:15, measurementOptions:{query:{type}, resolver:<host name or public address>, protocol:'UDP', port:53}}` — one probe, **one credit per measurement**, finished in about 0.7 s. The probe runs `dig -t TYPE name @resolver -4 +timeout=5 +tries=2 +nofail +nocookie +nosplit +nsid` (RD set; an authoritative server ignores it) and the result carries `statusCode` / `statusCodeName` (the rcode), `answers[] {name, type, ttl, class, value}` (the **answer section only**, `value` in presentation format: TXT quoted, a split TXT as `"…" "…"`, names with the trailing dot), `resolver` and the dig text in `rawOutput`, whose flags line says whether the answer was authoritative (`aa`) and whose `;; AUTHORITY SECTION:` / `;; ADDITIONAL SECTION:` carry a referral's NS records and glue. `resolver` may be a host name (the probe resolves it itself; a name it cannot resolve fails the test, **charged**) or a public address; a private or documentation address, a host name with a trailing dot and an unknown option are free 400s. Query types: A, AAAA, ANY, CNAME, DNSKEY, DS, HTTPS, MX, NS, NSEC, PTR, RRSIG, SOA, TXT, SRV, SVCB — **CAA, TLSA and the rest are refused** (free 400). An underscore target (`_dmarc.example.com`) is accepted, a wildcard target (`*.example.com`) is not. A server that does not serve the zone answers REFUSED without `aa`.
- **DNS through the probes' own resolvers (Global DNS › ISP resolvers, verified 2026-10-08 with one live measurement of two probes; CORS as for every endpoint above; fixture `isp-default-resolvers.json`, written in its shape):** `{type:'dns', target:<name>, locations:[{continent:'EU', tags:['eyeball-network'], limit:3}, …], timeout:15, measurementOptions:{query:{type}, protocol:'UDP', port:53}}` — no `resolver`, so each probe asks its default one. The finished measurement echoes no `measurementOptions`; `result.resolver` reads the address asked, or `private` for a private one (the dig `SERVER` line is masked as `x.x.x.x` then); the answers' TTLs are what is left of that resolver's cache (204 s and 15 s for a 300 s record), and the flags line carries `ad` when the resolver validated.
- **A name's question at its zone's name server (Global DNS › Expected value, 2026-10-08):** the body of the DNS check at a chosen name server above with `query:{type}` — the check's own record type, whose answer carries the record set's authoritative TTL, or `'SOA'` (a new name, where only the negative-cache time counts; CAA, which Globalping cannot ask) —, `target` the name itself and `resolver` the zone's name server by host name (the SOA's primary when it is one of the NS set) — one probe, one credit; the request shape and the dig text (the flags line, the ANSWER and AUTHORITY sections) are those verified for Zone File › New name servers and Domain Health › Delegation, and RESEARCH's cutover row verified authoritative TTLs per name server (3600 at NS1 vs 900 at Route 53 for one zone) and the negative-cache SOA in the authority section of an empty answer. Read by `lib/soaprobe.js` (§5.91); not a new endpoint: the ledger notes the POST `dns-query`.
- **HTTPS GET at an address (Retire an IP › old and new server, verified 2026-09-28, fixtures `h01`, `h02`):** `{type:'http', target:<ip>, limit:1, timeout:10, measurementOptions:{protocol:'HTTPS', port, request:{method:'GET', host:<name>, path}}}` returns `statusCode`, `headers` (lowercase names), `rawBody` (decoded, cut at 10,000 characters, `truncated`) and `tls` like the host-name GET. `locations: <the first measurement's id>` sends the **same probe** again (one credit each), so the second address is asked from where the first one was.

### Domain Health › Web: the HTTP security grade (Mozilla HTTP Observatory, verified 2026-10-08)
`POST https://observatory-api.mdn.mozilla.net/api/v2/scan?host=<host>` (`lib/observatory.js`): Mozilla's HTTP Observatory loads the host from its own servers and grades the HTTP response headers it sends (CSP, HSTS, cookies, framing, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, the redirect to HTTPS, SRI, cross-origin). **ACAO `*`** (verified 2026-10-08 with `Origin: https://example.github.io`), so the browser may read it. One request per click, never on arrival. The JSON answer carries `grade` (`A+` … `F`), `score`, `tests_passed` / `tests_failed` / `tests_quantity`, `status_code`, `scanned_at` (a scan of the last few minutes is answered from Mozilla's cache, so it may be older than the click) and `algorithm_version`; no per-test list (that is on the MDN report page `https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/observatory/analyze?host=<host>`, a link). `429` carries `Retry-After`; a non-2xx body names the reason in `error` / `message`. Only a public host name is sent (`observatoryEligible`): an IP, a single label, an internal suffix (`.local`, `.internal`, `.home.arpa` …) or a host whose A / AAAA addresses are all private is never sent. The HSTS preload list has no CORS and is not fetched — `https://hstspreload.org/?domain=<domain>` is a link only.

## 4. Test fixtures (already generated in `tests/fixtures/` — do not regenerate)

`expected.json` holds openssl-derived ground truth per cert: `subjectCN, subjectDN (RFC2253), issuerCN, issuerDN, dnsNames[], ipAddresses[] (IPv6 in RFC 5952 compressed lowercase), emails[], serialHex (lowercase, no leading 00 sign byte), notBefore/notAfter (ISO UTC), sha256, sha1 (lowercase hex, no colons), keyAlgorithm ('RSA'|'EC'), keyBits, curve ('prime256v1' as printed by openssl — map to 'P-256' in our API), isCA, selfSigned`.

Files: `ca.pem` (test root CA), `rsa_multi_san.pem` (leaf signed by CA; SANs: 5 DNS incl. wildcard `*.cdn.example-test.com.tr` and IDN `xn--mnchen-3ya...`, IP 10.0.0.5, IP 2001:db8::1, email), `rsa_multi_san.der`, `rsa_multi_san_crlf.pem` (CRLF endings), `pasted_with_text.txt` (PEM surrounded by Turkish email text), `ec_wildcard.pem` (P-256, `*.wild.example.net` + `wild.example.net`, notAfter 2051 → GeneralizedTime), `cn_only.pem` (no SAN extension; CN=legacy.example.org), `many_sans.pem` (81 SANs → long-form DER lengths; serial 7fffffffffffffff01), `chain.pem` (leaf+CA), `chain_reversed.pem` (CA+leaf), `with_key.pem` (cert + PRIVATE KEY). Private keys `*.key` exist for rsa_multi_san, ec_wildcard, cn_only, many_sans — **test-only**, used by the Python CLI integration test to run local TLS servers.

`renew_a_rsa.pem`, `renew_a_ecdsa.pem` and `renew_b_rsa.pem` (crafted by `gen_x509_fixtures.mjs`, one made-up "DomainScope Test Renewal CA" whose key is never written, and listed in `x509_expected.json`) are a renewal week: set A is an RSA 2048 + ECDSA P-256 pair for `example.com` and `*.example.com`, set B one RSA 2048 certificate for `shop.example.com` and `pay.example.com`, both also under set A's wildcard (§5.43, `renewal.e2e.mjs`).

PKCS#12: `gen_p12_fixtures.mjs` (OpenSSL 3.4+ with the legacy provider) made a throwaway PKI — `p12_root.pem`, `p12_inter.pem`, the leaves `p12_rsa.pem` (RSA, p12.example.com), `p12_ec.pem` (P-256, `*.p12.example.net`), `p12_p384.pem` (P-384, p384.example.org) — and bundled them with `openssl pkcs12 -export` as `p12_*.p12` (the file order is leaf, root, intermediate): OpenSSL 3's AES default, `-legacy` (RC2-40 + 3DES), RC2-128 + two-key 3DES, AES-128 / AES-192 with a SHA-512 MAC, PBMAC1, the empty password, no MAC, a Turkish password with an emoji, a password as OpenSSL 1.0.x encoded it, nothing encrypted, certificates only, and a key that belongs to the intermediate. The keys exist only inside the bundles. `p12_expected.json` holds the passwords and what OpenSSL reads back (`-info`, certificate hashes in file order, whether the key belongs to the leaf); `test.pfx` (password `test`) is the older OpenSSL-default bundle of `rsa_multi_san` and `ca.pem`.

bundle-check (`gen_bundle_fixtures.sh`, OpenSSL 3.4+): a throwaway root and intermediate (EC P-256, keys never kept), `bundle_leaf.pem` (RSA 2048, `www.example.com` + `example.com`, an AIA CA Issuers URL) with its key as PKCS#8, PKCS#1 and encrypted PKCS#8 (`bundle_leaf.key`, `.rsa.key`, `.enc.key`) and its CSR, `bundle_ec_leaf.pem` (P-256, `api.example.net`) with its SEC1 key with and without the public point and its CSR, another RSA key and a CSR made with it (`bundle_other.*`), `bundle_ca_reversed.pem` (root before intermediate), and `bundle_selfsigned_ca.pem` (P-256, `CN=www.example.com`, self-signed CA:TRUE without keyUsage or subjectAltName: what `openssl req -x509` makes by default). The CSRs also serve the Certificate view's CSR check (`tests/js/x509-csr.test.js`). `estate/report-a.json` and `estate/report-b.json` are `--estate --json` reports of the CLI over a made-up network (two sites a week apart, documentation addresses only; `python tests/python/test_estate.py --write-fixtures`): the Python tests keep them equal to what the CLI writes, `tests/js/estate.test.js` checks that `lib/estate.js` computes each one's own `estate` section, and the `estate` E2E suite imports them.

Revocation (§5.94; `gen_crl_fixtures.sh`, OpenSSL 3.4+): a throwaway CA, `crl_ca.pem` (Example Test CRL CA, EC P-256, its key never kept), its leaves `crl_leaf.pem` (`www.example.com` + `example.com`, serial 0c1001, CRL distribution point `http://crl.example.com/test-ca.crl`; its key `crl_leaf.key`) and `crl_leaf2.pem` (`api.example.net`, serial 0c1002), another CA `crl_other_ca.pem` (RSA 2048), and three DER CRLs: `crl_revoked.der` (0c1001 keyCompromise on 2026-09-01 12:00 UTC, 0c1002 superseded on 2026-08-15 08:30; user certificates only; CRL number 0x10), `crl_empty.der` (nothing revoked; 0x11) and `crl_other.der` (the other CA's, listing 0c1001 too), all issued 2026-10-01 with their next update on 2026-10-15 (the tests pass their `now`). `der-builder.mjs` crafts the CRLs OpenSSL will not write (delta, unknown critical extensions, other scopes, PSS parameters, malformed ones) in `tests/js/crl.test.js`.

Missing intermediates (§5.49): `gen_chainfix_fixtures.mjs` (no OpenSSL; the DER encoder `der-builder.mjs` is shared with `gen_x509_fixtures.mjs`) made a throwaway PKI whose keys are never written — a current root, a removed old root, the Issuing CA under the current root and its cross-signed copy under the old root, the old root cross-signed by the current one, a Policy CA → Deep CA pair, a distrusted root with its CA, an e-mail-only and an expired CA the build leaves out — and five leaves (`chainfix_leaf*.pem`: plain, without an authority key id, under an unlisted CA, under the Deep CA, under the distrusted CA), plus the test dataset `tests/fixtures/intermediates/` built by `tools/build-intermediates.mjs` from CCADB-shaped rows (empty shard files left out; the Deep CA comes from the certificate records and a PEM report row, as Let's Encrypt's YE issuers do; `--dataset` rebuilds only the dataset from the PEM files).

`tests/fixtures/globalping/*.json` (+ `README.md`: shape, trim rules, scrub map, measurement ids) are real Globalping measurements of public targets (plus the deliberate charged failures m21, localtest.me → 127.0.0.1, and m25, `3fff::1`), trimmed and scrubbed (the badssl.com origin becomes `54.1.2.3`, user tags become `u-probe`), plus the refused-request cases and a few synthetic bodies marked `"synthetic": true`. `real_github.pem` is the certificate served in `m01-github-valid.json`, so the pair is a fully real UPDATED case. It expires on 2026-11-29, so every fixture test classifies with `now = capturedAt`.

**The clock in tests.** The fixtures carry fixed dates (the nearest expiries: `real_github.pem` on 2026-11-29, the `sct/` leaves on 2026-11-30, `real_google*.pem` on 2026-12-03, `real_cloudflare.pem` on 2026-12-04; the made-up PKIs run from 2027-10-03 to 2052-01-01), so a test that reads the clock goes red one day without any change, and a pacing check on a real timer flips on a busy machine (a timer can fire a few milliseconds before `Date.now()` says it is due: the "at least 75 ms apart" check of the rdap.org slots failed in 7 of 25 loaded runs). No test does either:

- **Unit tests** are given their instant (`now`, `{ now }`). A test of code that waits or paces itself runs on `fakeClock(t)` of `tests/js/fake-clock.mjs`: `Date.now()`, `new Date()` and `setTimeout` on a clock that starts at 2026-10-08 12:00 UTC and moves only when the test moves it. `await clock.advance(ms)` stops at each timer that falls due and lets the promise continuations run, so a chain of waits unfolds as in real time; `await clock.settle(promise)` runs on until the promise has settled; `clock.pending()` and `clock.waits()` say what is waiting, `clock.elapsed()` what has passed. The real clock is back when the test ends (`tests/js/fake-clock.test.js`). A real timer stays only where the test is about the real thing (Node's warning for a timer past 2^31 ms) or about speed (the performance budgets).
- **Python tests** hold the CLI's clock with `fixed_clock()` of `test_ssl_origin_scan.py` (`_utcnow` at 2026-09-23 12:00 UTC): `run_main` and `sample_report` run on it, the bundle-check and compare modules set it for every test (`setUpModule`), and a test that wants another instant passes `now=` or patches `_utcnow` itself.
- **Browser suites** whose page shows what the clock says pin it with `pinnedClockScript(instant)` of `tests/e2e/clock.mjs` on every load (the estate, cert, chainfix, renewal, retire and revocation suites; the cutover suite, whose cards give a time of day only for today and the date before it for any other day; the scan suite for its Copy summary step). Its source is `shiftClock`, one function that moves `Date.now()` and `new Date()` and lets them run on.

`node tests/time-travel.mjs <day or instant> -- <command>` shows what a date breaks. The command runs with the clock of every Node process in it (`tests/time-travel/clock.mjs`, a preload), of every page `tests/e2e/cdp.mjs` opens and of every Python process (`tests/time-travel/sitecustomize.py`) moved to that day and running on from there, all by one shift (`DS_TIME_SKEW_MS`, so they agree with each other). Timers, `performance.now()`, `time.monotonic()` and `time.sleep()` are not touched, nor is the C library's clock (OpenSSL's certificate dates, a file's modification time): for the first, run the command under libfaketime in Linux (`FAKETIME_DONT_FAKE_MONOTONIC=1 faketime -f '@2050-01-02 12:00:00' …`); a test that writes a file and compares its time with the clock sets that time itself (the cache tests of `tools/build-*.mjs`). The unit tests, the Python suite and the offline E2E suites are green on the days tried, from 2026-11-28 to 2100-02-28. `tests/js/time-travel.test.js` covers the tool.

## 5. Module contracts (exports are stable — code against them; the code wins where it has moved on)

All hostnames are lowercase ASCII (punycode), no trailing dot. All IPs canonical (`normalizeIP`). Dates are `Date` objects inside libs.

### 5.1 `lib/util.js`
```js
export class AbortError extends Error {}          // name 'AbortError'
export class TimeoutError extends Error {}        // name 'TimeoutError'
export class HttpError extends Error { status; url; body /* first 500 chars */ }
export function sleep(ms, signal) -> Promise<void>                       // rejects AbortError on abort; a wait past a timer's range (2^31 - 1 ms) is held to it
export function createLimiter(concurrency) -> { run(fn) -> Promise, setConcurrency(n), get active(), get pending(), clear() }
export async function fetchWithTimeout(url, { timeoutMs = 15000, signal, fetchImpl = globalThis.fetch, ...init }) -> Response   // throws TimeoutError / AbortError / TypeError(network)
export async function fetchJson(url, opts) -> any                          // non-2xx → HttpError
export async function fetchText(url, opts) -> string
export async function retry(fn, { retries = 2, baseDelayMs = 500, maxDelayMs = 8000, signal, shouldRetry = defaultShouldRetry }) -> any   // exponential backoff + jitter; never retries AbortError
export function defaultShouldRetry(err) -> bool                            // network TypeError, TimeoutError, HttpError 429/5xx
export function errorKind(err) -> 'abort'|'timeout'|'rate-limit'|'http'|'network'|'parse'|'unknown'
export function uniq(arr) ; export function chunk(arr, n)
export function sharePercent(ratio) -> number                              // extension (wave 4): a share as a percentage with ≤ 1 decimal (0.9487 → 94.9), never 100 or 0
                                                                           // unless exactly so (0.99996 → 99.9); the reports view's headline and its Copy summary say it this way
export function randomLabel(len = 12) -> string                            // [a-z0-9] via crypto.getRandomValues
export function createCache({ maxEntries = 5000 }) -> { get(k), set(k, v), has(k), delete(k), clear(), size }   // LRU-ish
export function mergeSignals(...signals) -> AbortSignal
export function splitList(text) -> string[]                               // split on whitespace , ; newline; trims; drops empties and '#' comment lines
export function onceAsync(load) -> () => Promise                           // one shared run of an async loader (a module imported on first use); a rejection is forgotten, so the next call retries
```

### 5.2 `lib/x509.js` (pure JS DER/ASN.1; no deps)
```js
export class CertificateParseError extends Error {}
export function parseCertificates(input /* string | ArrayBuffer | Uint8Array */) -> {
  certificates: Certificate[],    // input order
  leaf: Certificate | null,       // non-CA cert that is not the issuer of another cert in the set; else first
  warnings: Array<{ code: 'PRIVATE_KEY_PRESENT'|'NO_CERTIFICATE'|'PKCS12_UNSUPPORTED'|'CSR_NOT_CERT'|'PARSE_ERROR'|'EXPIRED'|'NOT_YET_VALID', detail?: string }>
}   // never throws. Accepts: PEM (one or many blocks, CRLF, surrounding text), raw DER, bare base64 (no headers), PKCS#7/.p7b (PEM "PKCS7" or DER SignedData → extract certificates), detects PKCS#12 (.pfx; DER, base64 or PEM "PKCS12" / "PFX") → PKCS12_UNSUPPORTED (it takes no password: loadCertificates opens the bundle; detail `openssl pkcs12 -in file.pfx -nokeys -out cert.pem`), CSR ("CERTIFICATE REQUEST") → CSR_NOT_CERT.
export async function loadCertificates(input, { password = null, checkKey = false, now, subtle } = {}) -> {
  certificates, leaf, warnings,   // as parseCertificates; with a password the first PKCS#12 bundle's certificates join in file order (its PKCS12_UNSUPPORTED goes)
  pkcs12?: Pkcs12Summary          // only for a bundle that opened
}   // never rejects. No bundle or no password (null / undefined) → exactly parseCertificates()'s result. A bundle that does not open adds
    // PKCS12_BAD_PASSWORD (detail 'mac': the integrity check does not match; 'no-mac': nothing decrypts and no MAC tells a damaged file apart),
    // PKCS12_DAMAGED (detail: what is wrong) or PKCS12_UNSUPPORTED (detail: the algorithm or mode, 'iterations', 'webcrypto' without WebCrypto,
    // 'webcrypto-refused: <operation>' when the browser refused one, e.g. 'webcrypto-refused: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256'). No PRIVATE_KEY_PRESENT for a bundle: its summary counts the keys.
    // The leaf of an opened bundle is the certificate its private key is paired with by localKeyId, unless that one issued another certificate of the input
    // (a CA of the chain, e.g. the intermediate of p12_mismatch.p12); else pickLeaf as parseCertificates. The key check never moves it.
Pkcs12Summary = {
  certificates: number, keys: number, unencryptedKeys: number /* plain keyBags */, friendlyName: string|null /* the leaf's bag */,
  mac: { kind: 'hmac'|'pbmac1', hash: 'SHA-1'|'SHA-256'|'SHA-384'|'SHA-512', iterations, kdf: 'PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256'|null } | null,
  encryption: EncryptionInfo[] /* of the parts holding certificates */,
  keyEncryption: Array<EncryptionInfo | { unsupported }> /* of the encrypted keys, one per scheme; one this page cannot decrypt has unsupported: its name or OID alone, or 'iterations' on the EncryptionInfo */,
  passwordVerified: boolean       // false: no MAC and no encrypted certificates — read without the password, which nothing checked
  keyCheck: null /* not asked */ | { status: 'match'|'mismatch'|'nokey'|'nocert'|'unsupported'|'unsupported-encryption'|'failed', algorithm: 'RSA'|'EC P-256'|…|null, encryption: string|null, owner: Certificate|null }
}   // match: a key of the bundle belongs to the leaf; mismatch: none does (owner: the certificate of the bundle it belongs to, if any); nocert: no certificate read to check against;
    // unsupported: a key type the browser cannot check (algorithm); unsupported-encryption: the key's encryption cannot be undone here (encryption: its name / OID or 'iterations'); failed: the key did not decrypt although the rest did
    // One bundle per input: a second one is a PARSE_ERROR ("not opened … load it on its own"), never dropped silently.
export function parseCertificate(der: Uint8Array) -> Certificate           // throws CertificateParseError
export function issuedBy(child, parent) -> boolean                         // child names parent as its issuer: DNs equal, key ids agree when both exist (no signature check; lib/chainfix.js)
export function leafCertificates(certs) -> Certificate[]                   // every end-entity certificate of one input, in order: not a CA and not the issuer of another
                                                                           // (the rule `leaf` is picked by); a chain gives one, several pasted PEM blocks each (§5.43);
                                                                           // a self-issued certificate names itself as its issuer unless its AKI names another's SKI,
                                                                           // so self-signed twins with one subject (RSA + ECDSA) are both leaves
export async function computeFingerprints(der, { subtle = globalThis.crypto?.subtle } = {}) -> { sha256, sha1 }   // lowercase hex
export function pemEncode(der, label = 'CERTIFICATE') -> string
export function formatFingerprint(hex) -> 'AB:CD:...'
export function parseCertificateRequest(input /* string | bytes */) -> { csr: CertificateRequest|null, error: null|CSR_ERRORS, detail? }   // never throws; PEM (NEW) CERTIFICATE REQUEST,
                                              // bare base64 or DER; a private key (PEM label or DER shape) is never decoded: error 'private-key'; 'certificate', 'not-csr', 'invalid', 'empty'
CertificateRequest = { der, subjectDN, subjectCN, dnsNames /* extensionRequest SAN */, hostnames /* normalized; CN when none */, spkiDer, keyAlgorithm, keyBits, curve, signatureAlgorithm }
export function publicKeyId(spkiDer) -> string|null   // what identifies a key whatever its encoding: RSA modulus + exponent, EC curve + x + parity of y
                                              // (compressed = uncompressed), else the raw key; the CLI's bundle-check PublicKey.ident rule
export function csrMatchesCertificate(csr, cert) -> { match: boolean|null, missing: string[] /* asked, not in the certificate */, added: string[] /* in the certificate, not asked */ }
                                              // match: the certificate was issued for the CSR's key (from it or another CSR made with that key)
export function looksLikePrivateKey(text) -> boolean   // a `… PRIVATE KEY` PEM line (BEGIN or END; encrypted, OpenSSH) or bare base64 of a key's DER shape,
                                              // or of its first bytes only (a partial paste: SEQUENCE { INTEGER 0|1, SEQUENCE|OCTET STRING|INTEGER },
                                              // encrypted PKCS#8 by its PBE OID); only the outline is looked at (the CSR box drops a key the moment it lands)
export const CSR_ERRORS = ['empty', 'private-key', 'certificate', 'not-csr', 'invalid']
Certificate = {
  der: Uint8Array, version: number, serialHex: string, signatureAlgorithm: string /* e.g. 'sha256WithRSAEncryption','ecdsa-with-SHA256' */,
  subject: { CN?, O?, OU?, C?, ST?, L?, ... } (first value per attr), subjectDN: string /* RFC 2253/4514 like openssl -nameopt RFC2253 */, subjectCN: string|null,
  issuer: {...}, issuerDN: string, issuerCN: string|null,
  notBefore: Date, notAfter: Date,
  dnsNames: string[], ipAddresses: string[], emails: string[], uris: string[],
  hostnames: string[],            // dnsNames lowercased; if none, [subjectCN] when CN looks like a hostname (legacy fallback)
  keyAlgorithm: 'RSA'|'EC'|'Ed25519'|'Ed448'|'DSA'|'unknown', keyBits: number|null, curve: 'P-256'|'P-384'|'P-521'|string|null,
  isCA: boolean, pathLen: number|null, keyUsage: string[], extKeyUsage: string[] /* 'serverAuth', ... */,
  selfSigned: boolean, subjectKeyId: string|null, authorityKeyId: string|null,
  ocspUrls: string[], caIssuersUrls: string[], crlUrls: string[], isPrecertificate: boolean, sctCount: number|null
}
```

```js
export function installRanges(data|null) -> RangesInfo   // install a parsed { manifest, edges, networks } dataset (null → the built-in table); a wrong format or shape is refused whole with errorKind 'parse' and the ranges stay as they were
export function rangesInfo() -> { source: 'data'|'built-in', updated: 'YYYY-MM-DD', edges: {id:count}, networks: {id:count}, error: string|null, errorKind: string|null }
```
