```js
export function rdapStatus(rdap) -> SourceStatus|null  // Domain Health's RDAP card: null for an answer, a TLD without RDAP, an unregistered domain or bad input
export function dohStatus(response) -> SourceStatus|null   // DNS Lookup: a query that got no DNS answer (an rcode is an answer)
```

### 5.37 `lib/density.js` — compact result layouts
Pure: no DOM, network, clock or i18n.
```js
export const LOOKUP_FLAGS = ['aa', 'tc', 'rd', 'ra', 'ad', 'cd']
export function isNoData(response) -> boolean   // NOERROR with an empty answer section (no record of the type, no alias chain) and no Extended DNS Error
export function lookupLayout(types, responses /* DnsResponse|null per type */) -> {
  cards: string[],      // types that keep a card, in query order: pending, records or an alias chain, an error rcode, a failed query
  noRecords: string[],  // plain NODATA types: one "No records: AAAA, CAA, …" line of the summary instead of a card each
  failed: string[], pending: string[],
  shared: { resolver, nsid, flags: Record<flag, boolean>|null },   // what every DNS answer has in common, said once in the summary (null where they differ)
  own: { [type]: { resolver, nsid, flags } }                        // per card with a DNS answer: what it shows itself because it differs
}
export function foldZeroStats(stats /* [{ id, value }] */, { foldable }) -> { shown: string[], folded: string[] }   // zero counts of `foldable` ids fold into one sentence
```

### 5.38 `lib/jobprogress.js` — a long job's progress outside its view
A Subdomains / SSL Targets scan or a Bulk Resolve run takes minutes, and the user is often elsewhere meanwhile. `ui/jobs.js` shows its progress as a "(62%)" prefix of the tab title, a ring on the running view's navigation entry and a badge on the favicon, and can send a desktop notification when a long job ends. Pure: no DOM, clock, storage or i18n.
```js
export const LONG_JOB_MS = 30000
export const SCAN_STAGE_WEIGHTS = { sources: 10, mining: 0, wildcard: 5, bruteforce: 45, permutations: 20, resolve: 15, hints: 5, done: 0 }   // keys = scanner.SCAN_STAGES
export const ACTIVE_STAGE_CAP = 0.95
export function scanFraction(run /* { stages, progress } as applyStage / applyProgress record them */) -> number|null   // null before the first stage; skipped stages drop out;
  // an active (or stopped) stage counts for its done / total up to ACTIVE_STAGE_CAP of its weight — a stage whose counter is complete can keep running
  // (brute force waits for the passive sources), and one that reads as complete while the job does not move on looks like a hang
export function bulkFraction(job /* { names, done, ipTotal, ipDone, options } */) -> number|null   // names resolved; a quarter for PTR / ASN lookups when asked
export function advance(prev, next) -> number|null   // never below the last value (a stage's total can grow: the scan's recursive round)
export function combineJobs(jobs) -> { count, fraction }   // the least advanced determinate job, null when none is
export function percentOf(fraction) -> number|null        // whole percent, never 100 while running
export function progressTitle(base, label) -> '(62%) Subdomains · DomainScope'   // label null → '(…)'
export function faviconStep(fraction, { reducedMotion }) -> number|null   // 5 % steps, 10 % with reduced motion; never full
export const BRAND_ICON_SVG   // favicon.svg (tests/js/jobprogress.test.js keeps them equal)
export function badgedIcon(fraction, { svg }) -> string    // the icon with a white disc and a green pie in its corner (a dot when not known)
export function svgDataUrl(svg) -> 'data:image/svg+xml,…'  // the CSP allows img-src data:, which covers the favicon
export function pageNotifications({ api, userAgentData, userAgent }) -> boolean   // `new Notification()` usable: not Chromium on Android, tablets included (userAgentData.platform, else the UA string)
export function offerNotify({ elapsedMs, supported, permission, optedIn }) -> boolean   // "Notify me when done" once a job has run LONG_JOB_MS (or the session opted in)
export function shouldNotify({ optedIn, permission, status, durationMs, watching }) -> boolean   // opted in, granted, done or failed (never a cancel), ≥ LONG_JOB_MS, not watched
```

### 5.39 `lib/workspace.js` — customer workspaces
An engineer serving many customers keeps each one's data apart: the inventory (no DUPLICATE_IP across customers), the learned names (never tried under another customer's domains), the custom wordlist, the expected CAs (§5.42), free-text notes, the domains worked on, the Domain portfolio's policy (§5.64), the origin map of its proxied names (§5.70) and the accepted risks and known certificates (§5.95). Settings about the tool (theme, language, resolvers, parallelism) stay global (`state.js`, localStorage). DOM-free and storage-injected: the persistence is an async key-value `WorkspaceBackend` — IndexedDB in the browser (`assets/js/workspace-db.js`, database `ssds.workspaces`, one object store `records`), memory in the tests and where the browser refuses storage. The store keeps the active workspace in memory, so the views read it synchronously; every change is written through.
```js
export const DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_ID = 'default'   // always there; cannot be renamed or deleted (its name is null: the UI says "Default" / "Varsayılan")
export const WORKSPACE_PARTS = ['inventory', 'learned', 'wordlist', 'expectedCas', 'notes', 'recent', 'policy', 'origins', 'ctSeen', 'rdapSeen', 'rollout', 'waivers', 'reportHistory']   // origins: the origin map (§5.70); ctSeen: the CT watch's baseline (§5.75); rdapSeen: the registration watch's baseline (§5.96); rollout: the Rollout board's JSON text (§5.79), kept whole (≤ 262,144 characters) or not at all; waivers: the accepted risks (§5.95); reportHistory: the DMARC report history (§5.97)
export const WORKSPACE_LIMITS = { count: 100, name: 60, notes: 20000, recent: 20, expectedCas: 30, expectedCa: 120, learned: 5000, inventory: 16 MiB, wordlist: 8 MiB, policy: 16384, ctSeen: 1 MiB, rdapSeen: 512 KiB, waivers: 64 KiB, reportHistory: 4 MiB }
export const ACTIVE_WORKSPACE_KEY = 'ssds.workspace'   // the localStorage pointer to the active id: where a new page starts (tabs are independent)
export const LEGACY_KEYS = { inventory: 'ssds.inventory', learned: 'ssds.learned.labels', wordlist: 'ssds.wordlist.custom' }   // before workspaces (the last one in sessionStorage)
export class WorkspaceError { code: 'name-empty'|'name-taken'|'default'|'not-found'|'limit'|'part' }
export function normalizeWorkspaceName(input) -> string          // NFC, controls / zero-width / bidi overrides out, whitespace collapsed, ≤ 60 characters; '' when nothing is left
export function uniqueWorkspaceName(name, taken) -> string       // 'Acme' → 'Acme (2)' → 'Acme (3)' (case-insensitive; a trailing " (n)" is not doubled)
export function sanitizePart(part, value) -> value               // inventory { text, updatedAt } | null · learned { v: 1, seq, labels: { label: [hits, last] } } | null (isStorableLabel only) ·
  // wordlist string · expectedCas string[] (one per line / entry, de-duplicated without case) · notes string · recent [{ value, at }] (lib/session parseTarget: domains / host names only) ·
  // policy string (the editor's JSON as typed — a draft with a mistake too —, read and checked by lib/policy.js where it is used) ·
  // origins { v: 1, remember, entries } | null (lib/originmap.js sanitizeOriginMap: null while remembering is off and nothing is kept) ·
  // ctSeen string (the JSON text lib/ctwatch.js seenText writes, capped and kept as it is; read and checked by its readSeen, §5.75) ·
  // rdapSeen string (the JSON text lib/regwatch.js rdapSeenText writes, capped at 512 KiB and kept as it is; read and checked by its readRdapSeen, §5.96) ·
  // waivers string (the JSON text lib/waivers.js waiversPartText writes, kept whole up to 64 KiB, '' past it — a cut JSON text is no JSON; every entry checked when it is read, §5.95) ·
  // reportHistory string (the JSON text lib/dmarchistory.js historyText writes, kept whole — ≤ 4,194,304 characters: every write goes through its fitHistory, which prunes a longer one — or not at all:
  // a cut text is no JSON; read and checked by its readHistory, §5.97)
export function sanitizeWorkspaceData(data) ; emptyWorkspaceData() ; sanitizeExpectedCas(value) ; sanitizeRecent(value)
export function addRecent(list, value, at) -> list               // to the top; the top entry again changes nothing; IPs and junk never enter
export function readLegacyData({ local, session }) -> { data, present: [{ area, key }] }   // reads only
export function createMemoryBackend(entries?, { persistent = false, exists }) -> WorkspaceBackend & { entries(), fail: Set }   // `fail`: tests make operations reject
export function createWorkspaceStore({ backend, pointer, legacy, channel, now, newId }) -> {
  open() -> Promise<{ active, list, migrated: string[], persistent }>, persistent, database, lastError, active, data, list(),
  save(part, value) -> Promise<boolean>, recordRecent(value, at?), switchTo(id), create(name, data?) -> { meta, persisted }, rename(id, name),
  remove(id) -> { switched, persisted }, replace(id, data), load(id), destroy() -> Promise<boolean>, idle() -> Promise<void>, subscribe(fn) -> unsubscribe }
WorkspaceBackend = { persistent, exists() -> Promise<boolean|null>, get(keys), list(prefix), write(puts, deletes, { guard }) -> Promise<boolean> /* one transaction */, destroy() }
WriteGuard = { key, update(stored) -> value | undefined }   // read and written back in the write's transaction; undefined: nothing written (false)
```
Records: `'meta'` `{ v, createdAt, migrated }` (written with the first write), `'wsmeta/<id>'` `{ id, name, createdAt, updatedAt }` (a Default nothing was written to has no record, and its dates are null: the dialog shows no "changed …" for it), `'wsdata/<id>/<part>'` (an empty part has no record). **Opening** never creates a database: `exists()` (`indexedDB.databases()` where the browser has it) false means nothing is read either. **First run** (no `'meta'`): the legacy keys that are present move into Default in one transaction with `'meta'`; they are removed only after it committed, so an interrupted migration loses nothing: the page's next write that commits carries it (Default's parts as the page holds them, with what was saved to Default since, and `migrated` in `'meta'`; a write without them would end the migration), unless another tab wrote first, and otherwise it runs again on the next load; without persistent storage the data is read into memory and the keys stay. `migrated` lists the parts that moved (state.js `migrated`; the shell counts it as an earlier visit). **Writes**: `save` updates memory at once; one write per part at a time, and the values saved while it runs are written once after it as the latest (a burst of keystrokes in a long wordlist writes it once per write); a write still waiting is dropped by `destroy()` and by deleting its workspace (it would bring them back); `replace` updates a waiting write to the new value. Every write of parts reads the workspace's meta in its own transaction (a `WriteGuard`) and only moves its `updatedAt`: it never undoes a rename another tab made meanwhile, and writes nothing for a workspace another tab deleted (`lastError` `WorkspaceError('not-found')`). A failed write keeps memory and sets `lastError`; saving the same value again retries it (only a value that was written is skipped). A workspace whose creation could not be written (a full storage for a moment, an open that timed out) is kept in this tab with every part saved to it, and its next write stores its meta as this tab has it, with those parts: once storage works again it is stored, and `'not-found'` stays for a workspace that was stored and is gone. A workspace whose parts could not be read is never shown empty or saved over: `switchTo` rejects with the read error and switches nothing (the shell: "The workspace could not be opened: …"), the page opens in Default instead of it, `load` rejects, and a Default the page must enter all the same (its workspace was deleted) keeps what is saved to it in memory (`save` false, `lastError` the read error) until a read of it succeeds. A backend that cannot be read at all (a database of a later version, a broken one, an open that timed out, storage the browser refuses) makes the rest of the page work in memory (`persistent` false); `database` stays true when a database is there to delete — listed by `exists()`, or a failure only a database causes (`impliesDatabase`: VersionError, NotFoundError, `'idb-timeout'`) —, never for a refusal (Chrome's blocked site data answers every call, the deletion too, with an UnknownError). `destroy()` resets memory at once (Default only, empty) and deletes the database, also one the page could not read (IndexedDB deletes a database of any version without opening it); once it succeeded `lastError` is null. **Other tabs**: a BroadcastChannel-like `channel` carries `{ type: 'data', id, parts }`, `{ type: 'list' }` and `{ type: 'destroyed' }` after each committed write; a tab re-reads the parts of its active workspace, the list, and goes on in Default when its workspace was deleted elsewhere. `subscribe` reports only these external changes (`'data' | 'list' | 'switch' | 'destroyed'`). Tests: `tests/js/workspace.test.js`, `tests/js/state-migration.test.js` (through state.js), `tests/e2e/workspaces.e2e.mjs` (real IndexedDB).

`state.js` over the store: `ready` (the shell waits for it before the first view, at most 8 s), `workspace` / `workspaces` (`{ id, name, isDefault, createdAt, updatedAt }`), `workspaceData(part)` (a copy), `setWorkspaceData(part, value)` (not the inventory: `setInventory`), `recordRecent(value)`, `learnedStorage`, `switchWorkspace(id)` (clears `state.session`, emits `'inventory'` then `'workspace'`), `createWorkspace(name, data?)`, `renameWorkspace`, `deleteWorkspace` (the active one: a switch to Default), `replaceWorkspace(id, data)`, `loadWorkspace(id)`, `whenSaved()`, `workspacePersistence`, `workspaceDatabase` (a database is there, in use or not: "Delete all local data" deletes it), `workspaceError`, `migrated`. `setInventory()` returns `{ persisted, inventory, done }` (`done`: whether the write succeeded). `clearAll()` returns a promise (false only when something stored could not be removed: a localStorage that throws on removal, a database whose deletion failed; a blocked storage held nothing; afterwards `workspaceError` / `lastPersistError` hold only the error of the step that failed); memory is reset and `'inventory'`, `'settings'`, `'workspaces'`, `'cleared'` are emitted at once. New state events: `'workspace'` (another workspace is active: the views that keep a customer's results in module state — Subdomains, SSL Targets with Verify / DANE, Bulk Resolve, the Certificate view, Zone File, Reverse DNS — drop them, stopping what runs, as on `'cleared'`), `'workspaces'` (the list or a name changed), `'workspaceData'` (`{ parts }` other than the inventory changed; `origin: 'external'` from another tab). `handleExternalChange` re-reads only the settings now.

### 5.40 `lib/cryptobox.js` — password encryption of a file
WebCrypto only, `crypto` injectable. `sealText(text, password, { iterations = DEFAULT_ITERATIONS, context, crypto })` → `{ kdf: { name: 'PBKDF2', hash: 'SHA-256', iterations, salt }, cipher: { name: 'AES-GCM', iv }, data }` (base64): PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 over the password (NFC, UTF-8) and a random 16-byte salt derives a 256-bit AES key; AES-GCM with a random 12-byte IV encrypts the text, and its additional authenticated data binds the caller's `context` and every parameter, so a changed iteration count, salt, IV or ciphertext fails like a wrong password. `DEFAULT_ITERATIONS` 600,000; `MIN_ITERATIONS` 310,000 (refused below, sealing and opening); `MAX_ITERATIONS` 5,000,000 (refused above on opening); `MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH` 8 characters. `openText(box, password, { context, crypto })` → the text. `BoxError` codes: `password-required`, `password-short`, `wrong-password` (AES-GCM cannot tell a wrong password from a changed box: the message says both), `damaged` (not a readable box: bad base64, lengths, iteration count), `unsupported` (another KDF / hash / cipher), `crypto-unavailable` (an insecure context). `encodeBase64` / `decodeBase64` (strict, chunked), `checkBox`. The password is never stored. Tests: `tests/js/cryptobox.test.js`.

### 5.41 `lib/handover.js` — the workspace hand-over file
One JSON file with everything of one workspace, to move it to another browser or hand it to a colleague. Plain: `{ format: 'domainscope-workspace', v: 1, encrypted: false, workspace }`; sealed (§5.40, `context` `'domainscope-workspace/1'`): `{ format, v, encrypted: true, kdf, cipher, data }`, whose ciphertext is the JSON of `workspace` — a sealed file shows no name, server or address (and the dialog saves it as `domainscope-workspace-encrypted-<stamp>.json`, so its file name does not give the workspace away either). `workspace` = `{ name, default, exportedAt, app, parts }` (empty parts left out; the origin map, §5.70, is the part `origins`; the CT watch's and the registration watch's baselines, §5.75 and §5.96, the parts `ctSeen` and `rdapSeen`, so a colleague's next check compares with the last one made in the workspace; the accepted risks, §5.95, the part `waivers`, their JSON text as it is; the DMARC report history, §5.97, the part `reportHistory`, sealed with the rest when a password is given). `exportWorkspaceFile(ws, { password, iterations, crypto })` → text (indented); `readWorkspaceFile(text)` → `{ encrypted, file }` (the outside only); `openWorkspaceFile(text, { password })` → `{ name, isDefault, exportedAt, app, data, encrypted }`, every part through `sanitizeWorkspaceData` (so an imported file carries no IP-shaped learned label, no IP in the recent list, no tool settings). `HandoverError` codes: `too-large` (over 40 MiB), `not-json`, `not-workspace`, `newer` (a later format version), `damaged`, and §5.40's. Tests: `tests/js/handover.test.js`.

### 5.42 `lib/expectedca.js` — expected CAs
A workspace's `expectedCas` against an issuer. `resolveExpectedCa(entry)` → `{ entry, ca, needle }`: with lib/health.js's `CAA_ISSUERS`, a CA's name, id or CAA identifier (and a brand its regex knows: ZeroSSL → Sectigo, RapidSSL → DigiCert) is that CA; anything else is text to find (a private CA). Entries, names and issuers are compared case-insensitively, with whitespace collapsed and a typographic apostrophe (“Let’s Encrypt”, as iOS Smart Punctuation types it) read as `'`. `expectedCaStatus(issuer /* DN or parsed name */, entries)` → `{ expected, entry, ca }` or null without entries or issuer (no badge); `expectedCaaStatus(domain, entries)` → `{ expected, entry }` or null (a known CA by any identifier; a text entry must equal the domain). `ui/expected-ca.js` draws "Expected CA" / "Unexpected CA" (`data-expected-ca`) next to the issuer of the Certificate view's overview and summary (SSL Targets step 1 shows the summary), the CAA tab's issuer line, SSL Targets › Verify (a served certificate's issuer: only "Unexpected CA" in the table, either in the details) and Domain Health's CAA card (each issue / issuewild CA); the views redraw on a change (`expectedCasChanged`; the Certificate view only the certificate's part, so a "No file?" lookup running in its loader goes on and loads what it finds). Tests: `tests/js/expectedca.test.js`.

### 5.43 `lib/certsets.js` — several certificates at once (a renewal week)
A renewal week often brings more than one certificate: an RSA + ECDSA pair for the same names, plus a few others. SSL Targets takes them all, scans the union of their names once and plans which set each server needs. DOM-free and pure; certificates are §5.2 objects, files are views/cert.js CertLoads (`{ name, result: parseCertificates() }`) or bare results.
```js
export const SKIP_ISSUES = ['no-certificate', 'ca-only', 'no-names']
export function renewalBundle(files) -> { leaves: RenewalLeaf[], sets: CertSet[], chain: Certificate[], skipped: [{ file, index, issue, codes, subject?, count?, key? }], unread: [{ file, index, details }], replaced: [{ leaf, by, set, bySet }], duplicates, keyFiles: string[] }
  // every end-entity certificate of the files (x509 leafCertificates), in load order; the same DER from two files is one leaf with both `files`;
  // a file of CA certificates only gives its self-signed ones that issued none of its others and name hosts in subjectAltName, or by a host-name CN without
  // keyCertSign (`openssl req -x509` marks a server certificate CA:TRUE; the CLI bundle check's rule, §7), so a private root is still `ca-only`;
  // a file without a certificate (a key, a CSR, a PKCS#12 bundle: the parser's `codes`), with CA certificates only (`chain` material) or a leaf without a DNS name
  // is `skipped` (index = the file's position, key = that leaf's); keyFiles: files that also held a private key (ignored, never shown);
  // unread: files that gave certificates but also PARSE_ERROR warnings (`details` their text: a damaged block next to good ones, so a certificate may be missing);
  // replaced: replacedLeaves with the ids of the two leaves' sets
RenewalLeaf = { key /* leafKey: the DER as hex */, cert, names /* lowercase, sortHostnames */, files, keyType /* 'RSA 2048', 'ECDSA P-256', 'Ed25519'… */, keySlug /* rsa | ecdsa | ed25519 | ed448 | dsa | cert */ }
export function groupCertSets(leaves) -> CertSet[]   // equal name sets form one set; ids 'A', 'B', … 'Z', 'AA' (setId) in load order; a set's leaves by key type (RSA, ECDSA,
                                                     // Ed25519, Ed448, DSA), then the newest first (notBefore, else notAfter), then load order, so a folder listed by
                                                     // name gives the same set and file names, and of two with one key type the older is the CLI's `-2`
export function replacedLeaves(leaves) -> [{ leaf, by }]   // leaves another loaded leaf probably replaces (last year's certificate next to its renewal, which would
                                                           // count as new): the same keySlug, every name among the other's (names compared as they are), the other
                                                           // issued later (notBefore, else notAfter; of equal names and dates the one loaded later); `by` the newest
CertSet = { id, names, leaves, certs, keyTypes, files, notAfter /* latest */, expires /* earliest */ }
export function assignSet(name, sets) -> { set, by, exact }|null   // of the sets covering the name (domain.certCovers): exact before wildcard, the most specific
                                                                   // wildcard, the latest notAfter, the set loaded first
export function setOfName(sets) -> (name) => setId|null            // memoised assignSet (verify.buildVerifyPairs setOf)
export function planRenewal(scanResult, sets) -> { sets, assigned: Map<name, { set, by, exact }>, uncovered: [{ name, servers, resolving }], rows: PlanRow[], perSet: { [id]: { names, rows, servers, addresses } }, plain }
  // rows: each ServerGroup with a covered name (scan order), then each unmatched address; cells[setId] = [{ name, ips, via }] (dns over zone over hint, the
  // strongest kept); needsCert: a DNS or zone name, maybe: hints only. uncovered: scanned hosts no set covers (wildcard suspects left out), those on your servers
  // first, then resolving ones; perSet: the names assigned and the rows needing the set, `servers` of the inventory and `addresses` outside it
  // plain: the servers the names reach that never get a set (terminates_tls=no and not suspect, §5.69): [{ server: { id, name, ips }, behind, passthrough, backends }]; they are
  // in no row. A row of a server group with a topology carries it (`topology`), for the notes and the work list's Topology column
export const WORKLIST_COLUMNS; export function workListRows(plan) -> rows   // one per server (or address) × set: server, ip, names, candidates (origin hints),
                                                                           // set, setNames, keyTypes, expires, files (toCsv joins names and IPs with spaces;
                                                                           // key types, which hold spaces, with ' + ' and file names with '; ')
export function workListColumns(plan) -> columns   // WORKLIST_COLUMNS, then 'Topology' (lib/topology.js TOPOLOGY_CSV_COLUMN) when a row has a topology
export function cliCertFiles(sets) -> [{ file /* new-cert-<set>-<key>.pem, -2 … on a clash */, set, leaf }]   // one --cert file per certificate
export function certSetsJson(sets) -> object[]   // ids, names, key types and each certificate's identity and files, never the DER
export function leafKey(cert), withoutLeaf(files, key) /* every file loses it; a file left without a leaf goes */, primaryFile(files) /* the first with a leaf */,
  fileForLeaf(files, key) /* a file showing that leaf on its own, with the file's chain */, keyTypeOf(cert) -> { label, slug }, setId(index)
```

### 5.44 `lib/renewal.js` — Renewal readiness: will the next ACME renewal validate?
With 47-day certificates and multi-perspective issuance corroboration (MPIC: the CA repeats every domain validation and CAA lookup from several networks), a renewal that needs a hand fails. DOM-free; all DNS goes through an injected client with the DohClient contract, `query(name, type, { resolver, dnssec, cd, signal, noCache })` only, memoised per check (a parent's CAA record set is asked once per resolver for all its names); a failed lookup is a finding, only an abort rejects. What is sent: names and record types to the DoH resolvers, only after a click or on a shared link — CAA (tree climbing, on the chain and on each `CONSISTENCY_RESOLVERS` member by name), SOA with DO (and with CD after a SERVFAIL), TXT at `_acme-challenge.<name>` (with CD after a SERVFAIL), NS of the zone that takes the DNS-01 record (only when DNS-01 may be used, and not under an acme-dns delegation, whose registration is updated through the acme-dns API), A / AAAA (only when HTTP-01 / TLS-ALPN-01 may be used).
```js
export const RENEWAL_CHALLENGES = ['http-01','dns-01','tls-alpn-01','unknown'], RENEWAL_VERDICTS = ['fail','unknown','warnings','ready'] /* worst first */,
  RENEWAL_HEADLINES = ['fail','incomplete','warnings','ready','none'],
  RENEWAL_LIMITS = { names: 50, http01Names: 10 }, CONSISTENCY_RESOLVERS = ['cloudflare','google','dnssb','cznic'], ACME_CHALLENGE_LABEL = '_acme-challenge',
  HTTP01_PATH_PREFIX = '/.well-known/acme-challenge/', HTTP01_LOCATIONS = [{ continent: 'EU' }, { continent: 'NA' }, { continent: 'AS' }], HTTP01_TIMEOUT_S = 10,
  RENEWAL_AREAS = ['caa','resolvers','wildcard','acme','provider','dnssec','http','http01'], RENEWAL_FINDINGS /* 63 ids */, HTTP01_OUTCOMES /* 21, 'connect-timeout' apart from 'timeout' */, HTTP01_VERDICTS = ['ok','partial','failed','catch-all','inconclusive','untested'],
  RENEWAL_CSV_COLUMNS, RENEWAL_I18N /* renew.f.<id>.title / .detail, renew.o.<outcome>, renew.v.<verdict>, renew.head.<headline>, renew.ch.<challenge>, renew.area.<area> */
export const RENEWAL_CAS = [{ id, name, domains }]   // the form's CAs with lib/health.js CAA_ISSUERS identifiers: letsencrypt, zerossl (sectigo.com), google, sectigo, digicert, globalsign, buypass, actalis, sslcom, amazon, godaddy, harica, certum, entrust, microsoft
export const DNS_PROVIDERS = [{ id, name, ns: (suffix|RegExp)[], api, lego, acmesh, certbot: { pkg, official }|null }]   // Cloudflare, Route 53, Azure, Google Cloud DNS, DigitalOcean, Hetzner, OVHcloud, GoDaddy, Linode, Vultr,
  // Gandi, Namecheap, NS1, DNSimple, DNS Made Easy, Porkbun, IONOS, deSEC, Infomaniak, Bunny, Vercel, ClouDNS, Alibaba, Scaleway, Hurricane Electric, Akamai Edge DNS, UltraDNS, acme-dns;
  // api: false (no lego / acme.sh / certbot plugin): Natro (natrohost.com), Turhost (turhost.com), İsimtescil (isimtescil.net, dnsenable.com)
export function parseRenewalNames(input, { max = 50 }) -> { names: [{ name, base, wildcard }], invalid: string[], suffixWildcards: string[], overCap }   // host names and *. wildcards (URLs, a trailing dot, # comments ok); IPs, single labels, '_' → invalid;
  // a wildcard directly under a public suffix of the list's ICANN section (`*.co.uk`, `*.com.tr`; not `*.github.io`) → suffixWildcards: no CA issues it (Baseline Requirements §3.2.2.6)
export function renewalCa(id) -> RENEWAL_CAS entry|null ; export function caForIssuer(issuer /* DN or { CN, O } */) -> id|null   // ZeroSSL before Sectigo; an issuer outside the list → null
export function dnsProvidersFor(nsHosts) -> { providers, unmatched } ; export function isAcmeDnsTarget(name) -> bool /* a UUID first label */ ; export function pluginText(provider) -> 'lego --dns cloudflare · acme.sh --dns dns_cf · certbot-dns-cloudflare'
export async function checkRenewal({ names, ca = null, challenge = 'unknown' }, { dns, signal, resolvers = CONSISTENCY_RESOLVERS, noCache, concurrency = 4, onProgress, now })
  -> { startedAt, finishedAt, ca: RENEWAL_CAS entry|null, challenge, resolvers, names: NameResult[] }   // TypeError for an unknown challenge or CA
export async function checkRenewalName(entry, { run, ca, challenge, resolvers }) -> NameResult   // for tests
NameResult = { name, base, wildcard,
  caa: { name, foundAt, records: string[] /* '0 issue "letsencrypt.org"' */, parsed, chain, error, rcode },
  resolvers: [{ id, state: 'ok'|'servfail'|'error', rcode, error, foundAt, records, key, parsed }],
  acme: { owner, state: 'none'|'txt'|'cname'|'dangling'|'servfail'|'bogus'|'error', rcode, cnames, target, acmeDns, txt, ede, zone, error },
  dnssec: { state: 'secure'|'unsigned'|'bogus'|'servfail'|'unknown'|'error', zone, ede, resolver, rcode, error },
  dnsHost: { zone, ns, providers, unmatched, error }|null /* the zone that takes the TXT record: the delegation target's, else the name's own */,
  address: { status, cnames, ipv4, ipv6, error, kind, provider, hidesOrigin }|null, http01: Http01Test|null,
  findings: [{ id, area, severity: 'ok'|'info'|'warn'|'error', params /* strings and numbers, language-neutral */, unchecked?: true /* a lookup the verdict rests on got no answer here */ }], verdict }
export function nameFindings(nameResult, { ca, challenge }) -> findings   // pure, in RENEWAL_AREAS order ; export function nameVerdict(findings) -> 'fail'|'unknown'|'warnings'|'ready'
export function http01Token() -> 'domainscope-check-<16 [a-z0-9]>' ; export function http01Plan(nameResult) -> { ok, families: Array<4|6> }
export function http01Request(host, { token, ipVersion }) -> body   // globalping.httpGetRequest: port 80, HTTP01_LOCATIONS, timeout 10
export function redirectOutcome(location, { host, path }) -> outcome ; export function http01Outcome(result, { host, path }) -> { outcome, status, location, address, failure }
export function http01Verdict(probes) -> verdict ; export function interpretHttp01(measurement, { host, path, ipVersion }) -> { ipVersion, measurementId, path, verdict, probes: [{ place, probe, outcome, status, location, address, failure }] }
export function http01Families(planned /* http01Plan families */, read /* interpretHttp01 results */, { path, at, earlier /* the name's previous http01 */ }) -> families   // plan order, each with the time it was measured (`at`);
  // a planned family not measured this time (the test stopped) keeps the earlier test's family (its own `at`, else that test's) or → { ipVersion, measurementId: null, path, verdict: 'untested', probes: [], at: null }
export function http01Findings(test, { challenge, name }) -> findings ; export function applyHttp01(report, name, test|null) -> report   // a new report; that name's findings and verdict recomputed
export function renewalSummary(report) -> { total, counts: { ready, warnings, unknown, fail }, headline: 'fail'|'incomplete'|'warnings'|'ready'|'none', tested }
export function renewalRows(report) -> rows /* RENEWAL_CSV_COLUMNS, codes and record data */ ; export function renewalExport(report, { app, version }) -> { schema: 'domainscope.renewal/1', … }
```
Findings (challenge-dependent severities: a problem that stops the chosen method is an error, one that stops a method that may be used — the challenge 'unknown' — a warning; a wildcard is judged as DNS-01 whatever was chosen, since only DNS-01 validates one — CAA methods, `_acme-challenge` and the provider — and `wildcard.*` says when the chosen method is another):
- **caa** (checkCaaAllows with the CA's CAA identifiers; issuewild for a wildcard): `caa.none` / `caa.open` / `caa.allowed` (ok); `caa.restricted` (info, the RFC 8657 alternatives) with `caa.method-blocked` (error: no alternative allows the chosen challenge), `caa.method-check` (warn: challenge not known, every alternative lists methods) and `caa.account` (info: every usable alternative pins an ACME account); `caa.no-ca` (info, no CA chosen: who is authorized); `caa.denied` (error, with the identifier to add), `caa.deny-all`, `caa.critical`, `caa.unusable` (error); `caa.cname` (info: a level answered through its alias); `caa.servfail` (error: a CA must not issue) vs `caa.error` (warn, unchecked: this browser could not ask).
- **resolvers**: `resolvers.agree` (ok, two or more answered alike), `resolvers.differ` (warn; error when a variant denies the chosen CA: MPIC may hit it), `resolvers.servfail` (warn), `resolvers.unreachable` (info), `resolvers.unchecked` (warn: fewer than two answered, so nothing was compared; the CSV says `not compared`, never `agree (1)`).
- **wildcard**: `wildcard.dns01` (ok), `wildcard.unknown` (warn), `wildcard.method` (error: HTTP-01 / TLS-ALPN-01 chosen).
- **acme** (`_acme-challenge.<base>` TXT): `acme.none` (ok, only when DNS-01 may be used), `acme.leftover` (info), `acme.cname` / `acme.acme-dns` (info, alias mode), `acme.dangling` (a CNAME to NXDOMAIN: error for DNS-01 — the renewal fails and whoever creates the target can pass DNS-01 — else warn), `acme.servfail`, `acme.bogus` (SERVFAIL that answers with CD), `acme.error` (warn; unchecked for DNS-01).
- **provider** (only when DNS-01 may be used; none under an acme-dns delegation): `provider.known` (info, the plugins), `provider.no-api` (warn for DNS-01 or a wildcard, else info: delegate `_acme-challenge` to a zone a client can update), `provider.target-no-api` (the same for the zone `_acme-challenge` is already delegated to: point the CNAME elsewhere), `provider.multiple` (split hosting: the record must be at each), `provider.unknown`, `provider.error`.
- **dnssec**: `secure` / `unsigned` (ok), `bogus` (error: SERVFAIL that answers with CD — CAA and every method fail), `servfail` (error, not DNSSEC), `unknown` (info), `error` (warn).
- **http** (not for a wildcard or DNS-01): `http.ok` (ok), `http.ipv6` (info: both families must serve the challenge; Let's Encrypt tries IPv6 first), `http.cdn` (info) / `http.alpn-cdn` (error: a CDN that terminates TLS stops TLS-ALPN-01), `http.private` / `http.none` / `http.nxdomain` / `http.dangling` (error, warn when not known), `http.private-some` (warn), `http.error` (warn, unchecked for HTTP-01 / TLS-ALPN-01; left out when DNSSEC already says the name fails). When only one family's lookup got no answer (`address.failed`: `[{ type: 'A'|'AAAA', error }]`), `http.family-error` (warn, unchecked for HTTP-01 / TLS-ALPN-01: the CA may connect over that family) and `http.ok-partial` (ok: only the family read is counted, never "0 IPv6"); no `http.none` / `http.dangling` / `http.private` then (an NXDOMAIN answer still speaks for both), and the HTTP-01 test plans only the family read.
- **http01** (after a test, per family): `ok` / `redirect` (ok: every probe got 404 / 410 or a redirect a CA follows — http or https, port 80 or 443, not an IP address, the token kept), `partial` (warn: some regions only; an error for HTTP-01 when more than one probe could not reach the server — MPIC tolerates one failing remote perspective, two with six or more, Baseline Requirements §3.2.2.9), `failed` (error for HTTP-01, warn when not known), `v6-fallback` (warn: every IPv6 failure is the connection itself — a connect timeout, a refusal, an unreachable network — while IPv4 passed: Let's Encrypt retries such a connection over IPv4 (Boulder's dial-error fallback), other CAs may not, so only with Let's Encrypt or no CA chosen — another chosen CA keeps `failed`; such IPv6 failures in some regions only make `partial` a warning, not a quorum error; an IPv6 server that answers wrongly stays an error), `catch-all` (warn: 2xx for a made-up token), `inconclusive` (info: only probe-side failures), `untested` (info: the test stopped before this family's measurement was created and no earlier test measured it). Outcomes: timeouts (`connect-timeout` while establishing the TCP connection, `timeout` any other), refused connections, DNS failures, 401 / 403, 5xx, another status, a redirect to itself / another port / an IP / another scheme / dropping the token, or without a target fail.

Verdict per name: 'fail' with any error; 'unknown' ("Could not be checked") when a lookup the verdict rests on got no answer in this browser — the effective CAA lookup (`caa.error`), the addresses for HTTP-01 / TLS-ALPN-01 (`http.error`, or one family's: `http.family-error`), `_acme-challenge` for DNS-01 or a wildcard (`acme.error`), both of those when the method is not known — so a name whose lookups were all rate-limited or dropped never reads as ready; 'warnings' with any warning; else 'ready'. The summary's headline is the worst verdict ('incomplete' for 'unknown': "At least one name could not be checked — check again"); the counts, Copy summary (`sum.renew.unknown`), CSV and JSON (`summary.unknown`, `unchecked: true` on those findings, a per-family `at` in `http01`) carry it.

### 5.45 `lib/retire.js` — what still points at an address (Retire an IP)
Before a server is switched off or renumbered: every DNS record, CNAME chain, SPF mechanism, MX / NS host, HTTPS address hint and imported-zone record that still reaches its address. DOM-free; DNS through the injected client (`dns.query(name, type, { signal })`, `dns.resolveHost(name, { signal })`: a DohClient, whose cache makes a repeated check cheap). Nothing is sent by importing it; the addresses are only compared here.
```js
export const RETIRE_MAX_ADDRESSES = 256, RETIRE_MIN_PREFIX = { 4: 24, 6: 120 }, RETIRE_MAX_DOMAINS = 25, RETIRE_MAX_HOSTS = 1000 /* every domain together */,
  RETIRE_MAX_MX = 10, RETIRE_MAX_NS = 13, RETIRE_MAX_ZONE_REFS = 1000 /* zone records verified live */, PASSIVE_MAX_ADDRESSES = 8, PASSIVE_SOURCES = ['hackertarget', 'thc'],
  FAILURE_KINDS = ['name', 'mx', 'ns', 'spf', 'https']
export const SEVERITIES = ['mail', 'ns', 'live', 'origin', 'chain', 'file', 'stale', 'unknown'], VERIFIED_STATES = ['live', 'file', 'hidden', 'internal', 'unverified', 'unknown'],
  CHANGE_ACTIONS = ['remove', 'repoint', 'narrow', 'follow', 'glue', 'provider', 'origin', 'keep', 'check'], UNKNOWN_REASONS = ['macro', 'ptr', 'lookup-failed', 'skipped', 'include-failed', 'multiple'],
  HOST_SOURCES = ['scan', 'zone', 'passive', 'discovered'], TARGET_ISSUES = ['invalid', 'too-large', 'host-bits', 'over-cap', 'private', 'nothing'],
  RETIRE_CSV_COLUMNS = ['group', 'severity', 'name', 'type', 'value', 'address', 'action', 'verified', 'via', 'sources', 'line']
export function parseRetireTargets(text, { max = 256 }) -> { kind: 'empty'|'addresses', blocks: RetireBlock[], addresses /* every single address */, total, issues: [{ code, severity, params }], ok, label }
  // addresses (brackets, a mapped IPv4 → IPv4) and networks up to a /24 (IPv6 /120; wider: too-large, error); host bits masked (host-bits, info); a block inside
  // another counts once; over `max` distinct addresses: over-cap (error); junk: invalid (warn); private space kept with a `private` note (public resolvers
  // do not see split-horizon records); '#' comments. RetireBlock = { input, cidr, label, version, network, prefix, size, first, last, single }
export function parseDomainList(text, { max = 25 }) -> { domains, invalid, truncated }   // host names (URL, trailing dot, '*.' cleaned); addresses and single labels invalid
export function retireTokens(text) ; rangeOf(address, prefix?) ; blockOf(address, blocks)
export function rangeRelation(range, block) -> 'equal'|'contains'|'within'|null   // CIDR blocks nest or do not touch; never across families
export function effectiveQualifier(chain /* [{ kind: 'include'|'redirect', qualifier }] outermost first */, qualifier) -> '+'|'-'|'~'|'?'|null
  // what a term gives the checked domain (RFC 7208 §5.2): through an include only a pass counts, then the include's qualifier; a redirect passes it on; null = no match
export function spfCoverage(tree /* spfLookupCount().tree, §5.15 extension */, blocks, { mxAddresses /* host → { addresses, error } */ }) -> { matches: SpfMatch[], unknown: SpfUnknown[] }
  // ip4 / ip6: the range against each block; a / mx: each address of the named host (MX hosts from mxAddresses) widened by the term's CIDR length (a/24);
  // include / redirect followed with the path. "Cannot tell", never "not covered": a macro that needs the sender (%{i}, %{s}, %{l} …; %{d} / %{o} are
  // expanded by health.js), ptr, a failed or skipped lookup, an include whose policy could not be read. exists without such a macro does not depend on the address.
  // Term order (the first match wins): within one policy, the first ip4 / ip6 / a / mx term that covers a whole block decides for it — a later match gets
  // `shadowedBy` ({ term, qualifier }), and a later pass term joins the earlier match's `shields` (an include in between, or a term that cannot be told, is not weighed).
  // SpfMatch = { path, holder, record, term, mechanism, qualifier, effective, relation, block, range, via: { host, address }|null, shadowedBy, shields };
  // SpfUnknown = { path, holder, record, term, mechanism, reason, target }
export function spfMxHosts(tree) -> string[]   // lib/health.js spfMxHosts (§5.15), re-exported
export async function checkDomain(domain, { dns, blocks, hosts /* [{ name, source }] */, signal, onLookup(done, total) }) -> DomainCheck
  // its own name, the known hosts, MX (≤ 10) and NS (≤ 13) hosts, each resolved; its SPF tree (spfLookupCount) and the addresses of every host an mx
  // mechanism names; the HTTPS record's ipv4hint / ipv6hint. DomainCheck = { domain, names: [{ name, status, cnames, ipv4, ipv6, error, errorKind,
  // familyErrors /* with NOERROR, the family whose question got no answer (§5.9 HostResolution.familyErrors), [] otherwise */,
  // roles: 'apex'|'host'|'mx'|'ns'|'spf', sources }], mx, ns, spf: { status: 'ok'|'none'|'failed'|'multiple', record, lookups, matches, unknown }, https, failures,
  // missing /* its own name NXDOMAIN without a CNAME (a dangling alias exists) and no name server: the domain does not exist, a typo in the list most likely */ }.
  // A failed lookup is a failure (never "nothing points here"), and so is a failed A (AAAA) question of a name when a block is IPv4 (IPv6), even
  // when the other family answered; an SPF a / mx host in that state is also an `unknown` entry (lookup-failed) next to what its other family matched.
  // A domain SPF record that could not be read is also an `unknown` entry
  // (mechanism 'record', reason lookup-failed), so it is a "cannot tell" row, never "no SPF"; only an abort rejects.
export function zoneCandidates(records /* §5.22 referenceRecords */, blocks) -> ZoneRef[]   // A / AAAA with the address, CNAMEs whose in-zone chain ends at one,
  // MX / NS / SRV / HTTPS / SVCB whose in-zone target holds one (a DNS-only CNAME into a proxied name takes its proxy status), HTTPS / SVCB hints, SPF ip4 / ip6;
  // `targetInternal`: the target or a name on its in-zone chain looks internal
export async function verifyZoneRefs(refs, { dns, signal, max = 1000, labelFn = randomLabel }) -> ZoneRef[] with `live`: true / false / null (failed, or the address's family failed)
  // does public DNS still serve each? A wildcard owner `*.x` is asked at a random name under it (`<label>.x`, one per owner, kept as `probe`), like the
  // Zone File live check, and is a record like any other (live / file / unverified — never "zone file only" without an answer that says so). A proxied
  // record's origin and an internal-looking name are never asked (`live` undefined); a served record whose target looks internal is live without its
  // target being asked; past `max` records to ask, the rest keep `live` undefined with `capped: true`
export function knownHostsFor(domain, { scan, zone, passive, discovered }) -> [{ name, source }]   // names equal to / under the domain, first source wins
export async function runRetireCheck({ blocks, domains, hosts, zoneRefs, dns, signal, concurrency = 2, onEvent }) -> { checks, errors, zone, aborted }
  // events: start, progress, domain (a check, or its error), zone; an abort keeps what finished
export function retireGaps({ domains, checks, errors, zone, aborted, counts, unresolved }) -> { failed, failures: { name, mx, ns, spf, https, domain, zone }, unknown, notChecked, missing, unresolved, stopped, settled }
  // what the check could not settle: failed lookups (a domain's, a domain that could not be checked, a zone record's live lookup), "cannot tell" rows,
  // the domains a stop left unchecked, the checked domains that do not exist (`missing`), the known host names past the caller's cap on names, never
  // resolved (`unresolved`: the view's RETIRE_MAX_HOSTS). Only a settled check may say that nothing points at the address
export function inventoryOwners(blocks, servers) -> [{ name, addresses, others }]
export function buildChanges({ blocks, checks, zone: { origin, refs }|null, passive: [{ address, names }]|null }) -> { changes: Change[], groups,
  counts: { total, breaking, passive /* rows of the passive group */, bySeverity, byVerified }, gone }
export function breakingChanges(changes) ; passiveNewNames(passive, { checked, resolved }) -> { names, domains }
export function retireExportRows(changes) ; retireExportJson({ … }) -> { schema: 'domainscope.ip-retire/1', app, version, addresses, domains, missingDomains, zone, startedAt, finishedAt, aborted, counts, owners, changes, passiveGone, failures }
```
- **One row per record** (`Change`, key owner|type|value) with the retiring addresses it reaches, its evidence merged (`sources`: dns, spf, zone — the file holds the record —, passive and where a known host came from: scan, zone-name, discovered; `roles`; `foundFor`: the checked domains that led to it): the A / AAAA record that holds the address (the end of a CNAME chain), the CNAME that leads there, the MX / NS record whose host is on it, the HTTPS hint, each SPF term that covers it, each SPF term that cannot be told, the zone's records, the unchecked passive names.
- **Severity**, worst first: `mail` (an SPF term whose effective qualifier is a pass — renumbered, mail from the new address fails; switched off, whoever gets the address next can send as the domain — an MX record on it, the A record of an MX host) > `ns` (a name server's record and its A) > `live` (an A / AAAA or HTTPS hint that answers it) > `origin` (a proxied record's origin, from the zone file) > `chain` (a CNAME) > `file` (the zone has it, public DNS does not) > `stale` (an SPF term that does not authorize it — also a pass term behind an earlier term of its policy that does not pass, which decides for the address first —, a passive hit nobody checked) > `unknown`. `breaking` counts mail to chain.
- **What to change** (`action`): remove (or put the new address in), repoint (MX, NS, SRV, an HTTPS target: a host that stays, or that host's new address first), narrow (an SPF range wider than the retired addresses; an a / mx term whose CIDR length widens its host's address over them — `a/24`, `mx/24` —, whose text names the retiring address, the host and its address, and says whether moving the host is enough), follow (an SPF a / mx term whose host's own address is on the block and whose range is not wider than it, or a CNAME: change the record it names), glue (an in-bailiwick name server: its glue at the registrar too), provider (a term in the SPF policy of a domain that is neither under a checked domain nor the zone's origin — the text says to change it there if that domain is the user's, and that a provider's needs nothing but the include; a central `_spf` policy under any checked domain is the user's to narrow or remove), origin (a proxied origin: the proxy's origin setting, else 521 / 522), keep (an SPF term that does not authorize the address and either is a carve-out in front of a later pass term of its policy — `-ip4:192.0.2.10 ip4:192.0.2.0/24`: removed, the range would authorize the address — or covers more than the retired addresses), check (cannot tell, a passive hit). A term behind an earlier one that does not pass says it is not in effect today, and to remove or narrow it all the same: left in place, it authorizes the address as soon as the earlier one goes.
- **Verification**: live (seen over DoH; a wildcard zone record: at the random name under it, which its evidence names), file (zone only: public DNS answered without it), hidden (behind the proxy), internal (never asked), unverified (a passive hit, a zone record over the cap or left by a stop — with its type's severity), unknown (failed or depends on the sender).
- **Groups**: the checked domain the owner is under (the zone's origin as its own group when it was not in the list), `other` (a record in a zone nobody checked: a CNAME target, a provider's SPF include — each row names the domain that led to it), `passive`. `gone`: passive names whose lookup settled (an answer or NXDOMAIN) and that no longer point at the address; a passive name whose lookup failed stays in the passive group as `unknown` (lookup-failed), never gone.
- Tests: `tests/js/retire.test.js` (CIDR math, SPF coverage through includes, macros and failed lookups, one domain over a fake DohClient, a failed SPF record lookup, what a check could not settle, a domain that does not exist, a/24 and mx/24 terms, the first match of a policy (a carve-out in front of a wider range, in the live policy and the zone file), the zone's candidates and their verification — internal targets, a wildcard through a random name, the cap —, the merged list, SPF policies under checked domains, an abort, owners, passive hits — a SERVFAIL one —, exports), `tests/js/retire-view.test.js`, `tests/e2e/retire.e2e.mjs` (offline).

### 5.46 `lib/passport.js` — the Domain overview, one page per domain
For a migration or a customer takeover: the registration, DNS hosting, mail, web, certificates, SaaS verifications and health of one domain, the facts otherwise gathered from five or six tools. DOM-free: lookups through an injected DohClient and `fetchImpl` with the caller's `signal` (only an abort rejects), card data as codes the view translates.
```js
export const PASSPORT_CARDS = ['registration', 'dns', 'mail', 'web', 'certs', 'saas', 'health']
export const PASSPORT_LOOKUPS = ['rdap', 'ns', 'soa', 'ds', 'dnskey', 'mx', 'txt', 'dmarc', 'apex', 'www', 'https', 'wwwHttps', 'caa', 'health']
export const CARD_LOOKUPS   // card → its lookups (health: ['health', 'rdap'], its score includes the registration checks); a card's Retry asks only its failed ones
export const HEALTH_LOOKUPS = ['ns', 'soa', 'ds', 'dnskey', 'mx', 'txt', 'dmarc', 'apex', 'https', 'caa']   // the lookups whose questions the health run asks too
export const LOOKUP_SOURCES  // lookup → 'rdap' | 'doh'
export function passportDomain(input) -> { domain, host } | null   // the registrable domain of a host, URL or *.name; host set when reduced; null for IPs, suffixes, junk
export const DNS_PROVIDERS   // NS host → provider by suffix or pattern: Cloudflare (incl. Foundation DNS), Route 53, Azure DNS, Google Cloud DNS, NS1, Akamai, UltraDNS, Dyn,
                             // Oracle, CSC, MarkMonitor, Com Laude, Safenames, Nameshield, easyDNS, Constellix (the corporate platforms spread their name servers
                             // over several TLDs on purpose), Microsoft 365, DigitalOcean, Hetzner, OVHcloud, GoDaddy, Namecheap, IONOS, STRATO, Gandi, Hostinger, Natro, Turhost, İsimtescil, Wix,
                             // Squarespace, Vercel, Linode, Vultr, Porkbun, ClouDNS, DNS Made Easy, Hurricane Electric, deSEC, Yandex, Alibaba, DNSPod, Network Solutions, WordPress.com
export function dnsProviderOf(nsHost, { domain }) -> { id, name } | { id: 'self' } | null ; export function dnsHosting(nsHosts, { domain }) -> { providers: [{ id, name, hosts }], self, other }
export const MAIL_PLATFORMS  // { id, name, kind: 'mailbox'|'gateway'|'forwarding'|'sending', mx (suffixes), mxPatterns }: Microsoft 365, Google Workspace,
                             // Zoho, Yandex 360, Yaani, Türk Telekom, Mail.ru, Proton, iCloud, Fastmail, …, Mimecast, Proofpoint, Barracuda, Cisco, …, SendGrid, Mailgun, Amazon SES, …
                             // the MX side only: the SPF side is lib/senders.js SENDER_SERVICES (§5.93), whose ids and names these share
export function mailPlatformOf(exchange) -> { id, name, kind } | null ; export function spfSenders(spf) -> { senders: [{ id, name, kind }], other: string[] }   // include: / redirect=, macro includes by suffix; nothing past `all`, and no redirect= next to one;
                             // matched by senders.serviceBySpf (about seventy services), kind = senders.passportKind(type)
export const TXT_VENDORS     // { id, name, key, re }: ~100 verification-token prefixes, anchored at the record's start (google-site-verification, MS=, facebook-, apple-, atlassian-,
                             // docusign=, stripe-, ZOOM_verify_, adobe-idp-, hubspot-, openai-, anthropic-, …); `key` is the fixed prefix, the only part ever shown
export function txtVendorOf(record) -> { id, name, key } | null ; export function saasFingerprints(records) -> { vendors: [{ id, name, key, count }], other, policy, total }   // never a token
export const REGISTRY_WHOIS = { tr: TRABİS, de: DENIC, jp: JPRS, ch: SWITCH } ; export function registryWhois(tld, domain) -> { name, url, iana } | null   // else the TLD's IANA page
export function rdapStatusFlags(statuses) -> [{ code, kind: 'lock'|'hold'|'pending'|'ok'|'other' }]   // `code` as the registry spelled it (RFC 8056 or EPP camelCase), matched case-free
export function serialDate(serial) -> 'YYYY-MM-DD' | null   // YYYYMMDDnn only
export function lookupStatus(result, { now }) -> SourceStatus | null   // §5.36: a DoH failure or error rcode, a failed RDAP lookup or host resolution, a lookup that threw
export function registrationCard / dnsCard / mailCard / webCard / certsCard / saasCard(raw, { now }) -> Card ; export function healthCard(raw, { now, max = 3, waivers }) -> Card
export function passportCards(raw, { now, waivers /* the workspace's accepted risks, §5.95: the health card's */ }) -> { [card]: Card }
Card = { id, state: 'pending'|'ready', pending: string[], failures: (SourceStatus & { lookup })[], retry: string[], …the card's own fields }
  // registration: outcome 'ok'|'unsupported' (whois)|'not-found'|'invalid'|'failed', registrar, ianaId, created, expires, daysLeft, expiry ('expired'|'error' <30 d|'warn' <60 d|'ok'),
  //   flags, transferLock (true | false | null when the registry reports no status), dnssec, nameservers
  // dns: exists, nameservers, hosting, delegation (the registry's NS set when it differs from the zone's), soa { mname, email, serial, serialDate, provider },
  //   dnssec 'validated'|'signed'|'failing' (DS, the DNSKEY lookup failed)|'unsigned'|null
  // mail: mx { state 'some'|'none'|'null', hosts, platforms, other }, spf { state 'ok'|'none'|'many'|'invalid', all, redirect, senders, other }, dmarc { state, policy, pct, reports }
  // web: exists, hosts [apex, www] { state 'ok'|'nxdomain'|'nodata'|'dangling'|'failed', cnames, ipv4, ipv6, classification (netinfo), aliasOfApex, sameAsApex }, https { apex, www }
  // certs: exists, caa { state, issue, issuewild, wildcardOnly (an issuewild property exists), foundAt, iodef, criticalTags }, ct (after lookupCtIssuers) { state, issuers with health.checkCaaAllows' verdict, notAllowed }
  //   caa.state as checkCaaAllows reads the set (RFC 8659 §4): 'none' (no CAA) | 'critical' (an unknown tag marked critical: no CA may issue) | 'unrestricted' (no issue
  //   property — iodef / issuewild / other tags only: any CA for the name, issuewild still rules wildcards) | 'deny-all' (no issue or issuewild value authorises anybody) |
  //   'present' (issue names CAs; `issue` empty when only issuewild does: wildcard certificates only)
  // saas: the saasFingerprints of the apex TXT; health: the report with applyRdap, score, grade, light, summary, the worst three problems (+ moreProblems); pending until RDAP landed too;
  //   the accepted risks (`waivers`, lib/waivers.js healthWaivers) left out of score, grade, light, summary and problems as Domain Health leaves them out — `report` stays as checked —,
  //   waived { count, until, error, warn, score, grade /* with them */, checks: [{ id, severity, titleKey, params, reason, owner, expires }] } | null, expired (how many count again)
export function cardsOfLookup(lookup) -> string[]   // the cards to redraw when it lands: its own, the DNS card for RDAP, every card that says NXDOMAIN for NS / SOA
export function passportDns(dns, { signal, noCache }) -> client   // one question once per build; the Domain Health run shares it; resolveHost / detectWildcard go to the DohClient's own
export async function runLookup(id, domain, { dns, fetchImpl, signal, now }) -> result   // a thrown lookup comes back as { failed: true, error, errorKind }
export async function buildPassport(domain, { dns, fetchImpl, signal, now, lookups = PASSPORT_LOOKUPS, noCache, onLookup }) -> raw   // all at once, onLookup(id, result) as each lands
export function certspotterIssuersUrl(domain) ; export function crtshIssuersUrl(domain)
export function issuersFromCertspotter(rows, { now }) / issuersFromCrtsh(rows, { now }) -> { issuers: [{ name, dn, intermediates, caaDomains, count, newest }], certificates }
export function issuerName(dn, friendly) -> string   // the known CA (health.CAA_ISSUERS), else the DN's O, else its CN — the name an issuer is grouped under
export function dnPart(dn, key) -> string|null        // one attribute of a DN string (`,` or `/` separated); both also used by the headless runner's `ct` (§9)
export async function lookupCtIssuers(domain, { fetchImpl, signal, now, cooldown = ctcert.ctCooldown }) -> { status: 'ok'|'failed', provider, issuers, certificates, requests, failures }
export function passportSummaryFacts(cards, { domain, at, host }) -> facts   // §5.32 domainSummary: per card { pending, failed, exists, … } and the failed lookup by name; health.waived { count, until } | null
                                                                             // (dns.nsFailed, mail.mxFailed / spfFailed / dmarcFailed, web.httpsFailed: host names, certs.caaFailed / ctFailed);
                                                                             // certs: caa (the state), cas (issue), wildcard (issuewild exists) with wildCas, criticalTags
```
- **The health run:** `domainHealth(domain, { rdap: false })` on the build's `passportDns` client, so it asks no question twice; the card applies the build's RDAP result (`health.applyRdap`) and so shows exactly Domain Health's score — with the workspace's accepted risks left out as Domain Health leaves them out (§5.95: the view reads the `waivers` part when it draws the card and draws it again when the part changes; the card says "N accepted risks (until …). With it/them, the score would be …", or how many expired; Copy summary says "N accepted risks excluded", the customer report too, §5.88). After a Retry of one of `HEALTH_LOOKUPS` the view runs it again: the retried answers are in the resolver cache (`noCache` stores them), and so is the rest. A Retry pressed while the build still runs (a SERVFAIL lands in milliseconds, RDAP takes seconds) runs on its own controller; if the build's health run has not landed yet it read the failed answer too, so it runs again once it lands.
- **CT:** one Cert Spotter request (the single-host allowance: `expand=issuer&expand=issuer.caa_domains`, its first page of current issuances); crt.sh's identity search only when Cert Spotter fails or is cooling down after a 429 (`ctcert.noteCertspotterLimit`, the page session's cool-down). The view asks only on a click.
- **Tables:** checked against live answers on 2026-09-28 (NS of the hosting companies, MX of the mail providers, every SPF include publishing SPF, TXT tokens of large domains); the TXT prefixes were cross-checked with nuclei-templates `dns/txt-service-detect.yaml` (MIT). Tests: `tests/js/passport.test.js` (fake DoH + fake fetch), `tests/e2e/domain.e2e.mjs` (offline).

### 5.47 `lib/pkcs12.js`, `lib/ciphers.js`, `lib/sha.js` — PKCS#12 (.pfx / .p12) in the browser
IIS, Java keystores and many CAs hand certificates over as a password-protected PKCS#12 bundle (RFC 7292). `openPkcs12` reads one locally — pure, DOM-free, WebCrypto from `globalThis.crypto.subtle` unless passed — for `x509.loadCertificates` (§5.2); the views never call it directly.
```js
export const PKCS12_ERRORS = ['NOT_PKCS12', 'BAD_PASSWORD', 'DAMAGED', 'UNSUPPORTED']
export class Pkcs12Error extends Error { code; detail; encryption }   // detail: 'mac'|'no-mac' for BAD_PASSWORD, what for UNSUPPORTED ('pbeWithSHAAnd128BitRC4', 'envelopedData', 'signedData', 'SHA-224', 'iterations', an OID; 'webcrypto': no WebCrypto at all; 'webcrypto-refused: <operation>': WebCrypto refused HMAC-SHA-256, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256, a SHA-384 digest, …); encryption: the EncryptionInfo an 'iterations' count belongs to
export async function openPkcs12(bytes, password /* string, '' for none */, { checkKey = false, subtle } = {}) -> {
  certificates: Array<{ der: Uint8Array /* a copy */, friendlyName, localKeyId /* hex */ }>,   // certBag x509Certificate, file order
  keys: Array<{ encrypted, encryption: EncryptionInfo|null, unsupported: string|null /* why it cannot be decrypted here: a name / OID (encryption null) or 'iterations' */, friendlyName, localKeyId,
    check: null | { status: 'checked'|'unsupported'|'unsupported-encryption'|'failed', algorithm, certificates: number[] /* indexes it belongs to */ } }>,   // never the key
  mac: { kind: 'hmac'|'pbmac1', hash, iterations, kdf } | null, encryption: EncryptionInfo[], passwordVerified: boolean,
  passwordEncoding: 'bmp'|'none'|'utf8-bytes'|null, ignored: { crl, secret, other }
}   // throws Pkcs12Error only (a TypeError for a non-bytes input or a non-string password); never writes to the input
EncryptionInfo = { scheme: 'PBES2'|'PKCS#12', cipher: 'AES-256-CBC'|'3DES-CBC'|'2-key 3DES-CBC'|'RC2-128-CBC'|'RC2-40-CBC'|'DES-CBC'|…, kdf: 'PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256'|'PKCS#12 KDF (SHA-1)'|…, iterations, strength: 'ok'|'legacy'|'weak' }
export async function pkcs12Kdf({ hash = 'SHA-1', password /* BMPString */, salt, id /* 1 key, 2 IV, 3 MAC */, iterations, length, subtle }) -> Uint8Array   // RFC 7292 B.2
export function bmpPassword(password) -> Uint8Array          // UTF-16BE code units (surrogate pairs outside the BMP) + 00 00
export function passwordForms(password) -> Array<{ bmp, utf8, encoding }>   // the readings tried, in order
```
- **Structure:** PFX → AuthenticatedSafe → SafeContents → SafeBags with a BER reader (indefinite lengths, constructed OCTET STRINGs as Windows writes them; depth, bag count and lengths bounded). certBag certificates are returned; keyBag / pkcs8ShroudedKeyBag are counted and described; safeContentsBag nests; CRL, secret and other bags are counted. Public-key integrity (signedData) and privacy (envelopedData) modes are UNSUPPORTED. A file that starts like a PFX (SEQUENCE, INTEGER 3, SEQUENCE) and does not parse is DAMAGED (cut short), anything else NOT_PKCS12.
- **Integrity:** the RFC 7292 HMAC (key from the PKCS#12 KDF, id 3, over SHA-1 / 256 / 384 / 512 — SHA-224 and the SHA-512/t variants are UNSUPPORTED) or PBMAC1 (RFC 9579: PBKDF2 with the UTF-8 password, then HMAC). No reading of the password matching the MAC → BAD_PASSWORD 'mac'. With the MAC right, contents that do not decrypt or parse → DAMAGED. Without a MAC every reading is tried; the one that decrypts to SafeContents that parse wins, none → BAD_PASSWORD 'no-mac' (a damaged file looks the same). A bundle with neither MAC nor encrypted certificates opens with any password (`passwordVerified: false`).
- **Encryption:** PBES2 with PBKDF2 (HMAC-SHA-1 default, 256, 384, 512; the key length must fit the cipher, and any PBKDF2 key length, PBMAC1's and RC2's too, is 1 to 128 bytes or DAMAGED) and AES-128 / 192 / 256-CBC through WebCrypto — lib/ciphers.js when WebCrypto refuses the key (Chromium has no AES-192) — or DES / 3DES / RC2-CBC (RC2 version → effective bits: 160 → 40, 120 → 64, 58 → 128); the PKCS#12 PBE (RFC 7292 C: key id 1, IV id 2, SHA-1): pbeWithSHAAnd3-KeyTripleDES-CBC, 2-KeyTripleDES, 128BitRC2, 40BitRC2. RC4 and PBES1 are UNSUPPORTED by name, before any password is used. `strength`: weak = a 40- or 56-bit key (RC2-40, DES), legacy = 3DES, RC2-128, the SHA-1 PKCS#12 KDF.
- **Passwords:** the PKCS#12 KDF takes the BMPString, PBKDF2 the UTF-8 bytes (as OpenSSL). The empty password is also tried as no bytes (writers that leave the terminator out), a non-ASCII one also as OpenSSL 1.0.x encoded it (each UTF-8 byte one character), like `openssl pkcs12` retries. Iteration counts above 10,000,000 (PBKDF2, native; it runs the count once per hash-sized block of the key, so the cap counts iterations × blocks), 1,000,000 (the KDF in JS, which yields to the event loop every 20,000 rounds) or 200,000 (a SHA-384 / SHA-512 MAC key: one WebCrypto digest a round) are UNSUPPORTED 'iterations' — refused at once, never a hung tab.
- **Keys:** nothing decrypts a key without `checkKey`. With it, each key is decrypted (shrouded) or read (plain keyBag), imported with `importKey('pkcs8', …, extractable false)` (RSA as RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5, EC P-256 / P-384 / P-521 as ECDSA), signs a fixed challenge, and every certificate whose SPKI has the same algorithm (and curve) verifies it; a key type WebCrypto cannot import (RSA-PSS, DSA, Ed25519, …, or the browser refuses it) is 'unsupported', never a mismatch. A shrouded key under an encryption this page cannot undo (RC4, PBES1, too many iterations) keeps its `unsupported` reason and is 'unsupported-encryption'; the certificates still open. The password bytes, the KDF's working buffers (and lib/sha.js's padded copy and message schedule), derived keys, key schedules and decrypted buffers are zeroed once used — best effort: the password string itself cannot be cleared and the engine may keep copies (WebCrypto's buffers, uncollected garbage); no message carries the password.
- `lib/ciphers.js`: `desEde3CbcDecrypt(key /* 24 = 3DES, 16 = two-key, 8 = DES */, iv, data, { padding = true })`, `rc2CbcDecrypt(key, effectiveBits, iv, data, …)`, `aesCbcDecrypt(key /* 16, 24, 32 */, iv, data, …)` → Uint8Array; `CipherError { code: 'length'|'padding'|'key' }` for partial blocks, bad PKCS#5 / #7 padding (the output is zeroed) or impossible keys; inputs are never written to, key schedules are zeroed after each call. Table-driven (DES: the S-boxes and P merged into one lookup per box on 32-bit halves, IP / FP by byte tables; AES: InvMixColumns by product tables): about 150 ms for 5 MB of 3DES, RC2 or AES. `cbcDecryptInSlices(decrypt, blockSize, iv, data, { padding = true, sliceBytes = SLICE_BYTES /* 256 KB */ })` → Promise: the same result a slice at a time, yielding (setTimeout) between slices — lib/pkcs12.js decrypts every JS cipher this way, so a large legacy bundle never freezes the page. Tests: FIPS 46-3, SP 800-17, SP 800-67, RFC 2268, FIPS 197 and SP 800-38A known answers plus node:crypto as an oracle, 64 KB of 3DES under 500 ms, slice boundaries, errors and the yield (`tests/js/ciphers.test.js`).
- `lib/sha.js`: `sha1(bytes)`, `sha256(bytes)` → Uint8Array, synchronous — x509's fingerprints without WebCrypto (plain http) and the PKCS#12 KDF, which hashes its own output thousands of times (SHA-384 / 512 go through WebCrypto there).
- Tests (`tests/js/pkcs12.test.js`): the KDF against OpenSSL's published vectors and `openssl kdf` cases, every fixture against `p12_expected.json`, wrong passwords (MAC / no MAC), the old-OpenSSL and empty-password readings, BER as Windows writes it, a refused AES-192, missing WebCrypto and a refused WebCrypto operation, crafted damaged / unsupported bundles (MAC computed in the test), a key under RC4 or too many iterations, a 700 KB 3DES bundle that never holds the event loop for long, random corruption (only Pkcs12Error escapes), the input left untouched and no key bytes in the result; `loadCertificates` warnings, key-check verdicts and the leaf paired by localKeyId.

### 5.48 `lib/estate.js` — the certificate estate of the CLI's reports
DOM-free (imports `domain.js` certCovers, `netinfo.js` normalizeIP, `export.js` toCsv). Nothing is sent: the Certificate estate view reads the report files in the browser and keeps them in the tab.
```js
export function readEstateReport(text, { name }) -> { ok: true, report: EstateReport } | { ok: false, error: REPORT_ERRORS, detail? }   // never throws: 'too-large' (> ESTATE_MAX_BYTES = 64 MiB),
                                              // 'not-json', 'not-report' (no "tool": "ssl_origin_scan"), 'version' (another major; detail: it), 'no-results'
EstateReport = { name, doc, startedAt: Date|null, finishedAt: Date|null, estate /* options.estate */, keyHashes /* every certificates{} entry has spkiSha256 */, id /* the same scan read twice */ }
export function mergeReports(reports) -> { doc, origin: Map<'ip|port', index>, sources: Map<'ip|port|sha256', index[]>, overlaps: string[] }
  // one report: as it is; several: names asked = the union, certificates{} = the union (a certificate's entry from the newest report holding it, the fields it
  // lacks — an older CLI's missing spkiSha256 or kind — from the others, so the flags do not depend on the order); on an ip:port several reports scanned, each probe (no SNI, or one name)
  // takes the newest report's answer (finishedAt; a tie → the later one), so a name only an older report asked keeps its answer, and a port the newest report found
  // closed or silent drops the older answers there; `origin` = the newest report of each endpoint, `sources` = the reports behind a certificate on an endpoint
export function estateOf(doc, { now /* default: doc.finishedAt */ }) -> Estate   // the CLI's estate_from_report, field for field (tests/fixtures/estate)
export function expiryBucket(daysLeft) / weakReasons(keyAlgorithm, keyBits, signatureAlgorithm) / keyLabel(keyAlgorithm, keyBits, curve)   // the CLI's rules
export function estateMatches(cert, filter /* ESTATE_FILTERS */) / estateFilterCounts(estate)   // attention: any flag, expired / < 30 days, revoked (--revocation) or
                                              // its ARI window open or past (--ari); private: self-signed or private-ca
export function estateCsvRows(estate, { certificates, reportName }) / estateCsv(estate, opts)   // the CLI's --estate --csv rows (ESTATE_CSV_COLUMNS, then estateStatusColumns
                                              // and estateTrustColumns), plus `report` with several reports
export function estateTrustColumns(estate) -> [{ key, header }]   // ESTATE_TRUST_COLUMNS (cert_trusted, trust_detail) when an endpoint has a verdict
                                              // (the CLI's estate_trust_columns and TRUST_CSV_COLUMNS)
export function trustDetailCode(detail) -> number|null   // the verify code of a CLI trust detail ("… (code 20)") when it is one of
                                              // ESTATE_TRUST_CODES = [20, 21, 18, 19, 10, 9, 62] (the CLI's TRUST_DETAILS): the view words it in the page's language
export function estateStatusColumns(estate) -> [{ key, header }]   // ESTATE_ARI_COLUMNS when a certificate has an `ari` record, ESTATE_REVOCATION_COLUMNS when one has a
                                              // `revocation` record (the CLI's estate_status_columns; the same names as its ARI_CSV_COLUMNS / REVOCATION_CSV_COLUMNS)
export function estateAriWindow(ari, nowMs) -> { state: 'before'|'open'|'past', days /* until it opens, rounded up */ } | null   // the CLI's window_state
export function estateStatusCounts(estate) -> { ari: { open, past, before, error } | null, revocation: { revoked, unknown, good } | null }   // a part per record kind present
export const ESTATE_ARI_COLUMNS = ['ari_start', 'ari_end', 'ari_explanation', 'ari_error'], ESTATE_REVOCATION_COLUMNS = ['revocation', 'revoked_at', 'revocation_reason',
  'revocation_error'] /* as { key, header } */, ESTATE_ARI_STATES = ['open', 'past', 'before', 'error'], ESTATE_REVOCATION_STATES = ['revoked', 'unknown', 'good']
export const ESTATE_BUCKETS = ['expired', '7d', '30d', '90d', 'later'], ESTATE_KINDS = ['origin-ca', 'self-signed', 'private-ca', 'other'],
  ESTATE_WEAK_REASONS = ['rsa-short', 'sha1', 'md5'], ESTATE_FLAGS = ['name-conflict', 'stale', 'shared-key', 'weak', 'covers-none', 'untrusted'], WEAK_RSA_BITS = 2048,
  SHARED_KEY_MIN_HOSTS = 2, SHARED_KEY_WIDE_HOSTS = 5, ESTATE_FILTERS, REPORT_ERRORS, ESTATE_MAX_REPORTS = 20, ESTATE_CSV_COLUMNS
export function sharedKeyNeedsLook(group) -> boolean   // the CLI's shared_key_needs_look: 2+ certificates, or hosts >= SHARED_KEY_WIDE_HOSTS
Estate = { namesAsked, counts: { certificates, endpoints, openEndpoints, endpointsWithCertificate, expiry: {bucket: n}, kinds: {kind: n} },
  certificates: [{ sha256, subjectCN, subjectDN, issuer, issuerDN, serialHex, notBefore, notAfter, daysLeft, expiry, hostnames, keyAlgorithm, keyBits, curve, key,
    signatureAlgorithm, spkiSha256|null, kind, privateCa, isCA, weak, coversAsked, ari?, ariWindow?, revocation?, flags, endpoints: [{ servers, ip, port, defaultCert, names,
    trusted?, trustDetail? }] }],   // trusted / trustDetail: a report whose scan checked trust (its rows carry certTrusted), §7
    // soonest expiry first; ari / revocation: the report's records (--ari / --revocation, §7) when it has them, ariWindow: estateAriWindow of `ari` at `now`
  nameConflicts: [{ name, certificates: [{ sha256, stale, endpoints: [{ servers, ip, port }] }] }],   // newest first
  sharedKeys: [{ spkiSha256, key, hosts, servers, addresses, certificates }], weakKeys: [{ sha256, reasons }], coversNone: sha256[] | null }
```
- Every handshake that returned a certificate counts (with SNI or without, covering the asked name or not: a fallback certificate is served too). `names` of an endpoint: the names asked that got this certificate there.
- A **name conflict**: a name asked that two or more endpoints serve with different certificates, each covering it (the SNI rows; coverage by `certCovers` on the report's `hostnames`). `stale`: another certificate of the conflict with the same key algorithm and kind family (public / Origin CA / private) was issued later (notBefore, then notAfter): the endpoints serving it were left behind; an RSA + ECDSA pair or an Origin CA certificate next to a public one has no stale side.
- A **shared key**: one SPKI SHA-256 served by `SHARED_KEY_MIN_HOSTS` or more hosts or carried by two or more certificates; sorted by hosts, then certificates. `hosts` counts distinct addresses (several inventory names of one address, or its ports, are one host); `servers` lists the inventory names (case-folded; the address when a row has none), `addresses` the addresses. Every shared key is listed, but only one that `sharedKeyNeedsLook` (in two or more certificates — a renewal that kept the key, one key for several sites — or on `SHARED_KEY_WIDE_HOSTS` or more addresses) flags its certificates `shared-key`: one certificate on the members of a load-balancer pool is the usual case. A report of an older CLI has no `spkiSha256`: no key is shared there (the view says key reuse was not checked).
- **Weak**: RSA under 2048 bits, a SHA-1 signature, an MD5 / MD2 one. **Covering none of the names asked**: `null` when no name was asked (coverage cannot be told).
- Kind: the report's `certificates{}.kind` (`--private-ca` applied by the CLI); a report without it: `self-signed` from `selfSigned`, else `other`. Days left count from `now`.
- **--ari / --revocation** (the renewal radar, §5.94): a `certificates{}` entry's `ari` / `revocation` objects ride along as they are (anything else is left out, as the CLI's `_estate_entry` does); nothing is added to a certificate without them, and a report without them gives the CSV of before.
- **Trust** (the CLI's trust check, §7): an endpoint of a certificate gets `trusted` and `trustDetail` once one of its rows carries `certTrusted` (the CLI's `_estate_trust`, `endpointTrust` here): false with the first untrusted name's detail when a name's chain there is not trusted, true when one is, null when none was asked (served without SNI only, a failed handshake); merged reports keep each row's verdict. A certificate with an untrusted endpoint is flagged `untrusted` (a filter of its own, part of "attention"); the CSV gains `cert_trusted` (yes / no / empty) and `trust_detail` after the ARI and revocation columns. A report of an older CLI, or a scan without the check, adds nothing. The view flags the certificate (`estate.flag.untrusted`) and says why per endpoint in its details, the verify code in the page's language (`trustDetailCode`, `estate.trust.code<N>`; another detail as the CLI wrote it).
- Tests: `tests/js/estate.test.js` (the fixture reports' own estate sections — report-a.json's scan checked trust with a fake verifier, report-b.json's did not —, a week later, an older report, no names, merging both orders, a closed port, junk, filters, CSV and formula-safe cells; the ARI and revocation records, their window, filter, counts and columns, the column names against the CLI's source; the trust verdicts, the `untrusted` flag and filter, its CSV cells, none without the check, a merge of both, the verify codes against the CLI's TRUST_DETAILS), `tests/js/estate-view.test.js`.

### 5.49 `lib/chainfix.js` — the missing intermediate, and what the root faces in the root stores
The most common installation error is a server certificate installed without its intermediate: browsers often hide it, Android, curl, Java and API clients fail. The page cannot fetch the certificate's AIA caIssuers URL (plain http, no CORS; §3), so the site ships the CCADB list of public TLS intermediates (`assets/data/intermediates/`, built by `tools/build-intermediates.mjs`, rebuilt weekly by `.github/workflows/intermediates.yml`) and completes the chain from it. DOM-free; the network is `fetchImpl` (tests read the files from disk).
```js
export const DATASET_URL            // new URL('../../data/intermediates/manifest.json', import.meta.url): moves under v/<commit>/ with assets/
export const DATASET_FORMAT = 1
export const STORES = ['chrome', 'mozilla', 'apple', 'microsoft']        // display order
export const STORE_STATUSES = ['tls', 'other', 'not-before', 'removed', 'absent']   // a root's status in one store (roots.json)
export const LIFECYCLE_CODES = ['distrusted', 'renewal-distrusted', 'removed', 'not-for-tls', 'cut-off', 'not-included', 'root-expired', 'root-expires']
export const MAX_ADDED = 4                  // intermediates added to one chain at most
```
