```js
export function dnHash(dn) -> string        // the first 16 hex digits of SHA-256 over the DN as lib/x509.js writes it (the dn/ index key)
export function shardOf(key, digits) -> string|null   // a hex key's shard file name; null for anything but hex
export function datasetDate(value) -> Date|null       // 'YYYY-MM-DD' = the end of that day (UTC): "issued after 2024-11-11" is after 23:59:59.999
export function rootTable(json) -> { generated, roots: RootInfo[], bySki: Map, byDn: Map }
RootInfo = { sha256, name, owner, ski, dn, notAfter: Date|null, stores: { chrome|mozilla|apple|microsoft: STORE_STATUSES }, events: LifecycleEvent[] }
LifecycleEvent = { type: 'distrust-after'|'expiry', store: string|null, date: Date, basis: 'sct'|'notBefore'|null, url: string|null /* https only */, source: 'announcement'|'ccadb'|null /* what url is */ }
export function rootsIssuing(table, cert) -> RootInfo[]   // by the authority key id (the DN must agree where known) or, for a root without a key id (ski null: TWCA Global Root CA), by the issuer DN; by the issuer DN alone without an authority key id
export function rootsWithKey(table, cert) -> RootInfo[]   // the roots `cert` is a copy of (same key id and DN; the DN alone for a root or a certificate without a key id): a cross-signed root
export function rootEntryFor(table, rootCert) -> RootInfo|null   // a self-signed certificate of the file: by fingerprint, else key id + DN
export function issuedAt(cert, basis) -> Date               // 'sct': the earliest embedded SCT (Chrome's cut-offs), else notBefore
export function chainStanding(anchors, leaf, now) -> { stores: { [store]: { status, root } }, trusted: string[], warnings: LifecycleWarning[] } | null
export function rootStanding(root, leaf, now)               // chainStanding([root], …)
LifecycleWarning = { code: LIFECYCLE_CODES, severity: 'error'|'warn', stores: string[], root: RootInfo, date: Date|null, issued: Date|null, url: string|null, source: 'announcement'|'ccadb'|null }
export function createIntermediateStore({ url = DATASET_URL, fetchImpl, timeoutMs = 15000 }) -> { manifest(), roots(), bySki(ski), byDn(dn) }
  // each file fetched once (a failed fetch is forgotten: the next call tries again); bySki/byDn → [{ cert /* parsed */, owner /* CCADB CA owner */ }], a damaged entry skipped
export function fileChain(certs, leaf) -> { chain: Certificate[] /* leaf first, no root */, rootCert: Certificate|null }
export async function repairChain({ certificates, leaf }, { store, now, signal }) -> ChainRepair   // rejects when the dataset cannot be read
ChainRepair = {
  status: 'complete'|'repaired'|'not-found'|'self-signed'|'no-leaf', reason: 'missing'|'untrusted-root'|null,
  leaf, chain, rootCert, added: [{ cert, owner }], fullchain /* chain + added, never the root */, root: RootInfo|null, ownRoot /* where the file's own chain ends */,
  anchors: RootInfo[] /* the roots the chain can end at, nearest first */, standing, missing: { issuerDN, authorityKeyId }|null,
  alternatives /* ways to a root the dataset offered */, generated /* the dataset's date */
}
```
- **Dataset** (`assets/data/intermediates/`, format 1): `manifest.json` (date — kept when a rebuild changes nothing —, a digest of the data files and of the manifest without its date and digest, sources, licence, shard layout, counts, the lifecycle window; the skipped counts go to the build log only, so a change to them alone rewrites nothing), `ski/<xx>.json` × 256 (subject key id → `[{ owner, der /* base64 */ }]`, by its first two hex digits; ≈ 16 KB each), `dn/<x>.json` × 16 (dnHash → subject key ids), `roots.json` (`roots` and the lifecycle table `events`). Candidates: Mozilla's intermediate report, plus the certificate records' intermediates that are TLS capable, `Trusted` in at least one store, `Not Revoked`, unexpired and not in Mozilla's report (`extraIntermediateRecords`), their PEM from the PEM report of each notBefore year they need (`pemYears`), the fingerprint checked, de-duplicated by fingerprint, the owner from the record. Kept: CA certificates with a subject key id, valid on the build date, whose EKU allows TLS server authentication (none, serverAuth, anyExtendedKeyUsage) — ≈ 2,270 (≈ 275 of them from the records). Roots: every root CCADB marks TLS capable, the ones Mozilla includes for websites, the issuers of the listed intermediates and the roots of the lifecycle input; their status per store from CCADB (Mozilla: 'tls' only with the Websites trust bit; Apple / Microsoft: 'tls' when CCADB marks the root TLS capable; Microsoft NotBefore = 'not-before'; Removed / Blocked / Disabled = 'removed'); names shared by several roots get the DN's first OU (`GlobalSign (GlobalSign Root CA - R3)`). Lifecycle table: `tools/root-lifecycle.json` (hand-kept, each entry with its announcement: Chrome's Entrust / AffirmTrust cut-off, SCTs after 2024-11-11; Chrome's Chunghwa Telecom / Netlock, after 2025-07-31; Apple's Entrust, after 2024-11-15; Mozilla's Entrust announcement), Mozilla's `Distrust for TLS After Date` from CCADB (which wins over a hand-kept Mozilla date), and an `expiry` event for every root a store trusts that expires from January 1 of last year to December 31 of next year. A Mozilla date from CCADB carries `source: 'ccadb'` and the report's URL (the page labels that link "Source", a hand-kept announcement "Announcement"). The builder refuses implausible data (fewer than 500 intermediates or 100 roots) or a missing canary — a well-known current issuer (`CANARIES`: YE1, YR1, R12, Microsoft TLS G2 RSA CA OCSP 02, WR1, Amazon RSA 2048 M02, Sectigo DV R36, each until its own expiry) — and writes nothing.
- **Repair:** the file's chain from the leaf (x509 `issuedBy`); a self-signed issuer in the file is the root it holds (`complete`, never in fullchain). Otherwise the roots the file's last certificate names: `complete` when a store trusts this certificate through them (a cross-signed root inside the file counts as an anchor, so leaf + WE2 + the GlobalSign-signed GTS Root R4 is trusted through GTS Root R4); else the issuers are looked up — by the authority key id, or by the issuer DN when the certificate names none (a DN match under another key id would not be its issuer; only a root without a key id of its own, whose certificate has no subject key id extension, is matched by the DN under an authority key id) — valid now, never twice, up to MAX_ADDED, a root trusted by fewer than every store also looked past (its cross-signed copy may reach one more). Paths are ranked by the number of stores that trust the certificate through them, then reaching a known root, fewer warnings, fewer added certificates, the later expiry: so a cross-signed copy under a removed root loses to the one under the current root, and a file that ends at a root no store trusts is completed through a cross-signed copy of it (`reason: 'untrusted-root'`). Nothing found: `not-found` with the issuer looked for. Only the manifest, the roots table and the shards the key ids name are read.
- **Standing:** per store, the first anchor it trusts for this certificate ('distrusted' when a distrust-after event of that store is past the certificate's issue time, 'expired' when the root is); a store that trusts none is judged by the first anchor it knows. Warnings: distrusted (error; with the announcement), renewal-distrusted (warn: issued before the cut-off, the renewal is affected), removed / not-for-tls (error), cut-off (warn, Microsoft's NotBefore), not-included (warn, only while another store trusts the chain), root-expired (error), root-expires (warn: the table's expiry of a root a store trusts the chain through falls before the certificate's own).
- **UI** (`ui/chain-repair.js`, §6): one job per loaded file (a WeakMap on its parse result; a failed one starts again on the next call), `ChainRepairNotes(load, { lifecycle, onDownload })` and `ChainRepairChainPart(load)`, `onChainRepairEnd(load, fn)` (once, when a running job ends); pure helpers `repairApplies`, `repairText` (a Certificate Transparency load is titled "Intermediate found in the CCADB list", never "missing"), `notFoundText` (an expired certificate: its issuer may have expired or been withdrawn with it), `lifecycleText` (the store names as one or several stores), `lifecycleLinkLabel`, `storeList`, `trustText`, `repairedFullchain`.
- Tests: `tests/js/chainfix.test.js` (the fixture PKI over the test dataset: a leaf alone, a complete chain, the root in the file, the cross-signed alternatives, two levels, no authority key id, a root without a key id, not in the list, the lifecycle, an expired intermediate, scoring by stores, MAX_ADDED and a loop, a failed download retried, an unknown format, abort, a damaged entry), `tests/js/build-intermediates.test.js` (CSV, statuses, filtering, the records-only intermediates and their PEM, canaries, the lifecycle table, determinism and the manifest digest; every shard, index and root of both checked-in datasets; the site's dataset repairs a Let's Encrypt YE leaf through the Root YE cross-sign up to ISRG Root X2, and a TWCA Global EVSSL leaf up to TWCA Global Root CA, which has no key id, with or without the root's cross-signature), `tests/js/chain-repair.test.js` (the job and the sentences, EN + TR), `tests/e2e/chainfix.e2e.mjs` (offline).

### 5.50 `lib/fixes.js` — DNS change requests and fix-as-code
DOM-free, no I/O of its own (`readCurrent` / `countSpfLookups` take a DohClient). Loaded by the DNS change request view and, on the first "Show the fix", by Domain Health and Zone File (through `ui/fix-panel.js`: it brings the zone parser and linter).
```js
export const FIX_TYPES = ['A', 'AAAA', 'CNAME', 'TXT', 'MX', 'CAA'], FIX_MODES = ['is', 'has', 'none'], FIX_ACTIONS = ['add', 'replace', 'delete', 'ttl', 'rewrite', 'unchanged'],
  FIX_FORMATS = ['bind', 'route53', 'cloudflare', 'octodns', 'terraform-cloudflare', 'terraform-route53'], FIX_FORMAT_EXT, FIX_LANGS = ['en', 'tr'],
  FIX_LIMITS = { rrsets: 20, values: 40, valueBytes: 4000, ttlMin: 1, ttlMax: 2^31-1 }, DEFAULT_TTL = 3600, CLOUDFLARE_VARS = { token: 'CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN', zone: 'CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID' },
  TERRAFORM_VARS, CAA_FORM_METHODS, TXT_FAMILIES /* spf1, dmarc1, tlsrptv1, stsv1, dkim1, bimi1 */, FIX_CAS /* health CAA_ISSUERS minus distrusted, + ZeroSSL → sectigo.com */,
  FIX_FIELDS, CHANGE_TEMPLATES, TEMPLATE_IDS, CHANGE_LINT_CODES, HEALTH_FIX_IDS, LINT_FIX_CODES, ACME_TOKEN_RE, FIX_I18N /* fix.* EN + TR */
RRsetChange = { name, type, ttl, mode: 'is'|'has'|'none', family: string|null, values: Data[], before: Data[]|null, others: Data[]|null, beforeTtl, maxTtl, rewrite }
  // values in dnswire RR.data shape; `family` scopes a TXT set to one kind of record (the v=spf1 record, the v=DMARC1 record …): the other TXT
  // values at the name (`others`) stay; before / others null = not read. beforeTtl comes from a zone file only (a resolver's TTL counts down).
ChangeRequest = { v: 1, template, zone, rrsets, notes: FixText[], problems: FixProblem[], reads: { name, type }[] }
export function rrset(r), rrsetPlan(r) -> { add, remove /* null: not known */, keep, after, full /* the whole set afterwards, null when not known */, ttlOnly, rewrite, unchanged, complete },
  rrsetAction(r, plan) -> FIX_ACTIONS, changeRequest(spec), hasErrors(req), readPlan(req), readCurrent(queries, { dns, signal }) -> { 'name|TYPE': { status, values, ttl, cname } },
  currentEntry(res, name, type), applyCurrent(req, current), afterZoneText(req, current), validateChange(req, { current, spf }) -> FixProblem[] /* errors first */,
  countSpfLookups(req, { dns, signal }), renderFix(req, format) -> string, formatNotes(req, format) -> FixText[], changeInstructions(req, { lang, checkUrl }) -> string,
  editSpf(record, { add, remove, all }), mergeSpf(records), editDmarc(record, set), buildChange(templateId, input, { current }) -> ChangeRequest, templateInput(id, input),
  changeTemplate(id), unreadEdits(req) -> RRsetChange[], healthFix(check, report) -> Fix|null, currentFromReport(report), caaFixFromIssuers(fix, issuers), lintFix(finding, zone) -> Fix|null,
  absoluteName(input, zone), relativeName(name, zone), zoneName(input), txtChunks(text), txtText(data), normalizeValue(type, data), valueKey(type, data),
  valueText(type, data), parseValueText(type, text, zone), txtFamily(data), familyOf(type, values), mailtoUri(input), m365MxHost(domain), textIn(lang, key, params)
Fix = { id, kind: 'records'|'advice', request: ChangeRequest|null, template, input /* the builder form that makes the same change */, advice: FixText[], needsCt }
```
- **Templates** (`CHANGE_TEMPLATES`, form fields in `FIX_FIELDS`): `acme-txt` (the `_acme-challenge` TXT values, mode `has`; a value that is not 43 base64url characters is a warning; a `_acme-challenge` CNAME found by a read is an error: the TXT belongs at its target), `acme-cname` (the delegation; both take the record name an ACME client prints, `_acme-challenge.example.com`, for the certificate name it validates — the label is never doubled — with an info `fix.p.acme-name`), `m365` (MX `0 <domain-with-dashes>.mail.protection.outlook.com` unless given, the SPF include, Autodiscover, the selector1 / selector2 DKIM CNAMEs of a tenant, a p=none DMARC record when none is there — not read: `fix.n.dmarc-first-unread`, a record there stays), `google` (MX `1 smtp.google.com`, the SPF include, the DKIM TXT when pasted, the first DMARC record), `caa` (one issue value per CA, `accounturi` with exactly one CA, `validationmethods`, issuewild as issue / none / unset, iodef), `spf` (an include added before `all` / `redirect=` or removed, the `all` qualifier; a removal needs a read — without one it is an error, `fix.p.spf-remove-read`, and writes nothing —, an addition without one says what it cannot know, `fix.n.spf-unread`, and `fix.n.spf-new` only when a read found no SPF record), `dmarc` (the policy step-up keeping the other tags, `v` first and `p` second; pct empty keeps the record's own, 100 removes it; not read: `fix.n.dmarc-unread` names the tags the value leaves out and `fix.n.dmarc-to` names no policy it comes from), `ttl` (the listed sets with their read values and a lower TTL; `maxTtl` makes the check wait for resolvers' copies to expire within it), `record` (one A / AAAA / CNAME / TXT / MX / CAA set: set, add or delete; an SPF / DMARC value scopes the set to its family), `parked` (null MX, `v=spf1 -all`, `v=DMARC1; p=reject` — after a read, the DMARC record there with p=reject and its report addresses kept —, CAA `0 issue ";"` unless left out, optionally `*._domainkey` `v=DKIM1; p=`; a read that finds MX records, or an SPF record that lets servers send, is a warning: `fix.p.parked-mail`, `fix.p.parked-sends`). The templates that edit what is there (`needsCurrent`: m365, google, spf, dmarc, ttl) build from a read; without one the outputs say what they cannot know: a TXT family set such a template edits unread (`unreadEdits`: its note — `fix.n.spf-unread`, `fix.n.dmarc-unread`, `fix.n.dmarc-first-unread` — names it) is "Add or change" in the instructions (`fix.ins.action.set`, `fix.ins.editFamily`: add the value if the name has no such record, else follow the note) and in the set list, and every format carries `fix.fn.unread-edit` (it would replace a record there). What a template looks at in the current state is in `reads` too, so a read asks exactly that.
- **Validation**: the records afterwards, plus what a read found at the same names for other types, go through `lib/zoneparse.js` + `lib/zonelint.js` (as a partial zone); `CHANGE_LINT_CODES` of the change's names count (a CNAME next to other data, private addresses, SPF / DMARC syntax, CAA tags and flags …). Then the SPF budget (the record's own lookup terms; with `countSpfLookups`, the recursive count with the includes as published now — of the record it counted: `countSpfLookups` returns `{ record, count, exceeded, error }` per name, and a set the form changed since gets an info "read again" (`fix.p.spf-recount`) instead of the old count), the RFC 8659 / 8657 grammar of each CAA issue value (lib/health.js parseCaaIssueValue) and TTLs under 60 s or over a day.
- **Formats**: BIND (the changed sets afterwards relative to `$ORIGIN`, removals as `; delete:` comments; an unchanged set left out); a Route 53 change batch (UPSERT of the full set — the family's other TXT values included when read —, DELETE of a set with its values, `CURRENT_VALUE` when not read; TXT and CAA strings in Route 53's octal escape form); the Cloudflare API as a POSIX shell script (the token and zone ID read from `$CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` / `$CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID`, never written; a record name in a list call percent-encoded, `!` too, and the zone's name in the `${VAR:?…}` message only as a plain host name, so no name from a zone file — `` ` `` `$` `"` `\` — reaches the shell; request bodies single-quoted ASCII JSON; one value for another is a PATCH in place so two SPF records never coexist; a deletion or TTL change lists the records first and uses `RECORD_ID`); octoDNS YAML (the names and every mapping in octoDNS's natural key order — `ttl`, `type`, `values` —, `''` for the apex, a TXT value as its raw text with `;` escaped — and a header line saying to load the entries with `escaped_semicolons: true` when one has a `;` —, in one more pair of quotes when it starts with `"` (octoDNS strips them as it loads it), `octodns: lenient: true` where octoDNS's own check refuses the text — outside ASCII, a `\` before a `;`; a deletion says which record goes from the name's list, never the name's whole entry); Terraform `cloudflare_record` (provider v4, one resource per value) and `aws_route53_record` (one per set; the provider sends a TXT string in quotes as it is, so each is written in Route 53's escape form, as in the change batch, and one over 255 bytes is split with `\"\"`). `formatNotes` says what a format needs (a set not read in a whole-set format, a Route 53 DELETE that must match exactly, Cloudflare's TTL range, record ids). The Route 53 string escapes, the YAML quoting, the octoDNS TXT escapes and check and its key order are lib/zonetext.js's (`route53String`, `yamlString`, `octodnsTxt`, `octodnsTxtRefused`, `naturalCompare`, §5.68), which lib/zoneconvert.js writes whole zones with: the change request, its check page and "Show the fix" never load the zone converter.
- **Instructions** (`changeInstructions`): one numbered step per set — Add / Replace / Delete / Change the TTL / Rewrite, the name, the values, the TTL, what it removes or keeps — the template's notes and the check link, in English or Turkish whatever the UI language.
- **Fixes**: `HEALTH_FIX_IDS` — dmarc.missing (p=none with a report address to create), dmarc.policy-none (→ quarantine), dmarc.pct, dmarc.sp-none, dmarc.rua-missing, dmarc.multiple (advice), spf.missing (`-all` without MX, the platform include for Microsoft 365 / Google Workspace MX hosts, else advice only), spf.null-mx, spf.all-pass / all-neutral / all-missing (`~all`), spf.ptr, spf.after-all (both keep `exp=` and unknown modifiers; only a `redirect=` an `all` voids goes), spf.redirect-ignored, spf.multiple (one merged record, `mergeSpf`: the first `exp=` and every other modifier once), spf.lookups-exceeded / lookups-high (flattening advice naming the costliest includes, never a record), mx.none (the mail part of the parked lock-down; advice only when the domain's SPF record lets servers send: a send-only domain has no MX either), mx.null-mixed (advice), caa.missing (the CAs of the current certificates from Certificate Transparency, `needsCt`; `caaFixFromIssuers` keeps what the report read — no CAA set, so an add — and a CA the form does not list sends the edit link to the plain-record template with every value), caa.cert-denied (the current certificate's CA added to the property that decided, the listed CAs kept), caa.critical-unknown (the critical flag cleared on the unknown tags, as CAA_FLAGS), tls-rpt.missing. The DMARC fixes change only what they are about (p, sp, pct and rua otherwise as they are); for a policy inherited from the organizational domain (RFC 7489 §6.6.3) they change that record, at `_dmarc.<org>`, where the policy comes from — dmarc.policy-none then steps up its `sp` — and the advice says so (`fix.a.dmarc-inherited`). The CAA fixes change the set where the climb found it (the domain or a parent, `fix.a.caa-at`). Built over `currentFromReport(report)` (the TXT and MX of the domain, the CAA set at the name it was found, the DMARC record of `_dmarc.<domain>` and an inherited one at the organizational domain), so the whole-set formats are exact; a fix that changes existing records notes that its TTL is a default (`fix.n.report-ttl`: a resolver does not tell the zone's own TTL). `LINT_FIX_CODES` — TXT_STRING_TOO_LONG (the same text re-split, `rewrite`), LOCALHOST_RECORD (delete), CAA_FLAGS and CAA_CRITICAL_UNKNOWN_TAG (flags 0), TTL_TOO_LOW (TTL 300), MULTIPLE_SPF (merged, modifiers kept): from the file, so exact, TTLs included; they carry no check link (`ui/fix-panel.js` LintFixPanel), since nothing about an imported zone reaches a URL or the current target. The views keep a copy of the id lists (`FIXABLE_CHECKS`, `FIXABLE_LINT`; a unit test keeps them equal) and load the panel on the first click.

Tests: `tests/js/fixes.test.js`, and the goldens of `tests/fixtures/fixes/gen-fixes-golden.mjs` (every template in every format and both languages, with and without a read; `--write` after a deliberate change).

### 5.51 `lib/changecheck.js` — "is it live?"
```js
export const CHECK_VERSION = 1, CHECK_RESOLVERS = ['cloudflare', 'google', 'dnssb', 'cznic'], CHECK_LIMITS = { rrsets: 20, values: 40, chars: 4000 },
  CHECK_VERDICTS = ['done', 'pending', 'wrong', 'error'], PENDING_REASONS = ['missing', 'old', 'other', 'partial', 'ttl', 'present'],
  CHECK_HEADLINES = ['done', 'done-partial', 'wrong', 'pending', 'no-answer', 'unknown'], CHECK_STOPS = ['done', 'timeout', 'cached', 'failed'],
  CHECK_TIMING = { base: 15 s, factor: 1.6, max: 5 min, stopAfter: 2 h, maxTtlWait: 24 h }
ExpectedSet = { name, type, mode, family, values, old: Data[]|null, maxTtl }
export function checkFromRequest(req) -> { zone, sets }, encodeCheck(check) -> { ok, query, length, reason }, decodeCheck(query | URLSearchParams) -> { ok, check } | { ok: false, error, detail },
  linkEncode(value), linkQuery(URLSearchParams) -> string, judgeAnswer(expected, response) -> { verdict, reason, seen, ttl }, pairKey(set, resolver),
  checkRound(check, { dns, resolvers, only, signal, now, onResult, timeoutMs }) -> PairResult[], checkState(check, latest) -> { headline, counts, sets, settled, answered, pairs },
  nextCheck({ latest, check, round, startedAt, now, errorRounds }) -> { stop: 'done'|'timeout'|'cached'|'failed'|null, at, pairs, cachedUntil }
```
- **The link**: `#/change/check?z=<zone>&r=<set>&r=…`, one `r` per set in presentation form: `<mode>[/<maxTtl>] <name relative to the zone> <TYPE> <values separated by |>[^<old values>]` (`has _acme-challenge TXT "…"`, `is/300 www A 192.0.2.10^198.51.100.5`); `|` and `^` inside a value are written `\124` / `\094`; `@ : / , ; =` stay readable (`linkEncode`). A TXT set's family is read from its values (or a deletion's old values); where that would read it wrong the type names it: `TXT:*` (every TXT record, e.g. a deletion where the read found only an SPF record), `TXT:spf1`. Nothing else is in it. `encodeCheck` refuses a set whose name is outside the zone (`outside`: the link writes names relative to it). `decodeCheck` refuses a link over `CHECK_LIMITS` — its length as written: the page passes the hash's own query, and a URLSearchParams counts as `linkQuery` writes it back, never as its own `toString()`, which percent-encodes the readable characters —, another version, a name written absolute (outside the zone), an unknown type or family or a value its type does not parse; `encodeCheck` / `decodeCheck` are exact inverses.
- **Verdicts** of one set on one resolver (what a CA or a mail server sees: through a CNAME chain for any type but CNAME; a family set looks at its own kind only; TXT compared by the joined text): `done` (exactly the values / at least them / none left, and a `maxTtl` set's copy expiring within it); `pending` with `missing` (no record), `old` (still exactly the old values, when there were any: an empty answer where a read found nothing is `missing`), `other` (another value while the old ones are not known), `partial` (a `has` set not complete yet), `ttl` (the new values cached with the old TTL), `present` (a deletion not seen yet); `wrong` (neither the new nor the known old values); `error` (no answer, or an rcode other than NOERROR / NXDOMAIN). `ttl` is what the resolver's copy has left — the negative TTL of the SOA for an empty answer (RFC 2308).
- **Timing** (`nextCheck`): after round n the wait is min(15 s × 1.6ⁿ, 5 min) — counted from `now`, or from the last round's end when `lastAt` is given (so the cutover assistant's watch, §5.80, turned on long after a check stopped asks at once) — and a pair is asked again only once its resolver's cached copy can have expired (its TTL after it answered, + 1 s, at most 24 h); a resolver that fails keeps being retried until three rounds in a row had a failure. It stops when every pair is done (errors aside), two hours after the start, when no pair can change before then (`cached`, with the time the last copy expires), or — `failed` — when what was given up leaves a set that no resolver answered (DoH blocked, offline, rate-limited everywhere, a SERVFAIL). `checkState` gives `done`, `done-partial` (done wherever a resolver answered), `wrong`, `pending`, `no-answer` (every pair answered or failed, and a set got no answer at all) or `unknown` (still asking). The check page (views/change.js) words each stop but `done`; Stop (Esc) during a round lets that round's answers show and schedules nothing after it; Check again starts over and asks every set on every resolver (a finished change can be checked again); an error verdict reads as its kind in words (server error, timed out, network error, rate limited, unreadable reply) or its DNS rcode. Offline a round does not run: the page says so, schedules nothing and runs it on the `online` event. While a round runs Check now is disabled and the keyboard focus it had moves to Stop; once the check stops, to Check again. Next to Copy link, **Copy summary** (§5.32 `changeSummary`, facts from `checkSummaryFacts`) copies the headline (`checkHeadline`, the same key and counts the page shows), each set by name and type with its state and how many resolvers see it, and why the check stopped, with the check link as its link; never a value.

Tests: `tests/js/changecheck.test.js` (the goldens' links round-trip, the family named where the values would read it wrong; limits, a near-limit link as URLSearchParams; every verdict; the schedule, a check no resolver answers stopping as `failed`).

### 5.52 `lib/nsparity.js` — the zone compared with the NEW provider's name servers (before the NS switch)
DOM-free. The Zone File's live check compares the file with public DNS, which the current provider still answers; this module asks the new name servers themselves, before the registrar's NS records change. Each (name, type) is one Globalping DNS measurement (§3, `dnsQueryRequest`) with `resolver` = the new server's host name, read back into the DohClient response shape lib/zonedrift.js reads (the answers parsed by lib/zoneparse.js one line at a time, `aa` from the dig flags line, a referral's NS records and glue from the authority / additional sections), so the whole plan and evaluation of §5.23 applies: names and types only, internal-looking names skipped by default, the hidden targets of proxied / flattened / alias records never queried, one query per unique (name, type), `queryTypes: PARITY_QUERY_TYPES` (CAA, TLSA … are `not-queryable`: the CLI's job), `dnssecTypes: PARITY_SIGNED_TYPES` (DNSKEY and CDNSKEY are skipped `dnssec-type` with RRSIG and NSEC*, never asked: the signer publishes them, and the new provider's keys never match the old one's — cli/dns_parity.py's "signed live"; the runbook's DNSSEC step covers the keys).
```js
export const PARITY_MODES = ['first', 'all'], PARITY_MAX_PROBES = 100, PARITY_MAX_NAMESERVERS = 8, PARITY_CONCURRENCY = 4,
  PARITY_EXTRA_TYPES = ['A', 'AAAA', 'MX', 'TXT'], PARITY_WWW_TYPES = ['A', 'AAAA'], PARITY_QUERY_TYPES /* GP_DNS_TYPES without ANY */, PARITY_SIGNED_TYPES = ['DNSKEY', 'CDNSKEY'],
  PARITY_STATUSES = ['same', 'different', 'missing', 'unproxied', 'extra', 'skipped', 'error'], PARITY_SEVERITY,
  PARITY_REASONS = ['ttl-differs', 'ns-new', 'ns-mismatch', 'ns-by-address', 'extra-record', 'cname-kept', 'below-cut'] /* + DRIFT_REASONS */,
  NS_STATES = ['ok', 'refused', 'not-authoritative', 'no-zone', 'servfail', 'unreachable', 'failed', 'not-run'], NS_ISSUES, PARITY_STOPS,
  RUNBOOK_STEPS = ['ttl', 'fix', 'dnssec', 'switch', 'wait', 'after'], RUNBOOK_STATES, PARITY_TTL_LOW = 3600, PARITY_KEEP_OLD_HOURS = 48, PARITY_CLI = 'dns_parity.py'
export function parseNameservers(text, { fileNs }) -> { list, cliOnly, issues: [{ code /* NS_ISSUES */, value }] }   // host names (trailing dot dropped, IDN → punycode) or public IPv4 addresses → list (Globalping); private / documentation addresses → cliOnly + a 'private' issue, public IPv6 addresses → cliOnly + an 'ipv6' issue (a probe asks name servers over IPv4: Globalping's DNS ipVersion defaults to 4 and an IPv6 resolver is experimental there) — the CLI command carries them; ≤ 8 in both together; the file's own NS flagged 'in-file'
export function fileNameservers(zone) -> string[]
export function extraQueries(zone, { skipPrivate }) -> [{ name, type }]   // apex: PARITY_EXTRA_TYPES the file lacks; www: A / AAAA when no wildcard covers it; none at a CNAME, A / AAAA never at a proxied name
export function planParity(zone, { nameservers, mode, extras, skipPrivate, wildcardProbes, maxProbes }) -> { ok, why: null|'no-origin'|'no-nameservers'|'over-cap', mode, full, serial, cap,
  needed, probes /* the most the run sends */, capped, rrsets, checked, perServer, extras, driftBudget, skipped, targetsHidden, internalShare }
export function authoritativeFlag(rawOutput) -> bool|null ; export function digSection(rawOutput, 'AUTHORITY'|'ADDITIONAL') -> answers[]
export function dnsResponse(measurement, { name, type, resolver, origin, id }) -> { ok, rcode, aa, answers, authorities, referral, resolver, ede: [], error, errorKind, measurementId, probe, unparsed, failure }
export function nameserverState(soaResponse, origin) -> { state /* NS_STATES */, serial, aa, rcode }
export function createParityDns({ client, nameserver, origin, reserve, release, onMeasurement, onStop, stopped }) -> { query(name, type, { signal }), sent }   // a DohClient over Globalping, memoised
export function parityRow(driftRow, { ns, origin, hosts, autoTtl }) -> ParityRow
export async function runParity(zone, { client, nameservers, cliOnly /* never asked: an address among them makes the apex NS set ns-by-address */, mode = 'first', extras = true, skipPrivate = true, wildcardProbes = true, maxProbes = 100, dns, signal,
  onRow, onProgress, onQuota, onServer, labelFn, now }) -> { origin, mode, startedAt, finishedAt, nameservers: NsResult[], rows: ParityRow[], counts, spent, planned,
  notReached /* record sets a stop kept from a server to compare */, stoppedBy: null|'quota'|'unreachable'|'abort', resetAt, serials: 'same'|'differ'|'unknown', dnssec: { signedInFile, ds: 'present'|'absent'|'unknown'|null }, capped, measurementIds }
export function signedInFile(zone) -> bool ; export function paritySummary(result) -> { verdict: 'ready'|'fix'|'check'|'partial'|'blocked', counts, ttl, unchecked, badServers, compared, stopped /* stoppedBy or notReached > 0 */ }
export function parityRunbook(zone, result|null, { nameservers }) -> [{ id /* RUNBOOK_STEPS */, state /* RUNBOOK_STATES */, params }]
export function parityZoneFile(origin) -> '<zone>.parity.zone' ; export function buildParityCommand({ file, nameservers, shell, script }) -> { command|null, dropped }
```
Rules that are easy to get wrong:
- **Batching:** 'first' mode compares every record set on the first server and asks each other server for its SOA only (a provider's servers serve one copy; the serial shows they serve the same version; `serials: 'differ'` warns). A first server that does not serve the zone costs its SOA probe and the next one is compared instead. 'all' multiplies the cost and is refused past the cap (`over-cap`). Each server's SOA is asked first: REFUSED, no `aa`, no SOA, SERVFAIL or an unreachable name ends that server there.
- **The hard cap** (`PARITY_MAX_PROBES`): a zone that needs more is compared up to the cap in 'first' mode (`capped`; the rest `skipped` / `budget`, and the UI points at the CLI). The budget is reserved before each POST (`reserve` / `release` for a free 400), so parallel queries never overspend; the plan's `probes` is exactly what an uninterrupted run sends.
- **Stops:** a quota 429 (or three network failures in a row) refuses every later POST at no cost, while the measurements already created — paid — are still read; the caller's signal ends the run at once. The rows so far are kept, and `notReached` counts what the stop left out for each server to compare (the plan's record sets less the rows it got; a server stopped before its first row: what it would have compared or left to the CLI). `paritySummary`'s `unchecked` adds it to the record sets left to the CLI and those without an answer, so a stopped run's "not everything was compared: N record sets" is exact ("did not finish" when N is 0). Verdict order: `blocked`, `fix` (missing / different, a server that does not serve the zone), then `partial` for a run that stopped (`stopped`), left a server unasked or got no answer for a record set (an `error` row) — what it never got could hold anything, so unproxied or extra rows so far never make it a clean `check`; cli/dns_parity.py ranks its ERROR rows the same —, then `check`, then `partial` for a finished run that left record sets to the CLI (types, the cap) or could not compare them at all (`unsupported-type`: a value the file holds as text only; `escaped-name`: a name that cannot be asked), then `ready`. `blocked` needs every server asked: a stop before a server was asked is `partial`, never "no new name server serves the zone".
- **Statuses:** match / proxied-ok / flattened-ok / alias-ok / routing-ok → `same`; differs → `different`; missing-live → `missing`; origin-exposed → `unproxied` (a proxied record answered with its origin: at the switch it stops being proxied); occluded → `skipped` / `below-cut`. A flattened CNAME the new provider serves as a plain CNAME to the same target is `same` / `cname-kept`. `ttl-stale` is replaced by `ttl-differs` (any difference: an authoritative TTL is exact), never at a proxied name, an automatic TTL or the apex NS. The apex NS set is judged against the host names entered (`ns-new` when the new servers name exactly themselves, `ns-mismatch` otherwise, `ns-by-address` when any server was typed as an address, one only the CLI asks — `cliOnly` — included: the CLI's rule, with one address which names the set should hold is not known). Extra rows (`extra` / `extra-record`) come from `extraQueries`: a provider's parking address or default MX at the apex or www. An ALIAS / ANAME record set (a provider's flattening, kept as text by the parser, so lib/zonedrift.js skips it `unsupported-type`) is judged by the A and AAAA questions `extraQueries` asks at its name: an address (or a CNAME) is `same` / `target-hidden` and not an extra row, nothing is `missing` (`nodata` / `nxdomain`) — the new provider's import dropped it —, and without both questions (extras off, another name, a stop) it stays `skipped` and counts as not compared.
- **Runbook:** ttl (the apex NS TTL and the longest record TTL of the file against 3600 s; the TLD's own NS TTL cannot be lowered), fix (todo: missing / different / servers that do not serve it; warn: extra, unproxied, not compared, stopped, capped, serials out of step — after a stop `params.stopped` words it "nothing is missing or different so far, but the comparison did not finish", as the headline does), dnssec (todo when the file carries DNSKEY / RRSIG / NSEC* / CDS / CDNSKEY or the DS lookup finds a DS: remove the DS and wait for its TTL, or pre-publish the new provider's DNSKEY and DS when both support multi-signer, RFC 8901), switch (blocked while there is something to fix; warn — "compare again, or run the CLI, before you switch", with the count of record sets not compared — after a stop or when record sets were left out; todo otherwise), wait (48 h: the old zone keeps answering the cached delegation), after (check from outside, restore the TTLs).
- Tests: `tests/js/nsparity.test.js` (the live captures `d01`–`d14`, a fake authoritative Globalping with referrals, quota stops, budget, cancel and what a stop left out, a stop after unproxied rows (`partial`, the switch `warn`), host names mixed with an address and an address only the CLI asks, a public IPv6 server sent to the CLI, the runbook, the command with private servers), `tests/e2e/zone.e2e.mjs` (offline: the consent dialog, exactly the planned probes, nothing hidden sent, statuses, the runbook, redacted exports, the BIND download, a private server in the command, the privacy line with the internal skip off, Compare / Stop from the keyboard, the progress of a tab mounted during a run, a quota 429 while About is shown — the warning toast "stopped, N record sets not compared", the `partial` headline, the fix step's "so far" and the switch `warn` —, Forget during a run — no toast, no result —, the table inside its card at 1280 / 1440 px, 320 / 375 px).

### 5.53 `lib/origincompare.js` — the old and the new server of a name, side by side
DOM-free. Before DNS moves a name to a new address: one HTTPS GET of a path at each address with the name as SNI and Host (§3, `httpsGetAtRequest`), the second from the first one's probe (`locations: <id>`), compared field by field. Addresses a probe cannot reach go to the CLI (`buildCompareCommand`: `ssl_origin_scan.py --compare`, §7).
```js
export const COMPARE_FIELDS = ['reach', 'status', 'location', 'contentType', 'title', 'body', 'hsts', 'server', 'certSubject', 'certCovers', 'certTrusted', 'certIssuer', 'certExpires', 'certFingerprint'],
  COMPARE_VERDICTS = ['same', 'differs', 'broken', 'incomplete', 'unreachable'], COMPARE_NOTES, COMPARE_SHARED = ['cert-untrusted', 'cert-name', 'cert-expiring'], COMPARE_ISSUES, COMPARE_EXPIRY_WARN_DAYS = 14, COMPARE_BODY_LIMIT = 10000, COMPARE_PROBES = 2,
  COMPARE_CERT_NAMES = 3
export function checkCompare({ host, oldIp, newIp, path, port }) -> { ok, probeable, host, oldIp, newIp, path, port, issues: [{ code, value }], private: string[] }
export function compareRequest({ ip, host, path, port, locations }) -> body
export function pageTitle(body) -> string|null ; export function parseHsts(value) -> { raw, maxAge /* null unless valid */, includeSubDomains, preload, valid }|null   // as a browser reads it (RFC 6797 6.1, 8.1): the first of joined headers, exactly one max-age of digits, no directive twice, a valueless includeSubDomains, token syntax
export function readSide(measurement, { ip, host, now }) -> CompareSide   // { ip, ok, failure: verify.parseFailure, status, location, contentType, server, hsts, body: { sha256, length, truncated, title }, cert: { sha256, subjectCN, hostnames, covers, issuer /* its CN · O, all Globalping reports */, issuerCN, selfSigned /* the probe's DEPTH_ZERO_SELF_SIGNED_CERT, or an issuer CN that is the subject CN: an expired self-signed certificate reports CERT_HAS_EXPIRED */, notBefore, notAfter, daysLeft, authorized, error }, probe, measurementId }
export function certNames(cert, limit = 3) -> string|null   // the subject CN first, then the SAN host names not listed yet, three and '+N' (the CLI's cert_names_text)
export function compareSides(oldSide, newSide, { now }) -> { verdict, fields: [{ key, old, new, same, severity: 'ok'|'info'|'warn'|'error', note, shared }], differences, worst /* of the fields that count */, shared /* COMPARE_SHARED notes */ }
export function sideFields(side) -> [{ key, value }]   // one side alone (the old server after a stop or a failure before the new one was asked)
export async function runCompare({ client, host, oldIp, newIp, path, port, signal, onSide, now }) -> { old, new, comparison, spent, ids, at }   // a Globalping error after the first measurement carries err.spent and err.first
export function buildCompareCommand({ host, oldIp, newIp, path, port, shell }) -> string|null
```
Rules: the new server not answering (compared no further), answering 4xx / 5xx where the old one did not, or a certificate that does not cover the name or that the probe did not trust while the old one was is an **error** (`broken`); another status, redirect, content type or title, a lost HSTS header (a policy is on with one valid max-age above 0, `parseHsts`; none: `hsts-lost`; one browsers ignore — no single valid max-age, a directive twice, `max_age` —: `hsts-invalid`; `max-age=0`, which tells browsers to forget the policy: `hsts-off`; a shorter max-age, or without the old header's `includeSubDomains` or `preload`: `hsts-weaker` — an old header that is off or invalid is no policy to lose), a new certificate expiring within 14 days or an untrusted certificate after an untrusted one that does not fail alike from the same issuer (`cert-untrusted-other`: whatever trusts the old one — a CDN that knows its origin CA, clients that know an internal CA — may refuse it) is a **warning** (`differs`); another body (a page with a token or a time differs on every request), Server header, the certificate's names (subject CN and SANs), issuer, expiry or certificate is **information** (`same`). A certificate problem **both servers share** — an untrusted certificate, the same one, or one that fails alike from the same issuer (`sharedUntrust`: the same probe error — a chain that lost its intermediate reports another —, the new one valid by now, neither self-signed, the issuer compared by its CN and O only, case and spacing aside, as that is all Globalping reports: Cloudflare's RSA and ECC origin CAs have no CN and are both "CloudFlare, Inc."; an origin CA certificate behind a CDN, renewed or not, is the usual case), a certificate that covers the name on neither, both expiring within 14 days with the new one no sooner — is no difference: the field is `shared` (severity `warn`, no `differs` highlight when the values match), its note goes to `shared`, and the verdict is taken from the other fields, so two identical servers are `same`; the card says each shared problem apart under the verdict (`oc.shared.<note>`), the JSON download carries `shared`. An old server that does not answer makes the comparison `incomplete` (the new values are information); neither answering is `unreachable` (the reach row a warning), never `broken`: the probe's network may be the cause as much as the servers. The body hash covers what the probe returned (the first 10,000 characters, decoded): `body-cut` says so. An untrusted certificate shows why (`no: <the probe's error>`, as the CLI's `no: <reason>`). Certificate identity and coverage reuse lib/verify.js `servedCert` and lib/domain.js `certCovers`. Tests: `tests/js/origincompare.test.js` (the live captures `h01` / `h02` and edits of them), `tests/e2e/retire.e2e.mjs` (offline: the prefill from the form, the CLI block for a private address, the consent dialog, two probes from one probe, `differs` then `broken` then `unreachable` (the failure in TR and EN), the same untrusted certificate on both → `same` with the shared warning (TR and EN, the JSON), an origin CA certificate then a self-signed one → `differs`, each side's reason and the note (TR and EN), Compare / Stop from the keyboard, a stop after the old server keeps its answer, a trip to About during a run ends on the card shown on return, the JSON download, 320 / 375 px).

### 5.54 `lib/egresslog.js`, `ui/egress-meter.js` — what this page sent, counted
The product says everything runs in the browser; the ledger lets a user check it without developer tools. `ui/egress-meter.js` starts with the shell's boot (before the first view mounts) and feeds one page-session log from two witnesses: a wrapper around `window.fetch` (each request the page's code starts; a redirect it followed, by `response.url`; a request that got no answer — a network error, a response the browser blocked, a cancel) and a buffered `PerformanceObserver` on `'resource'` entries (every request the browser made for the page, the app's own files loaded before the boot included). The wrapper passes the same arguments to the browser's fetch (called on the window) and returns a promise with the same outcome, so an unhandled rejection is still reported as one. Nothing is stored; a reload starts from zero.
```js
export const EGRESS_VIA = ['fetch', 'resource', 'redirect', 'failed'], MAX_SIGNATURES = 400, OVERFLOW_PATH = '/…'
export const MAX_NOTES = 8
export function requestSignature(url, base?) -> { key, origin, host, path, query } | null
  // path: plain lower-case words kept, every other segment (a name, an address, a hash, an id) '*', and so is the one after
  // a word an API puts a value after (domain, ip, autnum, entity, nameserver, measurements, subdomains; after repos the next two:
  // GitHub's owner and repository), at most 8 segments;
  // query: the sorted parameter names (odd ones '*'), never a value; null for anything but http(s)
  // 'https://crt.sh/?q=%25.example.com&output=json' → key 'https://crt.sh/?output&q'
export function requestCount(entry) -> max(fetch, resource) + redirect   // a completed fetch is seen by both witnesses
export function countRequests(entries, pageOrigin) -> { thirdParty, self, hosts }
export function noteRequest(url, note)   // the sender says what a URL cannot, just before its fetch: a fixed word
                                         // (/^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$/), never a value; anything else is dropped
export function onRequestNote(fn) -> unsubscribe   // fn(url, note): the meter
export function createEgressLog({ now, maxSignatures }) -> {
  record(url, { via, base, from }) -> boolean,   // never throws; past maxSignatures new shapes of an origin share one '/…'
                                                 // entry; a 'redirect' takes the notes of its request `from`
  note(url, note, { base }) -> boolean,          // adds a note to the signature (at most MAX_NOTES)
  snapshot() -> { since, at, entries: Array<{ key, origin, host, path, query, notes, fetch, resource, redirect, failed, first, last }> },
  clear(), subscribe(fn) -> unsubscribe    // fn once per microtask burst, never per request
}
// ui/egress-meter.js (browser only): export const egressLog; startEgressMeter(win) -> { fetch, resourceTiming } (once; it
// also hears the notes); egressMeterStatus()
```
**Notes.** A URL does not always say what a request carried. `lib/globalping.js` notes each measurement it creates as `ip-target` (the body sends a public address with the host name and port: SSL Targets › Verify, Retire an IP › Compare the old and the new server, which sends the path too), `host-target` (a host name alone: Domain Health's MTA-STS check, Renewal readiness's HTTP-01 test) or `dns-query` (a DNS measurement: a name and a type asked at a name server, Zone File › New name servers) — the kind, never the value; `lib/rdap.js` notes each registry server it asks as `rdap` (one the IANA bootstrap named, or rdap.org, whose redirect takes the note to the server it reached).
Both modules are on the start route (the budget of §6 names them). The footer's **What this page sent · N requests to third parties** (`countRequests`, refreshed at most once a second) links to `#/about?section=sent`.

### 5.55 `lib/egress.js` — the registry of third parties and the ledger
Every third party the page can contact, what each endpoint receives, and the rows of About › What this page sent. Loaded with the About view.
```js
export const DATA_KINDS = ['appFiles', 'nothing', 'dnsQuestions', 'nameServers', 'domains', 'hostnames', 'ipNamePairs', 'ipAddresses',
  'asNumbers', 'certSerial', 'keyHash', 'measurementIds', 'repository', 'apiToken']   // nameServers: the servers a Globalping DNS measurement asks (Zone File › New name servers);
                                                                         // repository: the user's own repository's path, owner/repo (Monitoring › GitHub);
                                                                         // apiToken: the user's own token, in a header, for one fetch (Zone File › Fetch) or one read (Monitoring › GitHub)
export const EGRESS_ROLES = ['site', 'dns', 'ct', 'passive', 'ip', 'registration', 'probes', 'dnsHosting', 'repository', 'ca']   // dnsHosting: the user's own DNS provider;
                                                                         // repository: the user's own code host
export const NEVER_SENT = ['certificates', 'keys', 'zone', 'inventory', 'workspace', 'tracking']   // egress.never.<id>, each with its exceptions
export const EGRESS_SERVICES: Array<{ id, name, role, hosts: string[], noteHost?: string,
  endpoints: Array<{ id, sends: DATA_KINDS[], path? /* '*' one segment, '**' any run */, param? /* a query parameter name */,
    notes?: { [note]: DATA_KINDS[] } /* what a request carried by its sender's note; `sends` without one */ }> }>
  // doh (hosts from lib/resolvers.js RESOLVERS and ECS_RESOLVERS — AliDNS's JSON form for the mainland China locations; the row named as the resolver), crtsh (search → domains, serial → certSerial,
  // spkisha256 → keyHash), certspotter, hackertarget (hostsearch → domains, reverseiplookup → ipAddresses), anubis, otx,
  // thc (subdomains → domains, lookup → ipAddresses), ripestat (each data call by name: announced-prefixes → asNumbers;
  // prefix-overview, maxmind-geo-lite, reverse-dns-ip → ipAddresses; no catch-all, so a new call is an unknown endpoint),
  // ipwhois (its one API, /<address>), rdap-bootstrap (data.iana.org → nothing), rdap (rdap.org, rdap.identitydigital.services — §5.14 RDAP_OVERRIDES —, and noteHost 'rdap': any other https host whose
  // requests lib/rdap.js noted — a path that merely looks like an RFC 9082 lookup is not enough — with the endpoint by path:
  // …/domain/<name> → domains, …/ip/<address>[/<length>] → ipAddresses),
  // globalping (limits → nothing; POST measurements → hostnames by the note host-target, ipNamePairs by ip-target (Verify,
  // Retire an IP's old and new server), dnsQuestions + nameServers by dns-query (a DNS measurement: Zone File › New name
  // servers), all four without a note; GET measurements/<id> → measurementIds),
  // desec (dnsHosting; /api/*/domains/*/rrsets/ → domains + apiToken), digitalocean (dnsHosting; /*/domains/*/records → domains + apiToken),
  // github (repository; api.github.com: /repos/*/*/contents/** and /repos/*/*/issues → repository + apiToken)
export const SELF_SERVICE        // the page's own origin: appFiles
export function getEgressService(id) -> service | SELF_SERVICE | null
export function classifySignature(sig /* with notes */, { origin }) -> { service|null, endpoint|null, sends, label /* resolver name */ }
  // an unknown endpoint of a known service: every kind the service can receive; an unknown host or plain http: service null
export function classifyUrl(url, { origin, notes }) -> the same, or null for a non-http(s) URL
export function serviceSends(service) -> DATA_KINDS[]
export function ledgerRows(snapshot, { origin }) -> Array<{ host, origin, kind: 'self'|'service'|'unknown', serviceId, name, role,
  requests, fetch, resource, redirect, failed, sends, endpoints: Array<{ id, requests, sends }>, first, last }>
  // one row per origin; unknown hosts first (a host is one service only when every request of it classifies as it), then the
  // services in registry order (a service's hosts by requests), the page's own origin last; an endpoint's kinds add up over
  // its signatures
export function ledgerTotals(rows) -> { requests, services, hosts, self, unknown, failed }   // requests / hosts / failed: third parties
```
**The guarantee** (`tests/js/egress.test.js`): the sources (`assets/js/**` and `sw.js`) are scanned (a small lexer: comments, strings, templates, regular expressions) for network call sites — `fetch(`, `fetchJson(`, `fetchText(`, `fetchWithTimeout(`, `fetchAndRead(`, a `fetchImpl` passed on, the global fetch touched — and every file that has one must be declared with the registry services it sends to (a transport such as `lib/util.js` or a forwarder such as `lib/scanner.js` with none). Every `http(s)://` literal of **every** file — not only the call sites: a URL constant can live in a module without a fetch call (`lib/sourceinfo.js`, `ui/globalping-gate.js`) and be fetched by one that imports it — must classify through the registry (in a call site, as one of its declared services), or be a link host declared for that one file (the repository on GitHub, the registries' WHOIS pages, the platforms' and resolvers' home pages, the SVG namespace …), or a reserved `.invalid` name — a link host may be a service's API host only where the test says why and none of its links is one of the service's endpoints (`lib/netinfo.js` names `https://api.github.com/meta`, where GitHub publishes the Pages ranges it copied; the page calls only the repository endpoints of Monitoring › GitHub); a URL whose host is data (a template's `${…}` there) is refused in a call site and elsewhere needs a declared reason (a name read through the URL parser, a probe's URL that is only shown). A self-test plants a new API constant in `lib/sourceinfo.js` fetched from `lib/sources.js` and must see it fail. Every RIPEstat data call the code builds (a literal path segment after `RIPESTAT_BASE`, or the literal first argument of `lib/ipintel.js` `ripeUrl()`, the one template that takes the call from a variable) must be a named endpoint, every named one must still be called, and ipwho.is keeps its one caller and request. Every registry service must have an endpoint in the code (DoH: every resolver of `RESOLVERS`); XMLHttpRequest, beacons, sockets, EventSource, workers and `new Image()` are refused outright; the senders' notes are checked against the real `lib/globalping.js` and `lib/rdap.js`. A new endpoint therefore cannot ship without a registry line — the ledger names it and says what it receives — and a host that is still unknown at run time (a browser extension's request) is listed first, flagged.
**UI** (`ui/egress-panel.js`, About › What this page sent, `#/about?section=sent`): the summary ("Since 14:02 · 42 requests to third parties on 6 hosts · 38 files from this site"), a warning for hosts not in the registry, the table (service with host and role, requests with "N got no answer", what it received — per endpoint with counts when a host got several kinds —, last time; labelled cards at ≤ 640 px), refreshed at most once a second; **Clear**; how it is counted; the never-sent list; the deploy line from the version file (§5.35: "This page runs deploy <version> · commit <12 hex>" linking `<REPO_URL>/commit/<sha>`, "built without a commit name" or "its version file could not be read" once the file answered — a file of another deploy counts as not read, never as "no commit" —, until then the deploy alone, `data-state="reading"`; "Development copy …" in the repository).

### 5.56 `lib/ctrelated.js` — related domains from the certificates a scan already has
Other registrable domains named in the same certificates as the scanned domain's hosts (SAN co-occurrence) — a forgotten brand or campaign domain often shows up only that way. Pure; the certificates are a scan's CT `SourceResult.certs` (lib/sources.js CtCert: `names` is every name a source gave), so nothing is asked again.
```js
export const SHARED_CERT_DOMAINS = 12, RELATED_NAME_CAP = 12, RELATED_CERT_CAP = 10, RELATED_MAX = 200
export function uniqueCerts(certs) -> Array<CtCert & { complete }>
  // exact keys folded; a crt.sh certificate folded into the Cert Spotter issuance with the same validity whose names include
  // all of its own (the complete ones indexed by validity: linear); complete: Cert Spotter reported it (its whole name list)
export function relatedDomains(certs, { domains, now }) -> {
  related: Array<{ domain, certs, names /* ≤ 12 */, moreNames, certificates: Array<{ key, sources, issuer, notBefore, notAfter,
    url /* crt.sh page, or a crt.sh search by SHA-256 */, ownNames, domains, shared, partial }> /* newest first, ≤ 10 */,
    latest, current, sharedOnly, platform /* netinfo provider name */ }>,
  more, certs /* certificates of the scanned hosts read */, withOthers, partial /* crt.sh-only: names may be missing */, shared
}   // a scope (shop.example.com) counts its registrable domain as its own; a certificate naming more than SHARED_CERT_DOMAINS
    // registrable domains is a shared one (usually a CDN's or a host's) unless most of its other domains carry a scanned
    // domain's label (example.de, example.fr … for example.com: one company's multi-brand certificate, never shared); a
    // domain only in shared certificates is sharedOnly and listed last, a platform's domain after the brands; order then
    // by certificates, newest, name
```
**UI** (`ui/related-domains.js`, loaded by the Subdomains view only with a run that asks crt.sh or Cert Spotter): Sources › **Related domains in the same certificates** — waiting / failed states; "N other domains share certificates with these hosts (M certificates read)" counting the brand domains; per brand domain its certificate count, Current / Expired, a platform badge, its names, **The certificates** (issuer, validity, the scanned names it carries, a crt.sh link, "N registrable domains" / "crt.sh only" flags) and **Scan too** (its accessible name "Scan too: <domain>"), which starts a new scan of the run's domains together with it and moves the keyboard focus to the new run's title (disabled while a scan runs; the hint says the passive sources are asked again); the shared-only domains in one Disclosure ("N domains appear only in certificates that name more than 12 registrable domains"), hedged — usually a CDN's or a host's certificate for many customers, which says nothing about ownership, but it can be one company's for its many brands — and each with **Scan too** as well (never a platform's domain); the crt.sh partial-names note. The card is drawn again only when the run's CT results change — a scan starting or ending only turns the buttons on or off — and the disclosures the user opened stay open.

### 5.57 `lib/keycontinuity.js` — was the key reused across renewals, or rotated?
Everything is said of crt.sh, not of CT: its coverage is incomplete and can lag by days or weeks (checked 2026-09-28: letsencrypt.org's leaf issued on 2026-09-04 with embedded SCTs, which Cert Spotter lists with its `pubkey_sha256`, came back `[]` from crt.sh by key and by serial, while the previous leaf's key was found). Only other certificates with the key on crt.sh are evidence (a reuse); only this one is "no earlier certificate with this key on crt.sh", never proof of a rotation; none at all is "logged, but not on crt.sh yet" for a certificate with SCTs or from a known public CA.
```js
export const CRTSH_BASE = 'https://crt.sh/', KEY_TIMEOUT_MS = 60000, KEY_RETRY_DELAY_MS = 4000, KEY_MAX_ROWS = 2000
export const KEY_STATUSES = ['reused', 'single', 'not-indexed', 'not-found']
export async function spkiSha256(cert, { subtle }) -> hex   // SHA-256 of spkiDer (x509.computeFingerprints: WebCrypto, else lib/sha.js)
export function crtshKeyUrl(hex) -> 'https://crt.sh/?spkisha256=<hex>&output=json'   // TypeError unless 64 hex digits
export function parseKeyRows(rows, { cert, maxRows }) -> { certs: Array<{ ids, serialHex, issuer, notBefore, notAfter, isThis, url }>, rows, truncated }
  // one entry per issuer + serial (the precertificate folded in), oldest first; isThis: the looked-up certificate's serial and issuer CN
export function keyContinuity(certs, { cert, now, publicCa }) -> { status, sctCount, expectLogged, total, others, thisLogged, before,
  after, current, firstSeen, lastUntil, days /* firstSeen → now, or → lastUntil once all expired */, issuers }
  // status: reused (crt.sh has others), single (only this one), not-indexed (none, but cert.sctCount > 0 or publicCa: it was
  // logged), not-found (none, and nothing says it was logged); publicCa: the issuer is a known public CA (health.caaIssuerInfo)
export async function lookupKeyContinuity(cert, { fetchImpl, signal, timeoutMs, retryDelayMs, now, subtle, publicCa })
  -> KeyContinuity & { spki, url, certs, rows, truncated, checkedAt }   // one crt.sh search, retried once on a server / network
                                                                       // error (never after a timeout); throws its failure or AbortError
```
**UI** (`ui/key-continuity.js`, Certificate › CT logs, per shown certificate, kept per certificate for the page session): the public key's SHA-256 (computed locally, with copy), **Look this key up in CT** (only on the click; "Sends only this hash to crt.sh"; `ctx.requireOnline`), then **Key reused across renewals** ("crt.sh lists this key in N other certificates: in use since at least …", how many days, how many issued before and after this one), **No earlier certificate with this key on crt.sh** (the key may be new, or crt.sh lacks the earlier ones), **Logged, but not on crt.sh yet** (the certificate's SCT count, or its public CA) or **crt.sh has no certificate with this key** (no SCTs, not a known public CA: a private CA's certificates are never logged); for the first two, "crt.sh does not list this certificate itself" when it is missing, what it means for TLSA `3 1 1` records (a reused key keeps matching until a renewal changes it; a key that did change needs the next record published 2 × TTL first, or a `2 1 1` pin of the CA) and for HPKP-style pins, **Open the DANE / TLSA tab**, and the certificates with the key (crt.sh links, this certificate marked). A CA certificate picked in "Certificate shown" (`isCA`) is worded for a CA key: the same key in re-issued and cross-signed CA certificates is normal (**Key also in other certificates**), the consequences are a TLSA `2 1 1` record and a CA pin of that key (with a backup), none on crt.sh says crt.sh has most public CA certificates and a private CA's are never logged, and `publicCa` is not passed (a CA's issuer promises no log of it). A failure shows the error with Retry ("crt.sh is often busy"). The lookup runs on its own AbortController kept with the result per certificate, so leaving the view (to watch it in About › What this page sent), switching the language or loading another certificate does not stop it (its answer is kept for its certificate; another certificate's card never shows it); only a switch to another workspace or "Delete all local data" does (`cancelKeyLookups`).

### 5.58 `lib/zipread.js` — the containers mail reports arrive in
Reporters mail DMARC reports as `.zip` (Google) or `.xml.gz` (Microsoft) and TLS reports as `.json.gz`; a mailbox export is a zip of those. DOM-free, no dependency: gzip and deflate go through the platform's `DecompressionStream` (browsers, Node ≥ 21), the zip structure is read here.
```js
export const ZIP_ERRORS = ['not-zip','truncated','multi-disk','encrypted','method','crc','too-large','too-many','corrupt','overlap','nested','unsupported']
export const ZIP_LIMITS = { maxEntryBytes: 32 MiB, maxTotalBytes: 128 MiB /* inflated per dropped file, failed parts included */,
  maxEntries: 2000 /* per dropped file, the archives inside it included */, maxDepth: 2 /* a zip of .xml.gz */ }
export class ZipError extends Error { code /* ZIP_ERRORS */; detail; inflated /* bytes decompressed before it failed */ }
export function containerOf(bytes) -> 'gzip'|'zip'|null            // by the first bytes (1f 8b; PK 03 04 or an empty archive's PK 05 06), never by the name
export function crc32(bytes) -> number ; export function toBytes(input) -> Uint8Array
export function readZipDirectory(bytes, { maxEntries }) -> { entries: [{ name, method, flags, encrypted, directory, compressedSize, size, crc, localOffset }], total }
  // the end of central directory record (the last one; a comment may hold its signature), ZIP64 end record + locator + the 0x0001 extra field;
  // data descriptors (bit 3) need nothing more; UTF-8 names (bit 11, or valid UTF-8), else one character per byte. Throws not-zip, truncated, multi-disk
export async function extractZipEntry(bytes, entry, { maxBytes, signal }) -> Uint8Array   // stored or deflate only (method names deflate64, bzip2, lzma, zstd, xz, aes …);
                                                   // inflates no further than the declared size (one byte more is corrupt, found at once), checks the
                                                   // size and the CRC-32; throws encrypted, method, too-large, truncated, corrupt, crc
export async function inflate(bytes, 'gzip'|'deflate-raw'|'deflate', { maxBytes, signal, DecompressionStreamImpl }) -> Uint8Array   // stops as soon as the output passes maxBytes;
                                                   // an abort cancels the stream even while a read waits on it
export async function gunzip(bytes, { maxBytes, signal }) -> Uint8Array   // the trailer's ISIZE is not trusted (mod 2^32; a cut file has none): the stream is capped instead
export async function unpackFile({ name, bytes }, { maxEntryBytes, maxTotalBytes, maxEntries, maxDepth, signal }) -> {
  files: [{ name /* .gz taken off */, path /* 'outer.zip › dmarc/inner.xml.gz' */, bytes, via: Array<'zip'|'gzip'> }],
  problems: [{ path, code /* ZIP_ERRORS */, detail }],
  inflated   // what it cost: the bytes charged to maxTotalBytes (inflated, failed parts included, or a stored entry's size; 0 for a plain file)
}   // directories, __MACOSX/ and .DS_Store skipped; one broken entry never stops the others; rejects only with an AbortError
```
**A hostile archive** (anyone can mail a "report" to a rua mailbox) costs no more than the caps: an entry inflates only up to its declared size, every byte inflated is charged to the dropped file's budget whether its part then unpacks or fails (a lying CRC or size, a gzip whose trailer fails), and through `inflated` to the drop's (§5.59 `MAX_DROP_BYTES`), entries are counted across the nested archives, and entries whose bytes (local header and data) overlap — the trick of a small zip that unpacks to terabytes, where every central directory entry names one stream — are refused as `overlap` before any is inflated. A 50 KB zip of 1,000 entries naming one 40 MB stream takes milliseconds.
`tests/js/zipread.test.js` reads archives Python's `zipfile` and `gzip` wrote (`tests/fixtures/mailreports`, `gen_mailreports.py`: deflated, stored, a zip of zips and gzip files, data descriptors) and builds the broken ones byte by byte (ZIP64, encrypted, bzip2, a bad CRC, a lying size, several disks, truncation, the caps, overlapping entries, failed parts paid for, a read the abort ends).

### 5.59 `lib/dmarcreport.js` — DMARC aggregate reports (RFC 7489 Appendix C)
Who sends mail as a domain, whether it passes DMARC and what stands between the domain and `p=reject`. DOM-free. **XML:** a minimal reader in the lib, not DOMParser in the view — the reports are a small data-only subset of XML, the same code then runs and is tested in Node (which has no DOMParser) on real report bytes, and a reader that refuses a DTD internal subset cannot expand an entity (no billion laughs, no external entity).
```js
export function parseXml(text, { maxElements = 2e6, maxDepth = 64 }) -> XmlElement { name /* local, lowercase */, attrs, children, text }   // throws XmlError: unterminated,
                                                   // mismatch, unclosed, doctype (an internal subset), empty, limit; the five predefined entities, character references,
                                                   // CDATA, comments and processing instructions; xmlChild / xmlChildren / xmlText(el, name). Linear time: attributes are read
                                                   // by a forward scan, never a backtracking pattern (a megabyte tag with no '=' reads in milliseconds)
export function parseAggregateReport(text, { file }) -> { ok: true, report } | { ok: false, code: 'xml'|'not-dmarc'|'incomplete', detail }
AggregateReport = { kind: 'dmarc', key /* org|report_id: a report dropped twice counts once */, file, org, email, extraContact, reportId, begin: Date, end: Date,
  errors: string[] /* the reporter's <error> notes */, policy: { domain, p, sp /* default p */, np, pct /* default 100 */, adkim, aspf /* 'r'|'s' */, fo, testing /* DMARCbis t */ },
  records: [{ ip, count, disposition /* DISPOSITIONS: none, pass (DMARCbis), quarantine, reject */, dkim, spf /* policy_evaluated: aligned results */, reasons: [{ type, comment }], headerFrom, envelopeFrom, envelopeTo,
    dkimAuth: [{ domain, selector, result, human }], spfAuth: [{ domain, scope, result /* 'hardfail' read as fail */ }] }], messages, skipped /* records without an address or count */ }
  // Google-, Microsoft- and DMARCbis-style reports (a version, namespaces, np, discovery_method, no pct); dates in seconds (milliseconds read as such)
export function looksLikeAggregate(text) -> boolean   // a feedback document element after the XML declaration, comments and a DOCTYPE without an internal subset
export function decodeReportText(bytes) -> string   // BOM, then an XML declaration's encoding, else UTF-8
export async function readReportFiles([{ name, bytes }], { signal, limits /* unpackFile's + maxDropBytes */, onProgress }) -> { dmarc: AggregateReport[], tls: TlsReport[],
  problems: [{ path, code /* REPORT_PROBLEMS */, detail }], read /* plain files looked at */, files /* dropped files read */, inflated /* what the drop's archives cost */, stopped }
  // archives unpacked (§5.58); each file told apart by its content (XML with a feedback element / JSON with policies), never by its name; at most
  // MAX_REPORT_FILES = 2,000 plain files, the dropped files after that named (too-many), not unpacked; a plain file past ZIP_LIMITS.maxEntryBytes (32 MiB)
  // is named too-large, never parsed, whether dropped as it is or unpacked. One inflation budget for the whole drop: MAX_DROP_BYTES = 1 GiB across the
  // unpackFile calls (each still within its own maxTotalBytes), so 200 dropped gzip bombs inflate 1 GiB, not 200 × 128 MiB; past it an archive is
  // too-large ('the drop as a whole') and never opened, a plain report is still read. Before each dropped file and each plain file an archive holds,
  // the event loop gets a turn once READ_YIELD_MS = 50 ms of work have passed and the signal is checked: a Stop acts in the middle of a zipped mailbox
  // folder. A Stop (the signal's abort) resolves with what was read before it — the reports of the archive it cut too — and stopped: true; `files` then
  // counts the dropped files done and the one it cut once unpacked.
  // onProgress(done, total) counts files: a dropped file is one until it is unpacked, then the plain files inside it (at least one), so `total` grows
export function aggregateDmarc(reports) -> { domains: DomainAggregate[] /* most messages first */, duplicates }
DomainAggregate = { domain, reports, messages, pass, fail, begin, end, days, policy /* the latest report's */, policies /* every p seen, latest first */,
  reporters: [{ org, email, reports, messages, pass, begin, end }], sources: SourceRow[] /* most messages first */, errors, skipped }
SourceRow = { ip, version, private, messages, pass, fail /* DMARC: an aligned DKIM or SPF pass */, dkimAligned, spfAligned, dispositions: { none, pass, quarantine, reject },
  headerFrom, envelopeFrom, spfAuth / dkimAuth / overrides: [{ …, messages }], reporters, records, begin, end }
export function spfDomainsFor(agg) -> string[]   // the header-from and SPF-checked domains of the policy domain's organisation, by volume, at most SPF_MAX_DOMAINS = 10;
                                                   // a domain of another organisation a report names is never looked up (a crafted report picks no names)
export async function loadSpfContext(domain, { dns, signal, noCache }) -> { domain, status: 'ok'|'none'|'failed'|'multiple', record, tree, mxAddresses, error, at }
  // spfLookupCount (§5.15) + the addresses of its mx hosts (≤ 10); names and types to the DoH resolvers only; a lookup with no answer is 'failed', never "no SPF";
  // noCache: every query past the client's cache ("Check again"); rejects only with an AbortError
export function classifySources(agg, { spf: Map<domain, SpfContext>, index /* inventory.buildIpIndex */ }) -> Array<SourceRow & { cls, reason, detail, servers, spfNow, spfDomain,
  spfListed /* a permerror's strict: false verdict */, atRisk /* messages that passed through SPF alone while spfNow is a permerror */, fixes }>
export function dmarcOverview(agg, rows, { spfChecked }) -> { domain, messages, pass, fail, compliance /* null without mail */, byClass, verdict,
  enforced /* p=reject at 100 %, not t=y: what fails is refused now */, blockers, blocked,
  atRisk, atRiskMessages, spfError /* { domain, reason, sources }|null */, unknown, unknownFail, notes }
export function dmarcCsvRows(agg, rows, { serviceOf }) -> object[]   // DMARC_CSV_COLUMNS; serviceOf(row) → §5.93 identifySource's { service, type, via, confidence } fills the
                                                   // service, service_type, service_via and service_confidence columns (empty without it)
export const SOURCE_CLASSES = ['yours','third-party','forwarder','unknown'], CLASS_REASONS, FIX_CODES = ['spf-permerror','dkim-sign','dkim-align','dkim-fix','spf-add','spf-align'],
  DMARC_VERDICTS = ['no-mail','enforced','ready','fix-first','spf-broken'],
  DMARC_NOTES = ['short-range','pct','testing','mixed-policy','spf-unknown','spf-permerror','quarantine','rejected-now','spf-all'], DISPOSITIONS = ['none','pass','quarantine','reject'],
  FORWARD_OVERRIDES = ['forwarded','mailing_list','trusted_forwarder'], REPORT_PROBLEMS /* ZIP_ERRORS + not-report, xml, not-dmarc, incomplete, not-json, not-tlsrpt, empty */,
  DMARC_CSV_COLUMNS /* … servers, service, service_type, service_via, service_confidence, messages, …, disposition_none, disposition_pass, …, spf_now, spf_now_term, spf_now_reason, … */,
  SHORT_RANGE_DAYS = 7, MAX_REPORT_FILES = 2000, READ_YIELD_MS = 50,
  MAX_DROP_BYTES = 1 GiB, XML_LIMITS
```
**Classes**, in order: an address of the server list is **yours** (`inventory`); one the current SPF authorizes (`spfEvaluate` for each domain of `spfDomainsFor`, the first pass wins) is **yours** when the deciding term is the domain's own (`spf`: an ip4 / ip6 / a / mx term, or an include of its own organisation) and an **authorized third party** through an include (or an a / mx host) of another organisation (`spf-include`, the first foreign domain on the path); when the SPF could not be checked (no context, a failed lookup, `unknown`, several SPF records), an aligned SPF pass in the reports counts as yours (`spf-report`). **A permerror** (a syntax error, more than 10 lookups or 2 void lookups before the address, …) is what receivers get, but it hides whom the record means: the same tree is then asked with `strict: false`, only to tell whose the sender is — **yours** (`spf-listed`) or an **authorized third party** (`include-listed`) when the broken record lists it —; such a known source gets the `spf-permerror` fix first, and `atRisk` counts its mail that passed through SPF alone (no aligned DKIM), which fails from now on. Then an aligned DKIM pass: a **forwarder** when the receiver says so (`forwarded`: an override `forwarded` / `mailing_list` / `trusted_forwarder`, or `local_policy` with `arc=pass`), **yours** when all its mail passed SPF aligned too (`dkim-signed`: forwarding breaks SPF; this happens when the current SPF passes every address or no longer lists it), a **forwarder** when it carries a selector the known senders sign with (`dkim-forwarded`: the original signature survived the relay), an **authorized third party** when SPF passes for a bounce domain of another organisation (`dkim-service`), else a forwarder (`dkim-only`). The rest is **unknown**: `spf-removed` (the reports saw an aligned SPF pass the current SPF no longer gives), `foreign` (it authenticates only as another domain), `none`. **Fixes** (a known source that fails DMARC, or has mail at risk), `spf-permerror` first when the current SPF gives it a permerror (the record, not the sender, breaks SPF), then the most robust first: no DKIM result for the organisation → `dkim-sign` (`dkim-align` when it signs as another domain), a signature that does not verify → `dkim-fix`; the organisation's SPF not passing (and not authorizing it now) → `spf-add`, SPF passing only for another domain → `spf-align`. **Verdict:** `no-mail`; with blockers (yours and third parties that fail, most failing messages first) `enforced` when `p=reject` is in force at 100 % and not in DMARCbis test mode (`t=y`) — mail refused now — else `fix-first`; `spf-broken` when none fails but known sources passed through SPF alone and the current SPF gives them a permerror (`atRisk`; with `enforced`, that mail is refused now); else `enforced` or `ready` (only unknown senders would be turned away). **Notes:** the reports span < 7 days, pct < 100, test mode (`t=y`: receivers apply the next lower policy), the policy changed in the period, SPF not checked, the current SPF gives a permerror (`spfError`: its domain, the reason of the most mail and how many sources), `p=quarantine` and ready (next: reject), known sources already rejected, an SPF record that passes every address (`+all`, or a /0 range of the address's family such as `ip4:0.0.0.0/0`: such a pass never classifies a source).

### 5.60 `lib/tlsrpt.js` — SMTP TLS reports (RFC 8460)
```js
export function parseTlsReport(textOrObject, { file }) -> { ok: true, report } | { ok: false, code: 'not-json'|'not-tlsrpt'|'incomplete', detail }
TlsReport = { kind: 'tlsrpt', key /* org|report-id */, file, org, contact, reportId, begin, end, success, failure,
  policies: [{ type /* 'sts'|'tlsa'|'no-policy-found' */, domain, strings /* policy-string */, mode /* an MTA-STS mode: line */, mx /* mx-host or the draft's mx-host-pattern */, success, failure,
    failures: [{ type /* lowercased */, known, sendingIp, mx, helo, receivingIp, sessions, reason /* failure-reason-code */, info /* additional-information */ }] }] }
export function summarizeTls(reports) -> { domains: [{ domain, reports, begin, end, success, failure, rate /* null without sessions */, orgs, policies /* by type and mode */,
  byType: [{ type, known, sessions, mx, orgs, receivingIps, reasons }], byMx: [{ mx, sessions, types }], failures /* TLS_CSV_COLUMNS rows */ }], duplicates }
export function tlsAdvice(type) -> { type /* 'other' for one RFC 8460 does not define */, area: 'starttls'|'certificate'|'dane'|'sts-policy'|'other', tools: Array<'health'|'tlsa'|'cert'> }
export function tlsCsvRows(summary) -> object[]
export const TLS_RESULT_TYPES /* the 11 of RFC 8460 §4.3 in its order */, TLS_POLICY_TYPES, TLS_REPORT_ERRORS, TLS_ADVICE_AREAS, TLS_CSV_COLUMNS
```
Counts sent as strings and result types in capitals are read; a report dropped twice counts once.
