The view words the advice (`rpt.tls.advice.<type>`) and links the tools: Domain Health (`#/health?domain=…&run=0`, the MTA-STS card and its policy check), the MX host's TLSA records in DNS Lookup (`_25._tcp.<mx>`, DNSSEC on) and its certificate in the Certificate view (`?host=<mx>&run=0`, then the DANE / TLSA tab).

### 5.61 `lib/zonefetch.js` — a zone read from the DNS provider's API (Zone File › Fetch)
DOM-free; I/O through the injectable `fetchImpl`. Only providers whose API a page can call with an `Authorization` header (§3).
```js
export const ZONE_PROVIDERS = [{ id: 'desec', name, api: 'https://desec.io/api/v1', format: 'desec-api', scheme: 'Token', tokenUrl, docsUrl },
  { id: 'digitalocean', name, api: 'https://api.digitalocean.com/v2', format: 'digitalocean-api', scheme: 'Bearer', tokenUrl, docsUrl }]   // the links are opened, never fetched
export const ZONE_FETCH_ERRORS = ['provider', 'domain', 'token', 'auth', 'forbidden', 'not-found', 'rate-limited', 'http', 'network', 'timeout', 'response']
export const DESEC_TYPES /* deSEC's manageable types, the common ones first */, MAX_RECORDS = 20000, DO_PAGE_SIZE = 200, MAX_WAIT_MS = 60000, DEFAULT_WAIT_MS = 20000
export class ZoneFetchError extends Error { code /* ZONE_FETCH_ERRORS */, params: { status?, detail? /* the provider's text, plain, ≤ 200 chars */, retryAfterS? } }   // never holds the token
export function getZoneProvider(id) ; export function cleanToken(token) -> string|null /* trimmed, 16–512 printable ASCII, no white space */ ; export function zoneName(domain) -> string|null
export function retryAfterMs(res) ; export function desecTotal(body) -> number|null   // "Pagination required … (N total)"
export async function fetchZone(providerId, domain, token, { fetchImpl, signal, onProgress, timeoutMs = 20000, sleepImpl } = {})
  -> { provider, domain, format, text /* the provider's JSON documents, one per line, for parseZone */, requests, records, total, partial, byType }
```
- The token is a parameter of one `fetchZone` call: sent only to the provider's API host in `Authorization` (never in a URL), never stored, logged, returned or put in an error. Requests: `credentials: 'omit'`, `referrerPolicy: 'no-referrer'`, `cache: 'no-store'`, `redirect: 'error'` (a redirect would carry the header elsewhere).
- deSEC: `/domains/{zone}/rrsets/`; over 500 RRsets (a 400 with the total) it reads `?type=` by `DESEC_TYPES` until the total is in, a type over 500 by its first page (`&cursor=`): the listing is then partial and zoneparse says so. DigitalOcean: `/domains/{zone}/records?per_page=200&page=N` until `meta.total` (or no `links.pages.next`), merged into one listing.
- Requests 150 ms (deSEC) / 100 ms (DigitalOcean) apart. A 429 waits for a readable `Retry-After` — neither provider exposes it to a page —, else deSEC's "Expected available in N seconds", else 20 s; past 60 s or a fourth 429 it fails `rate-limited`. 401 → `auth`, 403 → `forbidden` (DigitalOcean: no `domain:read` scope; deSEC: a login token that needs MFA), 404 → `not-found`, any other status → `http`, a body that is not a listing → `response`, transport → `network` / `timeout`; cancellation stays an AbortError.

### 5.62 `lib/dohjson.js` — the JSON form of DNS-over-HTTPS (AliDNS)
DOM-free, no I/O; loaded by lib/doh.js with the first question to a `format: 'json'` resolver (§5.8, §5.9).
```js
export const DNS_JSON = 'application/dns-json'
export function ecsSubnet(ecs /* 'a.b.c.d/24' | { subnet } | { address, sourcePrefix } */) -> string|null   // IPv4 host bits zeroed; a bare address → its /24 (IPv6 /56)
export function dnsJsonUrl(base, { name, type, ecs }) -> string   // ?name=<encoded>&type=<number>[&edns_client_subnet=<subnet>]; unknown type → DnsWireError
export function decodeDnsJson(json) -> message   // the shape lib/dnswire.js decodeMessage returns; not a DNS JSON answer → DnsWireError
```
Each record's presentation text (A, AAAA, NS, CNAME, PTR, DNAME, MX, TXT / SPF with `\DDD` escapes and several strings, SOA, SRV, CAA, DS, DNSKEY, TLSA — also as AliDNS's bare RDATA hex —, SSHFP, SVCB / HTTPS, NAPTR, HINFO, URI, RFC 3597 `\# n hex`) becomes dnswire `data`, is encoded and decoded again, so its `text` is exactly what a wire answer of the same record gives and Global DNS groups JSON and wire answers together; a record it cannot read keeps its presentation text as `data` and `text`. An echoed `edns_client_subnet` becomes `edns.ecs` with `scopePrefix: null`; no NSID, no EDE. Fixtures: `tests/fixtures/dns-json/alidns.json` (captured 2026-10-02, scrubbed).

### 5.63 `lib/portfolio.js` — the Domain portfolio: many domains, one row each
DOM-free; the view (§6) and the runner's `audit` (§9). Every network call takes the injected DohClient (through §5.46 `passportDns`: each question once per domain) or `fetchImpl`, and the caller's signal; only an abort rejects.
```js
export const PORTFOLIO_MAX_DOMAINS = 300, PORTFOLIO_CONCURRENCY = 4 /* domains' DNS questions at once */, RDAP_CONCURRENCY = 4 /* requests in flight */
                                                   // (to registry servers); a row's RDAP — its own, its name servers' domains' — is waited for outside its domain's place, and a lookup
                                                   // waiting for its registry's turn or 429 holds no request's place: a registry that turns requests away never slows another
export const PORTFOLIO_DKIM_SELECTORS = ['google', 'selector1', 'selector2', 'default', 'k1', 's1', 'dkim', 'mail']   // and one random label first: a
                                                   // `*._domainkey` wildcard (often "v=DKIM1; p=" of a domain that sends nothing) answers every selector, so its record is no key
export const PORTFOLIO_LOOKUPS = ['rdap', 'ns', 'ds', 'dnskey', 'caa', 'mx', 'txt', 'dmarc', 'spf', 'dkim', 'mtaSts', 'tlsRpt'], LOOKUP_SOURCES /* rdap → 'rdap', the rest 'doh' */
export const PORTFOLIO_CELLS = ['expiry', 'status', 'registrar', 'dnssec', 'ns', 'caa', 'spf', 'dmarc', 'dkim', 'mtaSts', 'parked'], CELL_LOOKUPS /* a column's lookups */
export const CRITICAL_STATUSES = ['serverHold', 'clientHold', 'redemptionPeriod', 'pendingDelete'], EXPORT_COLUMNS
export function parsePortfolioInput(text, { max }) -> { domains /* registrable (§5.46 passportDomain), in order, once */, reduced: [{ input, domain }], invalid, capped }
export function statusRisk(statuses) -> { flags, critical, transferLock: boolean|null, registryLock: boolean|null, lockLevel: string|null, serverLocks: string[],
  transferCodes: string[], risk: 'critical'|'pending-transfer'|'hijack'|'ok'|null }   // RFC 8056 and EPP spellings. transferLock: any transfer prohibition — the
  // registrar's (clientTransferProhibited), the registry's (serverTransferProhibited: RFC 5731, transfer requests MUST be rejected) or RFC 9083's plain
  // "transfer prohibited" —, as Domain overview and Domain Health read it; registryLock: server transfer, update and delete prohibited, all three (one or two
  // of them is no registry lock: serverTransferProhibited alone is also a dispute's or the 60-day lock after a transfer); lockLevel: lockLevel(statuses);
  // serverLocks: 'server transfer prohibited', 'server update prohibited', 'server delete prohibited' as far as set; transferCodes: the statuses that prohibit it;
  // risk 'hijack' only with no transfer prohibition at all, 'pending-transfer' a transfer under way (no critical status). Every status (the flags, the
  // codes, the facts' `statuses`) is said in its RDAP spelling (RFC 8056 / RFC 9083: 'client transfer prohibited'), each once: EPP's
  // 'clientTransferProhibited' arrives lower-cased from §5.14
export const LOCK_LEVELS = ['none', 'registrar-transfer', 'registrar-full', 'registry-partial', 'registry']   // weakest first: what policy `lock.level` orders
  // (any server prohibition outranks the registrar's lock: registry-partial, serverTransferProhibited alone too, ranks above registrar-full)
export function lockLevel(statuses) -> 'none'|'registrar-transfer'|'registrar-full'|'registry-partial'|'registry'   // 'registry': server transfer, update
  // and delete prohibited; 'registry-partial': some server prohibition, not all three; 'registrar-full': client transfer, update and delete prohibited;
  // 'registrar-transfer': client transfer prohibited without both of the others; 'none': no transfer prohibition at all, whatever else is set (a server
  // delete prohibition alone leaves the domain transferable). RFC 8056 spellings with spaces and EPP camelCase, any case; RFC 9083's plain prohibitions
  // ("transfer prohibited") count as the registrar's: who set them is not said
export function nsProviders(hosts, { domain }) -> { count, providers: [{ id, name, known, hosts }] }   // one name under several public suffixes is one
  // provider (DNS platforms spread their name servers over TLDs on purpose): the hosts under the zone itself and under its name at another suffix
  // (example.com's ns2.example.net, a company's own name servers) as one ('self', named by the zone); a known host by §5.46 dnsProviderOf (Route 53's
  // awsdns hosts, CSC's cscdns / cscudns, Com Laude's comlaude-dns under four TLDs: one each), a host under the same name as one of its hosts at
  // another suffix with it; any other host by its registrable domain's name before the public suffix (id 'domain:<name>', named by its domains:
  // 'example.net / example.org'); in the order of the sorted hosts. Two or more: CSC's DNS redundancy
export function nsDomainsOf(hosts, domain) -> [{ domain, hosts, own }]   // a zone's name servers by registrable domain, its own first
export async function runPortfolioLookup(id, domain, { dns, fetchImpl, signal, raw, rdapFor, dkim, noCache })
export function createPortfolio({ domains, dns, fetchImpl, dkim = true, concurrency, rdapConcurrency, rdapOptions, onEvent, lookups = PORTFOLIO_LOOKUPS, nsDomains = true }) -> run
  // lookups: the lookups a row runs (the runner's `watch`: rdap, ns, ds and dnskey; run.pending and run.retry keep to them); nsDomains false: the name
  // servers' own domains are not looked up in RDAP
  // run.start({ signal }): rejects with an AbortError on a stop — the rows not finished are 'stopped', what landed stays; run.retry(domain, lookups, { signal }): those lookups
  // again past the DNS cache (RDAP too when listed); run.retryRdap(domain): a domain's RDAP again, a name server domain's too (every row reading it is told);
  // run.domains(), row(domain), facts(domain, { now }), allFacts, pending(domain), affectedBy(domain) /* the rows reading a domain's RDAP */; events: { type: 'lookup', domain, lookup },
  // { type: 'rdap', domain }, { type: 'row', domain, state: 'running'|'done'|'stopped' }
export function portfolioFacts(raw, { now, rdap /* the run's RDAP results */, dkim }) -> facts   // pure: codes and values, never text
export function cellFailures(facts, column) -> [{ lookup, status /* §5.36 */, nsDomain? }]   // what a column's "⚠ n/a" says and its Retry asks
export function rowRisk(facts) -> 'critical'|'ns-unregistered'|'pending-transfer'|'expired'|'expiring'|'ns-expiring'|'hijack'|'warn'|'ok'|null   // the first that
                                                   // applies, worst first: a name server domain nobody has registered is as urgent as a critical status
export function unregisteredNsDomains(facts) -> string[]   // the name server domains the registry answers 404 for (not the own ones)
export function expiryBand(daysLeft)               // Domain Health's bands: < 0, < 30, < 60
export function expiryEvents(factsList) -> [{ domain, expires, daysLeft, registrar, portfolio, nsOf }]   // one per domain, the name servers' domains too, soonest first
export function expiryUid(domain) -> 'expiry-<domain>@domainscope' ; exportRow(facts) ; portfolioSummaryFacts(factsList, { at, stopped, notLooked, audit })
                                                   // exportRow's dmarc: 'p=none' | 'p=quarantine' | 'p=reject' | 'missing' | 'invalid' (p=none and no record never alike);
                                                   // its statuses: comma-separated (a status has spaces); registrarClass, lockLevel, nsProviders (the count)
                                                   // portfolioSummaryFacts -> { …, nsUnregistered: [{ domain, of }], pendingTransfer: string[], dnssec: { validated, signed, broken, unsigned },
                                                   //   changed: [{ domain, at, tone, changes: [{ code, item }] }] /* opts.changed, the bad ones first: §5.96 */ }
```
- **Registration:** §5.14 `rdapDomain`: the registry's server from the IANA bootstrap, rdap.org only as its paced fallback. RDAP is asked once per distinct domain of a run — a portfolio domain and a name server domain alike (`rdapFor`, at most `RDAP_CONCURRENCY` in flight; a Retry of the NS answer never asks a known one again) — so a provider shared by every zone is asked once. `registration.state`: `ok` (expires, daysLeft and its band, the registrar, the statuses read for risk — a critical status `critical`, a pending transfer `pending-transfer`, no transfer prohibition at all `hijack` (any of clientTransferProhibited, serverTransferProhibited or a plain "transfer prohibited" locks; serverTransferProhibited is also the registry lock) —, the delegation's signed flag), `unsupported` (a TLD without RDAP; `whois` = §5.46 `registryWhois`: the registry's web WHOIS for .tr, .de, .jp, .ch, else the TLD's IANA page), `not-found` (the registry answers 404: not registered), `invalid`, `failed` (its §5.36 status) or `pending`.
- **Lock depth and registrar class:** `registration.lockLevel`, `registryLock` and `serverLocks` (statusRisk) and `registrarClass` (§5.92 `registrarClass` of RDAP's IANA Registrar ID: corporate, retail, or unknown without one or with a reserved one), never by the name the registrar writes.
- **What the registration watch compares** (§5.96): `registration.nameservers` (the name servers the registry delegates to, RDAP, canonical and sorted) and `dnssec.ds` (each DS record of the DS answer as `{ keyTag, algorithm, digestType }`, once, sorted; `[]` when unsigned).
- **Name servers:** their registrable domains (`own` when under the domain itself: they expire with it) with each one's registration from the run's RDAP and `minDaysLeft`, and their DNS providers (`ns.providers`, `nsProviders`; null until the NS answer landed). A name server domain the registry answers 404 for (`not-found`) is not registered: anyone can register it and answer DNS for every zone on those name servers — `unregisteredNsDomains`, the row's risk `ns-unregistered`, an answer and never a failed lookup. A row is done once its name servers' domains are read too.
- **DNSSEC:** DS at the parent (`unsigned` without one), `validated` when the DNSKEY answer carries AD, `failing` when the DNSKEY answer is an error rcode next to a DS (broken: validating resolvers refuse the domain; counted as `broken`, never as signed). **CAA** (§5.15 findCaa through §5.46 certsCard): its state, issuers and wildcard issuers. **Mail** (§5.46 mailCard): MX (`null` / `none` / `some`), SPF (one record, its `all`, the lookup count of §5.15 spfLookupCount once the TXT answer landed: `over` past 10, `partial` when a lookup in its tree failed), DMARC (policy, pct), DKIM (the selectors with a key, revoked ones, a wildcard; `off` when not asked, never "none"), MTA-STS (`v=STSv1` with an id) and TLS-RPT (`v=TLSRPTv1` with a rua): `present` / `none` / `invalid`. **Parked:** a domain without MX, or with a null MX, should say it takes no mail — null MX, `-all`, `p=reject` (`complete` true / false, or null while a part is not known).
- A lookup that failed is a §5.36 status on its part (`failure`), never "none"; `cellFailures` lists them per column (the name servers column its name server domains whose RDAP failed too, `nsDomain`).
- The run is the view's page-session state (§6 7c): a language switch or a visit elsewhere shows it again as it is, so nothing is rebuilt from a copy.
- Tests: `tests/js/portfolio.test.js` (the list, statuses read for risk, the lock depth as a truth table in both spellings, the DNS providers, the registrar class in the facts, the name server domains deduped, a run over a fake DoH and RDAP registry — a stop, a Retry past the cache, DKIM off —, the facts, the calendar dates, the exports, and no dead API: every export is read and every method of a run called by the view or the runner).

### 5.64 `lib/policy.js` — a domain policy and its audit
Pure (no DOM, network, storage or clock beyond the facts); the view's policy tab and the runner's `audit` (§9).
```js
export const POLICY_VERSION = 1, POLICY_MAX_CHARS = 16384, POLICY_MAX_RULES = 40, POLICY_OPS = ['>=', '<=', '>', '<', '==', '!=']
export const POLICY_STATUSES = ['pass', 'fail', 'unknown', 'waived'], POLICY_ERRORS = ['not-json', 'not-object', 'too-large', 'too-many', 'unknown-rule', 'outside-rules', 'bad-value', 'empty']
export const POLICY_RULES = [{ id, kind: 'number'|'ordered'|'bool'|'enum'|'list', op?, min?, max?, levels?, values?, area, example, health /* Domain Health check ids */ }]
  // expiryDays (number, >=) · transferLock (bool: any transfer prohibition, the registrar's or the registry's) · lock.level (ordered over §5.63 LOCK_LEVELS: none <
  // registrar-transfer < registrar-full < registry-partial < registry; any server prohibition outranks the registrar's lock, so registry-partial —
  // serverTransferProhibited alone too, a dispute's or the 60-day lock after a transfer, with updates and deletion not locked — passes >= registrar-full
  // (the rule's name says so; registryLock asks for all three server prohibitions); a partial lock's evidence names its server prohibitions) · registryLock (bool: server transfer,
  // update and delete prohibited, all three) · status.critical (bool) · registrar (list: a part of the RDAP registrar's name) · registrar.class (enum: corporate — by
  // the IANA ID, §5.92; retail fails, no ID or a reserved one is not known) · nsExpiryDays (number, >=; the name servers' other domains: in-bailiwick ones expire with the
  // domain, which expiryDays reads, so only those pass it; one the registry does not know fails it — anyone can register it and take over DNS) · ns.providers (number,
  // >=: the DNS providers of §5.63 nsProviders, named in the evidence) · dnssec (ordered: unsigned < signed < validated; DS whose
  // keys cannot be validated fails every requirement: broken) · caa (enum: present —
  // deny-all counts — | deny-all) · caa.issuers (list: the only CAs CAA may allow) · spf (enum: valid) · spf.lookups (number, <=) · spf.all (ordered: +all < ?all < ~all <
  // -all; no "all" reads as ?all) · dmarc.policy (ordered: none < quarantine < reject) · dkim · mtaSts · tlsRpt · mx.null (bool)
export const POLICY_PRESETS = { baseline, 'strict-mail', parked /* the change request's "Lock down a parked domain": null MX, -all, p=reject, CAA deny-all */,
  corporate /* CSC's eight measures (§5.92) and the registrar's full lock at least: lock.level >= registrar-full, registryLock, registrar.class corporate,
  dnssec signed, caa present, ns.providers >= 2, spf valid, dkim, dmarc.policy >= quarantine */ },
  POLICY_PRESET_IDS, POLICY_I18N /* en, tr: rule names, statuses, presets, parse errors, the evidence */
export function parsePolicy(textOrObject) -> { policy: { name, rules: [{ id, kind, op, value }] }|null, errors: [{ code, rule?, value?, detail?, example? }] }
export function policyObject(policy) -> { name, version, rules } ; policyText(policy) /* indented JSON + newline */ ; presetPolicy(id) ; policyRule(id)
export function ruleValueText(entry) ; requirementText(entry) /* ">= 30", "true", a list between semicolons: a registrar's name has commas */
export function evaluatePolicy(policy, facts /* §5.63 */, { waivers /* §5.95 */, now }) -> [{ id, status, actual, evidence: { key, params }, required, was?: 'fail', waiver?: { id, reason, owner, expires }, waiverExpired?: { id, expires } }]
export function auditPortfolio(policy, factsList, { waivers, now }) -> { name, rules: [{ id, required }], rows: [{ domain, cells, pass, fail, unknown, waived }],
  counts: { domains, failing /* a rule failed */, passing /* no rule failed or not known: an accepted one is neither */, unknown /* the rest */, pass, fail, waived, cells } }
export function auditCsv(audit, { t }) /* a row per domain, a column per rule: "FAIL · 20 days left (…)"; "Accepted" a count column only when a cell is waived */ ; auditJson(audit, { t, policy, app, version, at }) ; evidenceText(cell, t) ; waiverText(cell, t)
```
A policy is JSON, flat (`{ "dmarc.policy": ">= quarantine", "dnssec": "signed", "caa": "present", "transferLock": true, "expiryDays": ">= 30" }`) or `{ name, version, rules }` as the editor exports it. A number rule takes a number (its natural operator) or "OP N"; an ordered rule a level (at least it) or "OP level" (`p=reject` and a bare qualifier such as `-` read too); a bool true / false; an enum one of its values (true: the first); a list a string or a list, its entries between semicolons as the editor writes them (a registrar's name has commas; case-free duplicates dropped). An unknown rule, a value its rule does not take, or a key beside a nested `rules` object (`outside-rules`; such keys count toward the 40-rule limit) is an error and that rule is left out — the editor says so, the runner refuses the file —: a typo never passes. A rule whose facts could not be read (a lookup that failed, a TLD without RDAP, DKIM not asked, a lookup not landed yet — "not looked up", never "failed") is `unknown`, never a pass or a fail, its evidence saying why; the registration rules lock.level, registryLock and registrar.class fail for a domain the registry does not know (RDAP 404); a domain that does not exist in DNS fails its DNS rules with that reason; a partial SPF count fails only when it is over already; DS whose keys cannot be validated (an error answer to DNSKEY: broken, validating resolvers refuse the domain) fails every dnssec requirement, while DS whose DNSKEY answer was not read (its lookup failed, or has not landed) is "not known" where signed and validated would differ. The evidence is a key and params in both languages, so the view and the runner word a cell alike; a value from DNS or the registry is a param (a code part in a summary). **Accepted risks** (§5.95, kind `rule`, the domain and the rule id): a failed cell an active waiver accepts is `waived` — neither a pass nor a fail, counted on its own (`waived` per row and in all) —, keeps its evidence, says what it was (`was: 'fail'`) and carries the waiver; a cell that passes or is not known keeps its status and carries the waiver all the same (no longer needed / not known); a failed cell whose waiver is over stays `fail` with `waiverExpired`. The CSV writes `WAIVED · <evidence> · accepted until 2026-12-31 by Ops: …` (`waiverText`; an expired one: "accepted until …, expired: it counts again") and gains the "Accepted" count column when a cell is waived; the JSON carries `was`, `waiver` and `waiverExpired`. Tests: `tests/js/policy.test.js`.

### 5.65 `lib/ics.js` — an expiry calendar (RFC 5545)
```js
export const ICS_FOLD_OCTETS = 75, ICS_ALARM_DAYS = [30, 7], ICS_PRODID = '-//DomainScope//Domain portfolio//EN'
export function buildCalendar(events: [{ uid, date, summary, description?, alarm? }], { now, name /* X-WR-CALNAME */, prodId, alarmDays = ICS_ALARM_DAYS }) -> string   // alarmDays: the reminders in whole days before (the CT watch passes its radar's thresholds, §5.75)
export function icsEscape(value) ; foldIcsLine(line)
export const ICS_EVENT_MINUTES = 15, ICS_ALARM_MINUTES = [15]
export function buildEventCalendar(events: [{ uid, start, end?, summary, description?, alarm?, alarmMinutes? }], { now, name, prodId, minutes = 15, alarmMinutes = [15] }) -> string   // timed events (a cutover's steps, §5.80)
```
CRLF line ends; lines folded at 75 octets of UTF-8, never inside a character (a continuation starts with one space); TEXT values escaped (`\\`, `\;`, `\,`, a line break `\n`; other control characters dropped). One all-day event per entry (`DTSTART;VALUE=DATE` on the date's local day — the day the table shows; a `YYYY-MM-DD` string as written —, `DTEND` the next day, `TRANSP:TRANSPARENT`) with a display alarm 30 and 7 days before. No `METHOD`: a published file, not an iTIP message (METHOD:PUBLISH would need an ORGANIZER, RFC 5546). The caller's UID is stable per subject (§5.63 `expiryUid`: importing a newer file updates the event instead of adding one), `SEQUENCE` grows with the date (a renewal is a later revision), and `DTSTAMP` (`now`) is the only part that differs between two files of the same dates. An entry without a usable date is left out. **Timed events** (`buildEventCalendar`, 2026-10-08: the DNS cutover plan): `DTSTART` / `DTEND` in UTC (`…Z`, the same moment in every calendar's zone), `minutes` long unless an event's own later `end`, a display alarm `alarmMinutes` before each (an event's `alarmMinutes` replaces them, `[]` for none), `SEQUENCE` the minutes from 2000-01-01 to `now` (a file made later is a later revision of the same UIDs, so a changed plan moves its events), the same folding, escaping and no `METHOD`. Pure. Tests: `tests/js/ics.test.js` (a golden file, folding, escaping, the timed events).

### 5.66 `lib/zonediff.js` — two zones compared record set by record set (Zone File › Compare)
Pure, synchronous, DOM-free; nothing is sent or stored. A semantic diff: never a text diff.
```js
export function diffZones(a, b, { ignoreTtl = false, joinTxt = true, ignoreSoa = false, ignoreApexNs = false } = {}) -> {
  a, b /* About */, relative /* the origins differ */, options, rows: DiffRow[],
  counts: { added, removed, changed, same, ignored, total } }      // TypeError for a missing zone or one with a fatal issue
About = { origin, format, dialect, records /* no duplicates */, rrsets, partial /* an incomplete export */, changeBatch: { upserts, deletes /* a count */ }|null,
  guessed /* the origin is a low-confidence guess */, problems: { errors, warnings } /* parse issues, PARTIAL_EXPORT / RECORDS_TRUNCATED not counted again */ }
DiffRow = { key /* '<relative name>|<TYPE>' */, rel, name /* absolute */, type, status /* DIFF_STATUSES */, reasons /* DIFF_REASONS */, notes /* DIFF_NOTES */,
  a: Side|null, b: Side|null, added: string[] /* values only in b */, removed: string[] /* values only in a */ }
Side = { values: string[] /* the record's text, file order; a Route 53 alias "ALIAS <target>." */, ttl /* the lowest */, ttls, proxied: true|false|'mixed'|null, count }
export function recordSets(zone, { joinTxt, ignoreSoa }) -> Map<key, set> ; export function valueKey(record, { origin, joinTxt, ignoreSoa }) -> string
export function canonicalName(name) -> string ; export function relativeName(name, origin) -> '@' | labels | '<absolute>.'
export function diffFilter(row, filter /* DIFF_FILTERS */) -> boolean ; export function hasDifferences(result) -> boolean
export function diffCsv(rows, { redact }) -> string /* lib/export.js toCsv; DIFF_CSV_COLUMNS; values joined ' | ' */ ; export function diffJson(result, rows, { redact }) -> string
export function diffSummaryFacts(result, { max = 5, formatA, formatB }) -> { a, b /* { origin, format, partial, changeBatch, guessed, problems } */, relative, counts,
  options /* the ones on */, differences: [{ status, name, type, reasons }], more }
export const DIFF_STATUSES = ['added', 'removed', 'changed', 'same', 'ignored'], DIFF_REASONS = ['values', 'ttl', 'proxied', 'routing', 'soa-names', 'soa-serial', 'soa-timers'],
  DIFF_NOTES = ['ttl-ignored', 'txt-split', 'soa-ignored', 'soa-one-side', 'apex-ns', 'not-in-batch', 'batch-delete', 'partial', 'other-variants'], DIFF_DEFAULTS, DIFF_OPTIONS,
  DIFF_FILTERS = ['diff', 'added', 'removed', 'changed', 'same', 'ignored', 'all'], DIFF_CSV_COLUMNS
```
- **Matching:** records by owner and type; each record set is a set of values (order, duplicates and the file format do not matter). The first zone is the starting point: `added` only in the second, `removed` only in the first, `changed` in both with other values, a TTL (unless `ignoreTtl`), a Cloudflare proxy flag (only when both sides have flags: a provider without them never differs) or Route 53 / octoDNS routing (the variants, and the values each holds: values swapped between SetIdentifiers is a change of `routing`, a value changed inside a variant one of `values`).
- **Names** relative to each zone's own origin ('@', 'www', '*.apps'; outside the zone absolute with its dot), in RDATA too (a CNAME target, an MX exchange, an SOA's names …), so a copy under another name compares; lowercase, no trailing dot, `\042` = `*` (the parser has done most of it; an escaped dot is never a label boundary).
- **Values** by lib/zoneparse.js `rdataKey` (IPv6 compressed, MX / SRV fields not spacing, CAA tags lowercase) with: the SOA by every field (`ignoreSoa`: its mname and rname only — the serial, the timers and the SOA's own TTL become the note `soa-ignored`; a changed SOA says which of `soa-names` / `soa-serial` / `soa-timers`), a CAA issuer domain in lowercase, TXT by the bytes of its character-strings (lib/zonetext.js `txtBytes`: a byte that is not UTF-8 never equals its Latin-1 look-alike), joined with `joinTxt` (strings split differently, even inside a character: the note `txt-split`), a Route 53 alias by its target, an undecoded value by its whitespace-collapsed text. With `ignoreSoa` an SOA only one side has (a provider's export leaves it out) is `ignored` (note `soa-one-side`).
- **`ignoreApexNs`:** the NS set at the apex is `ignored` (note `apex-ns`): two providers each name their own.
- **A Route 53 change batch** on either side (lib/zoneparse.js `changeBatch`) is changes, not a zone: a set it does not name is `ignored` (note `not-in-batch`), never removed or added; a set its DELETE names is compared as gone (note `batch-delete`). It names routing variants by SetIdentifier: of the other side's set only those variants are compared (note `other-variants` when it has more; a DELETE of a variant it lacks leaves the set `ignored`). **An incomplete export** (`partial`): a set only the other side has, or a changed set's values it lacks, get the note `partial` (they may be in the part that is missing).
- **Record sets** of a zone object are kept per `joinTxt` / `ignoreSoa` in a WeakMap (made again when its records or origin are other ones): toggling the TTL or apex NS option compares again without reading the zones (20,000 against 20,000 records: about 70 ms instead of 350).
- **Rows** in order: the apex first, then by labels from the right, names outside the zone last; per name SOA, NS, A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, then the rest alphabetically.
- **Exports** (`diffCsv`, `diffJson`): the absolute name (a spreadsheet takes `@` for a formula), both TTLs, both sides' values, what was added and removed, the proxy flags, reasons and notes; `redact` maps every value list (the view hides proxied origins unless opted in).

Tests: `tests/js/zonediff.test.js` (the BIND zone of `tests/fixtures/zonediff/` against its move to Route 53 — names in another case, a relative target, a decimal-escaped wildcard, IPv6 spellings, CAA case, MX spacing and TXT chunks equal; a new, a gone and a changed set, TTLs, the SOA and the apex NS found — with every option, both directions, proxy flags, two zone names, routing and swapped variants, TXT bytes, a change batch and an incomplete export on either side, the record sets kept per option, filters, exports and summary facts); `tests/e2e/zone.e2e.mjs` (offline: the Cloudflare sample against the Route 53 sample — the rows the library finds, the options from the keyboard, redacted exports, Copy summary without values, Forget —, a one-change batch named after this zone, an incomplete Cloudflare page, a long owner that wraps, at 320 / 375 px).

### 5.67 `lib/zoneconvert.js` — a zone written for another tool or provider (Zone File › Convert)
Pure, synchronous, DOM-free; nothing is sent or stored. Nothing is dropped silently: a record a target cannot hold is left out (BIND and DNSControl keep it as a comment with the reason) and every such case, and every change of meaning, is a pitfall.
```js
export function convertZone(zone /* with an origin, no fatal issue (TypeError) */, target /* CONVERT_TARGETS (RangeError) */) -> {
  target, text, filename /* the first file's */, mime, written /* records (values) in all files */,
  files: [{ filename /* convertFilename */, text, written }] /* one; several change batches for a Route 53 zone over its quotas (batch-split) */,
  pitfalls: [{ code /* PITFALL_CODES */, severity: 'error'|'warn'|'info', count, names /* relative */,
    params: { target /* TARGET_NAMES */, types?, flags?, tags?, keys? /* lists */, ttl?, max?, records?, zone? } }],
  omitted: [{ id, code }] /* left out or commented out */,
  changed: [{ id, code }] /* written differently: 'cname-apex' (as ALIAS), 'alias-record' (an ANAME as ALIAS), 'proxied-mixed' */ }
export function convertFilename(origin, target, part = 0) -> '<zone>.zone' | '<zone>.route53.json' ('<zone>.route53.<part>.json' for one of several) | '<zone>.yaml' | 'dnsconfig.js'
export function pitfallKey(code, target) -> 'zconv.pit.<code>.<target>' (a code in PITFALL_VARIANTS for that target) | 'zconv.pit.<code>' ; export function pitfallKeys() -> string[]
export function route53Name(name) ; export { route53String, yamlString, octodnsTxt, octodnsTxtValue, octodnsTxtRefused, naturalCompare }
                                                    // the escapes, checks and orders of the formats: lib/zonetext.js's (§5.68; lib/fixes.js uses them too)
export const CONVERT_TARGETS = ['bind', 'route53', 'octodns', 'dnscontrol'], TARGET_NAMES, CONVERT_MIME, TARGET_TYPES, TARGET_BY_HAND, DNSSEC_TYPES,
  PSEUDO_TYPES = ['ALIAS', 'ANAME', 'URLFWD'], OCTODNS_SVC_KEYS, ROUTE53_ROUTING = ['weighted', 'latency', 'failover', 'geolocation', 'multivalue'],
  ROUTE53_BATCH_LIMITS = { records: 1000, chars: 32000, upsert: 2, setValues: 400 }, CAA_COMMON_TAGS, CONVERT_DEFAULT_TTL = 3600, ALIAS_ZONE_PLACEHOLDER, DNSCONTROL_PROVIDER = 'main',
  PITFALL_SEVERITY /* code → { target: severity } */, PITFALL_CODES, PITFALL_VARIANTS
```
- **Record types** (`TARGET_TYPES`, what this module writes; CAA, SRV, TLSA, HTTPS and SVCB everywhere): Route 53 its own list (HTTPS, SVCB, SSHFP and TLSA since 2024; DS, NAPTR, SPF); octoDNS its record types that lib/zoneparse.js reads back (DNAME, DS, NAPTR, SSHFP, HTTPS / SVCB since octoDNS 1.8, URI, OPENPGPKEY, SPF); DNSControl its record functions (DNAME, DS, NAPTR, SSHFP, RP, SMIMEA, OPENPGPKEY). A type the target has but this module cannot write from a file (`TARGET_BY_HAND`: LOC and URLFWD for octoDNS, LOC and DHCID for DNSControl — the parser keeps LOC as text) is `by-hand`, never `unsupported-type`. A provider's ALIAS / ANAME is `ALIAS(…)` in DNSControl at any name and an ALIAS record in octoDNS at the apex (`alias-record`); elsewhere a type no target has.
- **BIND:** RFC 1035 with `$ORIGIN` and `$TTL` (the zone's, else the commonest TTL), the SOA first, owners relative (absolute where a relative name would look like a whole domain name), RDATA as the parser prints it, the Cloudflare flags and routing as lib/zoneparse.js `bindComment` writes them; everything the parser decoded or a server reads as text. TXT from its bytes, every character-string at most 255 bytes (a longer one in the source is split, as RFC 1035 requires); HTTPS / SVCB with tls-supported-groups by number, `key9`, as its wire bytes (dnspython 2.8 and DNSControl 5.3 have no name for it: `svc-key`). Commented out with the reason: a CNAME at the apex, a Route 53 alias, a provider pseudo-type, an unreadable value, a duplicate is written once.
- **Route 53:** `{ Comment, Changes: [{ Action: 'UPSERT', ResourceRecordSet }] }` for `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --change-batch`: one set per name and type (and routing variant of a policy in ROUTE53_ROUTING: SetIdentifier, Weight, Region, Failover, GeoLocation, MultiValueAnswer, HealthCheckId), the lowest TTL of its values, names and RDATA in Route 53's octal escapes, TXT strings from their bytes (at most 255 bytes each) and CAA values by `route53String`, aliases as `AliasTarget` (ALIAS_ZONE_PLACEHOLDER where the source names no hosted zone), tls-supported-groups as `key9`. AWS counts every ResourceRecord (an alias as one) and every character of the Value elements twice for an UPSERT (1,000 and 32,000 a request: 500 and 16,000), so a zone over that is written as several change batches (`files`, `<zone>.route53.1.json` …, `batch-split`), sent one after another: whole record sets in each, filled in order, the aliases last and an alias after any alias it targets (a same-zone alias needs its target first; one set too big for a batch alone is no reason to split); a set no batch takes (over 400 values, or over 16,000 characters of values) is `batch-size` (error). Left out: the SOA and the apex NS (the hosted zone keeps its own), an apex CNAME, DNSSEC records, types Route 53 lacks, names outside the zone.
- **octoDNS:** the zone's YAML (`<zone>.yaml`) as octoDNS 1.22's YamlProvider loads it as written: every mapping in its natural key order (`enforce_order`, the default `order_mode` natural: `naturalCompare` = Python `natsort_keygen()`, runs of digits as whole numbers of any size); a scalar PyYAML would read as a number, a date or a boolean (`0x1f`, `1_000`, `2026-10-02`, `on` …) quoted; `''` for the apex; `value` for one value, `values` for several; a string with a character outside printable ASCII double-quoted with every such character escaped (`\xHH`, `\uHHHH`, `\UHHHHHHHH`: PyYAML refuses C1 controls, U+FFFE and U+FFFF written raw and folds a raw NEL, LS or PS, and octoDNS reads its files in the system code page on Windows — the file is ASCII only); TXT as one text (`octodnsTxtValue`), its raw text with every `;` written `\;` (the provider splits it again), inside one more pair of quotes when it starts with `"` (octoDNS strips the first and last character of such a value as it loads it: `txt-quote-start`); the header says to load the file with `escaped_semicolons: true` (octoDNS warns over the default, deprecated, which becomes false in 2.0, and with false refuses `\;` as "double escaped ;"; `semicolons` lists the TXT values with a `;`); HTTPS / SVCB as `svcpriority`, `targetname`, `svcparams` (lists for mandatory, alpn and the hints, null for a key without a value — also a key written by number whose value is no bytes, `key65001`: octoDNS would write '' as `key65001=`, which no parser reads) with the keys octoDNS has no name for — and `ech`, whose check fails on a valid value in octoDNS 1.8–1.22 — by number, `key<N>`, as their wire bytes in `\DDD` escapes (ech decoded from base64, tls-supported-groups as 16-bit numbers, dohpath as UTF-8: `svc-key`); URI, OPENPGPKEY; `octodns.cloudflare.proxied` (one flag per set) and `auto-ttl`; `octodns.lenient: true` where octoDNS's own checks refuse a record (`txt-lenient`: TXT outside ASCII or a `\` before a `;`; `name-lenient`: SRV / URI not at a `_service._proto` name); an apex CNAME as `type: ALIAS`; a CAA value with a `"` or a `\` flagged (`caa-quote`: octoDNS hands it to a provider between quotes, unescaped). Left out: the SOA, the apex NS, Route 53 aliases, DNSSEC records, types octoDNS lacks, a TXT with `" "` inside (`txt-quote`: octoDNS deletes it as it loads the file), a TXT that is not UTF-8 (`txt-bytes`), a record whose target needs escapes (`escaped-target`: octoDNS refuses the whole file).
- **DNSControl:** `var REG_NONE = NewRegistrar("none"); var DSP_MAIN = NewDnsProvider("main");` then `D("<zone>", REG_NONE, DnsProvider(DSP_MAIN), DefaultTTL(n), A(…), …, END);` — `TTL(n)` where a set differs from the default, `CF_PROXY_ON`, `CAA_CRITICAL`, a TXT value as one string from its UTF-8 text (DNSControl joins a list itself and splits the text again every 255 bytes), HTTPS / SVCB parameters with tls-supported-groups as `key9`, a space inside a value as `\032` (DNSControl splits them at every space, quoted or not) and a key written by number without a value as `key65001=""` (DNSControl refuses the bare key), an apex CNAME as `ALIAS("@", …)`, a Route 53 alias as `R53_ALIAS(name, type, target, R53_ZONE(id)[, R53_EVALUATE_TARGET_HEALTH(true)])`, `DISABLE_REPEATED_DOMAIN_CHECK` on a name that repeats the zone name (`repeated-domain`: DNSControl refuses it otherwise); names relative, strings as JSON literals (U+2028 / U+2029 escaped). Comment lines: a CAA tag DNSControl refuses (anything but CAA_COMMON_TAGS — `dnscontrol check` would refuse the whole file), a record whose target needs escapes (`escaped-target`, the same), a TXT that is not UTF-8 (`txt-bytes`), types it has no function for (SPF, URI …) or `by-hand`. Left out: the SOA, the apex NS, DNSSEC records, names outside the zone.
- **Pitfalls** (severity per target): `cname-apex` (BIND warn, Route 53 error, octoDNS / DNSControl info), `cname-alone` (error everywhere: a CNAME next to other records at its name, or two CNAMEs — every target refuses it; its RRSIG / NSEC may stay), `r53-alias`, `alias-zone-id`, `alias-record`, `proxied` (Route 53 warn: the origin becomes public), `proxied-mixed` (octoDNS), `cname-flatten`, `txt-long` (how each format splits a TXT over 255 bytes), `txt-split` (octoDNS and DNSControl split the text again), `txt-bytes` (octoDNS / DNSControl: not UTF-8), `txt-quote` / `txt-quote-start` / `semicolons` (octoDNS), `caa-flags` (not 0 / 128), `caa-tag` (not in CAA_COMMON_TAGS; DNSControl warn, as a comment), `caa-quote` (octoDNS), `svc-key` (every target: octoDNS its keys by number, the others tls-supported-groups), `txt-lenient`, `name-lenient`, `unsupported-type`, `by-hand`, `unreadable`, `dnssec`, `routing` (variants merged where the target has no place for them; a CNAME, or a set led by an alias, keeps its first and lists the others in `omitted`: two targets never merge), `out-of-zone`, `wildcard-inner`, `escaped-name`, `escaped-target` (octoDNS / DNSControl), `repeated-domain` (DNSControl), `no-soa` (BIND), `soa`, `apex-ns`, `wildcard`, `duplicate`, `ttl-mixed` (the set gets the lowest), `ttl-default`, `batch-split` (Route 53: several change batches), `batch-size` (Route 53 error: a set no change batch takes). They list errors first, then warnings, then notes, each with its record names.
- **Round trip:** the BIND, Route 53 and octoDNS files parse back with lib/zoneparse.js into the same record sets lib/zonediff.js compares (octoDNS with `joinTxt`), and `dnsconfig.js` run against stub DNSControl functions does too (with `joinTxt`), less `omitted`, with `changed` as said, routing merged where flagged. Checked by hand against the tools themselves (2026-10-02, again after the review): every fixture's octoDNS file loads in octoDNS 1.22's YamlProvider, every `dnsconfig.js` passes `dnscontrol check` (5.3.0) and every BIND file loads in dnspython 2.8, but for a source whose own CNAME is not alone (`cname-alone`); on zones of hostile names, values and every record type, the BIND and Route 53 records equal dnspython's reading of the source byte for byte (a zone of 1,200 A and 40 DKIM records as four change batches within the quotas), and octoDNS's and DNSControl's too but for what the notes say (`txt-split`, `txt-bytes`, `txt-quote`, `escaped-target`, `caa-quote`, `caa-tag`, `caa-flags`) and a CAA value outside ASCII, which dnspython itself reads as Latin-1.

Tests: `tests/js/zoneconvert.test.js` — the goldens of `tests/fixtures/zoneconvert/gen-convert-golden.mjs` (a zone with every pitfall, a Cloudflare export, Route 53 JSON with aliases and routing, octoDNS YAML, each in every format with its pitfalls; `--write` after a deliberate change), the round trip of every zone fixture in BIND, Route 53 and octoDNS through the parser, and of `dnsconfig.js` run against stub DNSControl functions, octoDNS's HTTPS / SVCB parameters (by number as wire bytes), key order (digits as numbers past 2^53), quoting and TXT quotes, TXT bytes and 255-byte strings, Route 53's quotas and its several change batches, escaped targets, and each pitfall per target; `tests/e2e/zone.e2e.mjs` (offline: every format of the sample, its notes, the download read back, Copy all; a zone of 600 records as two Route 53 change batches, each downloaded and copied).

### 5.68 `lib/zonetext.js` — the text helpers the zone formats share
Pure, synchronous, DOM-free, no imports. lib/zoneconvert.js writes whole zones with them and lib/fixes.js a change request's entries, so the change request, its check page and "Show the fix" never load the zone converter.
```js
export function charStringBytes(text) -> Uint8Array[]      // a TXT presentation text's character-strings as bytes: quoted or bare, \DDD a byte, \X the character, else UTF-8
export function txtBytes(record) -> Uint8Array[]           // a TXT / SPF record's strings: from its text (exact), else its data as UTF-8
export function joinBytes(list) -> Uint8Array ; export function utf8Text(bytes) -> string|null /* not UTF-8 */ ; export function split255(bytes) -> Uint8Array[]
export function route53String(s | Uint8Array) -> string    // quoted, `"` and `\` escaped, every byte outside printable ASCII as Route 53's octal escape
export function yamlString(s) -> string                    // plain, single-quoted, or double-quoted with every character outside printable ASCII escaped (PyYAML reads it back)
export function octodnsTxt(data) -> string                 // the joined text, every `;` as `\;` and nothing else escaped
export function octodnsTxtValue(data) -> string|null       // octodnsTxt in one more pair of quotes when it starts with one; null with `" "` inside
export function octodnsTxtRefused(escaped) -> boolean      // octoDNS's chunked-value check refuses it (outside ASCII, `\` before `;`): written lenient
export function naturalCompare(a, b) -> number             // octoDNS's natural key order (Python natsort_keygen(), digits as whole numbers of any size)
```
Tests: `tests/js/zonetext.test.js` (YAML escapes read back by the parser's YAML subset, bytes of a presentation text, Route 53 bytes, the octoDNS TXT value); the formats through `tests/js/zoneconvert.test.js` and `tests/js/fixes.test.js`.

### 5.69 `lib/topology.js`, `ui/topology.js` — where TLS really terminates
The inventory's topology keys (§5.5) say where TLS ends: a load balancer and the servers behind it, the backends that never get the certificate, the address an HA pair shares, the public address of a server behind NAT. SSL Targets, its Renewal plan, the Verify pairs, the CSV exports, targets.txt and the CLI (§7) follow them; an inventory without them works exactly as before. `lib/topology.js` is DOM-free and pure; it loads with the scanner (`ENGINE_MODULES`), off the start route. **The guiding rule**: when the inventory and DNS disagree, the tool errs toward "needs the certificate" and says the inventory looks wrong; it never quietly answers "no certificate needed".
```js
export function terminatesTls(server) -> boolean                 // false only for terminates_tls=no
export function topologyTokens(server, cliName = (n) => n) -> string[]   // the keys targets.txt writes after the addresses: terminates_tls=no, backends=…
                                                                 // (each as the CLI names it), vip=…, nat=… (ports= is already the ip:port tokens)
export function inventoryTopology(servers) -> { any, lbs: [{ server, backends: Server[] }], backendOf: Map<Server, Server[]>,
                                                vips: [{ ip, servers: Server[], plain: Server[] /* its holders saying terminates_tls=no */ }],
                                                nats: [{ ip, server }], plain: Server[] /* terminates_tls=no */, ported: Server[] /* with ports= */,
                                                nowhere: Set<Server> /* passthrough load balancers with no server terminating TLS behind */ }
  // any: the inventory has a topology key at all (false: nothing changes anywhere)
export function applyTopology(groups, servers) -> groups   // §5.12: the backends a reached load balancer forwards to (entries with `lbs`); `topology` on the groups it
                                                           // concerns; each group's entries are indexed by name and address (a VIP pair's thousands of names)
GroupTopology = { terminatesTls, backends: [{ id, name, terminatesTls }], behind: string[] /* the load balancers of the scan it was reached through */,
  vips: [{ ip, servers: string[] /* every holder of a VIP a name answered with */, plain: string[] /* those saying terminates_tls=no */ }],
  nats: [{ ip, addresses: string[] /* its own */ }], tlsPorts: number[],
  suspect: boolean /* the inventory and DNS disagree: it gets the certificate (§5.12) */, nowhere: string[] /* covered names sent here that terminate nowhere */ }
export function orderByLoadBalancer(groups) -> groups      // each load balancer (a VIP pair together) followed by what is behind it; the rest stays in order
export function rankServerGroups(groups) -> groups         // a scan's order: needsCert, then maybeNeedsCert, then name (numeric) and id, then
                                                           // orderByLoadBalancer (lib/scanner.js; lib/originnow.js after the origin map changed a group)
export function topologyNotes(t) -> string[]               // the English CSV text: 'load balancer for web01, web02', 'behind lb01, lb02 (plain HTTP, no certificate)',
                                                           // 'behind lb01 (re-encrypts)', 'VIP 203.0.113.50 (lb01, lb02)', 'NAT 203.0.113.10 -> 10.0.0.30', 'TLS ports 443,8443';
                                                           // a suspect group: 'terminates_tls=no, yet DNS points here directly (check the inventory)', never 'no certificate'
export const TOPOLOGY_CSV_COLUMN                           // { key: 'topology', header: 'Topology', get } over rows carrying a GroupTopology
export function tlsNowhere(groups) -> string[]             // the covered names that terminate TLS nowhere (ScanResult.tlsNowhere)
export function scanTargetsKeys(result, cliName) -> (server) => string[]   // targetsForCli's keys for a scan: topologyTokens, no terminates_tls=no for a suspect server
// ui/topology.js (h() only; styles in assets/css/views/topology.css, injected with SSL Targets and Servers)
export function TopologyNotes(topology) -> HTMLElement|null       // one line per fact, the action first (below)
export function noCertStatus(group) -> 'plain'|'passthrough'|null // terminates_tls=no: plain HTTP, or a load balancer passing TLS through; null when suspect
export function TopologyCard(servers) -> HTMLElement|null         // the Servers view's card; null without a topology key
export function TopologyWarnings(warnings, { href, limit = 5 }) -> HTMLElement|null   // the inventory's TOPOLOGY warnings in SSL Targets (registers inv.warn.TOPOLOGY.*)
```
- A load balancer that terminates TLS gets the certificate (its status says so: "Install the certificate"; its note "Load balancer → web01, web02"). Its backends say "Behind lb01, lb02 — plain HTTP, no certificate needed" (`terminates_tls=no`: status "No certificate needed", not counted as needing it) or "Behind lb01, lb02 — re-encrypts: install here too". A load balancer with `terminates_tls=no` passes TLS through (status "TLS passthrough"): its backends get the certificate.
- **The inventory and DNS disagree.** A `terminates_tls=no` server forwarding to no backend that a covered DNS, remembered (§5.70, `via` `known`) or zone name reaches directly (its own address, a VIP or NAT address it holds), and the server DNS sends a name to that would terminate TLS nowhere, are `suspect`: they need the certificate, stay in the Renewal plan, the work list, Verify, Copy summary and targets.txt (without `terminates_tls=no`, so the CLI scans them), and say "DNS points here directly but the inventory says terminates_tls=no — check the inventory" (behind a load balancer too: "Behind lb01", no claim about the certificate). The run summary adds "N servers of your list say terminates_tls=no, but DNS points at them directly: they are counted as needing the certificate — check the inventory" (`topology-suspect`) and, for names reaching only `terminates_tls=no` servers, "TLS terminates nowhere in your inventory for …" (`topology-nowhere`).
- Every holder of a VIP gets it: "VIP 203.0.113.50 — install on both: lb01 and lb02" ("on all N" for more), and the holders are listed together. Holders that disagree: the card installs only on those that terminate TLS ("install on db01; db02: terminates_tls=no — check the inventory"), a VIP held only by plain servers says so, and a scanned holder saying no gets the note "VIP 203.0.113.70: the inventory says terminates_tls=no for db02 — check it" (DNS reaches every holder, so each needs it). A holder that gets no certificate (a VIP pair of load balancers passing TLS through, status "TLS passthrough") says only who holds it ("VIP 203.0.113.50 — held by lb01, lb02"), with no install note and no contradiction, and the card says "lb01, lb02 pass TLS through (terminates_tls=no) — no certificate". A name answered at a NAT address says "Reached at 203.0.113.10 (NAT) → 10.0.0.30"; for it the Verify tab's CLI card scans the server's own addresses (`cliTargets`). A server's own TLS ports: "TLS ports 443, 8443".
- SSL Targets › Servers (§6): an intro line, the inventory's `TOPOLOGY` warnings (`TopologyWarnings`: they change the grouping; also in step 3 before a run), the notes under each server's name, a backend indented under its load balancer; each name says which load balancers it came through ("Through lb01, lb02" — both of a VIP pair), the details also VIP / NAT. The Servers CSV and the Renewal plan's work list end with a `Topology` column only when a row has a topology.
- The Renewal plan (§5.43): the server cells carry the notes; the servers with `terminates_tls=no` that are not suspect are in no row but listed under the matrix ("1 server the names reach needs no certificate"), and the renewal line does not count them.
- The Servers view (§6): the card shows each load balancer with its backends as a tree (a short badge — "re-encrypts", "plain HTTP" — and what it means after it, wrapping on a phone, never cut), "TLS terminates nowhere behind it" under a passthrough load balancer whose backends all say no, the VIPs with their holders, the NAT pairs, the servers outside a load balancer that never get the certificate and the servers with their own TLS ports (each section's key as written, never upper-cased or broken).
- targets.txt (the Servers view, SSL Targets) writes the keys the CLI reads (`topologyTokens`, `scanTargetsKeys`; `ports=` as ip:port tokens).

Tests: `tests/js/topology.test.js` (a scan through an emulated DoH zone: the matches through the VIP and the NAT address, the backend groups, `lbs`, the order, the inventory and DNS disagreeing, VIP holders that disagree, backends that loop, the Renewal plan and its work list, the Servers CSV, the Verify pairs, targets.txt read back by the CLI's test, a timing guard: a VIP pair with 40 backends and 5000 names well under a second), `tests/js/inventory.test.js` (the keys in every format, the shared fixture), `tests/js/ui-dom.test.js` (Turkish wording, `TopologyWarnings`), the topology group of `tests/e2e/scan.e2e.mjs` (§8).

### 5.70 `lib/originmap.js`, `lib/originfill.js` — the origin map: which server and port really serves a proxied name
A proxied name's origin is found once — by a CLI sweep, a zone file, a Verify check of a zone file's origin, an old / new server comparison — and is then remembered in the workspace (the part `origins`, §5.39), opt-in; Verify checks the remembered ones again. DOM-free and pure (no storage, no network; callers pass `at`, and `now` — the real clock when absent — caps every date). `lib/originmap.js` is the model and how it is read, small enough for the start route (the workspace store sanitizes the part with it); `lib/originfill.js` how it is written and what each source observes (loaded by the views that write).
```js
OriginMap = { v: 1, remember: boolean /* "Remember origins in this workspace", off by default */, entries: OriginEntry[] /* by name, active first, newest first */,
  refuted?: OriginEntry[] /* stale only: what a CLI report or Verify ruled out where the name had no entry (merge rules); capped like the entries, shown nowhere */ }
OriginEntry = { name /* `*.x` allowed */, ip /* canonical */, port /* 1–65535 */, source: ORIGIN_SOURCES, firstSeen, lastConfirmed /* ISO */, server: string|null /* an inventory name */,
  stale: null | { reason: STALE_REASONS, at, ip?, port? /* where the name was found instead */ } }
// lib/originmap.js
export const ORIGIN_SOURCES = ['cli-json', 'zone', 'verify', 'compare', 'manual'], STALE_REASONS = ['cli-elsewhere', 'cli-not-hosted', 'verify-elsewhere', 'verify-not-hosted', 'zone-other'],
  ORIGIN_MAP_LIMITS = { entries: 2000, perName: 16, server: 80 }, ORIGIN_DEFAULT_PORT = 443
export function sanitizeOriginMap(value, { now }?) -> OriginMap | null   // every entry checked (normalizeHostname, normalizeIP, port, dates, source, server name, stale reason), one per name|ip|port
                                                              // (the latest confirmation), capped per name and in all (active, then recent, kept first); `refuted` the same, stale ones only;
                                                              // null while off with no entry
export function originIndex(map) -> { map, byName }             // sanitized once, entries by name: what a render reads (an index passes through)
export function originsFor(mapOrIndex, name) -> OriginEntry[] // its own entries and a `*.parent` one covering it (not where it has its own entry
                                                              // at the wildcard's address and port), active first
export function knownForScan(mapOrIndex) -> Array<{ name, ip, port, server, source, lastConfirmed, except? }>   // the active entries: lib/scanner.js
                                                              // knownOrigins (§5.12); a wildcard's `except`: names with their own entry at its address and port
export function originWildcard(name) -> '*.parent' | null     // the wildcard that covers a host name
export function rememberedRows(mapOrIndex, name, used) -> Array<{ ip, port, target, entry, stale, used }>   // a proxied host's remembered
                                                              // origins as a result shows them now: the ones the scan used (stale in place), then its other stale entries
export function originName(s), originPort(v) /* '' → 443 */, originKey(e) /* name|ip|port */, originTarget(e) /* ip, ip:port, [v6]:port */,
  originTime(v, nowMs?) /* an ISO time, at most nowMs */, originServer(v), originNow(now) /* ms; the real clock when absent */
// lib/originfill.js
export function applyObservations(map, observations, { source, at, now, proxied, serverOf }) -> { map, off, added, confirmed, staled /* keys the map kept: counted after the caps; one added stale counts as added only */, skipped /* names */ }
  // observations: [{ name, ip, port /* null: the address (a zone file names no port) */, outcome: 'hosted'|'not-hosted'|'unknown' /* asked, no answer */, server? }]
export function addManualOrigin(map, { name, ip, port, server }, { at, now, replace /* key */, serverOf }) -> { map, error: null|'off'|'name'|'ip'|'port'|'limit', key }
export function removeOrigins(map, keys) -> map ; setRemember(map, on) -> map
export function zoneObservations(proxiedOriginMapRows) ; cliReportObservations(doc) -> { observations, at, originCertNames } ; readCliReports(files) -> { reports /* oldest first, undated last */, errors }
export function verifyObservations(verifyRows) ; compareObservations(compareResult) ; outcomeOf(status) ; HOSTED_STATUSES = ['UPDATED', 'NEEDS_UPDATE', 'ORIGIN_CERT', 'PRIVATE_CERT'], NOT_HOSTED_STATUS
// lib/originnow.js (2026-10-09) — a finished scan read with the map now (DOM-free; the scan result is never changed)
export function originStaleMark(mapOrIndex, name, ip, port) -> { reason, at, ip?, port? } | null   // rememberedRows' entry at that address and port
export function staleKnownUses(result, mapOrIndex) -> Map<'name|ip|port', mark>   // the origin hints' reasons of kind 'known' the map now marks stale
export function hintsNow(result, mapOrIndex, stale?) -> originHints   // such a reason carries `stale: mark`; the scan's own array when none is
export function serversNow(result, mapOrIndex, stale?) -> servers     // such an entry (`via` known) carries `stale`, and so does one a load balancer passed
                                                                      // on (`lbs`) when every tie of that name there is one; a group keeps needsCert only
                                                                      // with another dns / zone / active known tie, else is maybeNeedsCert with a hint tie;
                                                                      // ranked again (lib/topology.js rankServerGroups, the scanner's order)
export function resultNow(result, mapOrIndex) -> result               // hintsNow + serversNow + stats.needsCert recounted; the result itself when nothing is stale
export function markStaleOrigins(verifyRows, mapOrIndex) -> number    // `originStale` on each row `via` known: the mark, or null
```
Merge rules (`applyObservations`):
- **Off:** with `remember` false nothing is added, confirmed or marked (`off: true`); removing entries always works, and turning it off keeps the entries (still used for hints until deleted).
- **Hosted** confirms the matching entries (`lastConfirmed` and `source` when the run is newer, `firstSeen` when older, a stale mark not newer than the run cleared — a newer one stays, the server name filled in) or adds one — only for a proxied name: one the map already has, or `proxied(name)` (absent: every name); the others are `skipped`. An entry added from a run older than one that ruled its address and port out (`refuted`, below) starts stale with that run's mark, and one added from a run older than a zone file that named the name at other addresses and not at this one starts `zone-other` (with that zone file's time and address; an entry the zone file gave keeps its date when a probe marks it later); the newest of those wins. A zone gives no port: it speaks for the address on 443 — it confirms that entry unless a probe of the port marked it (`cli-*` / `verify-*`: a port-less observation never clears those), or adds one — and leaves an entry on another port as it is.
- **Contradictions** (the CLI JSON, Verify, a zone; never a comparison or a manual entry). The CLI and Verify contradict only what they asked: an entry whose address and port the run asked, and got 'not-hosted' or 'unknown' (TLS_ERROR, TIMEOUT, CLOSED, an error: asked, no answer; PRIVATE_CERT is a covering certificate, so hosted) while it found the name on another address, is `cli-elsewhere` / `verify-elsewhere` (with where it was found; another port of an address it found the name at is the same server); 'not-hosted' with the name found nowhere else is `cli-not-hosted` / `verify-not-hosted`; an entry the run did not ask is left alone (a name may have several origins), and 'unknown' alone says nothing. A zone file names a proxied name's origins: the name's entries at other addresses are `zone-other`. An entry the same run confirmed, or one confirmed at or after the run, is never marked; a stale entry keeps the newest contradiction (an older run's mark never replaces a newer one), and a mark is always newer than `lastConfirmed` (a stored one that is not is dropped). What the CLI or Verify ruled out by these rules for a proxied name with no entry there is kept in `refuted` (an entry-shaped stale record, dated just before the run, the newest per name|ip|port, capped like the entries; never read as an origin and shown nowhere; an entry at that key — a newer finding, a manual save, a wildcard's mask — ends it, and removing every entry forgets them all): an older report imported later then cannot bring the address back. So CLI reports and Verify runs land the same in any order (the tests run every order of three reports, and a seeded search over 400 sets of three, against the date order). A zone file names no port, so it never outweighs a probe of a port; imported out of date order among probe reports it can still land differently (a zone file confirmation newer than an older probe's NOT_HOSTED, say): zone files are best remembered in date order with them.
- **Stale entries** are kept and shown, never a scan's known origin; a later confirmation or a manual save clears the mark. Results on screen read the map as it is now: SSL Targets › Behind CDN and the Subdomains Origins block render again when the part changes (a Verify batch, another tab, a hand-over import, "Delete all local data"), and so do SSL Targets' Servers tab, summary, counts and Verify rows (2026-10-09, `lib/originnow.js`): a remembered origin a scan used that the map has since marked stale reads "Origin map · Stale" with the reason (the Servers tab's host and its details, the Verify row's address line and details, queued after the rows that still count), it no longer makes its server need the certificate nor ranks it first, and the exports say so too — SSL Targets' JSON (`scan.servers[].hosts[].stale`, `scan.originHints[].reasons[].stale`, `stats.needsCert`), Servers CSV (`Needs certificate`), Verify JSON (`rows[].originStale`), targets.txt (left out, as the sweep command leaves it out) and the Subdomains JSON's `origin.hints`. The Renewal plan and the Rollout board keep the scan's own needsCert.
- **Wildcards:** a `*.parent` entry covers every name one label under it (such a name counts as proxied, and 'hosted' at the wildcard's address and port adds nothing of its own). A probe (the CLI, Verify) that contradicts it for one name, by the rules above, after the wildcard was first seen there, masks it for that name only: the name gets its own stale entry at the wildcard's address and port (from that probe, first and last seen when the wildcard was first seen; made when the wildcard arrives later from an older report too, from `refuted`), so `originsFor` and `knownForScan` (`except`) no longer apply the wildcard to that name, while the other names keep it. A zone file's own record for a name masks nothing (both are shown until a probe says otherwise).
- **The clock:** no date is later than now (`originNow`; the callers' `now` in the tests): a run dated in the future (a fast clock, an edited report) counts as now, and a stored or imported date from the future (a hand-over file) is read as now, so nothing is pinned beyond the reach of a later check. An undated report is applied as now, so it is read last.

The sources: **Zone File** › Origins & servers, "Remember these N origins" (every exact address of a proxied name; a host, Tunnel or provider origin is no address); **CLI reports** imported in Servers › Origin map (`readCliReports` reads each with lib/estate.js `readEstateReport`, the Certificate estate's reader; per `sni` / `wildcard` row: UPDATED / NEEDS_UPDATE / ORIGIN_CERT / PRIVATE_CERT (every covering certificate: a self-signed or private-CA one is a Cloudflare "Full" origin or an internal host) hosted, NOT_HOSTED not hosted, TLS_ERROR / TIMEOUT / CLOSED asked without an answer, and a port that did not open — a `connect` row, no name: a server switched off — asked without an answer for every name of the run (`names`, else what its rows probed); a bare-address target names no server; applied oldest report first); a name counts as proxied there when the map has it, the page session's imported zone (`state.session.zone.proxied`) or last scan (`state.session.scanHosts.proxied`) lists it, or a server answered it with a Cloudflare Origin CA certificate — "Also names not known to be behind a CDN" takes every name; **SSL Targets › Verify** at the end of each batch, into the workspace the scan ran in (the checks of exact origins — `via` known or zone: the origin map's own entry, the zone file's origin — of a proxied name with a verdict, an unanswered one included; never a `hint` pair: an SPF / MX / sibling candidate is paired with every proxied name, and answering for one with a covering certificate, a shared wildcard say, does not make a server its origin; the tab says what the batch changed or that remembering is off, and nothing after a batch without such a check); **Retire an IP** › the old and the new server, "Remember <address> as the origin of <name>" when the new server answered with a certificate covering the name and the verdict is neither broken nor unreachable; **by hand** in Servers › Origin map. `ui/origin-map.js recordOrigins(observations, { source, at, proxied })` applies them to the active workspace (inventory server names from `lookupServers`) and saves the part when something changed, a run that only ruled an address out (`refuted`) included. Privacy: the map lives with the workspace in IndexedDB and leaves the browser only inside a hand-over file the user exports (§5.41); "Delete all local data" deletes it with the database. Tests: `tests/js/originmap.test.js` (the model, caps, merge rules, edits, the workspace store, the hand-over file), `tests/js/originfill.test.js` (each source), `tests/js/originnow.test.js` (a result read with the map now), `tests/js/scanner-known.test.js` (§5.12), the offline `origins` E2E suite (§8; SSL Targets › Servers following a stale mark too) and the `verify` one (a Verify row following it).

### 5.71 `lib/reverseip.js`, `ui/reverse-ip-panel.js` — Domains on this IP (reverse IP v2)

Every name tied to an address (or up to `MAX_REVERSE_IPS` = 10), honestly sourced and checked as DNS answers now. The panel lives in IP Intel (§6): no view of its own, loaded on the first "Find domains" (`onceAsync`), its styles in `ip.css`.

- **Sources** (`REVERSE_SOURCES`, the chip order): `workspace` (the view's `workspaceFor(ip)`: the origin map's active entries at the address, as names, and the server list's servers there, named in a note only — server names are never sent), `ptr` (`dns.ptr(ip, { throwOnError: true })`), `hackertarget` and `thc` (lib/ipintel.js `reverseIp` / `reverseIpThc`, with their caches and quotas: the view passes its own ipintel service), `otx`, `robtex`, `internetdb`, and with a key typed in the panel `shodan` and `whoisxml` (`KEYED_SOURCES`). Endpoints and shapes: §3. Each source answers a `SourceResult` `{ source, state: 'ok'|'failed'|'skipped', skip, names: [{ name, first, last }], total, truncated, failure, extra, at }`; `skip` is one of `SKIP_REASONS` (`local`: a private / reserved address, `no-key`, `locked`: InternetDB's lockout, `no-dns`); `failure` is a lib/sourcestatus.js SourceFailure, so `sourceStatus()` words it (§5.36: `STATUS_SOURCES` has every source, `srcst.source.<id>` names it). `extra`: InternetDB's and Shodan's `{ ports, tags, vulns, cpes }`, the workspace's `{ servers }`.
- **What stays here:** `isLocalOnly(ip)` — private (lib/ip.js `isPrivateIP`), or not globally routable (`isGloballyRoutable`) except the documentation ranges (they hold no server, so asking about one reveals nothing; the offline tests use them) — sends nothing at all, not even the PTR question: only `workspace` answers and the panel says so. A name that looks internal (`looksInternal`: a single label, or under .local, .internal, .lan, .corp, .home.arpa, .localhost, .invalid, .test) is status `internal`, and a name only the workspace knows is `workspace`: neither is ever sent to a resolver nor handed to another tool. A key is used for one request per address, appears in no result or message (`redact`), and stays in its password field (never in a snapshot, a link, an export or storage).
- **Limits:** InternetDB is asked one address at a time (`createLimiter(1)`), each address once per session (a 30-minute cache of answers, also for OTX, Robtex, Shodan and WhoisXML; a Retry passes `noCache`), and its first 429 locks it for the `Retry-After` it sends or `INTERNETDB_LOCK_MS` (1 h): until then no request is made (`skip: 'locked'`, "rate limited — try again in N min", no Retry button, a note with the time; `lockedUntil()`). Shodan's API is paced one request a second. OTX gets a 45 s timeout (a busy address is slow), the others 15 s. At most `MAX_NAMES_PER_SOURCE` (5,000) names per source and address.
- **Names:** `normalizeName` — lower case, no trailing dot, punycode, leading `*.` dropped; null for an address written as a name, a reverse-zone name, a single label or an invalid label. `mergeNames(lookups, { previous })` makes one `NameRow` per name `{ name, domain (registrable), ips, sources (source order), first, last, status, resolvesTo, provider, rcode, error }` (earliest first and latest last any source gave), sorted like `sortHostnames`, keeping the check of a previous row of the same name. Times: `seenTime` (ms, Unix seconds, ISO without a zone as UTC; before 1990 or more than a day ahead is null).
- **The check** (`verify(rows, { signal, limit = VERIFY_BATCH, onRow })`, 300 names a batch, eight at a time over the shared DohClient's `resolveHost`; "Check N more names" asks the next batch): `forwardStatus` — `here` (it resolves to an address it was found on: a PTR name so is forward-confirmed), `cdn` (lib/netinfo.js `classifyResolution` says its addresses hide the origin: loaded on the first check, `provider` named), `moved` (other addresses: `resolvesTo` says where), `none` (NXDOMAIN, or NOERROR without an address), `failed` (no usable answer; `rcode`); `unchecked` before, `pending` while asked (`NAME_STATUSES`). Only an abort rejects; names it did not reach stay `unchecked`.
- **Panel:** an address box (canonical, deduplicated, at most 10; "Not an IP address" otherwise), the optional key fields in a disclosure, the privacy line; then a chip per source (count of names, "N of M" when the source holds more, "asking…", "add a key to ask", "not asked (private address)", or "n/a · reason" with a Retry that asks that source again for every address it failed on and then checks the new names; the tooltip carries the status and the quota note `rip.quota.<source>`), the servers and InternetDB's ports, tags and vulnerabilities per address, a "refused the key (HTTP 401 / 403)" note, the DataTable (name — a DNS Lookup link —, status, registrable domain, sources, first / last seen, resolves to, found on; search, filters by status and source, CSV / JSON export: `reverseExportRows`), Check more, and hand-offs (`run=0`, so the next tool sends nothing before a click): Subdomains of each public registrable domain (six at most), SSL Targets for them, Retire this IP (`ips` and `domains`). `onNames(ip, names, state)` gives the view each address's names for its row cell (count and first names, kept in the view's snapshot and JSON export as before); `snapshot()` / `restore()` keep a finished lookup across a language re-mount without a request. `generatedKeys()` lists the keys built from codes (i18n coverage).

Tests: `tests/js/reverseip.test.js` (normalising, the local gate, every parser on the live shapes, merge, forward status, the service with a fake fetch / DohClient / ipintel: nothing sent for a private address, keys never in a result, InternetDB's lock, Retry of the failed sources only, the cache, batches, abort); the offline group of `tests/e2e/ip.e2e.mjs` (§8).

### 5.72 `lib/ipenrich.js`, `ui/ip-enrich-panel.js` — IP Intel's routing enrichment: RPKI, routing sanity, abuse contact, PeeringDB and the CIDR breadcrumb
One public address at a time, from a row's details in IP Intel (§6), only after **Check routing**: the announced prefix and origin AS, the RPKI route-origin validity of prefix + origin (RFC 6811), routing sanity, the abuse contact, the origin's PeeringDB record, and a CIDR breadcrumb with the workspace's servers in each range. `lib/ipenrich.js` is DOM-free and runs in Node 22 (`fetchImpl`, `sleep` and `now` injectable); only an AbortError rejects, and every other failure is an entry of `errors` that lib/sourcestatus.js turns into "⚠ n/a" with its reason (§5.36; `STATUS_SOURCES` has each source).
```js
export const ENRICH_SOURCES = ['ripestat-network', 'ripestat-rpki', 'ripestat-routing', 'ripestat-abuse', 'peeringdb'],
  RPKI_STATUSES = ['valid', 'invalid-asn', 'invalid-length', 'not-found' /* RIPEstat's 'unknown' */], ROUTING_FLAGS = ['not-announced', 'moas', 'more-specifics', 'low-visibility'],
  ENRICH_SKIPS = ['invalid', 'not-routable'], CIDR_BLOCKS = { 4: [8, 16, 24], 6: [32, 48, 64] }, PEERINGDB_TYPES /* PeeringDB label → code */, PEERINGDB_TYPE_CODES,
  PEERINGDB_NET, PEERINGDB_INTERVAL_MS = 4000, PEERINGDB_PAUSE_MS = 10000, PEERINGDB_WAIT_CAP_MS = 15000, MAX_ORIGINS = 4, MAX_MORE_SPECIFICS = 20, LOW_VISIBILITY = 0.5
export function networkInfoUrl(ip), rpkiValidationUrl(asn, prefix), routingStatusUrl(prefix), abuseContactUrl(ip), peeringdbNetUrl(asn)   // RIPEstat ones carry sourceapp=domainscope
export function parseNetworkInfo(json) -> { prefix: string|null, asns: number[] }
export function parseRpkiValidation(json) -> { status, roas: [{ origin, prefix, maxLength, validity }], validator }   // an unknown status is a ParseError
export function parseRoutingStatus(json, { version }?) -> { announced, origins, moreSpecifics /* ≤ 20 */, moreSpecificCount, lessSpecifics, visibility: { seeing, total }|null, firstSeen, flags }
export function parseAbuseContact(json) -> { contacts: string[] /* plausible addresses only */, rir: 'ARIN'|'RIPE NCC'|'APNIC'|'LACNIC'|'AFRINIC'|null }
export function parsePeeringdbNet(json) -> { id, asn, name, aka, website /* http(s) only */, types, scope, policy, irrAsSet } | null /* no record */ ; peeringdbTypeCode(label) -> code|null
export function cidrLevels(ip, prefix?) -> [{ cidr, length, announced, address }]   // broadest first: the fixed blocks, the announced prefix where it falls (merged with a block of
                                                              // its length; ignored when it does not hold the address), the address; an IPv4-mapped address is its IPv4 address
export function serversInLevels(levels, inventoryIndexEntries, ip?) -> levels + { servers: [{ id, name, ips /* inside the level */, here }] }   // the address's own servers first
export function knownFromInfo(ipInfo) -> { prefix, asns, announced } | null   // what IP Intel's row already knows (§5.13)
export function createIpEnrich({ fetchImpl, timeoutMs = 12000, retries = 1, concurrency = 4, now, sleep, peeringdbIntervalMs, routable = isGloballyRoutable }?) -> {
  enrich(ip, { known, signal, noCache }?) -> EnrichResult, retry(prev, { sources, signal }?) -> EnrichResult, peek(ip) -> EnrichResult|null, clearCache() }
EnrichResult = { ip, version, skipped: null|ENRICH_SKIPS, prefix, origins, prefixFrom: 'ip-intel'|'ripestat-network'|null, announced, rpki: [{ asn, status, roas, validator }]|null,
  routing|null, abuse|null, peeringdb: [{ asn, net /* null: no record */ }]|null, errors: [{ source, error, errorKind, status, retryAfterMs, asn?, at }], at }   // null: not asked
```
- **What is sent:** nothing for an invalid address or one that is not globally routable (lib/ip.js `isGloballyRoutable`: private, reserved and documentation space; `skipped`).
