Tests: `tests/js/exposure.test.js` (the targets and caps, the leak classification and severities, the TXT literal matcher, the probe bodies and the reachability verdict, the roll-up and CSV), the offline `origins` E2E suite (§8).

### 5.88 `lib/report.js`, `ui/report.js`, `ui/report-button.js` — the customer report: one self-contained HTML file, Print / save as PDF, the re-run link

ROADMAP P0.14 (the report and the snapshot link; its print stylesheet shipped in wave 2, §5.32). A result of the Domain overview, Domain Health or DMARC & TLS reports becomes a report a customer can open, print or archive outside the app.

- **Where:** **Report** next to Copy summary — in the Domain overview's result header (disabled while a build runs; made from the finished overview, the CT issuers included when they were asked for) in Domain Health's hero (next to Report (JSON)) and in DMARC & TLS reports' results head (next to Copy summary; the DMARC domain on screen, the History tab's when that tab is shown, with or without reports read: §6 7b, §5.97). `ui/report-button.js` is one call in each view and carries only its label; the panel (`ui/report.js`) and the builder (`lib/report.js`) load on the first click (a failed load: `ctx.checkOutdated()` and a toast, and the next click tries again). Nothing is added to the start route.
- **The file** (`reportHtml(doc, { t, lang, version, generatedAt, link })`): `<!doctype html>`, `<html lang>` in the UI language, `<meta charset>` then the CSP meta `default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data:; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'` (`REPORT_CSP`; inline styles only because the file stands alone), `referrer: no-referrer`, `color-scheme: light`, a generator meta with the version, the title "<kind> · <domain>" and `REPORT_CSS`: the app's light palette and type, one column, severities always as a colour with a glyph and a word, a ≤ 640 px layout and `@media print` without backgrounds, sections kept whole. No script at all.
- **One escaping helper:** the document is a tree of nodes (`el(tag, attrs, ...children)`). `renderHtml()` writes every text node and every attribute value through `escapeHtml()` (`&`, `<`, `>`, `"`, `'` and the backtick as entities; C0 / C1 controls and every bidi control as U+FFFD, so a value can neither hide text nor reorder it), throws on an element or attribute outside its allow-lists (no `script`, `iframe`, `img`, `svg`, `object`, `link`, `base`, `form`; no `on*`, `style`, `src`, `srcdoc`), keeps an `href` only for an absolute http(s) URL (written with `rel="noreferrer"`) and writes no stylesheet but `REPORT_CSS`. No builder writes markup: the file is opened outside the app, where an unescaped DNS, RDAP or CT value would run.
- **Content (`ReportDoc`):** the head (kind, domain, the host it was reduced from, the result's time and the report's in UTC, "DomainScope <version>", the verdict with score, light and counts), **Problems and advice** first (errors, then warnings, in Domain Health's group order and then check order, each with its title, its explanation — the advice — and its group), the sections, **What was checked** and the footer.
  - `domainReport({ cards, domain, host, at })` takes lib/passport.js `passportCards()`: the seven cards in their order and in the overview's own words (`dov.*`) — Registration (registrar, dates with the days left, transfer lock with its note, status flags, DNSSEC delegation, the registry's name servers; without RDAP the registry's WHOIS and its link; not registered; failed), DNS hosting, Mail, Web, Certificates (CAA; the CT issuers when they were asked for, else "Not looked up"), SaaS verifications (vendor names, never a token) and Health (verdict and counts). Its problems are those of the health card's full report.
  - `healthReport({ report, selectors })` takes lib/health.js `domainHealth()`: the problems, then **Notes** (the info checks with their explanations), **Passed checks** by group and the **Records read** (NS, SOA, MX, A, AAAA, SPF, DMARC, DKIM, CAA, MTA-STS, TLS-RPT, BIMI, DNSSEC, registrar, expiry). A record whose lookup is in `failedLookups` reads "⚠ n/a — the lookup failed", never "none"; the extra DKIM selectors are named under What was checked.
  - `dmarcReport({ domain, at, current, history })` takes views/reports.js `dmarcReportFacts()` (the view words what only it can — the verdict, why a source is in its class, each fix — in the UI language; a source of the server list is "In your server list", never its name): the verdict of the reports read in the tab with the compliance as the figure (`verdict.display`, instead of "score/100") and its counts, **Problems and advice** = the sources to fix first (≤ 25, the rest counted) with their fixes as steps (`ReportItem.steps`), then the reports (period, reporters, messages, compliance, the published policy, the current SPF line with its record, the unknown senders' line), the addresses by class and by service, the notes; and, when the workspace keeps a history of the domain, the trend of the History tab's period (its totals, the last published policy, one line a day — a week over 400 days — with a report) and the senders new since `newSince`. With the history alone (no report read in the tab), its roll-up verdict and trend, and the problems section says the sources to fix are not known without the reports (`problemsNote`). Numbers and shares in the UI's formats (the injected `num` / `share`).
- **No silent dashes:** a failed lookup is "⚠ n/a — <reason>" (the injected `statusText`, ui/source-status.js); a card a stopped build never looked up says so; an overview without health checks says its problems are not known.
- **Words:** the injected `t` in the UI language (`has(key)` lets a missing key fall back to readable text, as the views do); `REPORT_I18N` (`crep.*`, English and Turkish) is registered by `ui/report.js`. Dates are UTC (`utcDay`, `utcTime`), the same for every reader of the file.
- **The re-run link** (the snapshot link): optional, ticked by default, and it is the view's permalink — `reportLinkParams(kind, input)` gives the overview's `{ name }` and Health's `{ domain, selectors }`, passed through lib/summarycore.js `permalinkParams` and `ctx.shareUrl`: the inputs only, never a result, a record or workspace data, so whoever opens it runs the check again with their own requests (a link only fills the view's form, as every shared link). "Copy the link" copies the same URL; the hint names what it carries. A DMARC report has none (`reportLinkParams('dmarc')` is `{}`: its reports are files only the sender has), and the panel offers neither the box nor Copy the link.
- **Download HTML:** `ui/download.js` `downloadText(timestampedName('domain-overview-report' | 'domain-health-report' | 'dmarc-report', 'html', domain), html, 'text/html;charset=utf-8')` (`REPORT_FILE_BASES`).
- **Print / save as PDF:** once the dialog has closed, `printReport(reportBody(doc, opts))` renders the same body through h() into a shadow root under `<body>` (`.crep-print-host`) with `REPORT_CSS` as a constructed stylesheet, adds a second constructed sheet to the document that hides the host on screen and everything else on paper (with its `@page` margins), and calls `window.print()`; `afterprint`, or print media ending, removes both. The app's CSP (`style-src 'self'`, no frames) refuses an inline `<style>`, every iframe and a blob: page (which inherits the CSP), but not a constructed stylesheet (verified in Chrome on 2026-10-08: no violation). A browser without shadow roots or constructed sheets is told to download the file and print it.
- **Privacy:** the report is made from the result on screen and sends nothing; it never holds a TXT verification token, the server inventory, workspace data or file contents. A DMARC report holds the reports' own facts (sending addresses, reporters' names, the domains they name) and, of the workspace's history, only the counts of the domain's trend and its new senders; never a server's name, a file name, a reporter's contact or a mail recipient.
- **Tests:** `tests/js/report.test.js` — `escapeHtml` against injection payloads, the serializer's allow-lists and links, UTC dates, the file's structure and order, crafted SPF, registrar and CAA values escaped in reports built from real `buildPassport()` and `domainHealth()` runs over a fake DoH client, both languages, failures as statuses, the link's keys within `PERMALINK_PARAMS`, every key the builders ask for in both languages; the DMARC report with crafted reporters, services, fix steps and an SPF record escaped, its sections in order, never a link, the history alone, Turkish, and built from the fixture mailbox through `dmarcReportFacts` with no server of the list; the Customer report group of `tests/e2e/domain.e2e.mjs` and the Report steps of `tests/e2e/dmarchistory.e2e.mjs` (§8).

**Accepted risks** (§5.95): Domain Health's input takes `waived: { applied: [{ id, reason, owner, expires }] }`: the accepted risks leave the problems and the counts, the verdict says "N accepted risks excluded", and a section "Accepted risks (N)" lists each with its title and "Accepted until DATE by OWNER: REASON", escaped like every other text. The Domain overview's report takes them from its health card (lib/passport.js `waived`, §5.46): they leave its problems and counts alike, the verdict and the Health card's counts say "N accepted risks excluded", and the Health card names each with its title and the same line. Tests: `tests/js/report.test.js`.

### 5.89 `lib/localeevidence.js` — adaptive locale packs (ROADMAP P1.9)
A domain whose TLD has market packs gets them (§5.6); one under a TLD without a pack of its own — one that names no market (`.com`, `.net`, `.org`, `.io` …) or a country ending without a pack yet (`.co.uk`, `.se` …) — used to get none, whatever its market. Under the automatic choice (`locales` undefined) the scan now picks its packs from evidence, just before its wordlist stage (§5.12), and says which and why. DOM-free, no I/O: the packs' labels come in (`lib/wordlist.js` `loadLocaleVocabulary`).
```js
export const LOCALE_EVIDENCE_MIN = 2            // points a pack needs
export const LOCALE_EVIDENCE_RELATIVE = 0.5     // … and at least this share of the strongest pack's points
export const LOCALE_EVIDENCE_VOLUME = 400       // distinct labels read before the word points are scaled by VOLUME / labels
export const LOCALE_EVIDENCE_MAX_LETTERS = 2     // the most points IDN letters give one pack
export const LOCALE_EVIDENCE_EXAMPLES = 8       // words / IDN labels a signal keeps for the explanation
export const NEUTRAL_WORDS                      // pack words that are English or international too (hotel, campus, personal, planning …): no evidence
export const GLOBAL_HOST_DOMAINS                // name / mail server domains that serve every market from one ccTLD (protonmail.ch, tutanota.de, ui-dns.de, hetzner.de, your-server.de …)
export const GENERIC_CCTLDS = ['co', 'ly']      // ccTLDs used worldwide: a server directly under them says nothing (ns1.example.com.co still does)
export const SCRIPT_HINTS                        // [cc, RegExp]: letters / scripts one pack's language alone uses
export function localeVocabulary(packs) -> Map<word, string[]>   // distinctive words → the packs that have them (≥ 4 characters, no WORDLIST_MEDIUM or NEUTRAL_WORDS word); cached per packs object
export function labelWords(label, vocab) -> string[]             // the pack words one ASCII label carries
export function unicodeLabel(label) -> string|null               // an xn-- label decoded (lib/punycode.js), others as they are; null when it does not decode, or decodes to anything but letters, marks, digits and hyphens (a control, a bidi override or isolate, a zero-width joiner)
export function foldLabel(text) -> string[]                      // ASCII forms the packs are folded to: 'şube' → ['sube'], 'prüfung' → ['prufung', 'pruefung']
export function labelLetters(text) -> string[]                   // the packs an IDN label's letters point to
export function hostLocales(host) -> string[]                    // the packs a server's ccTLD names (its registrable domain; GLOBAL_HOST_DOMAINS / GENERIC_CCTLDS → [])
export function localeEvidence({ domain, names = [], ns = [], mx = [], packs = null }) -> LocaleEvidence
LocaleEvidence = { domain, locales: string[] /* picked, strongest first, ≤ LOCALE_EVIDENCE_MAX_PACKS (3) */,
  signals: Array<{ locale, score, picked, points: { words, letters, ns, mx }, words: string[], wordCount, letters: string[], ns: string[] /* endings '.com.tr' */, mx: string[] }>
    /* every pack with any evidence, strongest first (ties in LOCALE_PACK_CODES order) */,
  names /* names read, the domain itself included */, labels /* distinct labels read */, ns, mx /* server registrable domains read */ }
```
- **Words.** The labels left of the domain of every name under it (and the domain's own labels left of its public suffix), each distinct label once, in `sortHostnames` order (the result never depends on the order the sources answered in). A label counts whole (`e-fatura`), else by its letter runs of four or more (`musteri` in `musteri-portal2`), each whole or as a two-part compound: two pack words (`bayisiparis`), or a pack word with a global word (`WORDLIST_MEDIUM` / `NEUTRAL_WORDS`) — five letters or more next to three (`destekapi`, `apidestek`), or both four or more (`lohnportal`); `terminal`, `motel` or `hotels` stay English. Each distinct pack word counts once: 1 with five letters or more, ½ with four, shared equally between the packs that have it (`cliente`: es, pt, it); with more than `LOCALE_EVIDENCE_VOLUME` distinct labels the sum is multiplied by VOLUME / labels, so a large zone's chance matches stay weak.
- **Letters.** An IDN label (`xn--…`) whose letters only one pack's language uses: Turkish ı ş ğ (and the dotted İ), German ß ä, Spanish ñ, Portuguese ã õ, Polish ą ć ę ł ń ś ź ż, French œ, Italian ì ò; Cyrillic → ru, Arabic → ar, kana → ja, Han without kana → zh. 1 per label, at most `LOCALE_EVIDENCE_MAX_LETTERS`; letters several languages share (ç, ö, ü, é …) point nowhere. A label is one piece of evidence: one whose letters point to a pack counts by them alone (a pack word in Turkish letters, `müşteri`, is one point, not two — one name is never enough), one whose letters point nowhere is read as words in its folded forms (`prüfung` → `prufung`, `pruefung`). A label that decodes to anything but letters, marks, digits and hyphens — a control or a bidi character a passive source may carry — is neither evidence nor shown (`unicodeLabel` → null).
- **Servers.** The zone's NS and MX hosts (mining, §5.12 `externalEvidence` and `evidence`), by registrable domain: 2 when at least half of them are under a ccTLD of the pack's market (lib/wordlist.js's TLD table), 1 when some are. Providers in `GLOBAL_HOST_DOMAINS` (Proton Mail, Tuta, IONOS's and Hetzner's name servers, Hetzner's webhosting `your-server.de`) and hosts directly under a `GENERIC_CCTLDS` ccTLD count in the total but name no market.
- **Choice.** A pack is picked with `LOCALE_EVIDENCE_MIN` points or more and at least `LOCALE_EVIDENCE_RELATIVE` of the strongest pack's, at most three, strongest first. `lib/wordlist.js` `localesForDomain(domain, evidence)` applies it — the TLD always wins.
- **In a scan (§5.12):** only with the automatic choice, from Smart up (Small is language-neutral), never for a `wordlist` override, the legacy 'medium' level or exact mode, and only for a base whose TLD has no packs. The pack files are read (≈ 16 KB, the cache the wordlist uses) only when names were found under such a base. `options.wordlist.perDomain[]` gains `localeSource` ('tld' | 'evidence' | 'none' | 'chosen', null without packs) and `localeEvidence`; the `bruteforce` stage event carries the same per base (`locales`). A pack the evidence picked that fails to load is reported like any missing pack (`localesMissing`, `WORDLIST_DEGRADED` `locale:<cc>`), with `localeSource` still 'evidence'.
- **Plan (§5.33):** `estimateQueries` counts what the evidence may add in `max` only (`breakdown.localeEvidence`, `evidencePackMax()` per such domain).
- **UI:** Subdomains › Advanced › Languages / markets ("Choose from the domain ending or the scan's evidence") says, for such a domain, that the scan picks packs from evidence ("Auto: .com has no market pack of its own, so the scan picks packs from evidence — …", the same for `.co.uk`; with a TLD pick: "Auto: Turkish (.com.tr), from evidence for .com"), and the plan line of Subdomains and SSL Targets adds "plus market packs if the scan finds evidence" (`wordlistPlan` marks the domain `evidence`). A run of either view says each pack the evidence added in its header as soon as the wordlist stage starts, and keeps it with the run: "Turkish pack added for example.com. Evidence: words in the names found (bayi, destek, kampanya), the mail servers' domain ending (.com.tr)." (`ui/locale-evidence.js`: `localeChoicesOf`, `localeEvidenceTexts`, `LocaleEvidenceBanner`; at most five words named, the rest counted; "domain endings" for several). The Overview's wordlist line marks those packs "(picked from evidence)", or says "no market pack: the evidence points to no market". The scan's JSON export carries `options.wordlist` with both fields.
- **Privacy:** nothing new is sent: the evidence is what the scan already read (names, the zone's own records); the pack files come from the site itself.
- **Tests:** `tests/js/localeevidence.test.js` (the vocabulary, labels, compounds, IDN letters — one label one piece of evidence, controls and bidi characters refused —, servers, the choice and its bars, the wordlist wiring), `tests/js/scanner-locales.test.js` (the scan: words from a source, MX hosts alone, an English zone, TLD / explicit / Small / override, several domains, a pack that fails to load, the estimate), `tests/js/locale-evidence-view.test.js` (plan and languages lines, the run's sentences, EN / TR, the banner in SSL Targets' run header), `tests/js/dnsmine.test.js` (`externalEvidence`); the offline `locales` E2E suite (§8).

### 5.90 `lib/records.js`, `lib/spfexplain.js`, `ui/explain-panel.js` — DNS Lookup › Explain: readable records

ROADMAP P1.5 (the wave 6 pick-up item "Readable records / SPF evaluator"). DNS Lookup › **Explain** says what the records of the looked-up name mean, term by term and tag by tag, and answers "may this address send mail as the domain?" the way a receiving server does. The SPF work is lib/health.js's (§5.15: parseSpf, spfLookupCount, spfEvaluate, spfMxHosts, the new expandSpfMacros / spfCheckHost / spfTreeChecks / findDmarc) and lib/retire.js's (`effectiveQualifier`, `rangeOf`); DMARC and CAA are read by health's parseDmarc / parseCaa / parseCaaIssueValue: there is no second parser.

```js
// lib/spfexplain.js (DOM-free, no network: it lays out a tree spfLookupCount expanded)
export const SPF_STEP_KINDS     // ['ip4','ip4-range','ip6','ip6-range','a','mx','include','redirect','exists','ptr','all']   (xpl.spf.kind.<kind>)
export const SPF_STEP_STATES    // ['ok','void','macro','skipped','dns-error','partial','no-record','multiple-records','loop','depth','too-many-mx']
  //   'partial': an `a` term whose A or AAAA question got no answer here, next to the other family's addresses (the step's `lost` families)
export const SPF_POLICY_STATES  // ['ok','no-record','multiple-records','dns-error']
export const SPF_FLATTEN_NOTES  // ['sender','failed','kept-include','exceptions','passes-all']
export const SPF_UDP_SAFE_LENGTH = 450, TXT_STRING_MAX = 255
export function spfPolicy(tree, { chain, scope }) -> SpfPolicy   // { domain, record, state, detail, steps: SpfStep[], ignored /* terms after all */, redirect,
  //   redirectIgnored, exp, modifiers, all, implicitNeutral, count, voidCount, errors, warnings /* parseSpf */, scope: 'top'|'include'|'redirect' }
  // SpfStep: { n, term, mechanism, qualifier, result /* where written */, effective /* at the checked domain: effectiveQualifier — inside an include only a
  //   pass counts, null = no match */, kind, params /* range, first, last, size (IPv4), prefix, hostBits | host, cidr4, cidr6 | target */, lookup,
  //   cost /* lookups with what is below */, target, macros, missing, addresses, hosts, lost /* 'A' / 'AAAA' that got no answer */, state, detail, child: SpfPolicy|null }
export function spfMeter(lookups) -> { count, limit: 10, voidCount, voidLimit: 2, exceeded, high /* 9 or 10 */, voidExceeded, branches: [{ term, cost }] /* costliest first */ }
export function spfStringIssues(strings) -> [{ after, left, right, joined }]   // TXT character-strings join without a space (RFC 7208 §3.3); reported only where
  // the join breaks a term (`/24` + `include:` → `/24include:`), never for a term split in its middle on purpose
export function spfFlatten(tree, { mxAddresses }) -> { record, terms, length, strings, lookups, addressTerms, exact, fits, notes: [{ code, term, holder }] } | null
  // `exact`: no `exceptions` note (a `passes-all` include is said, but its `all` is exact); an `a` / `mx` host one of whose families got no answer is kept (`failed`)
export function macroLetters(text) -> string[]
// lib/records.js (DOM-free)
export function explainDmarc(record, { domain, foundAt, inherited }) -> { valid, record, domain, foundAt, inherited, applies /* p, or the inherited sp */,
  appliesTag, pct, testing, tags: [{ tag, value, given, meaning /* DMARC_MEANINGS */, params, issue /* DMARC_ISSUES */ }], reports: [{ tag, uri, scheme, address,
  domain, sizeLimit, external }], issues: [{ code, token, severity }] }   // tags in DMARC_TAGS order (np, t, psd of DMARCbis too); sp, pct, adkim, aspf shown with
  // their default when left out; `external`: a report address of another organizational domain, which must authorize it (RFC 7489 §7.1)
export function explainCaa(records, { name, foundAt }) -> { name, foundAt, inherited, rows: [{ tag, kind /* CAA_KINDS */, value, flags, critical, issuer, ca,
  deny, accountUri, methods, otherParams, problem /* health CAA_PROBLEMS */, usable, valid }], anyone, blocked /* a critical unknown tag */, denyAll,
  issuers: [{ domain, ca }], wild: 'same'|'list'|'deny', wildIssuers, iodef }   // in record order, each row through parseCaa([rr]); issuemail (RFC 9495) and
  // issuevmc values through parseCaaIssueValue too (issuer, CA, parameters, `deny` for an empty issuer; only their syntax gives a `problem`)
export function decodeEch(b64) -> { ok, error /* ECH_ERRORS: base64, empty, truncated, length */, length, configs: [{ version, versionHex, supported /* 0xfe0d */,
  length, configId, kemId, kem, publicKeyLength, publicKey /* hex */, cipherSuites: [{ kdfId, kdf, aeadId, aead }], maxNameLength, publicName,
  extensions: [{ type, mandatory /* high bit */, length }] }] }   // an ECHConfigList; another version is listed and skipped, as clients do
export const ECH_VERSION = 0xfe0d, HPKE_KEMS, HPKE_KDFS, HPKE_AEADS /* RFC 9180 §7 */, ALPN_NAMES, TLS_GROUPS
export function compareHints(hints, actual) -> { hints, actual, status /* HINT_STATUSES: match, stale, partial, unknown, no-address */, stale, missing }   // sorted
export function explainSvcb(rrs, { owner, type = 'HTTPS', addresses /* target → { ipv4, ipv6 } */ }) -> [{ priority, mode: 'alias'|'service', target, targetName,
  ttl, alpn: [{ id, name }], defaultAlpn, port, hints: { v4, v6 }, ech, mandatory, dohpath, ohttp, groups, other, notes: [{ code /* SVCB_NOTES */, severity, params }] }]
export async function explainName(name, { dns, signal, known /* Map type → the lookup's DnsResponse */ }) -> { name, spf, dmarc, caa, svcb: [] }
export const EXPLAIN_SECTIONS = ['spf','dmarc','caa','svcb'], EXPLAIN_MAX_MX_HOSTS = 10
// ui/explain-panel.js
export function ExplainPanel({ ctx, name, types, responses, resolver }) -> { el, run({ noCache }), destroy() }
export function generatedKeys() -> string[]
```

**What is asked** (`explainName`, every section on its own: a question that got no answer — or anything else that breaks one — fails only its section, `state: 'failed'`; only an abort rejects). Nothing for a reverse name or the root (the summary offers no Explain there); no SPF, DMARC or CAA for a top-level domain (its TXT is not asked: check_host() needs two labels). SPF: the name's TXT records; one record is expanded once (spfLookupCount with the record, so it is not asked again), and the hosts of its mx terms (at most 10) are resolved for the flatten preview. DMARC: for a `_dmarc.<domain>` name its own TXT record; otherwise for a registrable domain, or a name that has an SPF record or MX hosts (the names that send mail: the lookup's MX answer, or MX asked once when the lookup did not ask it; an MX question that got no answer does not hide DMARC), `findDmarc` — the organizational domain's record applies to a subdomain without one; never for another `_` name (`_spf.<domain>` holds a policy and sends no mail). CAA: the set that applies (findCaa, RFC 8659 tree climbing; the lookup's own CAA answer when it has records), not for `_` names. HTTPS (SVCB too when the lookup asked it): the records and the A / AAAA records of every service-mode target, to compare the hints with. An answer the lookup already has is used as it is (`known`, the lookup's own responses for the same name): never asked twice. Every question goes to the DoH resolvers the lookup uses (its chosen resolver, or the failover chain), names and types only — no new third party; the panel says how many questions it added. "Explain again" and a section's Retry ask everything again without the cache.

**SPF.** The record (copy button); the lookup meter — DNS lookups of 10 (a bar: amber at 9–10, red past 10), void lookups of 2, the record's length and TXT strings, the costliest branches; Domain Health's own findings (`spfTreeChecks`, the `health.spf.*` words; ok ones left out but the catch-all), led by any TXT string join that breaks a term; then every term in the order receivers read them: its number, the term, the result a match gives (Pass / Fail / Softfail / Neutral), its cost in lookups, a sentence for its kind (`ip4:192.0.2.0/28` → "Mail from 192.0.2.0 to 192.0.2.15 (16 addresses) matches."), the addresses of an `a` term, the hosts of an `mx` term, a CIDR widening, host bits, and what went wrong with its lookup (void, a macro that needs the sender, a failed lookup, an A or AAAA question with no answer next to the other family's addresses — "only the addresses shown are known" —, an include without SPF, a loop …). An include's or a redirect's policy is one click away (a disclosure with its record and its own steps): inside an include a non-pass result is shown with "counts as no match" (it only means the include does not match). Terms after `all`, an ignored redirect, `exp=` and unknown modifiers are said under the steps; a record without `all` and redirect ends "neutral".

**Does an address pass?** An address (IPv4 / IPv6; an invalid one is a field error and the previous verdict goes), optionally a sender (MAIL FROM) and a HELO name for their macros (one that cannot be a sender — `parseSpfSender` — or a host name — `parseSpfHelo` — is a field error the same way, its disclosure opened), then `spfCheckHost` on the panel's client: the verdict as a badge and a sentence — the deciding term and the policy holding it, the include path, the host and address an `a` / `mx` / `ptr` matched through, the permerror's or the "cannot tell" reason (`xpl.check.perm.*`, `xpl.check.unknown.*`; a macro that expanded to no host name this page can ask names that name, `xpl.check.unaskable`), and, for an unknown macro, which of the sender and HELO fields would answer it; plus when and through which resolver it was expanded (a receiver asks its own resolver). Enter in any field checks.

**Flatten preview** (a disclosure): the record with include, a and mx replaced by today's addresses (`spfFlatten`): the checked domain's own terms keep their order and qualifiers, an include gives the addresses its policy passes with the include's qualifier, a redirect hands over its whole policy (its `all` too); a term that depends on the sender (`exists`, `ptr`, a macro) or could not be read — an `a` / `mx` host one of whose address families got no answer included: half an answer would fail the other family's mail — stays as written, an include whose policy has one is kept by the name it expanded to; inside an include only passes count, so a carve-out there makes the preview inexact (`exceptions`), and an include that passes everyone ends it with `all` (`passes-all`, a warning: the preview stays exact); a term an earlier one with the same qualifier covers is left out. Its address terms, characters, TXT strings and lookups left; longer than 450 characters (one UDP answer, RFC 7208 §3.4) and over 255 (several strings) are said; and that providers change their addresses, so a flattened record must be kept up to date.

**DMARC** — where the record was found (`_dmarc.<name>`, or the organizational domain's with its subdomain policy), the record, what applies to mail from the name (the policy, `pct` and `t=y` folded in), the record's problems (parseDmarc's codes and the policy notes: monitoring only, sp=none, pct, test mode, no rua), then tag by tag — written, then meant — with the defaults of the tags left out and every report address, an external one with the `<policy domain>._report._dmarc.<report domain>` record it needs. **CAA** — where the set was found (a parent's applies), who may issue (and wildcards: the same CAs, their own list or none; a critical unknown tag blocks every CA), then every record (`flags tag "value"`) with the CA it names (CAA_ISSUERS), its RFC 8657 restrictions and why a value authorizes nobody (`health.caa.problem.*`); an empty issue, issuewild, issuemail or issuevmc value says that no CA may issue those certificates. **HTTPS / SVCB** — per record: priority, mode and target, the protocols (an HTTPS record's implied http/1.1), port, each hint list against the target's A / AAAA records (stale, partial, the same, none, not compared), the decoded ECH configurations (config id, outer name, KEM, cipher suites, key size, extensions), mandatory keys, DoH path, TLS groups and unknown keys, and the notes: alias mode (to “.”, with parameters, mixed with service records), another target, HTTP/3 and its UDP port, no alpn, no-default-alpn (alone: unusable), a mandatory key missing, a port, stale hints (clients that connect from the hints reach the wrong server), ECH on, unreadable or of no browser version, a mandatory ECH extension.

**The panel** (`ui/explain-panel.js`, loaded on the first click of the lookup summary's **Explain** button, so the start route does not grow; styles `.xpl-*` in `views/lookup.css`): a section per record kind, its states said in words ("No SPF record …", "⚠ n/a" with a Retry); DMARC and CAA as two-column tag lists that stack on a phone; a new lookup closes it, leaving the view stops it. Every value from the network is rendered as text. Words: `xpl.*` in English and Turkish (`generatedKeys()` lists the ones built from codes) and Domain Health's `health.*` for the shared SPF findings and CAA problems.

Tests: `tests/js/spfcheck.test.js` (the RFC 7208 §7.4 macro table, IPv6 nibbles, escapes, URL escaping, the 253-character cut, what cannot be expanded; a tree expanded for one address and evaluated for it and for another; spfCheckHost through %{i} / %{ir}.%{v} terms, ptr forward confirmation, mx hosts, sender and HELO macros, a known record, a mapped address, an `a` / `mx` host whose A question got no answer over a query-only client, senders and HELO names that cannot be one, a macro that makes no host name; spfTreeChecks; findDmarc), `tests/js/spfexplain.test.js` (steps with results, effective results and costs, includes, failures, the meter, string joins, flatten with exceptions, kept includes, a redirect, passes-all, size, an `a` term with one family lost) and `tests/js/records.test.js` (decodeEch on configs built byte by byte, broken lists, hints, HTTPS / SVCB notes, DMARC tags, defaults and problems, CAA rows and summaries with issuemail / issuevmc, explainName over a fake zone: the lookup's answers reused, inheritance, failures, abort, a top-level domain, DMARC by MX asked once, `_` names), and the offline E2E suite `tests/e2e/explain.e2e.mjs` (§8).

### 5.91 `lib/expected.js`, `lib/soaprobe.js`, `ui/soa-probe.js` — Global DNS › Expected value and the worst-case wait (ROADMAP P0.6, the part wave 6 left)

The cutover assistant's Global DNS half (2026-10-08). DOM-free `lib/expected.js` judges the answers a check already has against the value a change should publish — nothing is asked again when the value changes — and `lib/soaprobe.js` asks the zone's own name server once, on a click.
```js
// lib/expected.js — no network, no clock of its own
export const EXPECT_MODES = ['exact', 'contains', 'regex'], EXPECT_ERRORS = ['empty', 'regex', 'long', 'address'], EXPECT_VERDICTS = ['match', 'mismatch', 'failed'];
export const EXPECT_MAX_LENGTH = 300, EXPECT_SPECIALS = ['NXDOMAIN', 'NODATA'], COMMON_TTLS, FLUSH_LINKS /* [{ id, name, url }]: Google Public DNS, Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 */;
export function parseExpected({ mode, pattern, type }) -> { ok: true, mode, type, pattern, values, special, re, whole } | { ok: false, error, mode, pattern, detail? }   // 'address': an exact A / AAAA value that is no address of that family (detail: it, as typed); whole: the regex over a whole value
export function canonValue(type, text) -> string            // an address canonical, a TXT record's strings joined and unescaped, else tokens lower-cased without quotes or trailing dots
export function matchExpected(values /* propagation.answerValues */, expected) -> boolean
export function expectedVerdict(row, expected) -> 'match'|'mismatch'|'failed'|null   // null: pending, skipped (not readable), notAsked, filtered (a filter's block)
export function expectedTally(rows, expected) -> { match, mismatch, failed, judged, done }
export function negativeTtl(response) -> number|null          // min(SOA TTL, SOA minimum) of the authority SOA (RFC 2308 §5)
export function cachedTtl(row) / cacheEnd(row) -> number|null   // the longest TTL of the answer (an empty one: the negative TTL; a row's own `ttl` / `expiresAt` — an ISP resolver's — kept); + `at`
export function worstCaseEta({ ttls, negativeTtl, negative }) -> seconds|null   // the highest TTL over the name servers; the negative-cache time only for an old "no such record"
export function expectedEta(rows, expected, { authoritative /* a SoaProbe: type, ttl, negativeTtl */ }) -> { mismatched, positive, negative, observedTtl, recordTtl, recordFrom, serverTtl,
  negativeTtl, negativeFrom /* recordFrom / negativeFrom: 'name-server'|'answers'|null */, seconds, least, exact, last }
export function probeQuestion(rows, expected, type) -> string   // the name server's question: the check's type, or 'SOA' when every source not there yet says no such name / record
export function likelyTtl(seen) -> number|null                // moved from lib/cutover.js (re-exported there)
// lib/soaprobe.js — the DohClient and the Globalping client injected
export const SOA_PROBE_PURPOSE = 'soa-probe', SOA_PROBE_COST = 1, SOA_ZONE_MAX_STEPS = 12;
export const SOA_PLAN_ERRORS = ['name', 'internal', 'lookup', 'no-zone', 'no-ns', 'not-probeable'];
export const SOA_PROBE_STATES = ['ok', 'not-authoritative', 'refused', 'servfail', 'timeout', 'unreachable', 'failed'];
export function parseSoaRecord(value) -> { mname, rname, serial, refresh, retry, expire, minimum } | null
export async function findZone(name, { dns, signal }) -> { ok: true, zone, soa, nameservers } | { ok: false, error, zone?, detail? }
export function pickNameserver(nameservers, mname) -> host|null   // the SOA's primary when it is one of them, else the first by name; probeable hosts only
export async function planSoaProbe(name, { dns, signal, type }) -> { ok: true, name, type, zone, ns, nameservers, soa, body, probes: 1 } | { ok: false, error, zone? }   // type: 'SOA' when absent or not one Globalping asks (CAA)
export function readSoaProbe(measurement, { name, zone, ns, type, id }) -> { name, type, zone, ns, state, rcode, aa, exists, alias, ttl, soa /* + ttl */, negativeTtl, probe, nsid, rttMs, error, measurementId }
export async function runSoaProbe(plan, { client, signal }) -> { result, id, cost, quota }   // Globalping errors thrown as they come
```
- **Matching:** exact compares the records of the queried type as a set (order, case, quotes and trailing dots aside; A / AAAA / CNAME / NS / PTR values separated by commas or spaces, MX by commas with an optional preference, CAA with optional flags, any other type one whole value — a TXT record may hold both); an exact A / AAAA value is an address of that family — a host name the name points to is refused at the field (`address`, which names Contains or the CNAME type) rather than leaving every source "Not yet"; `NXDOMAIN` / `NODATA` stand for "no such name" / "no record of the type" (a deletion is checked too). Contains (case-insensitive text) and regex (case-insensitive) read every answer value, the CNAME chain's targets included; NXDOMAIN and NODATA are statuses, not text — contains matches one only when the text is that word, a regex only over the whole word (`whole`), so Contains "main" never counts a "no such name" as serving main-lb.example.net. A failure (no DNS answer, or an rcode such as SERVFAIL) is `failed`, never a match; a filtering resolver's block, a row not readable in browsers and a location not asked are not judged.
- **The worst case:** the sources that do not serve the value yet keep their answer at most until `cacheEnd` (`last`: the latest of them, exact for these sources). Any resolver anywhere: at most the old answer's TTL after the change, and where the old answer is "no such record", the zone's negative-cache time. A TTL read from cached answers counts down (anycast caches out of step), so from the answers alone the figure (`seconds`) is an estimate — the highest TTL their records carried read as the zone TTL it most likely counts down from (`likelyTtl`), the negative time from their SOA (its minimum exact, its TTL counted down and read up) — with a lower bound (`least`: what those copies had left), never a worst case: a copy near the end of a 3600 s TTL with 400 s left reads as 600 s. The zone's name server makes it exact (`exact`): asked the check's own type, its answer carries the record set's TTL (`serverTtl`), which the figure takes (`recordFrom: 'name-server'`) unless the copies here carry more — the TTL lowered with the change, so the old one counts; an empty answer carries the SOA and its negative-cache time.
- **The name server** (`lib/soaprobe.js`): the zone of the name over DoH (its own SOA, else the authority section's, climbing past an alias, which a resolver follows into the target's zone; a public suffix is no zone of its own), its NS set, the primary or the first probeable server, then one Globalping DNS measurement — the check's own question at that server (§3; `probeQuestion`: its record type, or when every source not there yet says no such name or record, the SOA of the name, whose answer always carries the zone's SOA; a type Globalping cannot ask, CAA, asks the SOA too) — whose answer says whether the server answers with authority (else a lame delegation), the record set's TTL there (`ttl`: the longest TTL of an answer that holds records of the type asked; none for an alias leading out of the answer), from the SOA of an empty answer the zone's serial and primary and `negativeTtl` = min(SOA TTL, minimum), and whether the name exists there or is an alias. Never sent: an internal name (`lib/ispdns.js isInternalName`), an IP literal, a name Globalping cannot ask.
- **UI** (views/global.js, §6): the form's **Expected value** field and **Match** (exact / contains / regex; `expect=` / `match=` in the link — `PERMALINK_PARAMS.global`, §5.32 — and in the kept result's params); a mark on every judged answer ("Matches"; "Not yet", its tooltip until when that source may keep it); the card under the verdict (the value and mode, "Served by n of m sources" with a bar and the failures, "Every source that answered serves the expected value", until when the last cached old copy here expires, the worst case anywhere — "at least …, most likely …" with "cached TTLs count down" until the name server was asked, a worst case once all of it rests on the name server — with what it rests on (the record's TTL, read from the copies here or at the name server, which may now serve a lower one; the negative-cache time), the cache-flush links, "Show only the n sources not there yet" — a filter of the tables and the IP table, exclusive with an answer group's —, and, once the check has ended while some answer is not there yet, **Ask the zone's name server (1 Globalping probe)**); an export-only "Expected value" column in the CSV / JSON of the resolver and location tables while there is one; Copy summary's line (§5.32). A regex that came with a link is held: shown in the field (whose hint says so) and kept in the link, applied only once the user presses Enter in the field, edits it or picks a mode — it would run against answers the link's author may write (a TXT record), and a pattern that backtracks without end stalls the page; a re-mount keeps it held (`expectHeld` in the snapshot). `ui/soa-probe.js` (loaded on that first click, which also sends it): the plan (the question: `check().ask`), the gate (`gateProbes`, purpose `soa-probe`, its privacy text naming the name, the record type and the server), one measurement, statuses (looking up, the quota, asking, nothing sent and why, the quota used up with its reset, Globalping unreachable, no probe free, a failed measurement with its link), the answer as one alert (authority, the serial and primary, the name there — "The change has not reached the zone yet" when a record is expected and the name does not exist there —, the answer's TTL there, the negative-cache time, where it was asked from, the measurement link), **Ask again**; the card redraws on every answer, every edit of the value and a 30 s ticker, so `refresh()` rebuilds the status and the answer only when what they say changed (a warning is a role="alert", a status sits in a live region: each is announced once), and the card's "every source serves it" note is kept the same way; a new check resets it, leaving the view aborts it, a language re-mount shows its answer again (`snapshot()`), nothing sent. About › Privacy says what it sends (`about.privSoa`).
- **Tests:** `tests/js/expected.test.js` (parsing — an exact A / AAAA host name refused —, the matching table — exact / contains / regex, NXDOMAIN / NODATA only as whole words, MX, CAA, TXT —, verdicts and counts, cached TTLs, the worst case with mixed name-server TTLs and a Route 53-style SOA, a stale copy with little TTL left — an estimate and its lower bound until the name server's TTL makes it exact, or a lowered TTL does not —, the probe's question), `tests/js/soaprobe.test.js` (the zone over a fake DoH — an alias, a brand-new name, a public suffix —, the name server chosen, the question — the record type, CAA and none as the SOA —, refusals, the answer from dig-shaped measurements: NODATA, the apex, NXDOMAIN, an alias, records of the type asked and their TTL, a lame server, no answer), `tests/js/summary.test.js` (the line), `tests/e2e/cutover.e2e.mjs` (offline: a fake DoH and a fake Globalping; the marks, the card and its estimate, the filter, contains / regex / an invalid pattern / an exact A host name, the link and a link's regex held until Enter, Copy summary, the CSV column; the probe's consent, body and answer — the SOA for a new name, the A record for a changed one, whose TTL makes the worst case exact —, Ask again, an internal name, a Turkish re-mount, no alert inserted again when the card redraws, the quota; 375 / 320 px, light / dark).

### 5.92 `lib/registrars.js`, `lib/secscore.js`, `ui/secscore-panel.js` — lock depth, registrar class, DNS redundancy and a CSC-style domain security score
CSC's Domain Security Report scores companies' domains on eight measures: an enterprise-class registrar, a registry lock, CAA, DNS redundancy, DNSSEC, SPF, DKIM and DMARC. The Domain portfolio scores each domain on them from the facts it already has (§5.63): nothing more is sent.
```js
// lib/registrars.js (pure)
export const CORPORATE_REGISTRARS = [{ id, brand, name }]   // by IANA Registrar ID, checked in IANA's registrar-ids-1.csv on 2026-10-08: 292 and 3838
  // MarkMonitor, 299 CSC Corporate Domains, 447 Safenames, 470 Com Laude (Nom-iq), 642 Corsearch, 1011 101domain GRS, 1251 Nameshield, 1466 Lexsynergy,
  // 1639 EBRAND, 1750 Authentic Web, 3786 GoDaddy Corporate Domains
export const RESERVED_REGISTRAR_IDS   // IANA's "Reserved" IDs (the same file): 9994–9999 (the registry operator acting as registrar, test and SLA IDs), 1, 3, 8, 119,
  // 365, 376, 10009, 4000001, 8888888
export const REGISTRAR_CLASSES = ['corporate', 'retail', 'unknown']
export function registrarId(value) -> number|null   // '292', 292, ' 292 ' → 292; anything else (none, 'N/A', '0', '12a') → null
export function registrarClass(ianaId) -> 'corporate'|'retail'|'unknown'   // unknown: no ID (a country-code registry's own registrars), not a number, or reserved
export function corporateRegistrar(ianaId) -> { id, brand, name }|null

// lib/secscore.js (pure; texts SECURITY_I18N, en / tr)
export const SECURITY_MEASURES = [{ id, rule, value }]   // registrar (registrar.class corporate), registryLock (registryLock true), caa (caa present: deny-all
  // counts), dnsRedundancy (ns.providers >= 2), dnssec (dnssec >= signed), spf (spf valid), dkim (dkim true), dmarc (dmarc.policy >= quarantine) — the same
  // requirements as the corporate preset (§5.64)
export const SECURITY_MAX = 8
export function securityScore(facts) -> { domain, score /* measures met */, fail, unknown, max, measures: [{ id, rule, status, actual, evidence, required }] }
export function securityScores(factsList) ; securityAdoption(rows) -> [{ id, pass, fail, unknown, total, share /* pass / total, null without a domain */ }]
export function securityTotals(rows) -> { domains, average, full /* all eight met */, unknownDomains, unknownMeasures } ; scoreBand(score) -> 'ok'|'info'|'warn'|'error'
export function securityCsv(rows, { t }) /* a row per domain: its score, the measures not known, a column per measure "FAIL · <evidence>" */ ; securityExport(row) -> { score, max, unknown, measures: { id: status } }

// ui/secscore-panel.js (loaded with the tab on its first use)
export function mountSecurity(host, { ctx, source /* () => { facts, status } | null */, subject }) -> { refresh(), destroy() }
export function totalsText(totals, t) ; barModel(adoption, t) -> { segments: [{ kind, x, width, count }], text, label } ; generatedKeys() ; BAR_SEGMENTS
```
Each measure is a lib/policy.js rule (§5.64) evaluated with its fixed requirement, so a measure is met, not met or not known with that rule's evidence — the same words as the policy matrix and the runner's `audit`. A measure that could not be checked (a lookup that failed or has not landed, a registry without RDAP, a registrar without an IANA ID or with a reserved one, DKIM not asked) is not known: it never counts as met and is never called failed. The score is the measures met, 0 to 8; the average counts a measure not known as not met. **The tab** (§6 7c): before a check it says what it needs; with one, the line (domains, average score, how many meet all eight, the measures not checked; "still being checked" while the run goes on), one bar per measure — met, not met and not known as shares of the domains, each a `role="img"` SVG with its label for screen readers and its text beside it ("1 of 4 (25%) · 2 not known") —, a legend, and the table of scores (the lowest first; the domain, the score coloured by its band with the measures not known, each measure's status and evidence; search; sort; labelled cards below 640 px) with a **CSV** of the rows shown. It redraws with the run's rows while it is on screen and once the run ends. Tests: `tests/js/registrars.test.js`, `tests/js/secscore.test.js`, `tests/js/portfolio-view.test.js` (the line and the bars in English and Turkish), `tests/e2e/secscore.e2e.mjs` (offline).

### 5.93 `lib/senders.js`, `tools/build-senders.mjs` — the service behind a DMARC report source

DMARC & TLS reports names the service behind each sending address (dmarcian Source Viewer, Valimail Monitor). DOM-free; nothing is sent by the module but the bundled lists, read from this site.
```js
export const SENDER_TYPES = ['mailbox','security','forwarding','transactional','marketing','saas','cloud','hosting','msp','technology','isp','network']   // rpt.svcType.<id>
export const SENDER_VIAS = ['dkim','return-path','spf-include','ptr','isp','asn']   // the evidence, strongest first (rpt.svcVia.<id>, rpt.svcHow.<id>)
export const CONFIDENCES = ['high','medium','low'], SERVICE_GUIDES /* the 13 services with their own guide */, SENDER_GUIDES = [...SERVICE_GUIDES, ...SENDER_TYPES, 'forwarded', 'authorized']   // rpt.guide.<id>
export const UNAUTHORIZED_GUIDES = ['cloud','hosting','msp','technology','isp','network']   // the type guides worded for a server nothing authorizes ("authorize it in SPF", "if not, it is spoofing")
export const PTR_TYPE_MAP = { 'Email Provider': 'mailbox', 'Email Security': 'security', Marketing: 'marketing', SaaS: 'saas', IaaS: 'cloud', PaaS: 'cloud', 'Web Host': 'hosting', MSP: 'msp', MSSP: 'msp', Technology: 'technology' }
export const SENDERS_FORMAT = 1, SENDERS_FILES = ['manifest.json','ptr-map.json','isp.json'], SENDERS_TIMEOUT_MS = 15000, IDENTIFY_MAX = 200, SERVICE_CSV_COLUMNS, PASSPORT_KINDS
export const SENDER_SERVICES   // ≈ 70 frozen { id, name, type, guide, spf, dkim, returnPath, ptr } (suffixes): Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Zoho, Yandex 360, …,
                               // Mimecast, Proofpoint, …, Amazon SES, SendGrid, Mailgun, Postmark, SparkPost, Mandrill, Mailjet, …, Mailchimp, Brevo, HubSpot, Salesforce
                               // Marketing Cloud, Klaviyo, …, Salesforce, Zendesk, Freshdesk, Atlassian, Shopify, …; an entry's `owns` domains count for every kind of evidence
export function serviceById(id) ; serviceBySpf(domain) ; serviceByDkim(domain) ; serviceByReturnPath(domain) ; serviceByPtr(name) -> service|null   // the longest suffix on a label boundary
export function passportKind(type) -> 'mailbox'|'gateway'|'forwarding'|'sending'   // lib/passport.js spfSenders (§5.46)
export function suffixesOf(name) -> string[] ; lookupMap(map, name) -> { key, name, type }|null   // the name and its parents down to two labels; the longest key of the bundled map
export function spfPathOf(row) -> string[]   // the passing verdict's path (spfNow, else a permerror's spfListed), the a / mx host that matched last; [] when nothing authorizes it
export function identifySource(row, { domain, spfPath, ptrName, ptrConfirmed, maps, holder }) -> { id, service, type, via, confidence, domain, guide } | null
export function senderGuide(ident, row) -> guide|null   // by row.cls too: yours → null; forwarder → 'forwarded' whatever named it; third-party → 'authorized' for an UNAUTHORIZED_GUIDES guide; else ident.guide
export function groupGuide(group) -> guide|null   // senderGuide for the group's first class of unknown, third-party, forwarder; null when every source is yours, and for 'unnamed'
export function identifyCandidates(rows, { identOf, checked, max = 200 }) -> rows   // public, not yours (the server list or your own SPF terms say whose they are); unnamed, or named only by an unconfirmed reverse name, the ISP list or the network; not looked up yet; most mail first
export function groupKey(ident) ; groupSources(rows, identOf) -> { groups: ServiceGroup[], totals: { services, addresses, messages, unnamedAddresses, unnamedMessages } } ; serviceCsvRows(groups)
ServiceGroup = { key /* svc:<id> | isp | net:<holder> | name:<map name> | unnamed */, id, service, type, guide, vias, confidence /* the best */, evidence, rows, addresses, messages, pass, fail, spfAligned, dkimAligned, classes }
export function installSenderMaps({ manifest, ptrMap, isp }) -> { ptr: Map<domain, [name, type]>, isp: Set<domain>, info }   // TypeError on any other format or shape
export function loadSenderMaps({ fetchImpl, signal, timeoutMs }) -> Promise<SenderMaps>   // assets/data/senders once (fs in Node); a failed read rejects and the next call tries again; an abort ends the wait only
export function resetSenderMaps()   // tests
```
**identifySource**, the first that names it wins: (1) `dkim` — a DKIM signature that **verified** for a domain of another organisation than the header From (or the policy domain): the service's own signing domain (`d=sendgrid.net`, `d=<tenant>.onmicrosoft.com`, `d=<domain>.<date>.gappssmtp.com`); (2) `return-path` — an SPF **pass** for a return-path (or HELO) domain of another organisation (a failed one is a forwarder's or a forger's); (3) `spf-include` — a domain of another organisation on `spfPathOf(row)`: the include (or redirect, or the a / mx host that matched) that authorizes the address now — worded as it is, never as `include:` ("Named from your SPF, which authorizes it through mail.zendesk.com"); (4) `ptr` — the reverse name under a service of the table or a base domain of `maps.ptr`; (5) `isp` — its base domain in `maps.isp`: "an ISP or home network — spoofing, or a user forwarding their own mail" (the service shown is the base domain); (6) `asn` — the network's holder (lib/ipintel.js `holder`, `asn`). Within a step the table comes before the map (which counts for (1)–(3) too once loaded) across every candidate of the step — the signatures and return-paths the most messages first, then by name, the SPF path in its order —, so the name never depends on the order the reports were read. Confidence: (1)–(3) `high`; (4) and (5) `medium` when `ptrConfirmed` (the name resolves back to the address), else `low`; (6) `low`. Without `maps` (nothing loaded yet) only the table names sources, so naming them needs no request. **The guide** (`senderGuide`, `groupGuide`) follows the class as much as the service: none for your own server (its class and fixes say what it needs; a group of only yours has none), `forwarded` for a forwarder whatever named it (a forwarder's reverse name or rewritten return-path names the forwarder, a DKIM signature the sender: the text names neither), `authorized` for an authorized third party whose type's guide is worded for a server nothing authorizes; only an unknown sender gets the spoofing or ISP words. A group shows the guide of its first class of unknown senders, third parties and forwarders. Identify senders never looks up your own servers.

**The lists** (`tools/build-senders.mjs`, weekly in `.github/workflows/senders.yml`; Node 22, no dependency): parsedmarc's `parsedmarc/resources/maps/base_reverse_dns_map.csv` downloaded from raw.githubusercontent.com at the pinned commit `6effd80` (2026-04-20; `SOURCE` holds its SHA-256), with the LICENSE and the maps README of that commit. parsedmarc is Apache-2.0, and its map was until the maps README put it under CC BY-SA 4.0 on 2026-04-26 (rows added from IPinfo Lite): the pin is the last commit before IPinfo Lite came in, and the build refuses a map that its README puts under a share-alike licence, or a LICENSE that is not Apache 2.0. `parseCsv` (RFC 4180: quoted commas, doubled quotes, CRLF, a BOM); `buildSenders({ csv, csvSha256, readme, licence, previous, now, source, bounds, canaries })` → `{ files, manifest, report: { problems, counts, skipped } }` — the header `base_reverse_dns,name,type`, every row three fields, every type one the map defines (`KNOWN_TYPES`, any case), the counts within `BOUNDS`, the canaries (google.com → Google, Email Provider; outlook.com → Outlook, Email Provider; amazonses.com → Amazon SES, SaaS; sendgrid.net → SendGrid, Marketing; mcsv.net → Mailchimp, Marketing), the SHA-256 the pin names; a problem writes nothing (`run()` rejects, the files on disk stay as they were). `ptr-map.json`: the ten mail-relevant types, renamed by `PTR_TYPE_MAP` (1,348 at the pin, 17 KB gzip); `isp.json`: the ISP rows' base domains, no names (950, 5 KB gzip); a key that is no host name or a public suffix is left out, the first of a duplicate kept; both carry the Apache notice of the changes; `manifest.json`: format, date (kept while the digest does not move), the source (URL, commit, SHA-256, rows, types), the licence and its notice, each file's size and SHA-256, the counts per type. The service worker precaches the manifest only (§5.35). Tests: `tests/js/senders.test.js` (each way, the order, the own organisation, failed evidence, the ISP label, unknown, the candidates, the grouping and its totals, the lists read and refused, with classifySources over a fake DoH), `tests/js/build-senders.test.js` (quoted commas, the type filter, the manifest, the licence check, a bad download leaving the files untouched, the bundled lists matching their manifest).

### 5.94 `lib/crl.js`, `lib/revocation.js`, `ui/revocation.js`, `ui/revocation-card.js` — the renewal radar: ARI windows and revocation

What the CA says about a certificate that is still served: the window in which it wants it renewed (ACME Renewal Information, RFC 9773 — a window that opens early or moves earlier is how a CA announces a mass revocation) and whether it was revoked. Server side, the runner's `tls --ari --revocation` (§9) and the CLI's `--ari` / `--revocation` (§7) ask the CAs' ARI servers and read the CRLs (§3: no CORS, never the page); in the page, Cert Spotter's revocation fields (§3) and the CLI's records in Certificate estate. OCSP is never asked.
```js
// lib/crl.js — DOM-free; a DER CRL over lib/x509.js's DER reader (x509.js exports it as `DER`)
export const REVOCATION_REASONS /* { 0: 'unspecified', 1: 'keyCompromise', …, 10: 'aACompromise' } (7 unused) */, REVOCATION_REASON_NAMES,
  CRL_UNKNOWN = ['issuer-mismatch', 'critical-extension', 'delta', 'scope', 'reasons', 'stale'];
export function reasonName(code) -> string|null ; normalizeSerial(hex) -> lower-case hex without leading zeros ; class CrlParseError
export function signatureScheme(oid, params) -> { scheme: 'rsa-pkcs1'|'rsa-pss'|'ecdsa'|'ed25519'|'ed448', hash, saltLength? } | null   // PSS parameters read
export function parseCrl(der, { serials /* only these entries kept: a CA's CRL can list 100,000s */ }) -> { version, issuerDN, issuer, issuerRDNs, thisUpdate, nextUpdate,
  revoked: [{ serialHex, revocationDate, reasonCode, reason, invalidityDate, unsupportedCritical }], count, filtered: Set|null, crlNumber, authorityKeyId,
  idp: { urls: string[], relativeName, onlyUser, onlyCA, onlySomeReasons, indirect, onlyAttribute } | null, deltaCrl, unsupportedCritical, signatureAlgorithm, signatureAlgorithmOid,
  scheme, tbsDer, signature }   // throws CrlParseError on what is no CRL
export function crlIssuedFor(crl, cert) -> boolean   // the issuer DN, and the authority key id when both carry one
export function crlUrlsOf(cert) -> string[]          // the http(s) CRL distribution points, in order, each once (LDAP left out)
export function crlStatus(crl, cert, { url, now }) -> { status: 'good'|'revoked'|'unknown', code /* CRL_UNKNOWN */, reasonCode, reason, time, thisUpdate, nextUpdate }
  // unknown: another CA's CRL, an unknown critical extension (on the CRL, or on the certificate's entry), a delta CRL, an IDP for other certificates (CA or
  // attribute certificates, an indirect CRL, another distribution point than `url`, user certificates only for a CA) — a listed serial is revoked whatever
  // the CRL's age —, an unlisted one with an IDP for some reasons only or past nextUpdate; removeFromCRL (8) is good; RangeError for a CRL parsed without the serial
// lib/revocation.js — DOM-free
export const REVOCATION_STATUSES = ['good', 'revoked', 'not-found', 'expired', 'no-name', 'rate-limited', 'error'], REVOCATION_MAX_PAGES = 3, PROBLEM_REPORTING_MAX_CHARS = 2000;
export function spotterRevocation(item) -> { revoked, time, reasonCode, reason, checkedAt } | null   // null: no `revocation` object (an answer without the expansion)
export function problemReportingText(value) -> string|null   // controls and bidi overrides out, blank lines folded, cut to 2,000 characters
export function revocationName(cert) -> string|null          // the first DNS name that is no wildcard, else the first wildcard
export function revocationUrl(name, { after }) ; matchIssuance(items, { sha256, spkiSha256, notBefore, notAfter }) -> { item, by: 'certificate'|'issuance' } | null
export async function checkRevocation(cert, { fetchImpl, signal, now, cooldown /* lib/ctcert.js ctCooldown */, timeoutMs, maxPages })
  -> { status, name /* sent; null: nothing sent */, requests, matchedBy, revocation: { time, reasonCode, reason, checkedAt } | null, problemReporting, truncated, quota, error, errorKind, at }
  // only an abort rejects; nothing is sent for an expired certificate, one without a name, or during Cert Spotter's 429 cool-down
// lib/renewalplan.js (the page's Renewal readiness › Plan): fetchRenewalInfo(cert, { ca, directory: { url, hosts } | null, cache: Map | null, fetchImpl, signal, timeoutMs, now })
//   — the page asks ARI_DIRECTORIES (Let's Encrypt only: the others send no CORS header); the runner passes another CA's directory and a per-run cache of the
//   directories read; renewalInfo must be https and on the directory's host or `hosts`; the answer carries `certId` and `url`; a failed directory read is not cached
// ui/revocation.js — the strings ('rev.*'), light (no parser, no network)
export function reasonLabel(reason) ; RevokedLine(revocation, { className }) ; ProblemReporting(text, { className }) ; AriCell(ari, ariWindow) ; RevocationCell(revocation)
export function statusDetails(cert) -> [[label, value, mono]] ; generatedKeys() ; ARI_ERROR_CODES ; REVOCATION_UNKNOWN_CODES ; REASON_KEYS
// ui/revocation-card.js — the strings ('revc.*')
export function RevocationCard({ cert, ctx, cache, cacheKey, now }) -> HTMLElement
```
- **Cert Spotter's fields.** One request still: the CT tab's subdomain search expands `revocation` and `problem_reporting` (§3), and `lib/ctwatch.js` keeps them per certificate (§5.75). `revoked` is Cert Spotter's flag; the reason is the RFC 5280 code named (`reasonName`; a code the RFC does not define is none). The CA's problem-reporting text is the CA's own words: shown as text with its line breaks (CSS `pre-wrap`), never parsed into links or markup, after `problemReportingText`.
- **Is it revoked?** (Certificate › CT logs, a server certificate only: Cert Spotter lists no CA certificate). The card names the one name it would send and the cost (one of the 100 single-name searches an hour; up to three for a busy name), and sends nothing until **Ask Cert Spotter**; an expired certificate (Cert Spotter lists unexpired ones only) or one without a DNS name gets its note and no button. The answer is matched to the certificate here, by its SHA-256 (`cert_sha256`), or — Cert Spotter knowing only the precertificate — by the public key's SHA-256 and the exact validity ("matched by the public key and the exact validity period"); not on the pages read: "does not list this certificate" (a private CA's, a self-signed one, one issued in the last hours; "more than the 3 pages read" when cut). Revoked: "Revoked on DATE" (UTC), "Reason: …", replace it on every server, and the CA's contact folded; good: when Cert Spotter last read the CA's revocation list; a 429: until when the shared cool-down lasts. The lookup runs on its own controller, kept in the view's per-certificate cache (`certKey`), so a language switch or another tab shows its answer without a second request; another workspace or "Delete all local data" aborts and drops it. The module loads with the tab (views/cert.js `loadRevocationCard`), never on the start route.
- **Certificate estate** (§5.48, §6): the CLI's records as two columns, their counts and the details; the ARI errors and the reasons why a revocation is unknown are the CLI's codes (`_ARI_WHY`, `_REVOCATION_WHY`, kept equal by `tests/js/revocation.test.js`).
- **Privacy:** the page sends one certificate name to Cert Spotter on a click (lib/egress.js already lists Cert Spotter's issuances endpoint; `tests/js/egress.test.js` declares lib/revocation.js a call site); the CertIDs and CRL downloads are the runner's and the CLI's, from the machine they run on.
- **Tests:** `tests/js/crl.test.js` (the `crl_*` fixtures: two revoked serials with their reasons, an empty CRL, another CA's CRL, its scheme and the signed bytes; CRLs crafted with `der-builder.mjs`: a delta CRL, unknown critical extensions on the CRL and on an entry, onlySomeReasons, onlyCA, indirect, onlyAttribute, a relative name (no URL to compare), removeFromCRL, no reason code, an invalidity date, GeneralizedTime, v1, RSA-PSS parameters, malformed input, the serials filter), `tests/js/revocation.test.js` (Cert Spotter rows of `tests/js/ct-fake.mjs`: the fields, the problem-reporting text, the name and URL, matching by certificate and by issuance, good / revoked / not listed over pages / expired / no name, the shared 429 cool-down, errors, an abort; the page's words for every reason and CLI code), `tests/js/renewalplan.test.js` (a server-side directory, its hosts, the cache), `tests/js/ctwatch.test.js` (the expansions and the CSV columns), `tests/js/estate.test.js`, `tests/js/ds-tls.test.js` (§9), `tests/python/test_ari_revocation.py` (§7), and the offline `revocation` E2E suite (`tests/e2e/revocation.e2e.mjs`: the CT tab's lines, the CA's contact by keyboard, the CSV; Is it revoked? sending nothing before the click and then one GET with the name only, revoked and good, kept across a language switch and another tab, no card for a CA; the estate's columns, counts, details and CSV, none without the records; Turkish and dark at 375 / 320 px; no request leaves the page).

### 5.95 `lib/waivers.js`, `ui/waivers.js` — accepted risks and known certificates

A finding, a policy rule or a certificate someone decided to live with — for a reason, by an owner, until a day — so a nightly alarm does not stay red for what nobody will fix, and so it comes back on its own when that day has passed. One model for the app and the runner (§9 `--waivers`); kept in the workspace's `waivers` part (§5.39), carried by the hand-over file (§5.41) and exported from the Workspaces dialog as waivers.json, the runner's input. No endpoint: waivers leave the browser only in the hand-over file or the exported waivers.json.
```js
// lib/waivers.js — DOM-free; the clock is injected (`now`)
export const WAIVER_KINDS = ['finding', 'rule', 'cert'], WAIVERS_FORMAT = 'domainscope-waivers', WAIVERS_VERSION = 1, WAIVERS_MAX_CHARS = 65536, WAIVERS_MAX = 500,
  WAIVER_REASON_MAX = 200, WAIVER_OWNER_MAX = 80, WAIVER_MAX_DAYS = 366, WAIVER_DEFAULT_DAYS = 90, WAIVER_SOON_DAYS = 14, WAIVER_STATES = ['active', 'expiring', 'expired'],
  WAIVER_ERRORS = ['not-json', 'not-waivers', 'newer', 'too-large', 'too-many', 'not-object', 'kind', 'domain', 'ref', 'reason', 'owner', 'expires', 'too-far', 'created'],
  WAIVERS_I18N /* en, tr: the dialog, the lines and badges, the what-if planner, the Workspaces dialog's part, the errors ('wvr.*') */ ; class WaiverError { code }
// an entry: { id, kind, domain, ref, reason, owner, created, expires }
export function validateWaiver(entry, { now }) -> { waiver, error: null } | { waiver: null, error: { code, field } }
export function normalizeRef(kind, ref) -> string|null   // finding: a Domain Health check id, lower case; rule: a lib/policy.js rule id; cert: 64 lower-case hex (colons, spaces, a sha256: prefix dropped)
export function waiverKey(kind, domain, ref) ; waiverId(kind, domain, ref) -> 'w-' + 16 hex (FNV-1a 64): one waiver per item
export function sanitizeWaivers(list, { now }) -> { waivers, errors: [{ index, code, field }] }   // a later entry for the same item replaces an earlier one in place; ≤ 500
export function parseWaivers(textOrValue, { now }) -> { ok, waivers, errors }   // { format, v, waivers } or a bare list; ok false: not JSON, not a waivers file, newer, too large
export function readWaivers(text, { now }) -> waivers   // lenient (the workspace part)
export function waiversPartText(list) -> string ('' for none; WaiverError 'too-large' past 64 KiB, 'too-many' past 500) ; waiversFileText(list, { now, app }) -> indented waivers.json
export function addWaiver(list, input, { now }) -> { list, waiver, replaced }   // created now; an end date before today refused ('expires')
export function removeWaiver(list, id) ; mergeWaivers(list, incoming) -> { list, added, replaced } ; waiverCounts(list, { now }) -> { total, active, expiring, expired, next }
export function waiverEnd(w) -> ms /* the end of its last day, UTC */ ; waiverState(w, { now }) -> 'active'|'expiring'|'expired' ; isWaiverActive(w, { now })
export function matchWaiver(list, { kind, domain, ref | refs }, { now }) -> { waiver, active } | null   // the exact domain (a subdomain is not covered); an active one before an expired one
export function applyWaivers(items, list, { now, kind }) -> { kept, waived: [{ item, waiver }], expired: [{ item, waiver }] }   // expired ⊂ kept: they count again
export function healthWaivers(report, list, { now }) -> { ids: Set, applied: [{ check, waiver }], expired: [{ check, waiver }], until, byId: Map }   // errors and warnings only, never a name that does not exist
export function isWaivableCheck(check) ; defaultExpiry(now, days) ; maxExpiry(now) ; utcDay(now) ; addDays(day, days)
// ui/waivers.js — loaded on the first "Accept this risk…", "Accept…" or "Known certificate…" (and with the Workspaces dialog)
export function openWaiverDialog({ kind, domain, ref, subject, existing }) -> Promise<input|null>   // a Modal: what accepting does for its kind (a finding leaves the score, a rule's
                                                                                                      // cell reads "Accepted", a key is expected), the item, the domain, reason (required), owner, end date
export async function acceptRisk(input, state) -> { waiver, persisted } ; removeRisk(id, state) -> persisted ; currentWaivers(state) ; saveWaivers(list, state) ; waiverErrorText(code)
```
- **An entry.** `kind` finding (`ref`: a Domain Health check id such as `dmarc.policy-none`), rule (a policy rule id such as `transferLock`, §5.64) or cert (the SHA-256 of a certificate's public key — its SubjectPublicKeyInfo — or of the certificate: a known certificate, §5.75); `domain` exactly (a host name, normalized); `reason` 1–200 characters and `owner` 0–80 (controls, zero-width characters and every bidi control — the marks, embeddings, overrides and isolates, U+061C — out, whitespace collapsed: an imported file or hand-over cannot reorder what the page, the Workspaces dialog or a CSV shows); `created` an ISO time or null; `expires` the last day it applies (YYYY-MM-DD; an ISO time is read as its UTC day), required and at most 366 days ahead of the day it is read (one day of grace for a form in a time zone ahead of UTC). It applies to the end of that day, UTC; from then on it is **expired**: no longer applied, listed as expired, its item counts again. "Ending soon": 14 days or fewer left. An entry that cannot be read is left out and said — never applied, so its item counts.
- **The file.** `{ "format": "domainscope-waivers", "v": 1, "app", "exportedAt", "waivers": [ … ] }` (a bare list is read too; a later version is refused). The workspace part is the same JSON, compact and without `app` / `exportedAt`, sorted by domain, kind and ref.
- **Domain Health** (§5.78, §6): `healthWaivers` gives the report's accepted risks; the score, grade, light and counts leave them out (`scoreHealth(checks, { waived })`), the hero says how many and until when, with the score including them ("1 accepted risk (until 2026-12-15). With it, the score would be 89/100 (B)."); the problems card lists them apart with Remove, and "All checks" counts them apart on their category's card (a shield badge, never an error or a warning badge or colour); an expired one is a problem again with "Accept again…"; Copy summary (§5.32) and the customer report (§5.88) say "N accepted risks excluded". While a check runs, the report on screen is the previous one: its "Accept this risk…" and Remove are disabled until the new one lands. **Domain overview** (§5.46): its health card reads the same waivers and leaves them out alike — the same score, grade and light as Domain Health, the counts and the problems without them, the same lines —, and its Copy summary and report say "N accepted risks excluded" (the report names each with its waiver on the Health card). **Policy** (§5.64): a failed rule an active waiver accepts is `waived`. **CT** (§5.75): a known certificate is neither new nor unexpected; the tab matches the waivers when it draws its rows (`analyzeCt` `knownAt`), so the day after one ends its rows are flagged again and say "Accepted as known until DATE, expired: flagged again".
- **Tests:** `tests/js/waivers.test.js` (every refusal, the file and the part, expiry on an injected clock, matching, applyWaivers, a report's waivers, the list operations, the texts), `tests/js/healthv2.test.js` (the score without them, `full`, the what-if planner), `tests/js/policy.test.js` (the `waived` status, CSV, JSON), `tests/js/ctwatch.test.js` (known certificates, matched at `knownAt`), `tests/js/passport.test.js` (the overview's health card as Domain Health, the facts), `tests/js/sources.test.js` (Cert Spotter's key hash folded into crt.sh's twin), `tests/js/summary.test.js`, `tests/js/report.test.js` (both reports), `tests/js/workspace.test.js` and `tests/js/handover.test.js` (the part), `tests/js/ds-waivers.test.js` (§9), and the offline `waivers` E2E suite (`tests/e2e/waivers.e2e.mjs`: accept a finding by keyboard, the reason required, the hero, the "All checks" card, the summary, Accept and Remove disabled while a check runs, the Domain overview's health card with the same score, the what-if planner, kept across a reload and in Turkish, Remove, the end date passing on a moved clock; the Workspaces dialog's export, removal of the expired ones and import; the matrix's accepted cells, the rule dialog and CSV; the CT tab's known certificates, and one whose acceptance ended; 375 / 320 px in both languages and themes; nothing sent).

### 5.96 `lib/regwatch.js` — the registration watch (and the runner's change watch, §9)
A registrar, name server or lock change that breaks no policy rule is the first sign of a hijack, and was invisible: the portfolio showed each check on its own. DOM-free and pure; the Domain portfolio (§6 7c) and the runner's `watch` (§9) share it.
```js
export const RDAP_SEEN_VERSION = 1, RDAP_SEEN_MAX_CHARS = 524288   // §5.39 WORKSPACE_LIMITS.rdapSeen
export const TRANSFER_LOCK_STATUSES = ['client transfer prohibited', 'server transfer prohibited', 'transfer prohibited']
export const HOLD_STATUSES = ['server hold', 'client hold', 'pending delete', 'redemption period', 'pending transfer']
export const REG_CHANGE_CODES = ['unregistered', 'registered', 'registrar', 'registrar-name', 'lock-removed', 'lock-added', 'hold', 'status', 'ns',
  'ds-removed', 'ds-changed', 'ds-added', 'expiry-later', 'expiry-earlier'], REG_CHANGE_TONES /* bad, good or info per code */
export function registrationSnapshot(facts /* §5.63 portfolioFacts */) -> RegSnapshot
RegSnapshot = { state: 'ok'|'not-found'|null /* null: not known — no RDAP for the TLD, a lookup that failed */, registrar, ianaId, statuses /* lower case, RDAP spelling, sorted */,
  expires /* YYYY-MM-DD */, nameservers /* the registry's, sorted */, ds /* 'keyTag algorithm digestType' each, sorted; [] none; null not known */ }   // a part not known is null
export function diffRegistration(before, after) -> [{ code, tone: 'bad'|'good'|'info', item /* a status */, before, after, how? /* status: 'added'|'removed' */ }]   // in code order
export function worstTone(changes) -> 'bad'|'info'|'good'|null ; registrarKey(name) ; dsKey({ keyTag, algorithm, digestType }) -> '12345 13 2'
export function emptyRdapSeen() ; readRdapSeen(text) -> RdapSeen ; updateRdapSeen(seen, [{ domain, snapshot }], { now }) -> RdapSeen ; rdapSeenText(seen, { maxChars }) -> string
RdapSeen = { v: 1, domains: { <domain>: { at /* the check that read it */, state: 'ok'|'not-found', registrar, ianaId, statuses, expires, nameservers, ds } } }
export function seenChanges(entry, snapshot) -> { at, changes } | null   // null: no entry (the first check of the domain in the workspace)
```
- **The changes** (`diffRegistration`; a part not known on either side is not compared): `registrar` (bad) — another IANA Registrar ID; without an ID on both sides another name (case, punctuation and spacing aside); the same ID under another name is `registrar-name` (info) —; a transfer prohibition of `TRANSFER_LOCK_STATUSES` removed `lock-removed` (bad: whoever has the transfer code can move the domain), added `lock-added` (good); a status of `HOLD_STATUSES` arriving `hold` (bad: out of DNS, being lost, or a transfer under way); any other status added or removed `status` (info); the registry's name servers `ns` (bad); DS records all gone `ds-removed`, one gone with others there or new `ds-changed` (both bad), only new ones `ds-added` (info: a rollover publishes the new key first); the expiry later `expiry-later` (good: renewed), earlier `expiry-earlier` (info); the registry no longer holding the domain `unregistered` (bad), holding it again `registered` (info) — nothing else of the registration is compared then. The DS records come from DNS and compare on a check the registry could not answer.
- **The baseline** (the workspace part `rdapSeen`, as lib/ctwatch.js keeps `ctSeen`): `updateRdapSeen` gives each domain whose registry answered (it holds the domain, or answers 404) the check's snapshot and time; one whose registry could not be read keeps its entry as it was, and DS records a check could not read stay the last ones. `readRdapSeen` drops anything that is not an entry, entry by entry (a name not canonical, a time that is none, an unknown state; statuses in their compared spelling, host names in canonical form, at most 40 statuses, 26 name servers, 20 DS, a registrar's name cut at 200 characters, an IANA ID of digits). `rdapSeenText` keeps the JSON under 512 KiB, leaving out the domains read longest ago first; '' for an empty baseline (the workspace stores nothing).
- **The runner's `watch`** (`tools/ds/watch.mjs`, `tools/ds/watchdiff.mjs`, `tools/ds/authoritative.mjs`, §9) compares its reports' registrations with `diffRegistration` too (its tags REGISTRAR, LOCK, STATUS, NS, DS and EXPIRY), and adds the zone's own NS records, an expiry not renewed with less than 30 days left, the record sets and the name servers asked directly.
- Tests: `tests/js/regwatch.test.js` (the snapshot of a portfolio row, every code and its tone, several at once in order, the baseline: an update, a registry not read, DS not read, read back, hostile entries, the size cap, the changes since an entry); the view's helpers in `tests/js/portfolio-view.test.js`, its Copy summary line in `tests/js/summary.test.js`, the part in `tests/js/workspace.test.js` and `tests/js/handover.test.js`; `tests/e2e/regwatch.e2e.mjs` (offline).
