### 5.97 `lib/dmarchistory.js`, `ui/report-history.js` — the DMARC report history of a workspace (opt-in): trends, new senders, a roll-up across domains

Retention is what DMARC services price on (dmarcian, EasyDMARC, PowerDMARC, Red Sift, URIports, Mailhardener): a trend, a sender that appeared and an MSP's view across its customers need more than one drop. DOM-free and pure; browser only — nothing new is sent.
```js
export const HISTORY_VERSION = 1, HISTORY_DAYS = 400, RECENT_DAYS = 31, HISTORY_MAX_BYTES = 4 MiB /* = lib/workspace.js WORKSPACE_LIMITS.reportHistory */,
  HISTORY_PERIODS = [30, 90, 400], WEEK_BIN_AFTER = 92, NEW_BASELINE_DAYS = 7, NEW_WINDOW_DAYS = 30, SERVICE_MAX = 80,
  HISTORY_CLASSES /* = lib/dmarcreport.js SOURCE_CLASSES */, KNOWN_CLASSES = ['yours', 'third-party'], POLICIES = ['none', 'quarantine', 'reject'],
  DAY_FIELDS = ['msgs', 'dmarcPass', 'spfAligned', 'dkimAligned', 'quarantine', 'reject', 'unknownMsgs', 'knownFail'], RECENT_FIELDS /* the first six */,
  ROLLUP_VERDICTS = ['no-mail', 'enforced-losing', 'fix-first', 'ready', 'enforced'], ROLLUP_CSV_COLUMNS, TREND_CSV_COLUMNS
export function emptyHistory({ keep }) ; readHistory(text) ; sanitizeHistory(data) ; historyText(history) -> string /* '' when off and empty */ ; setKeep(history, on) ; forgetHistory(history, { now })
export function mergeReports(history, reports /* AggregateReport[] */, { now, classify }) -> { history, merged, duplicates, skipped: { old, future, cut, invalid }, domains }
export function reclassify(history, classify, { now, domains }) -> { history, changed }   // the same object when nothing changed
export function prune(history, { now, maxBytes }) -> { history, dropped: { recentDays, sources, days, domains }, bytes, text }
export function fitHistory(history, { now, maxBytes }) -> { history, text, dropped|null }   // the text every write stores: pruned first when over the cap
export function trend(history, domain, { days, now, bin }) -> { domain, from, to, bin: 'day'|'week', slots, totals, last }
export function newSince(history, domain, { now }) -> day|null ; newSources(history, domain, since) ; historySources(history, domain, { since })
export function rollup(history, { now, days }) -> { from, to, rows, totals } ; rollupVerdict(row) ; rollupCsvRows(rows) ; trendCsvRows(trend)
export function historyDomains(history) ; historySummary(history) ; reportHash(key) ; dayOf(value) ; addDays(day, n) ; isDay(s) ; utf8Length(text) ; daysSince(day, { now })
HistoryClassify = (domain, ip) => ({ cls, service, type, provisional } | null)
// ui/report-history.js (loaded with the History tab)
export function mountHistory(host, { ctx, read, preferred, onForget, classStyle, now }) -> { refresh(), destroy(), domain(), period() } ; resetHistoryPanel()
export function complianceBand(c) ; complianceStack(slot) ; volumeSegments(slot) ; barHeights(segs, { max, plot }) ; niceMax(v) ; labelIndexes(count, max) ; CHART_HEIGHTS ; STUB_PX ; VOLUME_SEGMENTS ; COMPLIANCE_BANDS ; VERDICT_LOOK ; SOURCE_CSV_COLUMNS
```
**The shape** (the workspace part `reportHistory`, §5.39, as the JSON text `historyText` writes, its keys in order; a text of another version is no history, and `sanitizeHistory` checks every entry on its own — a name not as stored, an address not in its normal form, a day that does not exist, a count that is not a whole number, a class or policy it does not know: each dropped or clamped, never trusted): `{ v: 1, keep, updatedAt, domains }`, per reported domain — the policy domain of each report (`policy_published.domain`), as `aggregateDmarc` groups them, so it covers the header-from names under it: `days` (a UTC day → the counts of `DAY_FIELDS`; `unknownMsgs` the mail of unknown senders, `knownFail` that of your servers and authorized third parties that failed DMARC — what p=reject would refuse; kept 400 days), `sources` (an address → `{ first, last, msgs, passMsgs, cls, checked?, service, type }`, dropped 400 days after `last`), `recent` (a day → an address → its six counts, for the last 31 days), `policy` (`{ p, sp, pct, testing?, seenAt }` of the report that ends last), `seen` (a day → the FNV-1a 64 hashes of the 'org|report_id' keys filed that day, kept 400 days), `cut` (the newest day `prune` dropped to fit) and `checked` (the last day the domain's sources were classed against its current SPF).
**Merging** (`mergeReports`): a report is filed under the UTC day of its date_range begin; one whose hash the domain has seen counts once (in the same drop or a later one; the same id from another reporter or for another domain counts); one older than 400 days, more than a day ahead of the clock or filed on or before `cut` is not taken. Each record adds to its day, to its source (first and last day, messages) and, in the last 31 days, to its recent row; the class `classify` gives the source decides whether its mail is unknown or a known failure. A class marked `provisional` (the reports and the server list only: the domain's SPF was not read) fills a class the history does not have, or replaces one of the same kind, never one the SPF decided (`checked`); a service is never erased. Never kept: the report XML, file names, envelope_to, the reporters' names, contacts and notes, a report id (only its hash).
**Classing again** (`reclassify`): when the page classes the sources again (the SPF landed, the server list changed, Identify senders named more), the history's classes and services follow, and the recent days of a source whose class changed are corrected by the delta of its rows; older days keep the classes they were kept with.
**The cap** (`prune`): the window first (days, reports seen and sources past 400 days, recent rows past 31, a domain with nothing left), then, while the text is over `maxBytes` (UTF-8 bytes, 4 MiB): the oldest recent days (every domain's at once), then the sources with the fewest messages, then the oldest days with the reports filed on them (`cut` moves past them, so they are not taken again). Each stage goes on until the text fits, and the next starts only when it has nothing left — no source goes while a recent day is kept, no day while a source is (an entry's weight is counted exactly — an object's last entry takes no comma with it — and the text is measured after each round) —; with the switch on, a byte is left for turning it off ("false" is a byte longer than "true"); a domain with nothing left goes, and a cap no domain fits leaves only the switch. A pruned text is always one the workspace part keeps (`sanitizePart` keeps it whole or not at all), and **every write** stores `fitHistory`'s text: `historyText`, pruned first when it is over the cap — so classing the sources again (`checked`, the services Identify senders names) or turning the switch off at the cap trims the oldest details instead of losing the whole history.
**Reading it back:** `trend` — one slot a day over the last 30 or 90 days up to today (UTC), a week over 400 (`WEEK_BIN_AFTER`; the last week ends today), each with its counts, `reportedDays` (0 is no report, not "no mail"), its compliance and unknown share, and the period's totals; `newSince` — 30 days back, but never before the domain's history covers 7 days (a first drop calls no sender new); `rollup` — every domain over the period, the most mail first: volume, compliance, the unknown share, the known failures, the policy, the senders seen and the new ones, `checked`, and `rollupVerdict` (no mail; p=reject at 100 % and not t=y: `enforced`, or `enforced-losing` when known sources fail; else `fix-first` or `ready`).
**The view** (views/reports.js, §6 7b): "Keep a summary of these reports in this workspace", a switch in the drop card, off by default like Remember origins (§5.70): while it is off nothing is written, not even a record in IndexedDB. Turned on, the reports read in the tab are kept at once; then each drop's DMARC reports are kept once the domain on screen has its SPF (or could not get it), with the classes the page gives them then (`historyClassifier`: lib/dmarcreport.js `classifySources` per domain, a domain classed when the history first asks about it; provisional unless `classesChecked` — every SPF record its classes need was read —; the service `identifySource` names, unless only the network names it). A toast says what was added, what was there already and what was not taken (`keepMessages`); the SPF landing, a server list change and Identify senders class the kept domains again a moment later (`HISTORY_SYNC_MS`; flushed when the view is left). Every write goes through `fitHistory`, and a write it had to trim says so ("The history reached its size limit (4 MB): its oldest details were dropped.", `historyTrimmed`). Turning it off asks first and keeps what is there. The History tab (`loadHistoryPanel`, loaded on its first show) is there while the switch is on or anything is kept — alone after a reload —, and the switch and the tab follow every change the view did not write (another tab's — turned off and on again too —, a workspace file that replaced the workspace): they are drawn again whenever the stored text is not the one they were drawn from.
**The tab** (`mountHistory`): one row of filters (the domain, the most mail first; the period: 30, 90 or 400 days); the domain's card — messages, compliance banded like the DMARC head (98 % and 90 %), the unknown senders' share, the days with a report, the last published policy, "No report for <domain> in the last N days. The last one is from <date>." —; two bar charts in inline SVG drawn to their box's width (a ResizeObserver; the axes in HTML, so their text never stretches): the messages of each day stacked by result (passed in the accent, failed from unknown senders and forwarders in slate, failed from your servers and third parties in red — checked for colour-blind separation —, a 2 px surface gap, 4 px rounded tops, a legend) and the day's compliance in its band's colour (`complianceStack`: at least `STUB_PX` = 2 px, so a day of 0 % is a stub in the error band, not a gap; only a day without mail has no bar). A bar answers the pointer, a tap and the arrow keys (Home / End; the plot is focusable and its label says how) with a tooltip and a polite live region, and the same values are in "The days as a table" with a CSV (`TREND_CSV_COLUMNS`). Then the sending addresses with the service behind them, the class, the first and last day, the messages and the pass rate, "New since <date>" on those first seen since `newSince` (and "Only the new ones"), a CSV; the roll-up (`rollup`: volume, compliance, policy, the unknown senders' share, the verdict — "SPF not checked yet" under a domain whose classes rest on the reports alone —, the last report; a domain shows its trend; a CSV of `ROLLUP_CSV_COLUMNS`); what is kept and for how long, "Keeping is off" when it is, and **Forget report history** (asked first; the switch stays as it is). "Delete all local data" clears it with the workspace. Below 600 px every table is a card of labelled lines and a badge wraps instead of widening it.
**Privacy:** sending addresses and counts are written to IndexedDB only while the switch is on; they leave the browser only inside a workspace hand-over file (§5.41; encrypted when a password is given), whose import says that it holds a history and that it switches keeping on (ui/workspace-panel.js `importSummary`). Nothing is sent: the history is made from the reports read in the tab and the classes the page already has.
**Tests:** `tests/js/dmarchistory.test.js` (the UTC day of a report, the counts of a day and of a source, the classes behind the unknown mail and the known failures, a report counted once — the same drop, a later one, the same id from another reporter or for another domain —, the window and a cut day, the recent rows and the policy, nothing it must never keep, the input never changed; classing again with the recent days corrected and the older kept, provisional against checked, a service never erased; pruning in its order and under the cap, a pruned text the workspace keeps, no day dropped while a source is left and no source while a recent day is (domains of a single source or recent day), room left to turn the switch off; `fitHistory` — a capped history classed again against the SPF with services named, or turned off, stored trimmed and never lost —; the stored text read back entry by entry, a stray `__proto__`; the trend by day and by week, the new senders with the baseline and the window, the roll-up's verdicts and CSV; the fixture mailbox merged twice to the same text), `tests/js/reports-view.test.js` (`classesChecked`, the classifier, `keepMessages`, the words the head and the report share, the report's facts without a server of the list, `historyTrimmed`, the panel's pure parts — a day of 0 % compliance a stub in the error band, no mail no bar —), `tests/js/workspace.test.js` and `tests/js/handover.test.js` (the part, sealed with the rest), `tests/js/workspace-ui.test.js` (the import summary), `tests/e2e/dmarchistory.e2e.mjs` (§8).

### 5.98 `lib/runreport.js`, `lib/monitor.js`, `lib/monitorfetch.js`, `lib/monitorsummary.js` — the Monitoring view over the runner's results (ROADMAP P2.2)
The headless runner (§9) commits a report per check every night (`results/NAME.json`) and, with `--history DIR`, one line per target and check (`results/history/YYYY-MM.jsonl`); today that history sat unread in git. The Monitoring view (§6) reads both, from a folder in the browser or from the repository on GitHub, into one row per target, three tiles, the change timeline and the sparklines. All four modules are DOM-free and load with the view; the runner imports `lib/runreport.js` and `lib/monitor.js` too.
```js
// lib/runreport.js — the report as data, one copy of its rules for the runner (--baseline) and the page
export const DS_TOOL = 'domainscope-ds', DS_VERSION = '1.0.0', AUDIT_STATUSES = ['pass', 'fail', 'unknown', 'waived']
export const TARGET_CHECKS = { health, subdomains, ct, drift, renew, dane, audit, tls: tlsTargetProblem, takeover: takeoverTargetProblem, watch: watchTargetProblem }
export function reportProblem(doc, command = null) -> string|null
  // not this tool, another major version, (with `command`) another command / (without) no command word, `options` not an
  // object, no `targets` list, a target without `target`, or a list its command's comparison walks damaged (with its index);
  // a command these rules do not know (a newer runner's): the envelope and the targets' names only
export function tlsTargetProblem(x), takeoverTargetProblem(x) -> string|null

// lib/monitor.js
export const HISTORY_VERSION = 1, HISTORY_MAX_CHANGES = 20, HISTORY_KEEP_MONTHS = 13, HISTORY_FILE_RE /* YYYY-MM.jsonl */,
  CHANGE_TONES = ['bad', 'good', 'info', 'quiet'], MONITOR_COMMANDS /* health, ct, tls, takeover, audit, subdomains, drift, renew, dane, watch */,
  MONITOR_MAX_BYTES = 64 MB, MONITOR_MAX_REPORTS = 60, MONITOR_MAX_LINES = 250000, MONITOR_RECENT_DAYS = 7, MONITOR_WARN_DAYS = 21,
  STALE_MS = 36 h, SPARK_MAX_POINTS = 60, MONITOR_FILE_ERRORS, HISTORY_LINE_PROBLEMS, TIMELINE_CSV_COLUMNS, TLS_WORST, TIMELINE_TONES
export function checkCompleted(command, target) -> boolean|null
  // health: no lookup failed; subdomains: the DNS answered (no DNS_UNREACHABLE) and a passive source did (exact: none asked);
  // ct: a source answered (one of two is a read); drift: the budget lasted and no record set's lookup failed; renew: a verdict;
  // dane: no endpoint's lookup failed; audit: every rule checked; tls: the host's DNS answered (NOERROR or NXDOMAIN; a failed
  // lookup checked nothing, its endpoints carried from the baseline or not); takeover: every lookup answered; watch: the registry read (not carried, not
  // failed: a registry without RDAP is a read) and every record set answered; another command: null
export function minDaysLeftOf(command, target, now) -> number|null   // tls: the certificates served this run; ct: the current ones
  // (the CT watch's `current`; a report without it: the ones still valid); whole days, floor, as the runner counts them
export function targetFacts(command, target, at) -> { ok, score?, grade? /* health */, minDaysLeft? }
export function historyLines(doc, { run }) -> HistoryLine[]   // one per target of the report; one per target of the baseline it
  // no longer checks whose changes it lists (`gone: true`); `at` = the run's end (finishedAt, else startedAt); `run` only a
  // GitHub Actions run link (runLink)
// HistoryLine: { v: 1, at, command, target, ok, score?, grade?, minDaysLeft?, counts: { bad /* the changes that count with a bad
//   tone */, info /* every other one listed */ }, changes: [{ tag, tone, item }] /* ≤ 20, the ones that count first */, run?, gone? }
//   an item names what moved: a finding or rule id, a host, an RRset key, an issuer, a certificate (its CT id or SHA-256), an
//   endpoint (address|port), a takeover risk's key; nothing else of the report is kept (no change's words, no value before or after)
export function historyFileName(at) -> 'YYYY-MM.jsonl' (UTC), monthIndex(nameOrTime) -> number|null
export function staleHistoryFiles(names, now, keep = 13) -> names   // month files the runner deletes: this month and the twelve before it stay
export function recentHistoryFiles(names, now, months) -> names     // the last N months, never one to come, newest first
export function runLink(value) -> string|null, repoOfRun(link) -> { server, owner, repo }|null
export function readHistoryLine(value) -> { line } | { why }        // why: HISTORY_LINE_PROBLEMS (not-object, version, at, command, target, ok, counts, changes, value)
export function parseHistory(text) -> { lines, skipped: [{ line, why }] }   // a BOM and CRLF fine, empty lines no lines, a bad line skipped and counted
export function lineKey(line), mergeLines(...lists) -> lines   // one per run, target and command (the first given wins), oldest first, the newest MONITOR_MAX_LINES
export function pruneLines(lines, since) -> lines
export function readReport(text, { name }) -> { ok: true, report: { name, id, command, startedAt, finishedAt /* ms */, doc, lines } } | { ok: false, error, detail? }
  // error: too-large, not-json, not-report, version (detail: the version), damaged (detail: reportProblem's words); `lines`: its own history lines
export function fileKind(file) -> 'report' /* *.json */ | 'history' /* *.jsonl */ | 'summary' /* *.md: left alone */ | 'other'   // pasted text: a report when it is one JSON value
export function emptyMonitor() -> { reports, lines, files }
export function readMonitorFiles(data, files) -> { data, added: { reports, lines, history }, problems, duplicates, capped, skippedLines }
  // a new dataset; the same report again a duplicate, the same month again replaces its entry; other files: not-results;
  // a history file of nothing but bad lines: empty-history
export function allLines(data) -> lines   // the history files' lines, then each report's own (the runs the history lacks); merged
  // once per dataset (a dataset is never changed in place), the list shared and frozen
export function cellFacts(command, target, report, now, changes) -> { command, ms, ok, stale, from: 'report', report, changes: { bad, info }, ... }
  // health: score, grade, errors, warnings (a finding an accepted risk covers, `waiver`, is neither: the score leaves it out too); ct: current, minDaysLeft, certs, newIssuers (the run's ISSUER changes that appeared),
  // unexpected, revoked; tls: endpoints, worst (TLS_WORST: EXPIRED, UNTRUSTED, NAME_MISMATCH, NOT_DEPLOYED, EXPIRING, TLS_ERROR, TIMEOUT, CLOSED, OK, SKIPPED),
  // problems, minDaysLeft, certs; takeover: risks (medium and worse), low, worst; audit: fail (a rule not checked that failed when
  // last checked too), unknown, pass, security { score, max }. certs: each certificate seen (tls: served; ct: the current ones) with
  // its name, notAfter, days left from `now` and what tells it apart; minDaysLeft: the soonest of them
export function expiringCertificates(rows, { days = 21 }) -> [{ target, command, name, notAfter, daysLeft }]   // the certificates the
  // rows' tls and ct cells saw (the cells the table's filter and each row's days left read, so the three agree), soonest first: a
  // report's cell each certificate, a history cell its soonest expiry (named by its target, notAfter null); a certificate seen twice
  // (by tls and ct, by two targets) once — the same serial number from the same CA (when both name it) with the same expiry (crt.sh
  // gives no SHA-256; a precertificate shares its certificate's serial), else the same SHA-256, else the same CT id —, named by
  // the served one when tls saw it
export function seriesOf(lines) -> { score, days }   // health's score; tls's soonest expiry when tls checks the target, else ct's; oldest first
export function sparkPoints(values, { width = 96, height = 24, domain }) -> { points /* 'x,y …' */, last }
export function monitorRows(data, { now, recentDays = 7 }) -> rows   // { target, cells: { [command]: cell }, commands, ms, incomplete,
  // bad7, minDaysLeft, lastChange, series }; a cell from the newest report naming the target, else (or when its line is newer) from
  // the command's newest history line ("from the history": its days left are the line's less the whole days since it was written,
  // what its report would say now); a command whose newest line is a "gone" line has none, and a target left with none is no
  // row; a cell older than the newest report or line by STALE_MS is stale (did not run since); minDaysLeft: the soonest of its tls
  // and ct cells; worst first: a check that did not complete, a bad change in 7 days, the soonest expiry under 21 days, then by name
export function monitorTiles(rows) -> { targets, bad: targets[], expiring: expiringCertificates(rows), incomplete: [{ target, command, stale, ms }] }
  // from the rows alone: each tile counts what its filter shows
export function rowMatches(row, filter /* all, bad, expiring, incomplete */) -> boolean
export function timelineEntries(data) -> [{ ms, at, command, target, tag, tone, item, counts, text, run }]   // newest first; a run whose
  // report is open gives its changes' words and whether they counted, the history alone the tag, the tone and the item
export function filterTimeline(entries, { command, target, tone /* all, bad, good, info (info and quiet) */ }) -> entries
export function timelineCsv(entries) -> string   // lib/export.js toCsv: a BOM, CRLF, spreadsheet-safe cells
export function latestRun(data) -> string|null, monitorSummaryFacts(rows, tiles, data) -> facts   // names only; a stale check with
  // its last run (`since`); the newest check the last line's or a report's (no list spread into a call's arguments: a year of 200
  // targets is ~220,000 lines)

// lib/monitorfetch.js — the GitHub source (§3: CORS checked 2026-10-08 and 2026-10-09)
export const GITHUB_WEB, GITHUB_API = 'https://api.github.com', GITHUB_API_VERSION = '2022-11-28', GITHUB_RESULTS_DIR = 'results',
  GITHUB_HISTORY_DIR = 'history', GITHUB_MAX_FILES = 30, GITHUB_HISTORY_MONTHS = 3, GITHUB_MONTH_CHOICES = [1, 3, 6, 13],
  GITHUB_ISSUE_LABEL = 'domainscope', GITHUB_TOKEN_URL, GITHUB_TOKEN_DOCS /* links the user opens */, GITHUB_FETCH_ERRORS
  // repo, token, auth (401), forbidden (403), not-found (404), rate-limited (429, or 403 with X-RateLimit-Remaining 0), http,
  // network, timeout, response, empty
export class GithubFetchError { code, params: { status?, detail? /* GitHub's message, plain, ≤ 200 */, resetAt? } }   // never the token
export function parseRepo(text) -> { owner, repo }|null   // owner/repo, a github.com URL or a clone address
export function cleanToken(token) -> string|null           // trimmed, 20–255 printable characters, no white space inside
export function repoLinks({ owner, repo }) -> { issues /* open, labelled domainscope */, actions, results }|null
export async function fetchResults(repoText, token, { fetchImpl, signal, months = 3, issue = false, now, onProgress, timeoutMs = 20000 })
  -> { owner, repo, files: [{ name, text, source: 'github' }], skipped: { tooLarge, overCap }, history: { months, available },
       issue: { number, title, url, updatedAt, comments }|null, issueError, rate: { remaining, resetAt }, requests }
  // the listing of results/ (and of results/history/ when it is there), the last `months` month files, then the reports by name,
  // at most 30 files a read (larger than MONITOR_MAX_BYTES by the listing's size: never fetched), each GET raw, one at a time;
  // the open issue only when asked, a failure of it an `issueError`, never the read's; the token in a local variable for that
  // read only, sent as `Authorization: Bearer` to api.github.com alone (credentials omit, no referrer, no-store, redirect: error)

// lib/monitorsummary.js
export function monitorSummary(facts, opts) -> SummaryDoc   // §5.32
export const MONITOR_SUMMARY_I18N
```
**History and pruning.** The runner writes the lines (`tools/ds/history.mjs`, §9) and deletes month files older than 13 months; the page reads every month file it is given, a GitHub read the last 3 by default. The two never disagree on a line: both go through `historyLines` / `readHistoryLine`, and a report's own lines (the night the history may not have yet) merge with the history's by run, target and command.
**Privacy.** Files are read in the browser and kept in the view's module memory only (a reload, Forget, another workspace or "Delete all local data" drop them); nothing is sent from them. A GitHub read sends the repository's path and the token to api.github.com only, after a click (`lib/egress.js`: the `github` service, `repository` + `apiToken`); the token field is read once and emptied, and the token is never stored, logged, put in a URL or an error. The Copy summary names targets and certificates only; the link is the bare `#/monitor`.
**Tests:** `tests/js/monitor.test.js` (the history line from a report, the soonest expiry, each command's completion, the month files the runner deletes and the page reads, run links, history parsing with a bad line skipped and why, merging and pruning, a dataset's lines merged once, reports read with the runner's own rules — the same verdict as `baselineProblem` —, a results folder, the cap, rows, the history standing in for a report and a target no longer checked, the tiles, the history alone or a report left out (the tile, its filter and the summary name the same certificates; a line's days left counted from now, as a report's), a certificate seen by tls and ct once (its serial and CA: a crt.sh row without SHA-256, a precertificate; else its SHA-256), the timeline and its filters, the CSV, the sparklines, the summary's facts, also over 160,200 lines), `tests/js/monitorfetch.test.js` (a fake GitHub API: the repository and the token, the listing, the months, the cap, a file too large, the issue and a token that may not read issues, every refusal, a redirect, a timeout, a stop; the token never in a URL, an error or the result), `tests/js/monitor-view.test.js` (the view's helpers over the fixture folder, the Copy summary in both languages — one report, the history alone, a stale check's day —, the badges, the repository of the links, every key it builds), the offline `monitor` E2E suite (§8).


## 6. UI (views)

Hash routing `#/<view>?param=...` (shareable: e.g. `#/lookup?name=example.com&type=MX`, `#/global?name=www.example.com&type=A`); a view may have one-word sub-pages, `#/<view>/<page>?…` (`parseRoute().sub`, `ctx.sub`; `setParams` and `shareUrl` keep it; a sub-page never brings a kept result back): `#/change/check`. Navigation groups (`lib/shellnav.js` NAV_GROUPS, §5.29; a view's `group` in app.js `VIEWS`): Discover (subdomains, domain, zone), Certificates (scan, cert, renew, estate), DNS tools (global, lookup, bulk, change), IP addresses (ip, ptr, retire), Mail & domain (health, reports, portfolio), Setup & info (inventory, about; “Workspace” names the customer workspaces, §5.39); a view with an unknown group is listed under "More tools". Views load lazily; when a view's module fails to load because the page belongs to an earlier deploy (`confirmStaleModule` in app.js: a missing export, or a failed fetch while the browser is online and this page's own `v/<commit>/assets/js/app.js` answers 404), the page body offers **Reload page**. Offline or on a dropped connection the same fetch failure keeps the plain network error with Retry and never claims an update. Once the failed module's own URL (named in Chrome's and Firefox's message) answers 2xx again, `moduleReloadReason` says `'stuck'`: the browser keeps a failed module fetch for the rest of the document (Chrome never fetches that URL again in it), so Retry and a revisit offer **Reload page** with a hint saying so (`shell.viewStuck`), and a DoH / Globalping module or the workspace dialog stuck that way shows that hint once as a toast. A stale DoH / Globalping module, or a scan whose wordlist tier, locale pack or engine module failed to load in a page whose `v/<commit>/` is gone, shows the same hint once as a toast. Every "Reload page" goes through `ui/pwa.js` `reloadPage()` (a waiting service worker takes over first, §5.35).

**Loading.** `index.html` links `style.css` only and modulepreloads app.js's static graph. `VIEWS[]` (app.js) gives each view its stylesheets (`css`, paths under `assets/css/`): they are injected as `<link rel="stylesheet">` resolved against app.js (so they follow `v/<commit>/`), before the view mounts, kept for the page's life and ordered by `VIEW_CSS_ORDER` whatever the visiting order; a sheet that cannot load leaves the view unstyled, never unusable, and a view whose module fails shows its message only once the stylesheets have settled too. The discovery engine (`ENGINE_MODULES`: scanner, sources, doh, dnswire, permute) is imported when a scan starts and modulepreloaded once the browser is idle on Subdomains and SSL Targets (`VIEWS[].preload`; not offline or with Save-Data); `lib/ipintel.js` loads on the first "Look up owner". On Subdomains the run's progress panel and results (`ui/subdomains-run.js`: the result tabs, the Hosts exports, the ORIGIN and sweep cards, the Copy summary facts and the strings only the results use; `ui/locale-evidence.js`, the evidence banner SSL Targets imports too) load with the DoH client on the first scan and are modulepreloaded with the engine. A module loaded on first use that fails to load (`views/subdomains.js` `loadOnFirstUse`, behind `runScanner` and `networkOwner`) calls `ctx.checkOutdated` first, so a tab left open across a deploy offers the reload instead of only the failed scan or lookup. zoneparse and x509 load with the views that need them (Zone File; Certificate / SSL Targets). `tests/js/start-route.test.js` holds the start route (index.html, boot.js, style.css, app.js's graph, the Subdomains graph and stylesheet) under a gzip budget of 370 KB (≈ 332 KB once a Subdomains scan's progress and results — `ui/subdomains-run.js`, with the result tabs `lib/subtabs.js`, the exports `lib/export.js` and the strings only the results use — load with its first scan, leaving the start route the search page alone; ≈ 365 KB before that once the Copy summary builders and texts of every view but the start view moved to `lib/summary.js`, which loads with the first view that has one — `ui/view-summaries.js`, §5.32 —, with `lib/summarycore.js` left on the start route; ≈ 379 KB before that with all of wave 4: the request meter and log, which count from the first request, and the senders' notes, §5.54, the new tools' navigation entries, FileDrop's `maxFiles`, one-decimal shares and a view's sub-pages, DMARC & TLS reports' own builder already loading with its view — `lib/reportsummary.js` —; ≈ 368 KB with wave 3's Copy summary builders of Renewal readiness, Retire an IP and the Domain overview and their navigation entries; ≈ 359 KB with the customer workspaces: the workspace store, its first-run migration and IndexedDB backend and the header switcher load before the first view, which reads its inventory at mount; ≈ 334 KB with wave 2's shell, page session, Copy summary, job progress and Subdomains tabs; ≈ 258 KB before them, ≈ 368 KB before the lazy engine) and keeps the heavy modules out of it.

**Installable app and offline.** The Pages bundle registers `sw.js` (§5.35) and links a web app manifest in the UI language, so browsers offer to install DomainScope; the development checkout registers nothing. With the worker in control every view opens offline. Certificate (parsing, the sample), Certificate estate (the CLI's reports), Zone File (import, lint, origins, the command), the DNS change request (the form, its checks and every output; its Read and the check page say in place what waits for a connection), DMARC & TLS reports (reading and classifying the reports; the SPF line says it was not checked), Servers and About need no network (`VIEWS[].offline`); offline, every other view shows a note between its header and body ("You are offline", what it needs the network for, links to the tools that work offline), and `ctx.requireOnline()` — called by every network action (Scan, Look up, Check, Run, CT Load, CAA / CT / DANE checks, the Live check, Verify, the MTA-STS check, owner and reverse-IP lookups) — says so in a toast and sends nothing (one such toast at a time: another click replaces it rather than stacking copies). A check a view starts by itself (the Certificate view's CAA check, and its CT search for a public CA, when their tab opens) calls `ctx.requireOnline({ quiet: true })`: offline it sends nothing and the panel says so in place (`cert.caa.offline` / `cert.ct.offline`, `data-offline="auto"`), without the toast — the user clicked nothing; the panel's button then runs it (and warns) as usual. A run on arrival (Lookup, Global DNS, Domain Health, IP Intel: `start({ auto: true })`) — a shared link, or a link from another view that carries params, such as a host name's DNS Lookup link — is quiet the same way: offline it fills the form and sends nothing, and the page's note says why. A click on the view's own button, or a new query on the view already open (`update()`), still gets the toast. Toasts stay at four on screen: past that the oldest timed one goes, never a sticky one (timeout 0, such as "Update ready — Reload"). A new deploy is announced by "Update ready — Reload". About › Privacy says what the worker keeps and what it never caches. Views:
0. **subdomains** "Subdomains" (**default route**, `#/subdomains?domain=…[&tab=overview|hosts|origins|sources]`; the brand link and About's Start button open it): domain(s) in, every discoverable subdomain out. Options: wordlist level **Off / Small / Smart (recommended, default) / Large / Huge** with exact counts (`wordlistInfo()`), the locale packs the typed domain gets and time estimates (candidates ÷ 120 queries/s at the full sweep width of 24, scaled down for a lower Settings value), and a plan line (≈ queries per domain, custom / learned / pack shares, per-domain caps); under Advanced options: languages / markets (auto from the domain ending — for a TLD without a pack of its own, from the scan's evidence, §5.89 —, a manual pack list, or none; remembered), custom wordlist (textarea + `.txt` file, accepted / rejected counts from `parseCustomWordlist`, this tab only, Clear), learned names (opt-in switch, off by default, with the count, Forget; never used at Off), permutations on/off with a budget (500 / 1,500 / 5,000; the switch also drives the recursive round), origin hints on/off, passive sources with quota notes, include expired, extra hostnames, DoH chain. A shared link (`run=1`) pre-fills the domain and asks before scanning. While running: a progress bar whose label names the stage, and stage pills in `SCAN_STAGES` order with per-stage counts. Results in four tabs (§5.31 `lib/subtabs.js`) under the run's header card (title, time, progress bar, the zone-file banner, the market packs the evidence added and why (§5.89), the cancelled / failed notice), each tab label with a live count: **Overview** — the stat cards (a click filters the host table and opens Hosts with the keyboard focus on its tab), the summary alerts (nothing found, sources that failed with a link to Sources, dangling CNAMEs, the Cloudflare count with a link to Origins, wildcard parents, scanner warnings; the tab counts the warnings and errors), a technique bar ("how the names were found": DNS records / wordlist / permutations / deeper level / passive sources), a wordlist usage line from `options.wordlist` (served level, packs — those picked from evidence marked so, or "no market pack" when the evidence pointed to none —, custom / learned tried vs found, fallback), the **Takeover risks** card (§5.73: CNAME chains ending at a released service resource and CNAME / NS / MX / SPF targets in a domain nobody holds, on demand — nothing is sent before its button —, with "⚠ n/a" and Retry, a CSV export and an optional Globalping page check) and a CTA that opens SSL Targets for the same domain; **Hosts** — copy all names / resolving only / `names.txt` / CSV / JSON and the host table (name → DNS Lookup link, origin badges, classification, IPs; on a phone each row is a card in which a host name wraps only after a dot — `hostNameNodes`: one unbreakable run per label, a `<wbr>` between — or inside a label too long for the line on its own, and an IP never breaks); **Sources** — the stage pills, the per-source status (`sourceHealthSummary`, quota explanations; a screen reader hears each new status line and the “still fetching” note from the run's header whichever tab is open) and the free limit of each source asked, then **Related domains in the same certificates** (§5.56, a run that reads CT); **Origins** — for proxied hosts an **Origin** panel ("Origin servers behind the proxy"), or why there is none (candidates are looked for at the end of the scan, no host hides its origin, the scan did not finish): origin networks (/24 · /48) with their DNS-only hosts, per proxied host its resolver-leak answers ("answered by <resolver>") and history ("seen by <source> · last <date>"), read from the structured reason fields, other SPF / MX / sibling hints, and the sweep command for **Linux / macOS** or **Windows PowerShell** (built from `cliTargets` / `cliNames` with `buildSweepCommand`, dropped entries counted; over 200 names it reads `-n proxied-names.txt`, offered as a download next to the command, and a target list still too long for one line reads `-t proxied-targets.txt`, offered the same way) with copy and a download link for the CLI. Hosts is the automatic tab once a host is listed (Sources before that while the run is live, Overview when it ended empty); an automatic move waits while the keyboard focus is inside the tabs (a focused tab, a tapped panel) and happens once the focus leaves them. A tab the user picks (a click, also on the tab already shown, ←/→/Home/End with a roving tabindex, a stat card, a link) stays for that run, goes into the URL as `tab=` next to `domain` (replaceState; after a return through the nav link, which has no `domain`, the run's domains are written with it) and comes back after a language switch or a visit to another view (the page session keeps it too); a new scan starts on the automatic tab and drops `tab=`, and an edited `tab=` opens that tab without a re-mount (`update`). Every panel is built up front, so a live run fills the hidden ones as well. At ≤ 480 px the four tabs share the row in equal columns with the count under the label.
   Later additions:
   - **Live rows:** while the wordlist, permutation and recursive stages run, `onFound` hits appear at once as "resolving…" rows and are replaced by the full record at the resolve stage.
   - **Stage pills:** they show which passive sources were still fetching when the sweep started (`sourcesStillRunning`).
   - **Plan line:** a query range from `estimateQueries`.
   - **Origin panel:**
     - per proxied host, its `originCandidates` in order: remembered (the origin map, §5.70), zone file, resolver leak, sibling domain ("same name as <sibling>"), history, then only the related networks;
     - first, **Remembered origins**: each proxied host's remembered origins, and a stale entry of one of them muted ("stale since <date>, not used"), with a link to Servers › Origin map;
     - per network, whether the command sweeps the whole /24 or only its addresses (and why), a **shared hosting / cloud** badge with a warning, and **Look up owner** (`describeNetwork`, one RIPEstat request on click);
     - an **Exclude addresses** box (→ `buildSweepCommand({ exclude })`). It is kept per run for the page session, so it survives a re-mount. The JSON export's `origin.cliSuggestion` is the panel's POSIX command with these exclusions (`originExport`), and `origin.exclude` reports what they did;
     - a tip to scan sister domains together;
     - on each IPv4 network, **Reverse DNS sweep**: a link to `#/ptr?target=<network>&focus=<registrable domain of its first host>` that only fills the Reverse DNS form (the user presses Sweep); on a shared cloud / hosting network (whose other addresses are other customers') **Reverse DNS of its N addresses**, with only the network's own IPv4 addresses as the target.
   - **Names from a reverse DNS sweep** (`state.session.namesScanIntent` = `{ v: 1, target: 'subdomains', source: 'ptr', names, domains, label, mode: 'exact', at }`, one-shot, memory only, honoured for `NAMES_INTENT_MAX_AGE` = 60 s): `namesFromIntent` re-validates the names (they come from PTR records; at most `NAMES_HANDOFF_MAX` = 4,000), the box gets the domains, and a chip ("N names from the reverse DNS sweep of <label>", `NamesChip`) offers Scan exactly these names (default) / Include in discovery / Leave out (`ZONE_MODES`), Back to Reverse DNS and Remove. Nothing starts by itself. Exact mode (`handoffScanOverrides`) runs `runScan({ extraNames: typed + names, exact: true, sources: [], bruteforce: 'off', … })` for one run (never stored), the plan line says so, and the results carry a banner; discover adds the names as extra names. The names apply only to a scan of their own domains (`handoffForDomains(handoff, domains)`: the names equal to or under a typed domain, like the Zone File chip's `zoneForDomains`): with another domain in the box the chip says "Not used for the domains in the box: these names are under <domains>", with some of them how many this scan uses, and the plan line, exact mode and the extra names follow. The chip stays for the page session until removed ("Delete all local data" drops it, whether or not the view is mounted).
   - **Zone File "Scan now" during a scan:** the zone scan waits for the running one (`zoneStartAction`). A prompt offers **Cancel it and scan the zone** or **Don't start**. Leaving the page drops the request; the box and the zone mode stay filled in.
0a. **domain** "Domain overview" (`#/domain?name=…`; §5.46): one page per domain. A route — a shared link, a carried target (`run=0`), a nav link — only fills the box (a host name is reduced to its registrable domain, and the results header says so) with "Opened from a link: press Build overview … Nothing has been sent yet."; nothing is sent before **Build overview** (Ctrl/⌘+Enter; Esc stops). The seven cards fill as their lookups land (a spinner while pending), each with **Open in <tool>** carrying the name: Registration → Domain Health (registrar with IANA id, registered, expires with a days-left badge, the transfer lock — "Off" explains `clientTransferProhibited` —, the status flags, DNSSEC delegation, the registry's name servers; a TLD without RDAP says so and links the registry's WHOIS: TRABİS, DENIC, JPRS, SWITCH, else the TLD's IANA page), DNS hosting → DNS Lookup (provider badges, "name servers of N providers" when several, the registry's delegation when it differs from the zone, SOA primary / serial with its date / contact, DNSSEC), Mail → Domain Health (the MX platform — a gateway, forwarding or sending service says which —, MX hosts, SPF and DMARC in one line each, the services SPF names), Web → Global DNS (apex and www with their `KindBadge`, addresses linking to IP Intel, "alias of", the HTTPS records with their ALPN), Certificates → the Certificate view's "No file?" box (filled, `run=0`) (the CAs CAA allows, restricted ones marked, the issuewild values on their own row; "any CA" when CAA has no issue property, and an error when an unknown tag is marked critical — read as Domain Health reads CAA, so it never contradicts the CT verdicts; **Look up issuers**: one Cert Spotter request, on the click only, the issuers of the current certificates with CAA's verdict — "not allowed by CAA" warns that the next renewal will fail, naming the cause: a critical unknown tag, or the issue property when only issuewild names CAs (`ctNoteKey`), else CAA), SaaS verifications → DNS Lookup › TXT (vendor badges with a count; the tokens are never shown), Health → Domain Health (traffic-light dot, score, counts, the worst three problems; the workspace's accepted risks left out as Domain Health leaves them out, with the line that says how many and the score with them, §5.95). A lookup that failed is "⚠ n/a" with the reason in its fields (`lookupStatus`, §5.36) and the card's **Retry** asks only its failed lookups again, past the DNS cache, at once even while the rest of the build runs (Stop ends the build, not a Retry); the keyboard focus stays on the card (a card redrawn under it keeps it, and so does Copy summary when the head is redrawn as a Retry lands), the answers on screen stay ("Updating…") until the new ones land, and a DNS Retry runs the health checks again on the cache. A stopped build keeps what landed; each card not looked up says so with **Look up** (`RetryButton({ first: true })`: its accessible name and tooltip say "Look up" too). Web and Certificates say NXDOMAIN like DNS, Mail and SaaS for a domain that does not exist (Certificates still offers the CT lookup). **Copy summary** (§5.32 `domainSummary`) and **Copy link** share the overview on screen (`name`); the print stylesheet hides the form and the card links and prints one card per block. The finished overview is kept for the page session (`result()` / `snapshot()`, CT issuers included). A **Lookalike domains** panel under the cards (§5.76, `ui/lookalike-panel.js`, loaded on the first click of **Find lookalikes**) lists the domain’s typosquats and lookalikes — misspellings, keyboard slips, lookalike letters, other endings — with which of them exist, when they were registered and whether they can take mail (NS, then A / AAAA / MX in DNS, then RDAP, and crt.sh for the top hits on request), worst first with a risk level and Copy as CSV; the names are made in the browser and nothing is sent until its own **Check**. At ≤ 600 px each card's links sit on their own row under the title; at ≤ 1100 px the cards are one column. **Report** in the header (§5.88) downloads the overview as one self-contained HTML file — the health problems with their advice first, then the cards — or prints it, optionally with the overview's permalink (its domain only).
0b. **zone** "Zone File" (`#/zone[?tab=overview|records|origins|problems|live|parity|compare|convert]`; only `tab=` ever goes in the URL):
   - **Import:** drop, choose or paste, with format / dialect auto-detection. The zone name override and a Confirm step apply when the name is only guessed; there are 3 built-in samples and "How do I export my zone?".
   - **Fetch from deSEC or DigitalOcean** (`ui/zone-fetch.js`, a disclosure in the importer; §5.61): provider, zone name and the API token in a password field (`autocomplete="off"`, password managers told to ignore it). Nothing is sent before Fetch zone; the field is read once and emptied at that moment, and the token then lives only in the running fetch. Offline (Zone File itself works offline) Fetch zone reads nothing and says the work needs the network (`ctx.requireOnline`): the token stays in its field for when the connection is back. The privacy line says where it goes, that it is never saved or logged and that the field is emptied; the advice and two links per provider say how to make a read-only token (deSEC: a policy without write permission; DigitalOcean: Custom scopes › `domain:read`). Progress counts record sets / records and requests; a 429 shows the wait; Stop imports nothing. Errors name the provider, the HTTP status (a 401's causes per provider), the provider's own words and the permission a 403 lacks, and say the field was emptied whenever a token had been pasted (a bad zone name too). The panel keeps the keyboard focus through every repaint: on the same control, on Stop while a fetch runs (progress updates only the status line), on the token field after a fetch error, on the zone field after a bad name, on Fetch zone after Stop. A fetched listing is imported like a dropped one with the zone name confirmed, so lint, origins, the live check and New name servers all work on it. Only the provider and the zone typed are kept for the page session, never the token; Forget, another workspace, "Delete all local data", another import (its listing would replace that zone) and leaving the view stop a running fetch, and the first three empty the zone field too (the zone was that customer's: the next zone imported names it again).
   - **Summary bar:** a format badge and counts ("39 records · 26 names · 10 proxied"), with Forget. Alerts are pinned for an incomplete export and a mostly-internal zone.
   - **Overview:** stat cards and next steps:
     - Scan these names: exact mode or discovery, with "Leave out names that look internal", on by default;
     - Sweep the real origins;
     - Find certificate targets;
     - Compare with live DNS: shows the planned query count;
     - Moving to another DNS provider?: opens the New name servers tab;
     - Another copy, or another provider?: opens the Compare or the Convert tab.
   - **Records:** type groups, proxied only, search, CSV / JSON, copy names; an expanded row shows its comment, tags and problems.
   - **Origins & servers:** one row per proxied name (`proxiedOriginMap`), a by-address table (`addressMap`; both re-matched when the Servers list changes) and the sweep command (`zoneSweep` + `cmdline.buildSweepCommand` with the zone opt-ins). The command has a proxied-only / everything scope, POSIX / PowerShell, an "at least N TLS handshakes" estimate and the two-file form with `zone-names.txt` / `zone-targets.txt` downloads. It uses exact tokens only, never a /24. **Remember these N origins** (only while the workspace remembers origins, else a note links to the switch) puts each proxied name's exact address into the origin map (§5.70) and says what it added, confirmed and marked stale.
   - **Problems:** parse issues and lint findings, errors first; a click jumps to the record.
   - **Live check** (`planDrift` / `driftZone`): nothing is sent until you click Check.
     - The card shows the record sets, the query count, the resolvers and what is sent.
     - Internal names are skipped by default, and wildcard probing is optional.
     - Progress, Cancel and Re-run; the check keeps running while you are on another view.
     - Banners: serial, name servers, a zone that does not exist. Status chips filter the rows.
     - CSV / JSON exports redact origins unless opted in, also inside a value (an SPF `ip4:` / `ip6:` / `a:` term, an MX or SRV target).
   - **New name servers** (`ui/parity-panel.js` over §5.52; confirmed zone name only): the new provider's name servers (issues under the box: not a server, a private address or a public IPv6 one — the CLI command below carries it —, more than 8, one of the file's own servers), what to ask ('first': every record set on the first server, the SOA serial on the others; 'all': every record set everywhere, disabled past the cap), look for extra records at the apex and www (shown only when the zone has something to ask), skip internal-looking names, and the plan line ("32 record sets → 35 Globalping probes (at most 100 per check)", the record sets of types Globalping cannot ask, the capped note). **Compare** goes through `gateProbes` (purpose `'ns-parity'`, its own privacy text — a second one when the internal-name skip is off, saying those names are sent —, again above 50 probes) and `runParity`; keyboard focus moves from Compare to Stop while it runs and back after it (or after Stop); the progress follows the tab on screen (a return to Zone File during a run mounts a new one); the job belongs to the Zone File module (it keeps running on another tab or view, and a toast offers the result, worded from the verdict — "ready, nothing to fix" only for a finished clean run, "N problems to fix", "stopped, N record sets not compared" after a stop (a warning), "N record sets not compared" for a partial one —; Forget / a new import / another workspace stop and drop it — `stopParity` marks the holder dropped: no result, announcement or toast for the zone that is gone —; a new import keeps the servers typed in). Results: the verdict (a `check` one adds the record sets it left to the CLI), a warning when proxied records are answered with their origins, serials out of step, each server (role, state, serial, where the probe asked from, the measurement link), status chips, the table (status, name — with the server under it when several were compared —, type, the file's and the new values as a diff with a highlighted "TTL file → new" line where the TTL differs, the note; six columns that fit a 1280 px screen) with CSV / JSON exports that redact origins unless opted in and add the server and both TTLs of every row (export-only columns, `DataTable` column `display: false`); labelled cards below 640 px. **The move, step by step** (`parityRunbook`, before and after a run) and **Every record, from your own machine (CLI)**: the zone as canonical BIND text (`toBindText`, `<zone>.parity.zone`), `cli/dns_parity.py` and the command for Linux / macOS or PowerShell (opened by itself when the check was capped or left record sets out).
   - **Compare** (`ui/zone-tools.js` over §5.66, loaded on the first of the two tabs with a spinner until then; modulepreloaded when the view is idle; styles in `zonetools.css`): a second zone by drop, file, paste (Compare, Ctrl/Cmd+Enter in the box) or one of the samples, in any format Zone File reads; its zone name is the one typed for it, else the file's own, else this zone's when the file names none or only guesses one from its records (and a change batch's DELETE names) and every name in it fits under this zone's (`readOther`: a Route 53 change batch of one `www` record is no zone named `www`); a new first zone reads the kept second file again. The second zone is held on the view's module session like the first (a new import or analysis of the first keeps it and compares again; "Forget the second zone" drops it alone; Forget, another workspace and "Delete all local data" drop both). Shown: the other zone (name, format, records, files) and what the parser said of it — a name guessed from its records (type it if it is wrong), an incomplete export (the "This export is incomplete" alert with its issue: a set missing from it shows as removed, though it may only be in the part that is missing), a Route 53 change batch (changes, not a whole zone: how many sets it creates or updates and deletes; only those are compared, the rest of this zone shows as ignored, "not in the change batch", never as removed), its parse problems (errors and warnings, the first 20 under a disclosure) —; when this zone's own file is a change batch or incomplete, the result says so too; a note when the two zone names differ, the headline ("N differences: a added, r removed, c changed; s record sets the same", ignored ones counted) with **Copy summary** (§5.32 `zoneCompareSummary`: names and types, never a value, and what the bar says of either file; a bare `#/zone` link; its group named “Summary of the comparison”, apart from the zone’s own), the four options (TTL differences, TXT strings split differently, the SOA serial and timers, NS at the apex; the keyboard focus stays on a toggled one), the legend ("added" is only in the other zone), status chips (Differences — the default —, Added, Removed, Changed, Same, Ignored, All) and the table (status, name — wrapping, so a long owner keeps the notes on the card —, type, this zone's values, the other zone's with + / − lines, the note: reasons, what an option hid, a change batch's or an incomplete export's note, with both TTLs and proxy flags; labelled cards below 640 px). CSV / JSON exports (`diffCsv` / `diffJson`, the rows the filter and search show) hide the origin addresses of either zone's proxied records unless "Include origin addresses in exports" is on.
   - **Convert** (`ui/zone-tools.js` over §5.67; confirmed zone name only): the format (BIND zone file, Route 53 change batch, octoDNS YAML, DNSControl), what it is for, how many records are written and how many are not written as they are, the notes (each pitfall worded for the target, with its record names and count, errors first), **Download** (`<zone>.zone`, `<zone>.route53.json`, `<zone>.yaml`, `dnsconfig.js`), **Copy all** — for a Route 53 zone over AWS's quotas the change batches instead, listed in the order to send them, each with its records, Download and Copy (named by its file for a screen reader) —, the reminder that the file holds every record, origins included, and a preview (the first 400 lines of the first file, and which file it is). Nothing is sent.
   - **Hand-off contracts:**
     - `state.session.zone` = `zoneScanInput(...)` + `{ label, counts, records, internalNames, originInternal }` (`records`: §5.22 `referenceRecords`; `originInternal`: the origin looks internal by its name, `looksInternalName`; `internalNames`: every name `privateLookingNames` flags, whatever the "leave out names that look internal" toggle put in `names` — Retire an IP reads both and never sends one of those names). It is published only once the zone name is confirmed, and cleared by Forget and "Delete all local data".
     - `state.session.zoneScanIntent` = `{ v: 1, target: 'subdomains'|'scan', domain, mode: 'exact'|'discover', autostart, at }`, one-shot. Exact mode maps to `runScan({ zone, exact: true })` and is never written to the stored options.
   - **Privacy:** nothing about the zone (or a second one compared with it) is persisted (no storage key, no URL data), and no network request is made before a click; Compare and Convert make none at all.
1. **scan** "SSL Targets": one requirement line above the steps — "A certificate or at least one domain is required" — turns into a check once met (`formProgress`, §5.27; no step is labelled optional), and a completed step shows a check in place of its number (plus "(done)" in its heading for screen readers). A loaded certificate the scan cannot use — a CA certificate, or one without DNS names — leaves step 1 open with a warning sign, a warn badge ("CA certificate" / "no DNS names") and "(needs attention: …)" in its heading; while nothing else meets the requirement the line adds "This certificate has no DNS names: enter at least one domain.", and Start's error says the same instead of "load a certificate"; steps — (1) drop/paste certificate → shows parsed summary (a PKCS#12 bundle asks for its password first and adds its note with the key check and Download fullchain.pem under the summary, as in the Certificate view below; a lone server certificate gets the Certificate view's "Missing intermediate found" note with Download fullchain.pem — not the root-store warnings — for one certificate, not in a renewal of several); without a file, the same "No file?" block as the Certificate view (a host name's certificate from CT, or **Try a sample**); loading either only fills step 2 like a dropped file and never starts a scan; a CT certificate carries the caveat and points at the Verify tab, which checks what each server really serves; a scan that ends while a lookup still runs hands the busy flag back to it (a language switch waits for the lookup instead of aborting it); (2) target domain(s) (auto-filled from cert via registrableDomain); (3) inventory (uses shared inventory from state; link to inventory view); (4) options, collapsed into one Disclosure line (the Subdomains › Advanced options component, its summary an `<h2>` via `Disclosure({ heading: 2 })` like the other step titles) whose summary lists what differs from the defaults (`optionChanges`) or "recommended defaults"; its open state lasts for the page session, and an invalid extra hostname opens it (sources checkboxes w/ notes about quotas, include expired, wordlist Off/Small/Smart/Large/Huge (default Smart) + permutations, DoH chain; a vocabulary line shows the languages, custom wordlist and learned names shared with Subdomains › Advanced options, with a link there — SSL Targets has no separate controls for them, but records learned labels after its scans too); a run bar with Start/Cancel, the plan line (≈ DNS queries and time; the zone's names in exact zone mode) and a summary — in the flow on wide screens; at ≤ 1100 px it is `position: sticky; bottom: 0` inside the form (edge to edge at ≤ 900 px, side safe-area insets; while it floats (`barStuck` → `data-stuck`) a shadow and the bottom safe-area inset, none of it at rest; no transition with reduced motion), rests at the form's end so it never hides the last field, and the view publishes its height as `--scan-runbar-h` on the root for `scroll-padding-bottom` so a focused field is never behind it (at ≤ 600 px Start goes full width and the summary gives way to the plan line); Run/Cancel with per-source status + progress (the keyboard focus moves from Start to Cancel and back; a cancelled run keeps its streamed hits in Hosts, and the hosts CSV / names.txt exports include them, with certificate coverage). The run header says which market packs the scan's evidence added and why, as Subdomains' does (`ui/locale-evidence.js`, §5.89). Results: stat cards; tabs Hosts / Servers / Behind CDN / Verify / Rollout / DANE / Sources / CT: **Hosts** (table: name, origins, status/classification badge incl. 🟠 Cloudflare, IPs, CNAME, cert coverage ✓/✗, matched servers; filters: covered only / resolving only / hide wildcard suspects / by kind; search), **Servers** (grouped: server → hosts; "needs cert" first; unmatched IPs group; with the inventory's topology keys (§5.69) an intro line, the inventory's topology warnings (also in step 3), each server's notes, "No certificate needed" / "TLS passthrough" for `terminates_tls=no` (never for a server DNS reaches directly: it needs the certificate and says to check the inventory), each load balancer — a VIP pair together — followed by its backends, indented, the load balancers each name came through, VIP / NAT badges in the details, and a Topology column in the Servers CSV), **Behind CDN** (first **Remembered origins** — each proxied host's remembered origins from the workspace's origin map (§5.70) with when it was last confirmed, a stale entry of one of them muted with why, a link to Servers › Origin map —, then proxied hosts + origin hints (a remembered one badged "Remembered") + explanation + ready-to-run CLI command with the same POSIX / PowerShell toggle & download buttons for names.txt/targets.txt + link to `cli/ssl_origin_scan.py`; one shell choice drives the quick sweep, step 3's command and the Verify CLI card; the provider network tier (§5.4 `lib/networklabel.js`, 2026-10-08): names in a CDN's own network outside its proxy ranges listed apart — "In a CDN's network, not necessarily proxied" (Spectrum, a customer's own block, the CDN's own services), with their network and addresses —, an operator's published space named on the origin networks' owner column (no lookup needed; such a /24 is shared and swept by its addresses, §5.12) and on an origin hint that is no server of the list; the tab is drawn again once the dataset arrives), **Verify** (only with a certificate; `ui/verify-panel.js` over §5.18–§5.19: every covered (public IP, name) pair of the scan checked from the internet through Globalping, with the CLI's verdicts (a Cloudflare Origin CA certificate and a self-signed one are labelled as such — ORIGIN_CERT / PRIVATE_CERT — never "Old certificate"; info behind a CDN, a warning where visitors reach them directly). Nothing is sent when the tab opens, not even `/limits`. Start and "Check again (n)" read the free quota and show the consent + cost dialog on the first send of the page session (consent is never stored; "Delete all local data" resets it); a partial run is offered when the quota does not fit, and a 429 stops cleanly with the reset time. Private, reserved and unaccepted pairs and checks past the 500 cap are listed as skipped and, with every pair the internet could not answer (TIMEOUT / CLOSED), go to a validated CLI command (`--cert new-cert.pem --json verify-cli.json`, POSIX / PowerShell) with a new-cert.pem download; CDN-edge pairs are listed as skipped too but stay out of it, because the CDN serves its own certificate there. Origin pairs (an inventory origin IP with a proxied name, from an origin hint, the zone file or the origin map — via 'known') are opt-in, off by default, and the first batch with one always shows the dialog with the origin sentence. At the end of a batch its checks of exact origins (`via` known or zone; never a hint's candidate) with a verdict go into the origin map of the workspace the scan ran in (§5.70, source 'verify'); a line under the headline says what that batch added, confirmed and marked stale, or that remembering is off (no line after a batch without such a check). The headline counts servers; the tab badge reads `live/total`; warnings carry tooltips; CSV (the CLI's 17 columns first) and JSON exports; the scan's full JSON gains `verification`. The job lives on the scan run: it survives navigation and language changes, toasts when it finishes in the background ("Show results" reopens this tab), and a new scan cancels it), **Rollout** (only with a certificate; `ui/rollout-panel.js` over §5.79, loaded on the tab's first show: one row per server that needs the certificate — per server and set with several — with three steps to tick (installed, reloaded, verified; a tick ticks the earlier ones) kept in the workspace under the certificate's fingerprints, rows from an earlier scan kept, a row the Verify tab confirmed on every check marked verified by itself, the Verify column, the counts and a bar, the tab badge `verified/total`, Export CSV and Clear the board; then Deploy snippets: a server and a platform (nginx, Apache httpd, HAProxy, IIS, Tomcat, a Kubernetes TLS secret, Traefik, Caddy, AWS Certificate Manager, Azure Key Vault, F5 BIG-IP), the platform's options kept in the tab only, and the sections with Copy, ending with the per-address fingerprint check and `curl --resolve`), **DANE** (only with a certificate; `ui/dane-panel.js` over §5.25, the panel of the Certificate view's DANE / TLSA tab. Nothing is sent when the tab opens. "Check TLSA records" looks up the MX hosts of the certificate's domains, its concrete names and the covered, resolving hosts the scan found under its wildcard names, with the file's other certificates as the chain. The summary points to the tab when the scan mined in-domain mail servers (`dns-mine:MX`). The tab badge counts the endpoints that would break or fail (error) or need a closer look (warn). The job lives on the scan run like Verify's: Stop ends it ("cancelled"), a new scan cancels it, and the scan's full JSON gains `dane` (`domainscope.dane/1`)), **Sources** (per-source status, counts, errors, timing), **CT certificates** (crt.sh/certspotter certs: issuer, validity, names; highlight the uploaded cert's serial and certs expiring ≤30 days). Exports CSV/JSON.
   **Several certificates at once** (a renewal week, §5.43, `ui/renewal-panel.js`). Step 1's loaders take several files (multi-select, drag & drop), a folder where the browser has `webkitdirectory` (FileDrop `directory`: only files whose extension `accept` lists; "Choose a folder") and several PEM blocks pasted at once (`CertLoader({ multiple, folder, onLoads })`); a single certificate has "Add certificates" next to Details / Remove (a hidden multi-file picker, after step 1's own drop zone so that one stays the step's first file input). Several files, or one file with several leaves, show the sets instead of the certificate summary: names, and per certificate its key type, validity, expiry, files, Details (the Certificate view shows that certificate: the shared current certificate becomes a file of it, and the renewal stays while it is one of its leaves; any other certificate chosen elsewhere replaces step 1's files) and Remove; files that add nothing are listed with why (a private key, a CSR, a PKCS#12 bundle, CA certificates only, no DNS name) and can be removed; a file that gave certificates but could be read only in part (a damaged PEM block next to good ones) gets a warning that a certificate may be missing, with the parser's details (`bundle.unread`); a certificate another loaded one probably replaces (`bundle.replaced`) gets a warning above the list — a server still serving it would count as updated, so remove it if it is the one being replaced — and a "maybe the old one" badge on its row; a drop zone for more and Remove all. Step 1's description says "Their names…" once several certificates are loaded. The step badge counts the certificates, the run bar says "with N certificates", step 2 is filled from every set's registrable domains. One scan covers the union of the names (`runScan({ cert: first, certs })`); the streamed hits are covered by the union too. With two or more certificates (`run.config.certSets`): the Hosts tab's Certificate column names each host's set; a **Renewal plan** tab after Servers shows the sets (key types, hosts, servers, expiry, files), the server × set matrix (rows = your servers, then addresses outside the inventory; cells = the names each needs from each set, an origin hint marked; on a phone labelled cards, `DataTable({ cellLabels })` + `td::before { content: attr(data-label) }`, a set a server needs nothing from left out) with the **Work list (CSV)** (`workListRows`; with the topology keys the server cells carry the notes, the work list ends with a Topology column, and the servers with `terminates_tls=no` are listed under the matrix instead, §5.69), and the hosts no certificate covers (labelled cards on a phone too); the summary's renewal line (with Renewal plan; `renewalSummaryText`: one set is named by its key types and "needs it", several "need one of them") stands in for "N servers need the new certificate", and the Verify line speaks of the certificates; Behind CDN's CLI card offers one download per certificate (`cliCertFiles`) and one `--cert` each in the command; Verify runs one queue for every set (one cost), with a Set column when there are two sets or more, the set sentence, `other-set` badges and the same `--cert` files in its CLI card; DANE checks one certificate at a time with a picker (a job holder per certificate on `run.daneHolders`, the tab badge over all of them); Copy summary names the sets; the full JSON gains `certificateSets`, `renewal` (assigned sets, plan rows, uncovered names) and a `dane` report per certificate checked. One file with one certificate is the classic flow, unchanged.
2. **cert** "Certificate": full parsed details (subject, issuer, validity with days left, SAN list, key, fingerprints, chain order, warnings), CAA check against issuer for each base domain (Allowed / Allowed, with restrictions — each distinct RFC 8657 combination and what it means for the next renewal / Blocked, with each unusable value and why; the Result column comes before Records, and below 600 px the record set moves under the name so the verdict stays in view), CT lookup of this serial via crt.sh and, below it, **Key continuity** (§5.57: the key's other certificates in CT, only on a click) and, for a certificate that is no CA, **Is it revoked?** (§5.94, `ui/revocation-card.js`, loaded with the tab: the one name it would send, Cert Spotter asked on a click), a **DANE / TLSA** tab and a "find targets for this cert" button that opens scan pre-filled. The DANE / TLSA tab (`ui/dane-panel.js` over §5.25) checks the leaf of the file and its chain, whatever certificate is selected, and only on a click. While it runs, Stop takes the place of "Check TLSA records" and ends it ("cancelled"); the keyboard focus moves from the run button to Stop and back, never to `<body>`. It shows the headline, a "Publish before you install" card with the exact records to add and the 2 × TTL wait (error styling when an endpoint would break, warn styling when every item is a warning), the endpoints worst first (DNSSEC state, published records, an expandable explanation), CSV / JSON exports and this certificate's own TLSA values, computed locally. The job is kept per file — its leaf (a precertificate apart from its final certificate) and its other certificates, which DANE-TA records are matched against — across navigation and language changes: another file with the same leaf starts with no result, and a file loaded again shows its own. **No file?** (`CertAlternatives`, shared with SSL Targets step 1): a host name field that loads the newest valid certificate covering it from Certificate Transparency (`lib/ctcert.js`, §5.26; only on a click, Cancel while it runs, the outcome kept across a re-mount; any certificate change — the sample, a file, a hand-over, Remove — goes through `setCurrentCert`, which aborts a lookup still running, so its requests, the busy flag and a deferred language switch end at once), and **Try a sample**, which fetches `assets/data/sample-cert.pem` relative to the module (so it moves under `v/<commit>/` in the Pages bundle) and sends nothing to a third party. A CT load is a `CertLoad` with `source: 'ct'` and `ct: { host, provider, issuance, precertificate, newerPrecertificate, truncated }` (`ctCertLoad`); the sample has `source: 'sample'`. Both show a badge in the overview / step-1 summary and a note (`CertSourceNote`): for CT "Loaded from Certificate Transparency — the server may serve a different one", the issue date, a newer precertificate or a partly read list, **Check servers in SSL Targets** (the Certificate view hands the certificate over; the scan there leads to Verify) and the crt.sh page; the Chain tab says a log holds the leaf only instead of blaming a file. A crt.sh-only find (`manual`) lists the `?d=` download links and why the page cannot load them itself (one link when crt.sh holds only one id, and then no "use the other link"); every outcome says why crt.sh was asked (Cert Spotter's hourly limit with the time it is asked again, no answer or a refusal, a partial list, an unreadable copy; `ctOutcomeMessage`). A not-found says flatly that nothing is logged (and that internal names and private CAs never are) only on a complete answer: a list cut at the page cap, or crt.sh leaving some or all of its searches unanswered (`ctCrtshIncomplete`; its literal search misses the `*.parent` certificate when only that search failed), gives a hedged text, with Try again in the crt.sh case; a crt.sh find with a search unanswered adds that a newer certificate may be missing. A precertificate gets a warning (another fingerprint than the served certificate); loaded from CT, its note adds that no final certificate is logged yet, so it has to come from the server or the CA. After a load from the block (Enter, Load, Try a sample) the keyboard focus moves to the new source note (`focusLoadedCert`, tabindex -1) instead of falling to `<body>`; "Try again" hands its focus to Load (then Cancel); the hint below the field is tied to it with `aria-describedby`. The PEM & OpenSSL tab's copy-ready `openssl s_client` line (`sClientCommand`) uses only a certificate name that passes `cmdline.validateNames` unchanged (a `*.x` wildcard as `www.x`, else `example.com`): SAN bytes are not validated by the parser, so a hostile name is skipped, never pasted into the command. **PKCS#12 (.pfx / .p12)** (`CertLoader`, so the Certificate view and SSL Targets step 1 alike; `ui/pfx-import.js` over `x509.loadCertificates`, §5.47): a dropped, picked or pasted bundle opens a password dialog (a Modal labelled by its title; the focus in the password field; "Leave it empty if the file has no password"; "Check that the private key matches the certificate", off by default, with what it does to the key; Enter in the field or on the checkbox opens). A wrong password keeps the dialog open with the reason under the field (`aria-invalid`, the text selected): "does not match the file's integrity check — if you are sure of the password, the file is damaged", or, without a MAC, "no integrity check to tell the two apart"; Cancel / Escape loads nothing, keeps the certificate shown and toasts "<file> was not opened"; the field is emptied when the dialog closes. An opened bundle loads like any file (the chain in server order, SSL Targets step 2 filled from the leaf) and the keyboard focus moves to the note about it (`CertPfxNote`, tabindex -1): what it held ("3 certificates and 1 private key. Private keys are never shown or kept."), the friendly name, the certificates' and the key's encryption (cipher · KDF · iterations, a "weak" / "legacy" badge with a tooltip), the integrity check or "none", a warning for a plain keyBag or a password nothing checked, the key check ("The private key matches this certificate" with the algorithm; an error callout "does not match this certificate … cannot complete a TLS handshake", naming the certificate of the bundle the key belongs to; "not checked" with how to check it; no key; a key type the browser cannot check; a key whose encryption this page cannot undo — its name in the Private key row with "not supported here", and "cannot be checked" whether or not the check was asked; a key that did not decrypt) and **Download fullchain.pem** (`<cn>-fullchain.pem`: the leaf and its intermediates in chain order, no root, no key; the overview then drops its own "Download full chain"). A bundle that cannot be opened shows its reason as an alert — damaged, or an algorithm / mode this page does not support (named, with the OpenSSL command, `-legacy` for the old PBE algorithms), no WebCrypto outside https / localhost, or an operation this browser's WebCrypto refused (named) — and the keyboard focus moves to that alert (`pfxFocusTarget`: the note, else the first warning, else a drop zone on screen). **Missing intermediate** (`ui/chain-repair.js` over §5.49, `CertChainNotes`): for a server certificate (not a CA, a self-signed or a precertificate) the view looks its chain up in the bundled CCADB list when it renders (files of the site only; nothing is sent). Above the overview: "Missing intermediate found" ("N missing intermediates found") saying the file holds only the server certificate (or stops at an intermediate whose issuer is not in it; a CT load: "Certificate Transparency logs hold the server certificate only"), each added intermediate (name, issuer, CA owner, expiry), the source ("From this site's copy of the CCADB list (date).
