Your certificate was not sent anywhere." with ccadb.org) and **Download fullchain.pem** (`<cn>-fullchain.pem`: the leaf, then the intermediates, never the root or a key); a file whose chain ends at a root no store trusts gets "A current root is reachable" (warn) with the cross-signed certificate; a certificate from Certificate Transparency is titled "Intermediate found in the CCADB list" (a log holds the leaf only: nothing says the server lacks it); a lone server certificate whose issuer the list does not hold gets an info line naming the issuer ("a private CA, newer than this copy of the list, or expired or withdrawn"; an expired certificate: the list keeps only intermediates valid today, so its issuer may have gone with it); when the list cannot be read (offline: the service worker keeps only its manifest and roots table), a lone server certificate says so with Retry (which moves the keyboard focus to the notes that replace it). **Root store warnings** (error or warn callout) list each LifecycleWarning as a sentence with its date (a calendar day, UTC), the announcement link ("Announcement"; "Source" for a Mozilla date taken from the CCADB report) and "Root store data: CCADB and the stores' announcements, as of <date>". The Chain tab adds "Added from the CCADB list" (the added intermediates as chain items, "Not in the file") and where the chain ends with the stores that trust it (grouped by the root they trust it through when a cross-signed root is in the chain); the overview's and the Chain tab's "Download full chain", a PKCS#12 note's Download fullchain.pem and the PEM & OpenSSL tab's fullchain.pem (shown again when a lookup still running as the tab opened ends) include the added intermediates once found. The containers carry `data-chainfix` (running | done | error | none), the notes `data-chainfix-note` (repaired | not-found | failed) and `data-lifecycle`. The Chain tab's verdict on a file whose chain stops at a CA whose issuer it lacks waits for that lookup (`chainEndVerdict`): it is complete (`data-chain-issue` `ends-at`, then `ok`) only when the issuer is a root of the list's roots table; an intermediate the list holds is a warning (`missing-intermediate`: servers must send it too, and Download full chain adds it), an issuer the list cannot place (a private CA) or a list that could not be read an info line (`ends-at-unknown`, `ends-at-unchecked`), and none of these says the chain is complete; a CA or a precertificate, which the list is not asked about, keeps the plain `ends-at` line.
   **Does this CSR match?** (PEM & OpenSSL tab, below the key-match card): paste a CSR and **Compare** (Ctrl/⌘+Enter in the box): `parseCertificateRequest` + `csrMatchesCertificate` (§5.2) compare its public key with the selected certificate's, in the browser. A match says the certificate was issued for this key (from this CSR or another one made with it), and lists the names the CSR asked that the certificate lacks and those a CA added; a mismatch says it was made for another key (both keys named) — not issued from it, or re-keyed since. A private key is recognised the moment it lands in the box (`looksLikePrivateKey` on every input: its label, or bare base64 of a key's shape), never decoded or kept — the box and the module's copy are emptied at once, Compare or not, and the view says why; a certificate or other text says what it is. The pasted text lives in the module's memory only and is forgotten with the page session (another workspace, "Delete all local data").
   **Compare with another certificate** (Compare tab, `ui/cert-diff-panel.js` over §5.81, loaded on the tab's first use): the loaded certificate's leaf against the one replacing it — another file, pasted text or a host name's newest certificate from Certificate Transparency (the view's own CT loader, only on the click; nothing is sent before, and a file or paste sends nothing) — with every difference ordered by impact and a one-line verdict ("Safe to deploy everywhere the old one is", or the blockers). The names and addresses it no longer covers (a wildcard's lost coverage too), the key (type, size and whether it was reused — the SPKI SHA-256 of both), the issuer and intermediates, validity and the overlap window, the signature, key usage and EKU (clientAuth dropped), the SCTs, must-staple and the OCSP / CRL / CA Issuers URLs; both certificates side by side, the unchanged areas named. **Swap old and new** compares the rollback, **Copy as text** gives it for a change ticket, and **Remove** asks for another. Kept in the module's memory for the page session; no new endpoint (the Certificate view's CT lookup).
2b. **renew** "Renewal readiness" (`#/renew?names=a,b&ca=<RENEWAL_CAS id>&challenge=http-01|dns-01|tls-alpn-01`; `unknown`, the default, is left out): will the next ACME renewal of these names validate (§5.44 `lib/renewal.js`)?
   - **Form:** the names (one per line, `*.` for a wildcard, up to 50; what is not a host name, and a wildcard directly under a public suffix, is said and left out); **Take the names from a certificate** — the Certificate view's loaders (a file, a host name's certificate from Certificate Transparency, the sample), sharing the page session's certificate with Certificate and SSL Targets — which fills the names and sets the CA from the issuer (`caForIssuer`; an issuer outside the list leaves "Not known" and the hint says so); the CA (Not known, or a `RENEWAL_CAS` entry) and the ACME challenge (HTTP-01, DNS-01, TLS-ALPN-01, Not sure). **Check readiness** runs `checkRenewal` with `noCache` (a check right after a fix asks the resolvers again); Stop keeps the previous report. A check started while an HTTP-01 test runs stops the test: the test card drops it at once (its buttons off while the check runs) and says the probes it had used were not read.
   - **Results:** a summary card (the worst verdict as the headline — "At least one name could not be checked — check again" when a name could not be checked —, counts per verdict, the CA and challenge, when and which resolvers, Copy summary, CSV, JSON) and one card per name, worst verdict first then as entered (a `<details>` with the name as an h3, its verdict and error / warning counts; open unless ready, all open for one or two names; the user's open / closed choice survives re-renders), its findings grouped by area with the data they rest on: the CAA record set and where it was found, each resolver's answer (only when they do not all agree), a delegation target, the name servers, a CNAME chain, the probes of a test.
   - **HTTP-01 test** (a card when the challenge is HTTP-01 or not known; a per-name button too): the names that can be tested (`http01Plan`: not a wildcard, a public address, a host Globalping accepts; at most 10), one measurement per name and address family (IPv6 too for a name with AAAA records) from Europe, North America and Asia, through `gateProbes` (purpose `'renew-http01'`: its own privacy text naming the hosts and the path, the cost in probes); every measurement is created before any is read. The results merge into the report (`applyHttp01`) and can change a verdict. A quota that cannot cover the test says when it resets; measurements already paid for that could not be read (an error, Stop, or the view was left) are read again for free. Once the probes are being sent, **Stop** ends the test ("stopped": the paid measurements can be read again; with nothing paid yet, as before the click). A test that stopped before all its measurements were created is partial: a planned family not measured this time keeps what the name's earlier test measured for it, with that time ("IPv6 · tested <earlier time>"), else reads "not tested" (`http01Families`) — less evidence never improves a verdict —; a name with none keeps what it had, and the done note says the test is incomplete.
   - **Keyboard:** the focus follows Check readiness ⇄ Stop; a test button keeps it while its test runs (busy through `aria-disabled`, not `disabled`), after the consent dialog closes (Escape too) and after the test; a Stop or "Read the results again" that goes away hands it to the next action of the card.
   - **Links and session:** Certificate (overview actions) and SSL Targets (step 1's certificate) link to `#/renew?names=<the certificate's names>&run=0` (`RenewalLink`): the names are filled in and nothing is sent. The CA comes from the shared certificate when the box holds exactly its names and the link names no CA — on arrival, when a carry has just replaced the box (with a kept report too, and in `update()`), or when the certificate is not the one the CA was last set from (a CA chosen by hand for the same names and certificate stays). A carry replaces the box while it is empty, still holds what the last check ran (every name, past the cap of 50 too) or what a carry or a certificate put there — never a draft; the CA and challenge a `run=0` link names are set only when the box took its names, and names other than those of the certificate that set the CA drop that certificate's CA hint (the CA stays). A shared link without `run=0` runs on arrival (quiet offline, like Domain Health), and in `update()` sets the CA and challenge it names, else none chosen and "Not sure". The current target fills the box (`TARGET_ROUTES.renew`); the finished report — with its tests — is kept for the page session (`result()` / `snapshot()`), and `update()` takes a new link while the view is open.
2c. **estate** "Certificate estate" (`#/estate`; nothing goes in the URL; §5.48): one or more `ssl_origin_scan.py --json` reports (`--estate` or not) as one inventory of every certificate the servers serve.
   - **Import:** a drop zone for `.json` files (several at once, one per site or jump host; '/' focuses it; Ctrl+V pastes), **Paste a report** (the JSON `--json -` prints; Ctrl/⌘+Enter reads it; a pasted text that is not a report stays in its open box), **How to make a report** (the `--estate` command, open while nothing is loaded). What is not a report is listed with the reason (`REPORT_ERRORS`: the `--csv` file is named as such); the same report again is a duplicate (a toast), never a second copy; at most `ESTATE_MAX_REPORTS`. The reports list shows each file, its scan time (UTC), servers, endpoints and certificates, a `--estate` / "without --estate" badge (only the `-n` names were asked) and a remove button; **Forget all**.
   - **Privacy:** the reports are read in the browser and kept in the module's memory only — no storage, no URL; a reload, Forget, another workspace or "Delete all local data" drops them; nothing touches the network.
   - **Notes:** an endpoint in several reports ("for each name, the newest report's answer is used"; reports of separate networks sharing private addresses one at a time), reports of an older CLI (key reuse not checked), no names asked (coverage cannot be told).
   - **Numbers:** tiles that filter the certificate list (pressed state, the focus stays on the tile), each a count of certificates, its hint what is behind them: certificates (on how many endpoints), expiring (expired or within 30 days), in a name conflict (hint: how many names), with a shared key (flagged `shared-key`; hint: how many keys need a look), weak, covering no name ("no names asked" when none were); the expiry buckets and the kinds as badge lines.
   - **Tabs:** *Certificates* — a filter select (`ESTATE_FILTERS` with counts, "Needs a look" among them), search, a DataTable of labelled cards below 640 px, soonest expiry first: the certificate and its name count, the expiry date and days left, the issuer with its kind, the key with its weak reasons, where it is served (two endpoints, then "+N more"), its findings as badges with what each means; a row's details: SHA-256, public-key SHA-256, serial, validity, signature, names, the names asked it covers, and every endpoint (servers, `ip:port`, "default" for the no-SNI certificate, the names it was served for, "untrusted" and why when the CLI's trust check did not trust the chain served there, with several reports the reports behind it); **CSV** of what the filter shows (`estateCsv`, the CLI's `--estate --csv` columns, plus `report`). *Name conflicts* — per name, its certificates newest first (days left, kind, key, issuer, endpoints), "older" on a stale one. *Shared keys* — per key, its addresses and certificates (warn badges from 2 certificates or `SHARED_KEY_WIDE_HOSTS` addresses), "needs a look" when `sharedKeyNeedsLook`, its public-key SHA-256, certificates and servers; "no certificate" when no server returned one, "not checked" for reports of an older CLI.
   - **Copy summary** (above the tiles; §5.32 `estateSummary`, facts from `estateSummaryFacts`): the counts, what expires first and the names served with different certificates — certificate names only, never an address or a server of the reports — and the bare `#/estate` link; its tooltip says the link carries no file contents.
   - **The CLI's --ari / --revocation** (§5.94, `ui/revocation.js`): when a report has the records, a "Renewal window (ARI)" column (the window as a short UTC date range and where today is in it — "opens in N days", "open: renew now", "ended: renewal overdue" —, or why there is none: not known to the CA, no ARI server for this CA …; "as of" a carried answer) and a "Revocation" column (Not revoked / Revoked "on DATE, reason: …" / Unknown and why) next to the expiry, each sortable; their counts as two lines of the overview (renew now, overdue, not open yet, not read; revoked, unknown, not revoked); in a row's details the window with its times, when the CA was asked, its Retry-After, "The CA explains" (its explanationURL, a link the user opens), the CA asked, the CRL's verdict with "CRL signature not verified", the CRL URL (text, never a link) and when it was issued. A revoked certificate and an open or past window are "Needs a look"; the CSV has the CLI's columns. A report without them shows none of it.
   - Tests: `tests/js/estate-view.test.js` (import, duplicates, errors, the cap, every generated string key, the summary's facts); the offline `estate` E2E suite (§8); the `revocation` E2E suite for the ARI and revocation columns.

3. **global** "Global DNS": name + type → table of all resolvers (answer, TTL, rcode, AD, latency) + geo table via ECS (flag, country, ISP, answer, scope) + consistency groups with color coding + answer IP classification (CDN badge). Re-run button; share link. Every answer group names the operator of its addresses, and the summary gives `propagationVerdict` (§5.10): "Differs by design: CDN / GeoDNS edges (<operators>)" as info (naming the names before the CDN that steer to the same CDN names, if any; "No <type> records anywhere — the CNAME chains differ by design (<operators>)" when only the chains differ), or a warning with one line per finding (the groups' letters, the sources — joined with "; ", as a location name has a comma of its own — and whether it looks like propagation or a misconfiguration: SERVFAIL as a resolution fault, REFUSED and other rcodes as a refusal, a provider move when the queried name points to different operators, a CNAME that differs as a change, GeoDNS / weighted records or name servers that disagree), or an error "No source could resolve the name" when every answer is an rcode; a SafeSearch rewrite of a filtering resolver is named in the summary and not counted as a difference; the Distinct answers stat warns only when the verdict does. **ISP resolvers** (§5.86, below the locations, loaded on first use): Globalping probes — 10 over the continents by default, or the countries / AS numbers / places typed, ISP networks only unless unticked — ask their own resolvers for the check's name and type; their rows (location, ISP / network with ASN, the resolver asked, the TTL left and until when, status, DNSSEC, latency, answer) join the answer groups, the IP table (their countries' flags) and the verdict, which says "Stale at n ISP resolvers" when only ISPs still give an older answer. **Expected value** (§5.91, 2026-10-08): an optional value under name and type, matched exactly, by text or by a regex — every judged answer marked "Matches" or "Not yet" (until when that source may keep it), a card under the verdict with the count, until when the last old copy here expires, the worst case anywhere (the old answer's TTL; for a name that did not exist, the zone's negative-cache time — estimated from cached TTLs, which count down, until the zone's name server is asked), the public resolvers' cache-flush pages, a filter of the sources not there yet and, on a click, one Globalping question to the zone's own name server — the record's own type, or the SOA for a new name (`ui/soa-probe.js`); editing the value asks nothing again; `expect=` / `match=` go into the link, and a link's regex waits for Enter in the field.
   **Mainland China** (2026-10-02): the three locations asked through AliDNS (§5.8) are a row group of their own under the location table — a heading with a decorative flag, a description (AliDNS on behalf of 3 mainland ISPs; the types asked; the control question; no ECS scope; no DNSSEC validation) and a table with a Resolver column ("AliDNS (ECS)"), its own CSV / JSON export (`global-dns-china`). They take part in the answer groups, the IP table and the verdict like every location; a CNAME only they get while every other source agrees on its branch is "by design" with "<name> sends <locations> to <CNAME>, unlike every other source: the name's own DNS answers the resolvers there from a line of its own (typically for a CDN inside mainland China), not a change" (`glb.sum.designGeo`; as a finding next to a real problem, `glb.find.cnameGeo`), and an operator only they get is not called multi-CDN steering. Without a confirming control the text gives both readings and the TTL of the CNAME they got (`glb.sum.designGeoUnsure`, `glb.find.cnameGeoUnsure`), and the title and the Copy summary say "most likely" (`glb.sum.designTitleUnsure`, `glb.sum.nodataTitleUnsure`, `glb.sum.geoTitleUnsure` with `glb.sum.geoBodyUnsure`; `sum.global.*Unsure`). A `geo` verdict with a split tells it too. The description also says AliDNS is asked once more for A and AAAA, on behalf of a US subnet, to tell a China line from an older answer. For a type AliDNS is not asked for, their rows read "Not asked" (muted, with the reason), the Answered stat counts the rows that were asked and its hint how many were not, and the summary names them (`glb.sum.notAsked`). A SERVFAIL only they give is never blamed on DNSSEC (`glb.find.servfailNoDnssec`). Finding sources are listed in table order.
4. **lookup** "DNS Lookup": name + type(s) (checkbox group or "ALL common"), resolver select, DNSSEC toggle → sections per type with parsed records (SOA fields, MX priority, CAA tags, SVCB params …), flags (AD), raw presentation text, copy buttons. Density (`lookupLayout`, §5.37): a plain NODATA type gets no card but a place in the summary's "No records: AAAA, CAA, …" line (a disclosure with what NODATA means, the negative-caching time and the raw answers); the resolver that answered ("answered by …"), its PoP and the header flags are said once in the summary, and a card repeats only what differs (a failover to another resolver, other flags) plus a failover note or a cache hit; on wide screens the cards flow in CSS columns (`column-width: 480px`), and once every answer is in the first card of each further column is pinned there (`break-before: column`, made again after a Retry or when the width fits another number of columns), so opening a card's raw answer lengthens its own column instead of moving cards between columns; on phones the SOA timers sit two to a row and the TXT list shows four records (SPF / DMARC / DKIM first) before "+N more". The "No records:" label is in the text font, the type list in mono. The summary is updated in place as answers and Retries come in: the line keeps its node while its types do not change (and is drawn anew with the same open state, raw answer included, and keyboard focus when they do). A query that got no DNS answer keeps its card: which resolver failed (or "Every resolver tried") and why (`dohStatus`, §5.36), the attempts de-duplicated, and a Retry that asks that type alone again — at once, also while other types of the lookup still run; a new lookup cancels it (the keyboard focus returns to the card). **DNSSEC chain** in the summary (`ui/dnssec-panel.js`, §5.74, loaded on its first click): the chain of trust of the name and one of the looked-up types (a select), validated in this browser from the IANA root trust anchors down — the verdict, the first break and what to fix first, then a card per zone (DS → DNSKEY KSK / ZSK with key tags and algorithms → RRSIG validity windows) and the answer; a new lookup closes it. **Explain** in the summary (`ui/explain-panel.js`, §5.90, loaded on its first click; not for a reverse name or the root), above the DNSSEC chain: the name's SPF term by term with the lookup meter, Domain Health's findings, every include's policy one click away, **Does an address pass?** (RFC 7208 check_host() for a typed address, an optional sender and HELO) and a flatten preview; the DMARC and CAA that apply, tag by tag; its HTTPS / SVCB parameters with the hints compared and ECH decoded. The lookup's answers are reused, what else it needs is asked through the lookup's resolver; a new lookup closes it.
5. **bulk** "Bulk Resolve": paste hostnames (hundreds; a text / CSV list, or JSON: an array, name-like fields of objects, JSON lines) → table: name, status, CNAME chain, IPv4, IPv6, classification, PTR (optional), ASN (optional; its PTR queries use the run's resolver too), inventory match; progress (a cancelled run shows unfinished IP lookups as "not looked up"); CSV/JSON export. A PTR or ASN lookup that could not be made says "⚠ n/a" with the source and the reason (§5.36) — with PTR only, the reverse lookup's own failure (`ptr(ip, { throwOnError })`: e.g. "Reverse DNS: answered SERVFAIL"), never a silent empty cell.
6. **ip** "IP Intel": paste IPs → PTR, ASN, holder, prefix, country, provider/CDN, private flag, inventory server, other domains on the address (a "Find domains" per row opens Domains on this IP below the table, §5.71; the cell then keeps the count and the first names; a private address gets the workspace's answer only; quota note). No silent dashes (§5.36): a PTR, network, prefix or location cell that a failed source left empty says "⚠ n/a" (tooltip and screen-reader text: each source and why, e.g. "RIPEstat: rate limited — try again in a few minutes"); a chip per service (RIPEstat, ipwho.is, reverse DNS) says how many rows it answered or where it failed; Retry — per row under the address, or per chip for every row its service failed on — asks only those sources again (`retry()`, §5.13) and the cells fill in; a Retry belongs to its run: a new lookup, Stop or leaving the view cancels it, and it never draws over a later run's row for the same address; after Stop, the rows never looked up leave no chip "asking…" (no chips at all when nothing was asked); a reverse lookup answered SERVFAIL / REFUSED says so ("Reverse DNS: answered SERVFAIL"); the row details list each failure in words, the JSON export gains `unavailable` (field → sources) and `sourceErrors`, and the CSV writes "n/a" in every UI language (a stable token for scripts). Stat cards whose count is zero (CDN / proxy, your servers — only with a saved server list —, private) fold into one muted sentence ("None of these addresses is behind a CDN / proxy."; `foldZeroStats`, §5.37). **Routing, RPKI and abuse contact** (`ui/ip-enrich-panel.js`, §5.72), in the details of every finished row: it sends nothing before **Check routing** (`data-action="enrich"`; the note says "Nothing has been sent yet.") and nothing at all for an address that is not globally routable (the note says so); then the announced prefix and origin AS (the row's own prefix-overview answer, else network-info), the RPKI status per origin with its ROAs, their max length and what the status means, the routing flags (not announced, several origins / MOAS, the more-specific routes listed, low visibility) or "One origin, seen by N of M RIS peers", the first-seen date, the abuse contact (mailto links, Copy, the RIR) and the origin's PeeringDB record (its name linked to its page, type, peering policy, scope, website); a failed source is "⚠ n/a" with its reason, and the panel's Retry (`data-enrich-retry`) asks only the failed sources again. Below, the CIDR breadcrumb (/8 › /16 › /24 › announced prefix › address; IPv6 /32 › /48 › /64) is a row of buttons (`aria-pressed`) with the number of the workspace's servers inside each range, the address's own server counted; the narrowest range holding another server is chosen, and the chosen range lists its servers (the address's own first, marked "this address"), matched in the browser. The answers are kept per address while the view is mounted, and a complete one for an hour, so a language switch shows it again at once without a request. On a phone the panel stays at the table scroller's left edge and wraps at the screen's width. **Domains on this IP** (`ui/reverse-ip-panel.js`, §5.71) loads on the first "Find domains" (that address, at once) or "Domains on these addresses" above the table (the run's first ten addresses, only filled in): a chip per source with its count or its "n/a" and Retry, the workspace's servers and InternetDB's ports, tags and vulnerabilities per address, the table of names checked in DNS now with filters by status and source, search and CSV / JSON export, "Check more" past 300 names, and hand-offs to Subdomains, SSL Targets and Retire an IP that only fill those tools in. Its finished lookup survives a language re-mount (no request; the key fields come back empty). **The provider network** (2026-10-08, `lib/networklabel.js`, §5.4): a plain direct address in an operator's published or announced space is named at once from the range dataset, which a run waits for (`loadRanges`) — "Cloudflare network · not necessarily proxied" (outside its proxy ranges: one of its own services, a customer's own block or a TCP / UDP proxy), "AWS network · cloud · published range" —, with the origin AS once RIPEstat names the same operator, else the AS-based hint alone; in the cell (`data-network`, `data-relation`, `data-source`), its tooltip (the provider list's date), the details, the CSV ("Direct · AWS network") and the JSON (`network: { id, name, asn, category, relation, source }`).
6b. **ptr** "Reverse DNS" (`#/ptr?target=…&focus=…`; a link only fills the form and says it waits for a click — "Nothing has been sent yet"; the target is read with `targetTokens`, so `192.0.2.10 - 192.0.2.20` stays one range; the target and focus the page last wrote (`routeTarget` / `routeFocus`) are its own URL, so a reload or a re-mount keeps the form, while a link with the same target and another focus domain — or one opened by a hash change while the form holds a draft — fills the form; a link opened while a sweep runs waits until that sweep ends or is stopped — the form keeps the running sweep's target and focus and says which target waits — and then fills the form): the reverse DNS of every address of an IPv4 network up to a /22, a range, a list of IPv4 / IPv6 addresses or an AS's prefixes, forward-confirmed (§5.28).
   - **Form:** the target (the parsed count and each `parseSweepTarget` issue live under it: why IPv6 networks are not swept, a network over the cap with **Use <its first /22>** — or, wholly private or reserved, why it is not swept at all —, private addresses left out), an optional focus domain, Sweep / Stop (keyboard focus moves between them), the Settings parallelism, one example (AS3333), and what is sent. An AS turns the button into **List prefixes**: one RIPEstat request, then a picker (`parseAnnouncedPrefixes`): IPv4 prefixes with their size, ticked up to 1,024 addresses together (the running total, **Sweep selected**, Clear), a larger prefix disabled with **Use <its first /22>** (fills the form), a wholly private or reserved prefix disabled with why ("private space: not swept"), IPv6 prefixes listed but not swept, "no longer announced" marked (on a phone these notes sit under the prefix, their column hidden). **Sweep selected** follows a running sweep (disabled while one runs) and, when the picked prefixes hold nothing to sweep, says why instead of doing nothing. While RIPEstat answers, Stop cancels the lookup, and changing the target to anything but that AS drops it (no prefix list turns up later for an AS the form no longer holds); the busy state follows the sweep and the lookup together. A typed network drops an earlier AS's list. A finished sweep or lookup is announced once, when it ends, never again on a re-mount.
   - **Sweep:** `runPtrSweep` through the shared DohClient with `min(64, 2 × Settings concurrency)` addresses in flight and balance mode; the job belongs to the module (like Bulk Resolve): it keeps running on another view, a toast offers the results, a language switch keeps them. The URL gets `target` (the form's `targetTokens` joined with commas, so a range typed with spaces or an en dash is one `192.0.2.10-192.0.2.20` token; ≤ 400 characters) and `focus` (a focus edited later replaces it, an invalid one never goes in); Copy link in the header reads the focus at the click.
   - **Results:** progress, six stat cards (addresses, with a PTR name / generated, forward-confirmed / not resolving back or could not be checked — "every name resolves back" only when there are names and each does, "no PTR name to check" when there are none —, no reverse DNS (NXDOMAIN · empty), lookup failed (SERVFAIL), names under the focus domain — or the matched servers without one), clickable as filters; the table (`sweepRows`): focus rows first with an accent bar, then named hosts, pattern rows ("8 addresses", the template with an IP chip, "8 of 8 confirm"), addresses without a name, failures; the forward check as a badge with its explanation, the operator (`KindBadge`, from netinfo ranges or a PTR name under a provider's domain), the matching server; a Show filter (`SWEEP_FILTERS`; every sweep starts at "With a PTR name", and one that ends without any PTR name shows all its addresses unless the user picked a filter meanwhile; "Under your domain" is disabled without a focus domain, and clearing the focus while it is shown goes back to "With a PTR name") and **Expand patterns**; the filter and the search judge a pattern's addresses one by one (`sweepRowResults`): a pattern row stays while one of them passes and then says "1 of 8 match"; on a phone the forward check sits under the address (its column hidden); row details: the reverse name, each PTR name's forward answer, an RFC 2317 delegation, the template, the resolver, links to IP Intel and DNS Lookup; a pattern's details list its members.
   - **Exports and hand-offs:** CSV (`SWEEP_CSV_COLUMNS`, one line per address the rows shown stand for: of a pattern row only the members that pass the filter and the search) and JSON (`domainscope.ptr-sweep/1`: the same addresses, with the table's filter and search recorded and the summary of the whole sweep); names.txt (`sweepNames`, generated names left out); **Add names to a scan** (`scanHandoff` → `namesScanIntent`, then `#/subdomains?domain=…`, the user presses Scan); **Add to Servers** (`inventoryAdditions` against the editor's unsaved draft, else the saved text, so a second click adds nothing; `inventoryDraft` writes the hosts in that text's own format as `state.session.inventoryDraft`, then `#/inventory` with a toast that names the group — "in a new reverse_dns group" or "under your reverse_dns group": the user reviews and saves; nothing is saved here. A format it does not write, or an addition that would not read back as expected, leaves the editor alone: a dialog says why and shows the hosts as `name ip` lines with Copy, Download and Open Servers).
6c. **retire** "Retire an IP" (`#/retire?ips=…&domains=…`; a link fills the form and says nothing has been sent yet — a check sends hundreds of DNS queries, so a link never starts one; the params the page wrote for its own last check are no new link): before a server is switched off or renumbered, what still points at its address (§5.45).
   - **Form:** the addresses (one or more, or networks up to a /24; the count and each `parseRetireTargets` issue under it) and the domains to check. An empty domain box is filled in from the page session — the last Subdomains / SSL Targets scan (`state.session.scanHosts`), the imported zone's origin, unless that name looks internal (sessionZone `originInternal`, zoneorigins `looksInternalName`: a label or suffix, never a private address; `prefillDomains().internal`, said in a note while the box does not hold it) — and says where from; a domain typed into the box is checked as typed; a carried target (`run=0`) goes into its box (an address into the addresses, a domain or host name into the domains) only while that box is empty or holds the last check or what it took from a carry before, never over a draft. A disclosure lists, per domain, the host names checked besides its own records (from the last scan, the imported zone, passive hits asked to be checked, a discovery; a name the imported zone marks as looking internal is left out whichever source brings it, whatever the Zone File hand-off toggle says); a domain with none gets **Discover host names (Small wordlist)** OFFERED (with the query estimate written out next to it, not in a tooltip; the discovery engine with the Small wordlist, no passive source, no permutations), never run by itself — after it the check runs again. Check references / Stop (the keyboard focus moves between them); what is sent.
   - **Check:** `runRetireCheck` through the shared DohClient, two domains at a time, then the zone's candidates verified; the job belongs to the module (it keeps running on another view, a toast offers the result, a language switch keeps it). `ctx.runStarted` with a single address makes it the current target.
   - **Results:** the head card (the verdict — how many records break something, or nothing to clean up, or nothing points at it — with what is never covered; "nothing points at it" (green) only for a settled check (`retireGaps`): after a failed lookup, a "cannot tell", host names past the 1000-name cap or a stop it reads "nothing found, but not everything could be checked" (warn) with the failed lookups, the "cannot tell" results, the host names not resolved and the domains not checked, and a verdict that lists records gets the same "the list may be incomplete" note; a domain card names the lookups that failed (MX, NS, the SPF record, the HTTPS record, host names) instead of "nothing in it points at the address", and a domain that does not exist (NXDOMAIN, no name servers) says so ("a typo?") and keeps the verdict off the green "nothing"; a chip of a source nothing reached reads "not checked"; Copy summary, CSV, JSON; progress; a status chip per evidence source: public DNS, SPF, zone file, your servers, passive reverse IP; the owners from the server list with their other addresses), stat cards (must change, breaks mail, zone file only, cannot tell, unverified — the zero ones left out but the first), then one card per group, each record with its severity, current value (and the addresses it reaches), what to change and the evidence (verification, the chain or include path, the qualifier, roles, the zone file line, the sources, the domain it was found for); on a phone each record is a card of labelled lines. Passive names that no longer point here are listed apart.
   - **Compare the old and the new server** (`ui/origin-compare.js` over §5.53), a card under the results and a shortcut form of its own (`data-shortcut-scope`: Ctrl/Cmd+Enter in its fields compares, Esc stops its run, never the view's check): host name, old address (the one address of the form while nobody has typed there), new address, path, port. **Compare (2 Globalping probes)** goes through `gateProbes` (purpose `'origin-compare'`, its own privacy text) and `runCompare`; the result is a verdict and a table of the fourteen fields (old · address / new · address, the certificate's names among them, the severity icon and note of a difference, a failure in the page's language with the probe's own line after it, labelled cards below 600 px), the probe's location, the two measurement links and a JSON download (`domainscope.compare/1`); a certificate problem both servers share is a warning under the verdict, not a difference. When the new server answered with a certificate covering the name (the verdict neither broken nor unreachable), **Remember <address> as the origin of <name>** puts it into the workspace's origin map (§5.70, source 'compare'; while remembering is off, a note links to the switch instead). **Stop** ends it (focus moves Compare ⇄ Stop); a run outlives its card: leaving Retire an IP or switching the language mounts a new one, and the run ends on the card shown then; the old server's answer, measured before a stop or a failure (a quota 429) kept the new one from being asked, stays on screen alone. A private, documentation or reserved address, or a port a probe cannot ask, gets the `ssl_origin_scan.py --compare` command (Linux / macOS or PowerShell) instead of the button. The form and the last comparison are kept for the page session; "Delete all local data" and another workspace drop them.
   - **Passive lookup:** only on a click (**Find other names on the address**, at most 8 public addresses; the button sits under the chips with its request count and HackerTarget's daily quota written out next to it, linked by `aria-describedby`): HackerTarget and ip.thc.org per address; an address whose ip.thc.org list was cut off (one page of 100 names: `truncated`, with `total` when the service counts them) gets a note that the passive list is incomplete. The names are "unverified until checked" in their own card, whose **Check these too** (`checkTooPlan`) adds their registrable domains to the list while it has room — every domain in the box counts, not only the first 25 a check takes —, the names under a domain that is checked then as known hosts, and checks again; it is offered only when that makes progress, and the domains that cannot be added are named ("the domain list is full"). A name the check already resolved joins its row (or is gone).
7. **health** "Domain Health": domain → checks list grouped with severity icons + record panels + RDAP (registrar, expiry countdown) + DNSSEC + email security. An RDAP lookup that got no answer (`rdapStatus`, §5.36) marks the card's registrar, dates, status and registry name servers "⚠ n/a" with the reason written out above them, and the card's Retry asks RDAP alone again: `applyRdap` (§5.15) puts the registration data, its checks and the new score on screen without a DNS query, and the keyboard focus stays on the card. The CAA card lists every issue / issuewild value: usable, restricted by RFC 8657 (only these methods / one ACME account, with what that means for the next renewal from `caaRestrictionNotes`), unsatisfiable or malformed. The **MTA-STS policy** card (shown when the domain has MX hosts or an `_mta-sts` record) sends nothing until **Check the policy (1 Globalping probe)**: `ui/globalping-gate.js` `gateProbes` (one free `/limits` read; nothing sent when the quota is used up; the consent + cost dialog on the first send of the page session, with its own privacy text: the host name `mta-sts.<domain>` and the path go to Globalping and the result, policy included, is public by id for about six months), then one measurement (`create` + `poll`) read by §5.24 with the report's MX hosts, `_mta-sts` and `_smtp._tls` records (`mtaStsContext`: a failed lookup is passed as not known, and a `_mta-sts` set the report flags as mta-sts.invalid as `txtInvalid`, the card's TXT row then marked "not valid: senders ignore it"): headline, mode, max_age, HTTP answer, certificate, an MX host → pattern table, the findings worst first, the policy file, the probe and a link to the measurement. A failed MX lookup reads "lookup failed" in the DNS card too, as do a failed NS, SOA, A, AAAA, TXT or HTTPS lookup (`failedLookups`) and a wildcard probe no resolver answered (never "No"); in the "Domain resolves" check a family whose lookup failed reads "IPv6: lookup failed" (`LOOKUP_FAILED_PARAM`, worded by the view like the 'yes' / 'no' of boolean parameters), never "IPv6: —". A paid measurement that could not be read is read again for free ("Read the result again"), also across a language re-mount; a new health check drops the result; "Report (JSON)" gains `mtaStsPolicy`. The check never changes the score. The Email security card ends with **Reverse DNS of the mail servers (FCrDNS)** (`report.mailIdentity`, §5.15): MX host (a provider's marked), address (with a Reverse DNS link to `#/ptr?target=<ip>&focus=<domain>`), PTR name (a generic one marked) and the forward check (on a phone it sits under the address, and long names break, so the table fits the card); the mail-identity checks count in the score like any other. **Report** in the hero (§5.88) downloads the check as one self-contained HTML file — problems and advice first, then the notes, the passed checks and the records read — or prints it, optionally with the check's permalink (its domain and extra selectors). The hero shows the **v2 score** (0–100) and its **letter grade** A–F (`lib/healthscore.js`, §5.78: each category loses 40 per error and 15 per warning, the score is their weighted mean, capped at 79 with any error and 89 with any warning, 0 for a name that does not exist). A **Problems first** card lists the errors then the warnings, grouped by category with counts, each with "Show the fix" where `lib/fixes.js` has one or a line of advice where it does not (`lib/healthadvice.js`, §5.78), under a per-category score breakdown. A **Web** card (`lib/healthweb.js`, §5.78, loaded with the first report in `ui/health-v2.js`) shows the HTTPS / SVCB record, www against the bare domain, the HSTS preload list (a link to hstspreload.org — it has no CORS) and the **HTTP security grade** of Mozilla's HTTP Observatory (§5.78): one POST on **Check HTTP security**, never on arrival, with the grade, the failing-test count and a link to the MDN report; a failure is a status with Retry, never a grade; a new check or leaving the view aborts it; an internal name or a host with only private addresses is never sent. Copy summary includes the score and grade. A **Dependencies** card (the whole width of the details) names what the domain depends on through its records — name servers, mail servers, the SPF domains, DMARC report addresses, the DKIM keys at the common selectors and the extra ones, CAA iodef, MTA-STS, the Autodiscover and SIP SRV records, the HTTPS record, the `_acme-challenge` delegation — and what a click sends; **Check dependencies (RDAP)** (also by keyboard) loads `ui/takeover-panel.js` and runs the Takeover risks audit (§5.73 `DependencyPanel`) for the domain alone: the same summary, n/a with Retry, table, CSV and page check; the holder stays with the report on screen (a language switch keeps the results; a new check starts the card afresh and stops one in flight; a stopped check offers the card's own button again). **Accepted risks** (§5.95): each error or warning of the problems card offers **Accept this risk…** (ui/waivers.js, loaded on the first click: the finding and its id, the domain, a reason — required, ≤ 200 characters —, an owner — ≤ 80 —, an end date from today to 366 days ahead, 90 by default); an accepted finding leaves the problems, the counts, the light, the score and the grade, is listed under "N accepted risks" with "Accepted until DATE by OWNER: REASON" and **Remove**, and its row in the checks is marked "Accepted until DATE"; the hero says "1 accepted risk (until DATE)" and "With them the score would be 79/100 (C)"; the day after its end date it is a problem again, saying "Accepted risk expired on DATE: it counts again" with **Accept again…**, and the hero counts the expired ones. The focus goes to the button that took the clicked one's place. Copy summary and the customer report say "N accepted risks excluded". **What if you fix…** (a disclosure closing the card): tick the open problems, read "Fixing 2 problems: 74/100 (C) → 92/100 (A)" by the same formula; nothing is saved.
7b. **reports** "DMARC & TLS reports" (`#/reports`; no param ever: the reports never go into a URL; §5.58–§5.60; offline-capable): a privacy note ("Everything stays in this browser"), then a drop zone (up to `MAX_REPORT_FILES` = 2,000 files at once — FileDrop `maxFiles`, bytes only —, a folder, "Choose files" — the view's Ctrl/Cmd+Enter —; up to 50 MB a dropped file, a plain report up to 32 MiB whether dropped or unpacked) that takes .xml, .xml.gz, .zip (a zipped mailbox folder too), .json and .json.gz, each told apart by its content. While it reads, a bar counts the files read ("3 / 10"; a dropped archive counts as the reports inside it once unpacked: "164 / 2,000") and **Stop reading** (Esc) ends it, between two reports, in the middle of an archive too: what was read before Stop stays, the reports of the drop and the archive it cut included, and the toast says how many ("Reading stopped. The 164 reports read before it are kept." / "Reading stopped. No report had been read yet."), the focus goes back to the drop zone; files dropped or chosen meanwhile join the read (announced) and the bar's total. A line counts the files, the DMARC and TLS reports, the reports dropped twice and what could not be used, listed with its path inside the archive and the reason (`rpt.problem.<code>`; the first 200, then "+N more"). Dropping more adds to what is read; **Forget reports** (offered once anything was read, files that were no report alone too) drops everything (and stops its lookups). The reports live in the module's memory: a language switch or a visit elsewhere keeps them (the page header then says "Reports read at <time>", without Run again), another workspace and "Delete all local data" drop them. A drop makes the busiest reported domain the current target. Then the DMARC tab looks up the current SPF of the shown domain (§5.59 `loadSpfContext` for each of `spfDomainsFor`; offline: `requireOnline({ quiet: true })`, no toast, the SPF line says so), and a **Check again** asks past the DNS cache. Results head: "Reports for example.com" / "Reports for 2 domains" with Copy summary (§5.32 `reportsSummary`: the DMARC domain on screen and the TLS summary of the same domain) and **Report** (§5.88: a customer report of the DMARC domain on screen, the History tab's when that tab is shown); with no report read but a history kept, "Report history of this workspace" with Report alone. **Keep a summary of these reports in this workspace** (a switch under the drop zone, off by default; turning it off asks first; §5.97) keeps each day's volume and results and every sending address's first and last day, class and service in the workspace, for 400 days; while it is on, the **History** tab (after DMARC and TLS-RPT, with the number of domains kept; alone when no report is read) shows the filters, the domain's numbers and its two bar charts with their table, the senders over time with the new ones, the roll-up across the workspace's domains and Forget report history. **DMARC tab:** a domain picker when the reports name several (busiest first, with its message count); the head card (period and reporters; compliance — one decimal when it has one, never 100 % unless all, the number Copy summary says (`headlineShare`) —, messages, sending addresses and failing messages; the published policy as code chips (`t=y` too); the verdict as an alert — `data-verdict`, `data-look` (`verdictLook`: with `p=reject` in force, `enforcedLosing` when known sources fail and `enforcedSpfBroken` when mail that passed through SPF alone meets a broken SPF record, both errors) —; **Fix first**: the known sources that fail, most failing messages first, then those at risk from a broken SPF record, ≤ 5, each with its class, why, "120 of 120 messages fail" (or "10 of 10 messages passed through SPF alone") and every fix worded with the domains it names — `spf-permerror` with the reason in words (`rpt.spfError.<reason>`); the unknown senders' line; the SPF line with the record and its time, and "a permanent error for receivers: <why>" (`data-error`) when the domain's own record gives one; the notes; the reporters' own error notes), four class tiles (messages, addresses, pass rate — every share on the page with `headlineShare` —; a click filters the table, "Show every class" clears it), the sending addresses **By address** or **By service** (a switch; §5.93): by service, one row per service (`groupSources` of the rows the tiles let through: the service with its type and evidence — every ISP or home network together, "Not identified" last —, addresses, messages, DMARC pass, SPF / DKIM aligned, the classes of its sources), a totals line ("6 services · 7 addresses · 89 messages · 1 address not identified (2 messages)"), each row's details with how to align that service (`groupGuide`: from its sources' classes, none when all are yours; `rpt.guide.<key>` with the policy domain), what named it, the evidence and its addresses (≤ 20), a CSV of `SERVICE_CSV_COLUMNS`; by address (DataTable — the SPF landing or a server list change classifies the sources once and redraws, in one `updateRows` batch, only the rows whose class, why, servers, current SPF or fixes changed (`sourceRowChanged`), so a table of 60,000 addresses keeps its search, sort and open details without a long task per row —: the address with the **service** behind it under it, in the same cell, so the table is no wider than without it (`identifySource` from the report and the current SPF, no request: the name with its type and evidence under it, "not confirmed" for a reverse name that does not point back; "—" until looked up — its tooltip says why: not looked up yet, or left out by Identify senders as a private address or your own server (`unnamedHint`) —, "not identified" after; the search finds it), class badge, messages, DMARC pass, SPF / DKIM aligned — pass, fail or a part —, the dispositions applied, why, and **Network**: a per-row **Look up** of its reverse DNS and AS through lib/ipintel.js, "private" for a private address; a bulk "Look up N addresses" for the rows shown, at most 25 per click; **Identify N senders** (both views; only on a click, online; its tooltip names RIPEstat and ipwho.is): for at most `IDENTIFY_MAX` = 200 public sources nothing names yet, not your own servers (`identifyCandidates`, of the rows shown), lib/ptrsweep.js `checkFcrdns` through the view's DohClient (8 addresses at a time, its limiter capping the requests) — the reverse name and a forward lookup of each name found —, the bundled lists read once (`loadSenderMaps`; a failure is said and only the table matches), then Look up's network for those still unnamed (≤ 25, RIPEstat / ipwho.is), the rows redrawn as each answer lands and the result announced ("Identified 2 of 3 senders."); the Fix first items name the service too; expandable details with the service (its name and type, how it was named, how to align it — `senderGuide`: none for your own server, `forwarded` for a forwarder, `authorized` for a third party whose type's guide speaks of spoofing —, the reverse name an Identify click found), Header From, Envelope From, the SPF checks and DKIM signatures with their message counts, the policy overrides, the current SPF's verdict with the deciding term and policy, the reporters, the period, the fixes and a link to IP Intel (`run=0`); **CSV** of the rows shown with every `DMARC_CSV_COLUMNS` column, the service columns filled), and the reporters (a table in a Disclosure). **TLS-RPT tab:** a domain picker; the head card (success rate, sessions, failed sessions, sending organisations; the policies senders found — MTA-STS with its mode, DANE, none — with their sessions; "every reported session succeeded" when none failed), the failures by type (the RFC 8460 type named and as code, sessions, MX hosts, reporters, the advice, the reasons given, the links of §5.60), the failure details (DataTable, CSV of `TLS_CSV_COLUMNS`) and the senders. Below 600 px every table is a card of labelled lines; the page never scrolls sideways at 320 px. Tests: `tests/js/reports-view.test.js` (the pure helpers), `tests/e2e/reports.e2e.mjs` (offline), `tests/e2e/dmarchistory.e2e.mjs` (offline: the switch, the History tab, the customer report).
7c. **portfolio** "Domain portfolio" (`#/portfolio?domains=a,b` — the list while it has at most 50 domains, `MAX_LINK_DOMAINS`; §5.63–§5.65): many domains, one row each, and the workspace's policy audit. **Form:** the domains (one or more a line; a host name or URL counts as its registrable domain; at most 300; the count, what is left out and why under the box), filled in from the workspace's recent domains while the box was never touched (and said so); a link only fills it and says nothing has been sent yet; **Look for DKIM keys at 8 common selectors** (9 more questions a domain); what is sent, in words. Nothing is sent until **Check portfolio** (Ctrl/Cmd+Enter; **Stop**, Esc). **Check:** §5.63 `createPortfolio` over the shared DohClient — 4 domains' DNS at once, RDAP once per distinct domain with at most 4 requests in flight and one at a time per registry (a registry that turns requests away fails its own lookups at once, rate limited, and holds no other's place), rdap.org paced —; the job belongs to the module (`startJob({ view: 'portfolio' })`: the tab title, the nav ring and "Notify me when done" after 30 s; a language switch or a visit elsewhere keeps it, another workspace or "Delete all local data" stops and drops it, and its toast says "Show results" when it ends elsewhere); rows fill as the lookups land (redrawn in batches of 120 ms through `updateRows`). **Domains tab:** tiles (domains; changed since last check — red when one change is bad —; expire < 30 days, the red band; critical status; no transfer lock; name server domain at risk — < 30 days or not registered; lookups failed) that filter, as the **Show** select does (`PORTFOLIO_FILTERS` with counts: needs a look — a bad registration change too —, changed since your last check, no RDAP, fails the policy …), and the search (domains, registrars, name servers, CAA issuers); the table — labelled cards below 640 px; above, the domain column stays in view while it scrolls sideways — with the domain (its risk, `rowRisk` — a name server domain not registered heads the row like a critical status, a transfer pending right after —, what changed in its registration since the workspace's last check of it, §5.96 — "Changed since your last check (date): registrar, lock removed", the badge red for a bad change, green for a renewal, info otherwise; nothing on the first check of a domain in the workspace —, and "Partial: no RDAP" for a TLD without RDAP), the expiry with its countdown coloured by the band (or "No RDAP" with the registry's WHOIS link, "Not registered"), the registry status (critical statuses, an operation under way such as a pending transfer, the lock by its depth, §5.63 lockLevel — "Registry lock" for server transfer, update and delete prohibited, "Partial registry lock" with what it is under it ("transfer only — also what a registry sets during a dispute or the 60-day lock after a transfer", or the server prohibitions it has), "Registrar lock" for client transfer, update and delete prohibited, else "Transfer lock" with the statuses that prohibit transfers in its tooltip — or "No transfer lock", a hijack risk, the other flags, those the lock's badge names left out), the registrar ("Corporate" for a corporate registrar by its IANA ID, §5.92), DNSSEC ("Broken" when the DS keys cannot be validated), the name servers' domains with their own countdown ("own" for in-bailiwick ones, "Not registered" for one the registry does not know: anyone can register it and answer DNS for the zone), CAA (one issuer a line, the wildcard's), SPF (its `all`, lookups of 10), DMARC (`p=`, `pct`), DKIM, MTA-STS · TLS-RPT, the no-mail lock-down (null MX, -all, p=reject; each value whole on a line) and, while the policy has rules, its result. A lookup that failed is "⚠ n/a" with its reason and a Retry of that cell's lookups only (past the DNS cache; a name server domain's RDAP for every row reading it), the keyboard focus kept in the row; after a stop the rows not looked up offer **Look up**, a name server domain never read too. Columns sort (empty last). **Exports** of the rows shown: CSV (`EXPORT_COLUMNS`), JSON (the rows and the facts) and **Calendar (.ics)** (§5.65: one event per expiry on the local day the table shows, the name servers' domains too — "example.net expires (name servers of …)" —, alarms 30 and 7 days before). **Policy audit tab:** the workspace's policy (its `policy` part, §5.39; another tab's or an imported workspace's change follows) — presets (Baseline, Strict mail, Parked domain), its name, one tile per rule (a value changed on a rule that is off turns it on; a list between semicolons) and the JSON, kept in step (a JSON that does not parse leaves the tiles as they were; an unknown rule or a value its rule does not take is said and left out), **Export policy** / **Open a policy file** (≤ 16,384 characters) / **Clear**; then the matrix (domain × rule with the evidence of each cell, "2 of 3 domains fail the policy · 1 meets every rule"; **Matrix CSV** / **Matrix JSON**), computed from the run's facts: the audit sends nothing. A failed cell offers **Accept…** (§5.95, kind `rule`): an accepted cell is "Accepted" with its waiver under the evidence, counted on its own ("· 1 failed rule is an accepted risk", "N rules accepted" in the Result column and the Domains tab's Policy column), and the CSV says WAIVED. **Copy summary** in the results head (§5.32 `portfolioSummary`; disabled while the check runs; its first line names the domains whose registration changed since the last check, with what changed, the bad ones first). **The registration watch's baseline** (the workspace part `rdapSeen`, §5.96): a check compares each row with the baseline as it was when the check started (`rowChanges`), and when it ends — done or stopped, not after another workspace or "Delete all local data" dropped it — writes what each registry answered (`updateRdapSeen`), as a Retry or Look up that read a registration does for its row; so the next check says what changed since, once. The page never scrolls sideways at 320 px, and the matrix's longest evidence wraps inside its card (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`; a date stays whole). **Domain security** tab (`ui/secscore-panel.js` over §5.92, loaded on its first use with a spinner until then; between Domains and Policy audit): CSC's eight measures per domain with a 0–8 score, the portfolio's adoption of each measure as bars and a CSV, computed from the check on screen — it sends nothing. **Certificates (CT)** tab (`ui/ctwatch-panel.js` over §5.75, loaded on its first use with a spinner until then): the CT watchlist of the same domains — the newest certificate of each name set, the expiry radar (30 / 14 / 7 days by default), what was logged since the workspace's last check, unexpected CAs, wildcards and precertificates only, a revoked certificate's date and reason and the CA's problem-reporting contact (§5.94), Cert Spotter paced within its hourly quota and crt.sh after it, n/a + Retry per domain, CSV and an .ics of the expiries; it says plainly that CT lists publicly trusted certificates only, and sends nothing before **Check CT**; a row flagged new or from an unexpected CA offers **Known certificate…** (§5.95: its public key accepted as expected, never new nor unexpected again until the end date). Tests: `tests/js/portfolio-view.test.js` (the pure helpers), `tests/js/ctwatch.test.js`, `tests/e2e/portfolio.e2e.mjs`, `tests/e2e/secscore.e2e.mjs` and `tests/e2e/regwatch.e2e.mjs` (offline).
7d. **monitor** "Monitoring" (`#/monitor`; nothing goes in the URL; §5.98): the headless runner's results over time, one row per target — the nightly template's `results/NAME.json` and `results/history/YYYY-MM.jsonl` (§9 `--history`).
   - **Results** (a segmented control, **Files or folder** / **GitHub**): a drop zone for `.json` and `.jsonl` files (several at once; '/' focuses it; Ctrl+V pastes a report or history lines), **Choose files**, **Choose the results folder** (a folder picker where the browser has one: its `.json` and `.jsonl` files, the Markdown summaries left out) and **Where the results come from** (the template and a `--history` command; open while nothing is). **GitHub:** the repository (`owner/repo` or its URL), a fine-grained token (a password field read once per click and emptied then), the months of history (the last 1, 3 — the default —, 6 or 13), **Also read the open nightly issue** (the token needs Issues: read-only), how to make the token with two links, the privacy note, **Load from GitHub** (Enter or Ctrl/Cmd+Enter; **Stop**, Esc; offline it says the read needs the network and keeps the fields; a missing or malformed token is said at once, before anything is sent, and "emptied" only when something was in the field), the progress, then what was read (files, those left out, the requests GitHub has left this hour; a token that may not read issues said) or GitHub's refusal in the page's words with what GitHub said and that the token field was emptied. A GitHub read replaces what is open, files add to it (the same report again is a duplicate; the same month again replaces its entry); **Forget** drops all of it. Under it: "Read: N reports · N months of history · N lines", the files not read and why, the history lines skipped (counted).
   - **Tiles** (each filters the table, the focus kept; the same one again shows every target; each counts from the rows, so it agrees with its filter): targets (from N reports, or from the history), bad changes (the targets with a counted bad change in the last 7 days), certificates under 21 days (the soonest named; the certificates the rows' checks saw — a check the history alone holds counts its soonest expiry, from now —, one seen by tls and ct once), did not complete (checks of the latest runs: a lookup failed, or the report is older than the newest one by more than 36 hours — a nightly check that failed leaves last night's file).
   - **Links:** the open nightly issue when it was read (#N, its title the tooltip), else the repository's open issues labelled domainscope; the latest run a history line names, else the repository's Actions runs (the repository from GitHub, or from a run link on github.com).
   - **Copy summary** (§5.32 `monitorSummary`, registered by the view with its texts): the counts, the targets with bad changes, the certificates expiring first, the checks that did not complete and the health grades, by name; the bare `#/monitor` link. What the page draws is computed once per dataset and minute: a tile, a filter, "Show more" or the copy reuse it.
   - **Targets** (labelled cards at ≤ 640 px; the rows that need a look marked): the target with its checks and, when it has a change recorded, a button that shows its changes in the timeline; **Trend**: inline-SVG sparklines of the health score (0–100) and of the soonest certificate expiry (tls's served certificates, else ct's current ones), each with its last value and a sentence ("Health score over 51 nights: 90 → 82") as its label and tooltip; **Health**: the grade and score (a lookup that failed said); **Certificates**: the days left (red under 7, amber under 21), a tls status worse than OK, CT's new issuers, unexpected CAs and revoked certificates; **Takeover · audit**: the open takeover risks (medium and worse), the rules that fail and the security score; **Last 7 days**: the bad changes and the last change's tag and day; **Checks**: completed, or each check that did not complete or did not run since a day. A row's details: each check's last run, state, what it found (with its report's name, else "from the history") and its changes.
   - **Changes** (the timeline): newest first, grouped by day (UTC); each change its time ("03:25 UTC"), tag (what it means as the tooltip), target, check, "counted" when its report says it opened the issue, the run's link, and the runner's own words when the run's report is open (else its item); filters by check, target and tone (All, Bad, Good, Other); 100 at a time ("Show 100 more"); **CSV** of what the filters show (`timelineCsv`).
   - Kept in this module's memory only: a reload, Forget, another workspace or "Delete all local data" drop it; leaving the view stops a GitHub read (the repository typed stays for the page session, never the token).
   - Tests: `tests/js/monitor.test.js`, `tests/js/monitorfetch.test.js`, `tests/js/monitor-view.test.js`; the offline `monitor` E2E suite (§8).
8. **inventory** "Servers" (`#/inventory[?tab=origins|exposure]`): three tabs. **Origin map** (`ui/origin-map-panel.js`, §5.70; placed here because the map, like the inventory, describes the customer's own servers, belongs to the workspace and works offline): the privacy note (while browser storage is unavailable: kept in this tab only, gone when it closes, and every change says so too; a write that fails warns in a toast), the switch "Remember origins in this workspace" (off by default; turning it off with entries asks first and keeps them), the entries (name, origin, server, source, last confirmed with first seen in its tooltip, Active or Stale with the reason; edit, delete, CSV / JSON), Remove the stale entries, Forget the origin map (confirmed), an Add / Change form (Enter or Ctrl/Cmd+Enter submits; the error is said and the field focused; Cancel puts the focus back on the entry's Edit button; each message is announced once, its line no live region of its own) and the CLI report import (`.json`, several at once, "Also names not known to be behind a CDN"; each file's result or why it was not read); the tab's badge counts the entries. **Inventory**: textarea + file import (txt/csv/ini/yaml/json), parsed table, warnings, saved in the active workspace (§5.39; a badge in the editor card names it; a failed write says so in a toast), clear button, privacy note. An address written with a port is shown and exported as `ip:port` and written so to targets.txt (§5.5). With topology keys (§5.5, §5.69) a **Where TLS terminates** card sits between the warnings and the table (`TopologyCard`: the load balancer → backends tree, the VIPs with "install on both: …", the NAT pairs, the servers outside a load balancer that never get the certificate, the servers with their own TLS ports, a line on how to write the keys), the table badges a load balancer and a server with no certificate, a malformed key, a key a letter off and an inventory that contradicts itself (TLS terminating nowhere, VIP holders that disagree, backends that loop, a VIP or NAT address a server owns) are warnings in words (`inv.warn.TOPOLOGY.<reason>`, registered by `ui/topology.js` for SSL Targets too), "Supported formats & examples" explains the keys and has a Topology example, and targets.txt carries them. The editor opens with `state.session.inventoryDraft` when one is waiting (its own unsaved edits after navigating away, or hosts another view appended, such as Reverse DNS › Add to Servers) and shows "Unsaved changes" until the user saves. **Exposure audit** (`ui/exposure-panel.js`, §5.87; built on its first show and torn down with the view; placed here because it reads the same workspace as the origin map): how exposed are the real origins behind the workspace's CDN-proxied names? It reads the origin map, an imported zone and the inventory for the (name, origin) pairs, stat cards (origins, probeable, findings, worst) and two actions. **Audit DNS leaks** checks each origin's domain over the configured DoH resolvers and lists the records that point straight at an origin address — a non-proxied A / AAAA, an MX or name-server host, an SPF ip4 / ip6 / a / mx mechanism, an HTTPS hint, a TXT literal —; **Probe N origins directly** is opt-in, through the Globalping consent gate (purpose `origin-exposure`, the result public by measurement ID, asked again above 20 probes), and for each public origin sends an HTTPS GET of the proxied name and one of the origin address with the name as Host / SNI from the same vantage, calling the origin `exposed` only when it served a certificate covering the name directly (the CDN bypassed). Private and reserved origins and wildcard names are audited for DNS leaks only and never sent; findings are a table worst first (severity, finding, name, origin, where, fixes — firewall the CDN's ranges, Authenticated Origin Pulls / mTLS, a Tunnel, move the service, rotate the address) with a CSV export and a Copy summary, failures shown with Retry, never a silent dash.
9. **about**: where to start (the first-visit jobs, always listed), how it works, sources & quotas, privacy (the origin map among the items: opt-in, kept with the workspace, sent nowhere, leaving the browser only in a hand-over file), **What this page sent** (§5.55; `#/about?section=sent`, the footer's link, scrolls to it, focuses its title and drops the param), CLI download & usage (ssl_origin_scan.py with its examples and statuses, then the dns_parity.py and ip_intel.py cards with a command each), Cloudflare explanation, GitHub link placeholder.

**Shell navigation (app.js over §5.29).**
- **Sidebar / Tools menu:** above 900 px a sidebar with the group headings (on a screen at most 1000 px high the spacing tightens — links of exactly 24 px, line heights in pixels so any platform's fonts fit alike —, so every link of the six groups (20 tools) — with room for one more — fits the ~650 px a 1366 × 768 laptop's browser leaves, and a 1440 × 900 one shows the whole sidebar without scrolling; where the links still do not fit, the sidebar scrolls itself, never the page, just far enough to show the open tool's link), 720–900 px a sticky strip of links (scrolled sideways to the open tool's link); below 720 px the strip gives way to a sticky bar with a **Tools** button (`aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded`) and the current tool's icon and name (`aria-hidden`: the page `<h1>` names it). The button (a 44 px touch target) opens a Modal with every view in its group (`groupViews(VIEWS)`, so a new view appears by itself), two large targets per row, the current tool marked (`aria-current="page"`, a check, focused on open); every other link leads where the sidebar's does (`navHref`: back to the tool's kept result, or with the current target filled in). While the open tool works its entry carries the sidebar's pulsing busy dot. Esc, the close button or the backdrop close it and the focus returns to the button; a link to another tool closes it and the new page title takes the focus, the open tool's own entry only closes it (its params stay); a Ctrl / ⌘ / Shift / Alt click is left to the browser (a new tab) and the menu stays open (`isPlainClick`); a hash change (the phone's Back) closes it, and so does a viewport widened past 720 px (a phone turned sideways: the button is gone, the page title takes the focus).
- **First-visit task picker:** above the start page's header (default route only) a dismissible region (`<section>` named by its title, which is no heading: it comes before the page `<h1>`), "New here? Pick a job to start with", with five job links (`START_TASKS`: Find every subdomain → subdomains, Where must this certificate go? → scan, Check a domain's health → health, Is my DNS change live everywhere? → global, Import a zone file → zone; `ui/start-tasks.js`); below 600 px two columns of short chips (the job alone, the tool's name read out but not shown, no lead line; below 360 px without their icons), so the start page's own field stays near the top. The start page's own job focuses its input instead of navigating (a Ctrl / ⌘ click still opens a new tab). It shows while `settings.startTasks` (state.js, default true, persisted with the other settings) is on. Dismissing sets it off (the focus goes to the page title; a toast names About › Where to start), and so does the first run: a view going busy (`ctx.setBusy`), an imported zone, a loaded certificate or saved servers (`isRunSignal`); a picker already on screen stays until the page is shown again, so nothing jumps under the pointer. A browser with saved servers or learned names at start-up (`hasUsedBefore`) never sees it; remembered view options do not count. "Delete all local data" brings it back. About › **Where to start** always lists the same jobs.
- **Keyboard shortcuts:** one `keydown` listener in app.js (`shortcutFor`); none while a dialog is open or after a handler called `preventDefault` (a field's own Enter). **Ctrl/Cmd+Enter** in a field of the view clicks the `data-shortcut="submit"` control of the field's own form (`pickShortcutTarget`, strict: nothing while the run is in progress): the view's Run for every field of the view's form, and inside a sub-form (`data-shortcut-scope`: the certificate paste box, the CT host name lookup, Zone File's importer — its paste box, zone name and format import the pasted zone — and its live check, whose options start it, Reverse DNS's prefix picker, whose Sweep selected answers its checkboxes) only that sub-form's button — so on SSL Targets the domains field starts the scan, never the paste box's Read. Results are no part of a form: each view marks its results container `data-shortcut-scope="results"` (Subdomains, SSL Targets, Certificate, Global DNS, DNS Lookup, Bulk Resolve, IP Intel, Reverse DNS, Domain Health, Servers, Zone File's analysis) and every DataTable is a `"table"` scope of its own, both without a submit, so a table's filter, a results option or a Verify / DANE panel field starts nothing — a new run from there would drop the results on screen (and a Verify run's spent Globalping quota). The help dialog's note says so. A control counts when it is enabled and visible (`checkVisibility()`, and never inside the collapsed part of a closed `<details>`). **Esc** clicks the nearest visible `data-shortcut="cancel"` control (a view's Stop / Cancel button, the Verify and DANE panels' Stop), else one that only a closed tab panel of the view hides (the Zone File live check or a DANE check running while another tab is open), and does nothing — not even `preventDefault` — when there is none; in a search field with text (a table's filter) Esc clears the field (`isSearchClear`: the shell empties it and fires `input`, as Chrome does by itself and Firefox does not) and the next Esc cancels; **/** outside a field focuses the view's `data-shortcut="focus"` element (Subdomains, SSL Targets, DNS Lookup, Global DNS, Bulk Resolve, IP Intel, Reverse DNS, Domain Health, Servers: the main field; Zone File, Certificate: the drop zone), else its first visible text field; **?** opens the Keyboard shortcuts dialog (also from the footer, whose button — `aria-haspopup="dialog"` — touch-only devices do not show), ⌘ on Apple platforms; the focus returns where it was. Views never bind these keys themselves; they only mark their controls — every view but About a submit, a focus control and a results scope (`tests/js/shellnav.test.js` fails for a view that misses one).
- **Command palette (Ctrl/Cmd+K, `ui/palette.js` over §5.77):** from anywhere — a field included — or the header's search button (`data-control="palette"`, `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, not shown below 600 px), a dialog finds a tool by its name or description in English or Turkish ("ters" finds Reverse DNS in English, "reverse" Ters DNS in Turkish; `İ`/`I`/`ı`/`i` alike) and offers the actions on a typed domain or host name (Subdomains, Domain overview, Domain Health, DNS Lookup MX / TXT / CAA, Global DNS, Renewal readiness), IP address (IP Intel, Domains on this IP, Reverse DNS, Retire an IP), network or AS number (a Reverse DNS sweep) or pasted certificate (Certificate), the current target and the workspace's recent domains. Every entry only fills its tool in (`run=0`); the keys list (`?`) names it. Only the key, the button and the lazy import are on the start route.

**Page session (`lib/session.js` §5.30, `ui/session-ui.js`, app.js).** A run in any tool (`ctx.runStarted`) sets the **current target**: Subdomains / SSL Targets their first domain, Global DNS, DNS Lookup and Domain Health their name, Bulk Resolve and IP Intel their list's one entry or shared registrable domain (else unchanged), the Certificate view its CT host or first DNS name (the bundled sample sets none). A chip after the brand shows it ("Target example.com ×"; on phones in place of the brand name; a long host name is cut in the middle, "a…example.com", the registrable domain whole and the full value in the text and title), titled with what it does; × clears it (focus moves to the page title, "cleared" is announced). Every `a.nav-link[data-view]` points to `navHref(id)`: the tool on screen to its own URL, a tool with a kept result back to it — unless the target was set after that result and is about something else (then the target, filled in, with the kept result still shown under it) — else the tool with the target filled in (`#/lookup?name=example.com&run=0`), else bare. `run=0` fills the form and runs nothing — the tools that run on a shared link (Global DNS, DNS Lookup, IP Intel, Domain Health) do not run — and every tool's box (Subdomains, SSL Targets, Bulk Resolve, Global DNS, DNS Lookup, IP Intel, Domain Health and the Certificate view's "No file?" field, `?host=`) takes it only while empty or while it still holds exactly the last run's input or the target it took before (never a draft), on arrival and in `update()` — so it follows every newer target, three in a row as well as one, until the user types in it; the Certificate view drops `host` once a certificate loads. Leaving a tool keeps its finished result (`result()` + `snapshot()` for Global DNS, DNS Lookup, IP Intel, Domain Health; the fact for the tools with module state: Subdomains, SSL Targets, Bulk Resolve, the Certificate view and a finished Zone File live check, which has no subject, so nothing about a zone becomes the target or reaches a URL); coming back shows it again with no request — through a bare route or the result's own params, which then go into the URL with `run=0` (a reload or a later Back only fills the form), and under a newer carried target too, which stays in the URL and the box (so after Domain Health for example.com and a lookup of www.example.com, Domain Health opens with www.example.com in the box and the example.com report under it, as Bulk Resolve shows its last job under a new name); Copy link gives the running URL of the result on screen, never the box's — and the page header says "Result from 14:02 Run again" (one run of text that wraps like a sentence; the date too on another day; announced with the tool's name). A tool with module state gets the note only for the result the shell kept when it was left: a certificate loaded in SSL Targets shows in the Certificate view without one. "Run again" calls `rerun()`: the kept query again, the last run's names (Subdomains' is its page-header Re-run, Global DNS's too, so their notes have none), for SSL Targets and Bulk Resolve with the options as set; a certificate from Certificate Transparency is looked up again (a file or the sample has no Run again); the Zone File live check runs again on its tab.
