- **Rows:** SAME, DIFFERENT (other values, a CNAME instead), MISSING (NXDOMAIN, no data), UNPROXIED (a proxied record answered with its origin; a proxied or flattened CNAME answered with Cloudflare / other addresses is SAME `proxied` / `flattened`), EXTRA (`--no-extras` turns them off: A, AAAA, MX, TXT, CAA a name of the file does not have — none at a CNAME, wildcard or delegation, no A / AAAA at a proxied name —, and A / AAAA at www when the file has no www; a CNAME served at such a name is one row, and none where a compared record set reports it as `cname`), SKIPPED, ERROR; notes `ttl` (a TTL differing from the file's; never at a proxied name or Cloudflare's automatic TTL 1), `txt-chunking`, `routing`, `ns-new` / `ns-mismatch` (the apex NS set against the `--ns` host names, every one given: names that share one address are one server, asked once), `referral`, `proxy-on` (a DNS-only A / AAAA of a Cloudflare export answered with Cloudflare addresses: DIFFERENT, the web app's `proxy-on-live`).
- **Output:** the servers with their state and serial (serials out of step said), then per server the MISSING / DIFFERENT / UNPROXIED / EXTRA / NOT ANSWERED sections, TTL differences and a count of what was not compared (`--show-all` lists it and the SAME rows; a server with the same answers as the first says so), the verdict and the order of the move (TTLs, compare again, DNSSEC first, switch, keep the old zone 48 hours). **Verdict** (`ParityReport.verdict`, the web app's `paritySummary`): `blocked`, `fix` (MISSING / DIFFERENT, a server that does not serve the zone), `partial` (ERROR rows: record sets without a usable answer, which the web app counts as not compared; the summary leads with "N record sets got no answer: run this again before you switch", `unanswered()` counting each record set once), `check` (UNPROXIED / EXTRA rows, TTL differences, serials out of step), `ready`; the web app's other reasons for `partial` (a stop, the cap, types a probe cannot ask) do not occur here. Server-provided text is printed as printable ASCII. `--json` (`domainscope.dns-parity/1`: `nameservers`, `rows`, `summary.verdict`), `--csv` (`CSV_COLUMNS`, formula-safe, BOM in a file). Exit codes: 0, 1 (`--fail-on-diff`: something missing, different, extra or unproxied, a record set without an answer, or a server that does not serve the zone — stricter than the verdict: UNPROXIED and EXTRA are `check` and still fail it), 2 usage, 3 a report not written, 130 interrupted.
- Tests: `tests/python/test_dns_parity.py` — the zone reader (a second `$ORIGIN` included), the messages, the `--ns` forms, and runs against tiny authoritative servers on 127.0.0.1 (UDP and TCP on one port, their own encoder with compression pointers, a delegation answered by referral, truncation over UDP, REFUSED, no `aa`, one that never answers, a name that does not resolve), `proxy-on`, the `check` verdict with `--fail-on-diff` still failing, a server that SERVFAILs some types (`partial`, `--fail-on-diff` fails), the reports and exit codes.

### 7.2 CLI `cli/ip_intel.py` (Python ≥3.8, stdlib only, single file)

The CLI counterpart of the reverse-IP lookups (IP Intel, Retire an IP › Find other names on the address), for what a browser cannot do: a certificate served by an address only your network reaches, PTR from the system resolver, a source without CORS headers (mnemonic) and the services that need a key of yours. A file of its own like §7.1: it shares nothing with the TLS scanner's options.
```
python3 ip_intel.py domains TARGET [TARGET ...] [-p 443,8443] [--sni-max 16] [--no-tls] [--no-ptr] [--no-passive] [--no-keys] [--sources LIST] [--no-verify] [--max 1024] [--timeout 10] [-w 8] [--json FILE] [--csv FILE] [--fail-on-error] [-q]
python3 ip_intel.py sources
```
- **Targets** (`parse_targets`): addresses (IPv4-mapped IPv6 as IPv4), CIDR ranges (an IPv4 range without its network and broadcast addresses, a /31 or /32 whole; IPv6 every address) and files of them (`-` = stdin; one or more a line, `#` comments; any other token a warning with its line), in order without repeats; at most `--max` (default 1024, an IPv4 /22; ≤ 65536), a range checked before it is expanded (exit 2).
- **Per address, at once** (`--workers` threads): (1) a TLS handshake without SNI on each of `--ports` (443; ≤ 16), the permissive client of §7 (nothing verified): `OK`, `CLOSED`, `TIMEOUT`, `TLS_ERROR` (connected, no handshake: often a server that wants an SNI), `ERROR`; (2) PTR with `socket.gethostbyaddr` (no PTR is `[]`, a resolver without an answer `ERROR`; names under `.arpa` dropped); (3) each third-party source, **only for a public address** (`is_public`: global unicast; private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT, documentation, multicast and reserved ranges get TLS and PTR only, the sources `SKIPPED`, nothing sent). Then (4) SNI handshakes on each port that served a certificate or failed in a way an SNI can change (`speaks_tls`: not a port that answered with no TLS at all, such as an HTTP server), for at most `--sni-max` names (the certificates' own names first, then PTR, then the names of the most sources; no wildcard), and (5) a forward lookup (`getaddrinfo`, the system resolver) of every name once.
- **Sources** (`SOURCES`; the answers' shapes checked live against 1.1.1.1 on 2026-10-08, the free ones answering, the key services without a key answering 401 / 403, which proves the paths; the `--no-tls` smoke run gave 500 HackerTarget, 500 OTX, 200 Robtex, 3 InternetDB, 999 mnemonic and 100 of ip.thc.org's 91,172 names): `hackertarget` `https://api.hackertarget.com/reverseiplookup/?q={ip}` (text, a name a line; quota and errors are HTTP 200 text; IPv4 only: `error check your search parameter` for IPv6), `otx` `https://otx.alienvault.com/api/v1/indicators/{IPv4|IPv6}/{ip}/passive_dns` (`passive_dns[{hostname, first, last}]`, `count`), `robtex` `https://freeapi.robtex.com/pdns/reverse/{ip}` (NDJSON `{rrname, time_first, time_last}`, epoch seconds), `internetdb` `https://internetdb.shodan.io/{ip}` (`hostnames`, and `ports`, `tags`, `vulns`, `cpes` shown as the address's intel; a 404 `No information available` is an empty answer), `mnemonic` `https://api.mnemonic.no/pdns/v3/{ip}?limit=1000` (no CORS: CLI-only; `data[{query, answer, rrtype, firstSeenTimestamp, lastSeenTimestamp}]` in epoch ms, the name being the `query` of an A / AAAA and the `answer` of a PTR; its `count` stops at the page size, so a full page is `truncated`), `thc` `POST https://ip.thc.org/api/v1/lookup` with the text/plain JSON body `{ip_address, limit: 100}` the web app sends (`domains[{domain}]`, `matching_records`, `next_page_state`; `count_unavailable` for IPv6; one page, 2 s apart for its token bucket). The key sources, each asked only when its variables are set (`load_keys`; `--no-keys` leaves them out) and as its documentation says: `securitytrails` (`SECURITYTRAILS_API_KEY` in the `APIKEY` header, `POST /v1/domains/list` with `{filter: {ipv4|ipv6}}`), `virustotal` (`VT_API_KEY` in `x-apikey`, `/api/v3/ip_addresses/{ip}/resolutions?limit=40`), `shodan` (`SHODAN_API_KEY` as `key=`, `/shodan/host/{ip}?minify=true`), `censys` (`CENSYS_API_ID` + `CENSYS_API_SECRET` as Basic authentication, Search v2 `/api/v2/hosts/{ip}/names`; its 401 says v2 shuts down on 2026-09-30, and it still answered on 2026-10-08), `viewdns` (`VIEWDNS_API_KEY` as `apikey=`, `/reverseip/?host={ip}&output=json`; IPv4 only), `whoisxml` (`WHOISXML_API_KEY` as `apiKey=`, `reverse-ip.whoisxmlapi.com/api/v1`; IPv4 only), `netlas` (`NETLAS_API_KEY` in `X-API-Key`, `/api/domains/?q=a:{ip}`). One page each: a source that says it has more is `truncated` in the report. `--sources` names the ones to ask (an unknown one, or a key source without its key, is exit 2).
- **Statuses of a source per address:** `OK`, `SKIPPED` (a private address, IPv6 at an IPv4-only source), `RATE_LIMITED` (HTTP 429 / 402, or the source's own quota text), `REFUSED` (HTTP 401 / 403), `TIMEOUT`, `ERROR` (network, another HTTP status, a redirect — never followed, so a key header never reaches another host —, an answer that could not be read). A source that answers `RATE_LIMITED` or `REFUSED` is not asked again in the run: the later addresses get the same status with `not asked: …`. Each source asks for one address after the other in a lane of its own beside the `--workers` threads (TLS, PTR, the SNI handshakes and the name checks), at its own pace (`Source.interval` between two requests: VirusTotal 15 s, its public quota of 4 a minute; Censys 2.5 s; ip.thc.org 2 s; the others 0.2–1 s), so a slow source holds no worker.
- **Keys** come from the environment only (never an option), go only to their own service, and are redacted (`redact`, as given and URL-encoded) from every status, the summary and both reports, even when a service echoes one. `ip_intel.py sources` lists the sources and whether each key is set, never the key.
- **Names** (`normalize_name`: lowercase, no trailing dot, IDNA, a certificate's `*.` kept; addresses, single labels and `.arpa` names dropped), merged per address with their sources (`tls` and `ptr` first), the earliest first-seen and latest last-seen date of the sources, and `tls`: `SNI` (asked with the name as SNI, the address served a certificate that covers it) or `CERT` (a certificate the address serves covers the name: its own name or a wildcard). **Now** (the forward lookup): `HERE` (it resolves to the address), `MOVED` (to other addresses only, listed), `NO_ADDRESS`, `WILDCARD` (not looked up), `LOOKUP_ERROR` (no answer from the resolver), `UNCHECKED` (`--no-verify`); sorted by that, then TLS evidence, then the number of sources.
- **Output:** per address the PTR names, each certificate (port, subject, issuer, expiry, names, the SNI it was served for), InternetDB's ports / tags / vulns, the name table (NOW, TLS, SEEN, SOURCES; MOVED with the current addresses) and every source's status with its reason (a private address: one line saying nothing was sent); then the counts and, when a source failed, "Incomplete: …". Server and source text is printed as printable ASCII. `--json` (`domainscope.ip-intel/1`: `addresses[{ip, public, ports, certificates, sources[{id, status, names, detail, asked, total?, truncated?}], intel, names[{name, status, resolvesTo, tls, sources, firstSeen, lastSeen}]}]`, `summary`), `--csv` (`CSV_COLUMNS`: one row per address and name, a `NO_NAMES` row for an address without any, `source_errors`; formula-safe, control and bidi characters escaped, BOM in a file). Exit codes: 0 done, 1 PTR or a source failed for an address (only with `--fail-on-error`; a TLS port that does not answer — an unused address of a range, a firewall — is a state of the address, `tls TIMEOUT` / `ERROR` in its row, never a failure there, in "Incomplete" or in `source_errors`), 2 usage error, 3 a report file not written, 130 interrupted.
