- `tests/e2e/monitor.e2e.mjs` (right after `revocation`, offline only, in `npm run test:e2e:offline`) — the Monitoring view (§5.98, §6) over `tests/js/monitor-fixture.mjs` written to a temporary results folder and a GitHub API answered in the page, every other request refused by a CDP network guard and noted: the empty page with '/' on the drop zone; the folder (five reports, three months, the two bad lines said, the Markdown left alone, a stray file named); the tiles and the rows worst first with their sparklines ("Health score over 51 nights: 90 → 82"), grade, certificates, takeover and audit and checks (a button to a row's changes only when it has some); a tile filtering the table with the focus kept; a row's details; the timeline newest first (its times in UTC) with the runs' words, by tone and by a row's target, its CSV; Copy summary by name with a bare `#/monitor` link; the links to the open issues and the latest run; GitHub: a missing token said before anything is sent, the token in the Authorization header to api.github.com only (no cookies, referrer or redirect), the field emptied, kept nowhere (the DOM, the URL, storage, IndexedDB), the ledger's GitHub row (repository and token), the open issue linked, a refused token in the page's words; Forget, "Delete all local data" and another workspace forgetting the results; Turkish + dark at 375 px (the table as cards) and English at 320 px without horizontal scroll; no console errors, CSP violations or missing keys. `--shots-dir <dir>` puts its screenshots elsewhere.
- No `innerHTML`/`outerHTML`/`insertAdjacentHTML`/`document.write` with dynamic data anywhere (grep-able).

## 9. Headless runner `tools/ds.mjs` (Node 22+, no dependency)

A closed browser tab monitors nothing: `tools/ds.mjs` runs eight of the app's checks, the served-certificate monitor with its renewal radar (`tls`) and the registration, delegation and record change watch (`watch`), under Node over the DOM-free libraries (and a few pure helpers of the views, DOM-free at import: `views/subdomains.js` countHosts / subdomainsSummaryFacts / scanConcurrency, `views/renew.js` localParams, `views/zone.js` redactValues / originSecrets and its drift labels, `ui/dane-panel.js`'s strings), for cron and scheduled CI. Node only: `tools/` is not in the Pages bundle. English output (the Python CLI's language); nothing goes to Globalping.
```
node tools/ds.mjs COMMAND TARGET... [--list FILE]... [--json FILE] [--md FILE] [--baseline FILE [--fail-on-change]] [--history DIR]
    [--resolver ID[,ID]] [--concurrency N] [--show-all] [-q] [--no-color] [-h] [--version]
    [--notify URL]... [--notify-bad URL]... [--notify-format FMT] [--notify-always] [--fail-on-notify-error]
  health DOMAIN... [--waivers FILE]                  lib/health.js domainHealth, one domain at a time; the summary: lib/summary.js healthSummary
  subdomains DOMAIN... [--level off|small|smart] [--sources a,b] | [--exact FILE]
                                                     lib/scanner.js runScan per domain (level default small; permutations and the recursive round as the app;
                                                     sweep concurrency views/subdomains scanConcurrency); --exact: exact mode with the file's names under each domain;
                                                     a stage of 1,000 names or more prints its progress in tenths (`stageProgress`)
  drift ZONEFILE [--origin ZONE] [--max-queries N] [--include-origins]
                                                     lib/zoneparse.js parseZone + lib/zonedrift.js driftZone (default budget 2,000, ≤ 10,000); a low-confidence
                                                     origin needs --origin (exit 2), a fatal parse is exit 2
  ct DOMAIN... [--days N] [--sources crtsh,certspotter] [--radar D,D,...] [--expected-ca CA]... [--waivers FILE]
                                                     lib/sources.js fetchAllSources (current certificates of the domain and its subdomains; Cert Spotter
                                                     with `certDer`, its DER read by lib/x509.js: the serial and a precertificate), grouped by
                                                     lib/passport.js issuerName of the issuer DN alone; "recent" = notBefore within N days (default 30);
                                                     then the Domain portfolio's CT watch (tools/ds/ctwatch.mjs over lib/ctwatch.js analyzeCt / updateSeen):
                                                     --radar as the tab's thresholds (lib/ctwatch.js parseRadarDays, default 30,14,7), --expected-ca
                                                     one CA each as a workspace's expected CAs (lib/workspace.js sanitizeExpectedCas: ≤ 30, ≤ 120
                                                     characters; an entry lib/expectedca.js does not resolve to a known CA and no issuer
                                                     read contains is a warning: a typo would make every issuer unexpected)
  renew NAME... [--ca ID] [--challenge ...]          lib/renewal.js checkRenewal (noCache), in batches of RENEWAL_LIMITS.names; never the HTTP-01 test (Globalping)
  dane CERT.pem                                      lib/x509.js parseCertificates + lib/dane.js checkDane (noCache); a PKCS#12 bundle is exit 2 (give PEM),
                                                     a private key in the file is ignored with a warning, never read or printed
  audit DOMAIN|FILE... --policy FILE | --preset baseline|strict-mail|parked|corporate [--no-dkim] [--waivers FILE]
                                                     lib/portfolio.js createPortfolio over each target's registrable domain (DKIM at the 8 common selectors unless
                                                     --no-dkim) + lib/policy.js auditPortfolio; a positional path or name ending .txt / .csv / .list / .lst is a
                                                     --list (a URL with a scheme is a target, never a file); the policy file (UTF-8 or UTF-16, as the app exports
                                                     it) is read and checked before anything is sent: an unknown rule or a value its rule does not take is exit 2
                                                     naming them; exit 4 while a rule fails, also one that could not be checked and failed when last checked
  tls HOST[:PORT]... [--from-subdomains FILE [--skip-cdn]] [--warn-days N] [--ct FILE] [--http] [--max-endpoints N] [--ari] [--revocation]
                                                     the served-certificate monitor, tools/ds/tls.mjs runTls: every address of each target (A and AAAA over
                                                     the run's DoH client; an address target: no SNI) gets one TLS handshake (node:tls, SNI = the host,
                                                     `rejectUnauthorized: false`, `requestOCSP`, ALPN http/1.1, 10 s, 8 at a time): the leaf served, the chain
                                                     as Node built it (`chainLength`) and as sent (`chainSent`: getPeerX509Certificate, after
                                                     getPeerCertificate, which it empties), the trust (Node's root store; tls.checkServerIdentity whatever the
                                                     chain, Node's own name error on a trusted chain is no trust error), the name, the expiry, the protocol,
                                                     cipher and key exchange (`ephemeralKey`, getEphemeralKeyInfo; null where Node says nothing), the OCSP
                                                     staple (`ocspStapled`, the OCSPResponse event: reported only). --warn-days (default 21, 0-398): EXPIRING;
                                                     --ct: the same night's `ct` report (tools/ds/tlsct.mjs; no CT query) for NOT_DEPLOYED; --http: GET / over
                                                     the handshake's connection and, for port 443, over HTTP to port 80 (tools/ds/tlshttp.mjs); --from-subdomains:
                                                     the hosts with an address of a `subdomains` report (private-only ones left out, `--skip-cdn` the
                                                     Cloudflare / CDN ones, warnings say how many); --max-endpoints (default 500, ≤ 10,000): the handshakes
                                                     of a run, the targets from the first that does not fit on carried; --ari: the issuing CA's ARI window
                                                     (tools/ds/ari.mjs over lib/renewalplan.js fetchRenewalInfo), --revocation: its CRL
                                                     (tools/ds/revocation.mjs over lib/crl.js, the signature verified with the issuer's key from the
                                                     handshake's chain); targets: `host`, `host:port`, `[v6]:port`, an address, an https URL (args.mjs
                                                     parseTlsTarget; default port 443)
  takeover DOMAIN... [--names FILE | --from-subdomains FILE] [--dkim-selectors a,b]
                                                     tools/ds/takeover.mjs: lib/takeover.js auditTakeover per domain (§5.73, every reference kind), the
                                                     run's other domains its own (ownDomains), lib/rdap.js rdapDomain over the run's fetch (paced per registry
                                                     there), a registrable domain looked up once a run (what one domain's audit read, the next reuses: known);
                                                     --names: host names whose CNAME chains are asked (parseHostList, invalid entries warned); --from-subdomains:
                                                     the hosts with a CNAME (or one their lastGood carried) of a subdomains --json report (subdomainHosts:
                                                     another tool, command or major version is exit 2; a name that is no host name skipped and warned);
                                                     one of the two; a host under none of the domains is
                                                     left out (warned, never sent); --dkim-selectors: up to 20 selectors besides the 8 common ones
                                                     (dkimSelectorOption). A service only its page can tell stays "to check": the page check is the app's
  watch DOMAIN... [--names FILE] [--types A,MX,...] [--authoritative [--ttl] [--max-queries N]]
                                                     tools/ds/watch.mjs: each target's registrable domain (as audit); lib/portfolio.js createPortfolio
                                                     (lookups rdap, ns, ds and dnskey, no name server domain: RDAP paced per registry as audit asks it)
                                                     and a DoH snapshot of the apex, www, _dmarc (TXT and CNAME) and the names of --names under the domain (at
                                                     most 200 in the file, more is exit 2; a name under none left out, warned, never sent), each of
                                                     --types (WATCH_TYPES: A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, TXT, CAA, SOA, DS, DNSKEY, HTTPS by default; SOA, DS and
                                                     DNSKEY at the apex and at a name with NS records of its own, a delegation; the apex's NS and DS are
                                                     the delegation's); --authoritative: every name server asked directly (tools/ds/authoritative.mjs);
                                                     --ttl compares the TTLs the name servers agree on (needs --authoritative: a resolver's cache counts
                                                     TTLs down); --max-queries: the questions to each domain's name servers (default 2,000, ≤ 10,000;
                                                     needs --authoritative)
```
- **Command line** (`tools/ds/args.mjs`, pure): `parseCommandLine(argv) -> { command, targets, options, help, version }` over `node:util` parseArgs, a `UsageError` for anything refused (an unknown option or command, an option of another subcommand, a value out of range, `-` for a file, `--fail-on-change` without `--baseline`, `--json` = `--md`, `--baseline` = `--md`, `--json` or `--md` = a `--list`, `--exact`, `--names`, `--from-subdomains`, zone or certificate file the run reads; `--names` with `--from-subdomains`; a DKIM selector no name can be built from). Targets on the command line must be valid (domains through `domain.normalizeHostname`, a URL gives its host; renewal names through `renewal.parseRenewalNames`); a `--list` file's invalid entries are warnings (`parseListText`). Also `COMMANDS`, `COMMAND_SPECS`, `EXIT = { OK: 0, FAILED: 1, USAGE: 2, WRITE: 3, CHANGED: 4, NOTIFY: 5, INTERRUPTED: 130 }` (3 wins over 5, 5 over 4, as in the CLI; 4 is also an `audit` whose policy a domain fails — a rule that could not be checked is no failure, unless the report carries it as failed: it failed when last checked), `USAGE`, `DS_TOOL = 'domainscope-ds'`, `DS_VERSION`.
- **DoH:** one `DohClient({ chain, concurrency, fetchImpl })` per run over Node's own fetch, which speaks HTTP/1.1 only. `NODE_UNREADABLE` (quad9, quad9-ecs, cznic: HTTP/2 only, measured 2026-09-28 with Node 22 and 24) are refused by `--resolver` and left out of `NODE_CHAIN` = DEFAULT_CHAIN minus them (cloudflare, google, dnssb). The concurrency is the app's Settings default (12; `--concurrency` 1–32) and the balance pool follows the chain as in the app. renew compares CAA on CONSISTENCY_RESOLVERS minus NODE_UNREADABLE, whatever `--resolver` says, since the app asks them by name.
- **Before anything is sent** (`tools/ds.mjs` main): the `--list` / `--exact` / zone / certificate files are read (UTF-8, UTF-16 with a BOM, UTF-16LE without one: `decodeText`), `tls`'s `--from-subdomains` and `--ct` reports too (tools/ds/tls.mjs `tlsInputs`: a file that is not the report asked for is exit 2, a `--ct` file that does not exist a warning; the hosts of the subdomains report join the targets, so it can give all of them), the `--json` / `--md` paths checked (`checkOutputPath`: an existing directory that takes a new file, not a directory, a writable file — nothing truncated or left behind), the `--history` directory checked (`tools/ds/history.mjs checkHistoryDir`: a directory where a file can be created, or a missing one whose parent exists — it is created with the first line; a file is exit 2) and the baseline loaded (`loadBaseline`: JSON, then `diff.baselineProblem`). A baseline that does not exist is a first run only when it is also the `--json` file (`baseline: { file, missing: true }`), else exit 2. The invalid entries of a `--list` / `--exact` file are warnings: the first 5 quoted (`summary.cleanText`, at most 80 characters), then how many more (`skippedWarnings`). Reports are written whole or not at all (a temporary file renamed over the old one), after the summary; a write that fails is an error line and exit 3. Ctrl-C (or `timeout -s INT`) aborts the libs' signal: exit 130, nothing written, and the program leaves 200 ms later even while a request nobody waits for is pending (lib/rdap.js' shared bootstrap download is bound by its own timeout, not by the run's signal). The entry runs as a program also through a symlinked path (`realpath` of `argv[1]`).
- **Report** (`--json`): `{ tool: 'domainscope-ds', version, command, startedAt, finishedAt, options, warnings?, targets: [...], baseline?, changes?, notify? }` (`notify: { open }`: the PagerDuty keys still open, Notifications below), one target per domain / name / zone / certificate (`tools/ds/commands.mjs`):
  - health `{ target, checkedAt, score (summary.healthScore), light, summary, failedLookups, checks: [{ id, severity, titleKey, params, title }], carried?: [{ area, from, checks }], report /* the view's Report (JSON) */ }`. `carried`: for each area whose lookup failed this run, that area's checks as the last run that read it found them (`from`: its `checkedAt`, null when no run read the area);
  - subdomains `{ target, mode: 'discover'|'exact', level, sources: [{ source, state, names, error, skipped? }], finishedAt, counts (views/subdomains countHosts), warnings /* codes */, seeded, hosts }`. The scanner's warnings (TRUNCATED, DNS_UNREACHABLE, BRUTEFORCE_TRUNCATED …) are also run warnings (stderr, the report's `warnings`) and "Warning:" lines of the summary, in the Subdomains view's words (`sub.warn.<code>`, `scanWarningParts`; the detail a code part). Hosts are `export.scanHostRows` without the TTL, the resolver, the certificate and inventory columns, addresses sorted. A discovery run seeds the previous report's resolving hosts, dangling aliases and hosts whose lookup failed (`baselineSeeds`, origin `baseline`), so a host is never gone, nor dropped from the watch, only because a source was down or one lookup failed, and lists (`reportHosts`) the hosts that resolve, dangling aliases, failed lookups and the seeded names; the rest — names the sources know that resolve to nothing (tens of thousands for a busy domain), wildcard look-alikes — are only counted. An exact run lists every name of its file. A host whose lookup failed (SERVFAIL, REFUSED, ERROR) keeps its last answer: `lastGood: { at, status, kind, provider, providerId, hidesOrigin, dangling, ipv4, ipv6, cnames }` (the baseline's, or the one it carried);
  - ct `{ target, days, readAt, sources: [{ source, state, ok, truncated, errorKind, error, skipped?, lastFullAt }], complete, answered, recent, issuers: [{ name, count, intermediates, newest }], names, certificates: [{ id, ca, intermediate, issuer, notBefore, notAfter, names, sha256, serialHex, sources, revoked, precert, carried?, wildcard, daysLeft, current, isNew, unexpected, flags, radar? }], watch: { radar, expected, comparedWith, counts: { current, expiring, new, unexpected, wildcard, precert, revoked } }, seen?: { at, ids: { id: 'YYYY-MM-DD' } } }` (options: sources, days, radar, expectedCas). `revoked` (Cert Spotter) and `precert` (only the precertificate logged: Cert Spotter's DER) are null where no source says. The CT watch (`tools/ds/ctwatch.mjs watchTarget`) is the app's analysis (lib/ctwatch.js analyzeCt) over every certificate the target holds, carried ones too: `current` (the newest valid certificate of its name set, not superseded), `daysLeft`, `radar` (the smallest threshold a current one is within), `isNew` (not in the baseline's store; null when no run read the domain), `unexpected` (null without --expected-ca), `flags` (CT_WATCH_FLAGS). `seen` is the store of the certificates seen, the workspace's `ctSeen` entry of the domain (lib/ctwatch.js updateSeen: the ids of every run that read the domain with their expiry day, the expired dropped, `at` = the last read); a run that could not read the domain keeps the baseline's as it was, and a baseline written before the store stands in with its certificates' ids (`seenOf`). `watch.comparedWith`: that store's `at`. Names are those under the domain (Cert Spotter lists every SAN); `id` = `ctCertId`, a digest of the validity, the names and the intermediate's CN, so crt.sh's and Cert Spotter's rows of one certificate are one; `ca` = `issuerName(issuer DN)` (the known CA, else the DN's O, else its CN), never Cert Spotter's friendly name, so a night on which only one source answers names the same issuers. `lastFullAt`: when the source last read the domain in full (this `readAt`, else the baseline's). `certificates` also holds the baseline's current certificates this run did not list while a source that listed them was not read in full (`carried: { from }`: when they were last read); `issuers` and `names` cover them, `recent` and the summary count this read (the summary says how many are kept for the next comparison);
  - drift `{ target /* origin */, file /* base name */, format, records, queries, planned, aborted, finishedAt, preflight, counts, rows: [{ key, name, type, status, reasons, file?, live?, added?, removed?, resolver?, rcode? }] }`. Values only for rows that need a look (warn, error, could not check), redacted with the Zone File view's rule (origin addresses behind proxied names → `[origin hidden]`) unless `--include-origins`;
  - renew `{ target, wildcard, verdict, findings: [{ id, severity, unchecked?, params, title }], detail /* renewalExport's entry of the name */ }` (options: ca, challenge, resolvers, chain);
  - dane `{ target /* subject CN */, serialHex, notAfter, headline, endpoints: [{ key: 'service|host', qname, service, port, host, status, severity }], domains, detail /* daneExportJson */ }`;
  - tls `{ target, host, port, checkedAt, dns: { status, ipv4, ipv6, cnames, error } | null /* null: an address target */, endpoints: [{ address, family, port, status /* TLS_STATUSES: OK, EXPIRING, NOT_DEPLOYED, NAME_MISMATCH, UNTRUSTED, EXPIRED (a certificate read, best first), TLS_ERROR, TIMEOUT, CLOSED, SKIPPED */, error, protocol, cipher, ephemeralKey: { type, name, size } | null, ocspStapled: true|false|null, trusted, trustError, nameMatch, chainLength, chainSent, missingIntermediate?: { name, owner, subjectDN, added } | null, outOfDateIssuer?: { name, subjectDN, notBefore, notAfter, expired } /* a certificate above the leaf out of its dates */, cert: { sha256, serialHex, subject, issuer, ca, caId, names, notBefore, notAfter, daysLeft, keyType, keyBits, curve, authorityKeyId, crlUrls }, newer?: { id, ca, intermediate, notBefore, notAfter, serialHex } /* --ct: the renewal not installed */, http?: { status, error, hsts: { maxAge, includeSubDomains, preload, valid } | null, plain: { status, location, toHttps, error } | null }, ari?: { ca, certId, start, end, explanationURL, checkedAt, retryAfter, status, error, carried?: { from } }, revocation?: { status: 'good'|'revoked'|'unknown', reason, reasonCode, time, crl, checkedAt, thisUpdate, nextUpdate, signature: 'verified'|'not-verified'|'failed'|null, signatureNote, error }, lastGood? }], ct?: { newest } /* --ct read: the newest current CT certificate of the name */, carried?: { from, why?: 'max-endpoints' } }` (options: ari, revocation, warnDays, http, ct: { file, finishedAt } | null, fromSubdomains, skipCdn, maxEndpoints, resolvers). The status, worst first (`statusOf`): EXPIRED (by the run's clock; the trust error kept), UNTRUSTED (not yet valid, or Node's verify error, its code kept — a dates error of Node's, CERT_HAS_EXPIRED or CERT_NOT_YET_VALID, on a leaf in its dates is a certificate above it out of its dates by the run's clock, looked for in the chain as Node built it (`chain`), its code kept and that certificate named, `outOfDateIssuer` (clients refuse such a chain, as with the AddTrust root in 2020; the summary says the chain holds it, the UNTRUSTED change names it), and no error only when every certificate is in its dates at the run's time, a test's clock —: UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE, the leaf's issuer neither sent nor in the store, gets `missingIntermediate` named from the CCADB list the site ships — lib/chainfix.js repairChain over the certificates as sent, `nameMissingIntermediates`, each distinct chain once; null when the list has no issuer for it: a private CA; a list that cannot be read is a warning), NAME_MISMATCH, NOT_DEPLOYED (`--ct`: tools/ds/tlsct.mjs `renewalNotDeployed`, the newest current CT certificate of the report that covers the host and carries every name of the served one under its domain — a CDN edge's and the origin's own certificates rarely share their names — issued more than `NOT_DEPLOYED_MS` = 48 hours after the served one; revoked, expired or not yet valid ones never count; CT gives no key type, so an address serving one of two lineages of the names — the ECDSA one of an RSA and ECDSA pair, a CDN's certificate in front of the origin's own — is NOT_DEPLOYED when the other was renewed later, which the usage says next to --ct; `ctReportProblem` refuses a file that is no `ct` report of this runner before anything is sent, a missing file is a warning: the nightly job's ct check writes it first), EXPIRING (`tlsdiff.mjs expiryState`: at most --warn-days days left and fewer than a quarter of its lifetime — tools/ds/ctwatch.mjs overdueDays: an automatic renewal, due at a third, is overdue —, so a 47-day or 6-day certificate inside --warn-days is OK until then), OK. `--http`: `http` from `httpRecord` (tlshttp.mjs `getHead`: the status line and headers only, the body never read; 10 s each; HSTS by lib/origincompare.js parseHsts; `toHttps`: a 301 / 302 / 303 / 307 / 308 whose Location read against `http://host/` is https; the summary words it with `httpParts`, the Location a code part); the plain GET only for a port-443 target. `--max-endpoints`: a host past the cap that the baseline knows is carried (`carried.why: 'max-endpoints'`, its last endpoints), one it does not is left out; a warning names how many and from which. SKIPPED: an IPv6 address this machine has no route to (`no-ipv6-route`; GitHub's hosted runners), a warning, never a change. A DNS failure carries the baseline's endpoints (`carried`); an endpoint whose handshake failed keeps its last certificate (`lastGood`). ARI: one directory read per CA and run, each certificate asked once (CertID), not before the `retryAfter` of its last answer (that answer is carried: `ari.carried`), a CA that answered "rate limited" not asked again in the run; 404 is `not-found`. Revocation: each CRL URL read once a run (≤ 20 MB, 15 s), the next distribution point tried when one tells nothing; `signature` `failed` (the CRL is not the issuer's) is `unknown` / `bad-signature`, `not-verified` with `signatureNote` `issuer-not-sent` (the server sent no chain) or `algorithm`;
  - audit `{ target /* the registrable domain */, checkedAt, pass, fail, unknown, rules: [{ id, status: 'pass'|'fail'|'unknown', required, actual, evidence /* English */, key, params, last? }], row /* lib/portfolio.js exportRow */, security /* §5.92 securityExport: CSC's eight measures, whatever the policy */ }` (options: policy — the policy file's object, `policyObject` —, policyFile, preset, dkim, resolvers). Warnings: a TLD without RDAP, an RDAP lookup that failed (a name server domain's too), a DNS lookup that failed: the rules that read them could not be checked; a name server domain not registered ("anyone can register it and take over DNS"); a rule not checked this run that failed when last checked ("it still counts as failed": the run ends with exit 4);
  - takeover `{ target, checkedAt, references, checked /* registrable domains with a verdict */, hosts /* asked for their chain */, spfMacros, domains: [{ domain, verdict, expires }], risks: [{ key /* kind|host|target */, kind, host, target, chain, term, severity, reason, reasons: [{ code, severity, domain?, name?, expires? }], domain, expires, service: { id, name, status }|null, evidence, fix /* the app's English words */, carried? }] /* worst first */, failures: [{ source, name, error, errorKind }] }` (options: dkimSelectors — the extra ones —, hosts: { source: 'names'|'subdomains', file, count }|null, resolvers). Warnings: per domain, the lookups that gave no answer (named without control or bidi characters, `cleanText`) and how many risks were carried for them; the hosts of the file under none of the domains; the host names of a `--from-subdomains` report that are none (quoted as a `--list` file's skipped entries are). The summary (`takeoverDoc`): the app's "N references at risk (M checked)" or "Nothing at risk", the hosts asked, each risk at low severity or above (at most 10, its first reason in the app's words, a carried one saying so), the hosts only the page can tell ("to check in the app"), the lookups without an answer, the SPF terms built from a macro.
  - watch `{ target, checkedAt, runs /* the last 7 run times */, registration: { state: 'ok'|'not-found'|'unsupported'|'failed', registrar, ianaId, statuses, expires /* day */, daysLeft, nameservers /* RDAP */, dnssecSigned, soon?, carried?: { from }, error? }, delegation: { ns /* the zone's NS records */, ds /* 'keyTag algorithm digestType' */, signed, nsCarried?, dsCarried? }, names, types, delegated, nxdomain, classes: { name: class }, records: [{ key /* name|TYPE */, name, type, values, serial? /* SOA */, ttl? /* --ttl */, flips?, flapping?, carried? }], failures: [{ name, type, error, errorKind }], authoritative?: { view: 'authoritative'|'recursive'|'none', servers: [{ address, family, hosts, status: 'ok'|'lame'|'unreachable'|'skipped', reason, serial, transport, error? }], serial, lagging, mismatches: [{ key, servers: { address: values }, since, confirmed?, carried?: { from } }], compared, ttls, queries, cut, unresolved } }` (options: types, names: { file, count }|null, ttl, authoritative, maxQueries — with --authoritative —, resolvers). A record set's values are `tools/ds/watchdiff.mjs rrsetOf` (its own records only: a CNAME's target answers for itself, but a `_dmarc.` name's TXT is read where its CNAME chain ends in the answer — a hosted DMARC record's policy —; lib/zonediff.js valueKey — TXT joined and compared by its bytes, IPv6 canonical, CAA in lower case, MX / SRV spelled one way —; a TXT verification record of lib/passport.js TXT_VENDORS kept as `token <service> <12 hex of its SHA-256>`, so the token is never written or printed; the SOA as its primary name server, the serial apart); only sets that hold values are listed, and a set emptied lately (`flips` within the window) stays with `values: []`. `classes`: each name's provider class from its A / AAAA answers (lib/netinfo.js classifyResolution: `cloudflare:cloudflare`, `cdn:<id>`, `platform:<id>`, `direct`, `private`, `dangling` — a CNAME chain that ends in no address); `flips`: the times of a set's last 10 value changes (a CDN's rotating edges none), `flapping`: 3 or more within the last 7 runs; `soon`: the expiry has not moved since the baseline and fewer than 30 days are left (EXPIRY is said once). `authoritative` (tools/ds/authoritative.mjs `checkAuthoritative`): the NS hosts' addresses over the run's DoH client, each address a server, IPv4 first; each asked the zone's SOA first over UDP (node:dgram, lib/dnswire.js encodeQuery with EDNS0 at 1,232 bytes, no recursion, the DO bit for DS and DNSKEY; decodeMessage, an answer counting only with the query's random id and question), over TCP (node:net, the 2-byte length prefix) when the answer is truncated (TC=1) or UDP got none — 3 s, one try over each transport, 4 servers at once —: no AA (`no-aa`), REFUSED, SERVFAIL, NOTAUTH or no SOA is `lame`, no answer at all `unreachable`, an IPv6 address the machine has no route to (ENETUNREACH, EHOSTUNREACH, EADDRNOTAVAIL, EAFNOSUPPORT) `skipped` (one warning a run); when the first two servers answer nothing over UDP or TCP (port 53 blocked on this network) nothing more is asked: `view: 'recursive'` (the DoH snapshot alone, a warning); then the snapshot's record sets — and the zone's own NS set; the apex's DS (the parent's) and a delegated name's (the child's) are not asked — within `--max-queries` (the sets past it `cut`, a warning); a server that leaves 3 of them without an answer over UDP and TCP (gone silent after its SOA, a firewall dropping a type) is not asked further this run (`unreachable`, reason `unanswered`, its `error` naming them), and one whose UDP goes unanswered 3 times in a row while TCP answers is asked over TCP alone (AUTH_GIVE_UP), so a silent server costs seconds, not the run. The servers at the highest serial are compared set by set where two of them or more answered it (`compared`; the values, and the TTL with --ttl: a TTL said only where they differ; an A / AAAA set whose addresses are all edges of one CDN — `cdnRotation` over every server's, which a CDN or a provider picking answers per query hands out — is the same set): `mismatches`; a server behind that serial `lagging`. Each mismatch is followed from run to run (`tools/ds/watch.mjs syncState`): `since`, the run that first found every server answering it as now, and `confirmed` once the next run finds it so again (an answer a provider picks per query, weighted or multivalue records, rarely is) or when it was confirmed and the servers still disagree; one this run did not compare (over the budget, fewer than two servers answering it, the name servers not asked at all) is carried from the last run (`carried: { from }`). Warnings: a registry without RDAP, a registry that could not be read (its last read carried) or never was, the lookups that gave no answer (their last read carried), the name servers not reachable over port 53, a lagging secondary (its serial and the others’), the cut, NS hosts without an address, the IPv6 addresses skipped. The summary (`watchDoc`): the registrar, its IANA ID and the expiry, the statuses, the name servers (the registry's and the zone's, or "agree"), the DS records, the record sets read and the SOA serial, the sets changing often, the lookups without an answer, the name servers asked directly (how many answer, the serial, in sync or not; each lame server and why, each lagging secondary, each set out of sync with each server's values, new this run or carried), and "First run for this domain" with --baseline.
- **Carried** (`tools/ds/carry.mjs`, pure; used by commands.mjs to write a report and by diff.mjs to read a baseline): what a run could not read, its report carries from the last run that read it, so the next run compares with that read and not with the gap. Health (`carryHealth`): per area — a check id's first part (`checkAreas`; `ns.rdap-mismatch` also needs RDAP) — whose lookup failed (`failedAreas`: the lookup-error checks and `failedLookups`, an MX failure also hiding `mail-identity`, a DMARC one `bimi`; `txt` feeds `spf`, `a` / `aaaa` `apex` / `ipv6`), the area's checks as last read (the lookup errors and the ids this run found left out); an area that failed in the baseline too goes on with its `from`. CT (`carryCt`): each source's `lastFullAt`; a certificate stays known until every source that listed it has read the domain in full without it, or it expires. Subdomains (`carryHosts`): `lastGood` of a host whose lookup failed. Audit (`commands.mjs auditTarget`): a rule not checked this run carries `last: { status, evidence, from }`, the status the last run that checked it found, while the requirement is the same. Takeover (`carryRisks`): a risk of the baseline one of whose lookups failed this run (lib/takeover.js `findingLookups`: the query its reference came from, its target's existence, the registration of a domain its chain names) is kept as last read with `carried: { from }` — never gone, and never better: this run's risk of the same key stands only when it is at least as severe. Watch (`tools/ds/watch.mjs watchTarget`): a registration the registry could not answer carries the last read (`carried: { from }`, `error`: why not this run, the countdown moved on from the last read's), the zone's NS and the DS records whose lookup failed (`nsCarried`, `dsCarried`), a record set whose lookup failed (`carried`), a name's class whose A or AAAA lookup failed — never a change, and the next run compares with that read.
- **Sources a run stops asking** (`createSourceBreaker`; ct and subdomains discovery over several domains): Cert Spotter after a rate limit (HTTP 429, or a readable X-RateLimit-Remaining of 0; about 10 full-domain queries an hour per IP address, shared on GitHub's runners) until its Retry-After, at most an hour (`ctcert.createCtCooldown`, CT_COOLDOWN_MS); crt.sh for the rest of the run once it failed as a service (unavailable, rate limited: up to three minutes of retries per domain) or timed out on 2 domains in a row. The domains after that list the source as `skipped` with its state ("not asked"); one warning says when and why.
- **Summary / Markdown** (`tools/ds/render.mjs`): English strings from i18n.js (`setupStrings` registers SUMMARY_I18N, HEALTH_I18N, RENEWAL_I18N, POLICY_I18N and SECURITY_I18N, and imports the Zone File view, the DANE panel and the Takeover risks panel for theirs). Each target is a lib/summary.js SummaryDoc — the app's own builders for health, subdomains and renew, the same model for ct, drift, dane and audit (one for the run — the policy, the counts, the rules still counted as failed (not checked this run, failed when last checked: why the run ends with 4 on a night no rule failed), its rules, the domains that meet every rule —, then the domain security score — a table doc (`commands.mjs securityDoc`: one row per domain, the lowest score first, at most `SECURITY_MAX_ROWS` = 100, its score and each of CSC's eight measures as ✓ met, ✗ not met or ? not known, then what the marks mean and each measure's adoption), whatever the policy —, then one per domain with a failed or unchecked rule, FAIL before NOT KNOWN, each with its evidence and a carried fail saying so) — rendered with `renderPlainText` (stdout) and `renderMarkdown` (`--md`); a table doc with `renderTableText` (aligned columns) and `renderTableMarkdown` (a GFM table; a `|` inside a value's code span escaped). With `--baseline` both open with "Changes since the baseline (FILE, run of …): N" in the CLI's words (at most 50 lines without `--show-all`; the Markdown at most 200, `MAX_MARKDOWN_CHANGES`), a tag per change, the not-counted note (the audit's names its own: rules not checked this run, a domain or rule added that meets the policy, a rule taken out of it) and `baselineNotes` (what the two runs did differently: the resolvers, the level / sources / mode, the CA or challenge, the budget, the certificate's serial). Untrusted values are code parts (`summary.textParts` for finding titles, `summary.renderParts` per line): a code span in Markdown, so no mention survives into an issue.
- **Changes** (`tools/ds/diff.mjs`, pure; the severity ranks, a check id's worst severity and a host's answer from `tools/ds/states.mjs`, which Notifications reads too): `diffReports(command, before, after, { t, localParams }) -> Change[]`, the ones that count first (`orderChanges`); `Change = { tag, tone: 'bad'|'good'|'info'|'quiet', counts, target, item, kind: 'appeared'|'disappeared'|'changed', before, after, parts }`, in the report with its `text`. Tags: NEW, GONE, WORSE, BETTER, CHANGED, FAILED (to a failure state), RECOVERED, FAILING (failure to failure), SCORE, ISSUER, NAME, CERT, CA, EXPIRING, REVOKED, EXPOSED, DANGLING, RENEW-NOW, MOVED-UP, CA-NOTICE, RISK (each at most 9 characters, the CLI's column: the research notes' WINDOW-MOVED and EXPLANATION are MOVED-UP and CA-NOTICE). Listed but never counted (no `--fail-on-change`, no nightly issue): FAILING moves; CT sources that could not be read (FAILED once, RECOVERED: the source's outage, not the domain's change); what a failed lookup may hide (a health finding gone while its area's lookup failed — said once, not again while it stays carried —, a finding "new" in an area no earlier run read, the score moved while a lookup failed in either run; a host missing from a discovery run's result); a renewed certificate from a known issuer for known names (CERT); a certificate crossing a radar threshold while its automatic renewal is not overdue (EXPIRING); a revoked certificate that was not the one in use or whose earlier state is not known (REVOKED); an issuer or a name "new" that none of its certificates shows surely new (surely new: a source that lists the certificate now has read the domain in full before — ok, not partial, not truncated, at its `lastFullAt` — or the certificate was issued after the first of those full reads); an issuer gone; drift rows skipped this run or gone from the file. A baseline that could not read something carried the last read of it (Carried, above): the run is compared with that. RECOVERED's tone is the new state's (a move out of a failure into "will fail", a warn / error status or a host that no longer resolves is red). Per command:
  - health: warn / error findings by id (a repeated id by its worst severity; the baseline's carried checks included) new, gone, worse or better; the score; domains checked or no longer checked;
  - subdomains (wildcard suspects left out): a new resolving host (NEW) or dangling alias (DANGLING), one no longer resolving (GONE), a lookup failing (FAILED / FAILING), a proxied host now direct (EXPOSED), another kind or provider, a direct host's addresses (CHANGED; a CDN's rotating addresses are no change), a name taken out of an `--exact` file (GONE, counts). A host answering again after a failed lookup is compared with its `lastGood` (EXPOSED, CHANGED … "compared with its answer of DATE, before the lookup failed"), else RECOVERED;
  - ct: CT not read this run (FAILED, nothing compared), read again (RECOVERED, compared with the last read the baseline carried), ISSUER, NAME, CERT, an issuer gone (only after a complete read). A certificate is new when the baseline's store (`seenOf`) does not hold its id: a certificate a source missed one night is no CERT the night after. The CT watch: CA — a new certificate from a CA the run was not told to expect (counted; a new issuer says it on its ISSUER line instead, which then counts even when it may only have been missed before); EXPIRING — a current certificate within a radar threshold it was outside at the last read of the domain (the store's `at`, so a night CT could not be read loses no crossing), measured with this run's thresholds (a changed radar moves nothing by itself), never a certificate the baseline did not know (a short-lived one issued within a threshold), counted once its automatic renewal is overdue: the threshold is at most a quarter of the certificate's lifetime (`overdueDays`; ACME clients renew at a third, so a 90-day certificate crossing 30 days is listed only, at 14 and 7 counted); REVOKED — revoked now and not before, counted when it was the baseline's current certificate known not revoked. Notes: the expected CAs or the radar differ from the baseline's;
  - drift: a row's status by DRIFT_SEVERITY (WORSE / BETTER / CHANGED), to or from `error` (FAILED / RECOVERED), a problem row whose live values changed (as a set: a rotating answer order is no change), a problem row new in the file, the name servers' match (`same` / `overlap` / `disjoint`);
  - renew: the verdict (fail < unknown < warnings < ready; to `unknown` is FAILED), warn / error findings within one verdict (unchecked ones left out), names new or gone;
  - dane: each endpoint (service and host) by DANE_SEVERITY, to or from `error`, endpoints new or gone; compared whatever the certificate's subject (a note says when the serial differs);
  - audit: per domain and rule, pass → fail WORSE, fail → pass BETTER (the evidence alone moving — a day fewer left — is no change); to "not known" FAILED (listed only), and checked again compared with the status it carried (no change when it is the same; RECOVERED when no run had checked it, counted when it fails); a rule new to the policy or with another requirement NEW (counted when it fails), a rule gone GONE (listed only), a domain new (counted when a rule fails) or gone. The evidence's values (a registrar, CAA issuers) are code parts. Notes: the policy differs from the baseline's; DKIM checked in one run only;
  - tls (`tools/ds/tlsdiff.mjs`): a target new or gone (NEW / GONE, counted; NXDOMAIN is GONE; a new target's certificates and addresses are compared with nothing: its problems, EXPIRING, EXPIRED, RENEW-NOW and REVOKED for what it serves, as the CLI does for an endpoint new to its baseline), a DNS lookup that failed or a host `--max-endpoints` left out (FAILED once, not counted, saying which: the next run compares with the endpoints it carried) and answering or checked again (RECOVERED, listed); an address new to a name or gone from it (listed: DNS rotates a pool's addresses); a handshake that stops completing (FAILED, counted), completes again (RECOVERED, the new status's tone) or moves between two failures (FAILING, listed); another certificate (CERT: listed when it renews the last one — the same CA and key type, every name kept —, counted when it drops a name or changes the key type or the CA). Per target, the problems of its addresses (`TLS_PROBLEMS`, item null: one PagerDuty incident per host and problem), counted, tone bad, with `after` the status they stand for: UNTRUSTED (`isUntrusted`: `trusted` false for a trust error that is not the leaf's dates — EXPIRED says that; CERT_HAS_EXPIRED on an endpoint that is not EXPIRED is an expired certificate above the leaf, which the change names (`outOfDateIssuer`) — nor Node's name error, which an earlier version kept for a name mismatch), MISMATCH (`nameMatch` false), NOT-LIVE (`newer`; only when both runs read CT, `ct` on the target), HTTP (GET / answers 5xx) and REDIRECT (http:// answers without a redirect to https://; a refused port 80 or a failed GET is no change), the last two only when both runs asked `--http` — said when an address read in both runs gets the problem, or a new address has it while none of the target's had it, so a pool's rotating addresses repeat nothing; BETTER (good, counted) once no address has it and every one that had it was read again for it (or left DNS; `TLS_PROBLEMS` `read`: a handshake — for UNTRUSTED with a leaf that has not expired, whose CERT_HAS_EXPIRED, Node's last error, hides the chain's —, and for HTTP a GET / that answered, for REDIRECT a port 80 that answered: no answer is no news); NOT-LIVE's BETTER says "CT no longer lists a newer certificate than the one still served" where an address that had it serves the same certificate (the renewal revoked, say), "every address serves the renewed certificate now" otherwise. A weaker HSTS header on an address read in both runs (a smaller max-age, or none) is HSTS, listed only. The old per-endpoint WORSE / BETTER of status ranks is no longer made (WORSE keys a baseline still has open are resolved as before). Per certificate served (the item is its SHA-256), counted, tone bad: EXPIRING when it entered `expiryState` `expiring` since the baseline last saw it served (each run's own --warn-days; entering --warn-days before its renewal is overdue is listed only, `after: 'soon'`, and a certificate first served inside --warn-days says nothing), EXPIRED (expired, still served; a night skipped says EXPIRED only), RENEW-NOW (the CA's ARI window opened, or ended with the certificate still served, since the baseline last saw it served — the window it knew, at that time: the target's check, the check a DNS outage carried the endpoints from, an endpoint's `lastGood.at`; never the answer's `checkedAt`, which an answer carried past its Retry-After keeps; the newest record when two endpoints know the certificate —; a certificate first seen in its window too), MOVED-UP (its window starts more than 24 hours earlier than the last answer said: a CA does that before a mass revocation), CA-NOTICE (an explanationURL none of the target's last answers carried, when the baseline had read one) and REVOKED (its CRL lists it, and did not at the last check or it is new). Notes: --ari or --revocation asked in one run only (their changes compare runs that both asked), the warning days differ, --ct read or --http asked in one run only. Every tag is at most nine characters (render.mjs CHANGE_TAGS): the research notes' NOT-DEPLOYED is NOT-LIVE, while the endpoint status keeps the name NOT_DEPLOYED.
  - **`--warn-days` of `tls`, as built (accepted).** The plan was EXPIRING for every certificate within `--warn-days` days. As built, `--warn-days N` (default 21, at most 398) is a ceiling: EXPIRING also needs the automatic renewal to be overdue — fewer days left than a quarter of the certificate's lifetime, `overdueDays` of tools/ds/ctwatch.mjs, since an ACME client renews at a third —, so a 90-day certificate counts at 21 days, a 47-day one at 11 and a 6-day one in its last day and a half, and a short-lived certificate is never flagged for being short-lived; inside `--warn-days` before that point it is listed only (`after: 'soon'`: not counted, not paged), because a certificate whose client has not yet renewed it is not failing. This behaviour is accepted as the monitor's (the usage text, both READMEs and `tests/js/ds-tls.test.js` say and pin it); `--warn-days` of the CLI (§7) is unchanged and lists every certificate within N days.
  - takeover (`tools/ds/takeover.mjs diffTakeover`, by risk key): a risk new (RISK: bad and counted at medium severity or above, low listed, "to check" quiet), gone (GONE: good, counted when it was at medium or above), worse or better (WORSE / BETTER: counted when the worse of the two is at medium or above); a domain that had lapsed (unregistered, pending deletion, expired) and is held now while a record still names it — registered or expiring, or in DNS again where RDAP cannot tell (`no-rdap`, `rdap-404-dns`) — says "registered now — make sure it is yours" on its GONE or BETTER line; a domain new (counted when a risk is at medium or above) or no longer watched. A carried risk compares as last read. Notes: the extra DKIM selectors or the hosts asked differ from the baseline's (`takeoverNotes`). The not-counted note names low risks and the ones only the page can tell.
  - watch (`tools/ds/watchdiff.mjs diffWatch`): the registration and the DS records by lib/regwatch.js `diffRegistration` (§5.96) over the two reports — never over a registration this run carried (FAILED once, quiet: the registry could not be read) —: REGISTRAR (another registrar, bad; the same IANA ID under another name, info), LOCK (a client or server transfer prohibition removed, bad — info while another still blocks transfers, which it names —; added, good), STATUS (a hold, a pending delete, a redemption period or a pending transfer arriving, bad; the registry no longer holding the domain, bad; any other status, info), NS (the registry's name servers, item `registry`, or the zone's NS records, item `zone`: bad), DS (removed or changed, bad; added, info), EXPIRY (later: good; earlier: info; not renewed with fewer than 30 days left: bad, said once — the report's `soon`); RECORD per record set both runs asked and read (a lookup that failed carried the last read: no change): MX, NS, CAA, the SPF TXT (v=spf1), the DMARC TXT (v=DMARC1 at `_dmarc.`, a hosted record's read where its CNAME leads) and the CNAME at `_dmarc.` (asked with its TXT whatever `--types`: who publishes the policy; said as DMARC) bad — a TXT set is said per kind of value (SPF, DMARC, each service's verification token, the rest: item `<key>|spf` …) —; A, AAAA and CNAME info unless the name's provider class moved (both resolve or dangle, and differ: off its CDN to a direct address, to a CNAME that ends nowhere): bad; an A / AAAA set whose old and new addresses are all edges of one CDN (matchProviderByIP, not DNS-only) quiet; a TXT verification token info, named by its service, never printed; a DNSKEY set whose key-signing keys stayed (a zone-signing key rolled) quiet; DS under a name as the domain's; TTLs (both runs with --ttl) info; a name that answers NXDOMAIN now one line (item the name), bad for the apex or when it had a bad record set; SERIAL (the SOA serial moved) quiet; FLAPPING — a set with 3 or more `flips` in the last 7 runs, said once (quiet) when it starts, its info changes then not listed while it keeps changing, a bad one still listed (a monitor that goes quiet is what an attacker wants) —; with --authoritative in both runs (a run that fell back to DoH: FAILED once, quiet): LAME (a server lame or unreachable now and not before — one that stopped answering after its SOA too —, bad; answering with authority again, good; a skipped IPv6 address never), SYNC (a record set the servers at one serial answer differently, bad, said once, when its mismatch is `confirmed` — found the same twice in a row —, and not again while the servers keep disagreeing (a run that could not ask them carries the mismatches, so the run after it compares with them); agreeing again, good, only for a set said and compared this run — nothing compared is no agreement —; a lagging secondary, info, listed only); a domain new (NEW, counted) or no longer watched. Notes: the types, the names file, --ttl or --authoritative differ from the baseline's (`watchNotes`).
  `baselineProblem(doc, command)`: not this tool, another major version, another command, or a list the comparison walks that is damaged (with its index) → exit 2 naming it. The rules (and `DS_TOOL`, `DS_VERSION`) are `lib/runreport.js` `reportProblem(doc, command?)`, the ones the Monitoring view reads every report it opens with (§5.98); `tools/ds/args.mjs`, `tlsdiff.mjs` (`tlsTargetProblem`), `takeover.mjs` (`takeoverTargetProblem`) and `watchdiff.mjs` (`watchTargetProblem`) re-export theirs from it.
- **Accepted risks** (`--waivers waivers.json` on health, audit and ct; tools/ds/waivers.mjs over lib/waivers.js, §5.95). The file the Workspaces dialog exports is read and checked before anything is sent, on the run's clock: one that is no waivers file (not JSON, another format, a newer version) is exit 2; an entry that cannot be read (its kind, domain, ref, reason, owner, a day past 366 days ahead…) is a warning per entry (the first five, then a count) and is left out — its item counts. health: an error or a warning an active waiver of its domain accepts (kind `finding`) carries `waiver: { id, reason, owner, expires }` and is left out of `score`, `grade` and `light` (`waived: { count, until, scoreWith, gradeWith }`), the summary says "N accepted risks excluded"; one whose waiver is over carries `waiverExpired`. audit: a failed rule a waiver accepts (kind `rule`) is `waived` (`was`, `waiver`; lib/policy.js §5.64) and fails nothing — no exit 4 —; a rule not checked tonight that failed when last checked still fails the run unless a waiver accepts it — one whose waiver is over carries `waiverExpired` and is listed as expired, counting again —; the run's summary counts the accepted rules. ct: a known certificate (kind `cert`: its public key's SHA-256 — Cert Spotter's `pubkey_sha256`, else from its DER — or its own) carries `known` and is neither new nor unexpected (`spkiSha256` on every certificate; `knownExpired` past its end date). Changes: an accepted item's NEW, WORSE, BETTER and GONE are listed only (`accepted`, the note under the changes says "accepted risks (--waivers)"; a GONE says "its waiver can go" only when it was read: one its failed lookup hides keeps its waiver), one newly accepted is WAIVED (listed only), a score moved because the accepted risks changed is listed only; an item accepted in the baseline run that is still a problem without its waiver now — its end date passed, or it left the file — is **LAPSED** (bad, counted: --fail-on-change, the nightly issue, the alerts; once, the night it ends); for ct only when the certificate is from an unexpected CA, and a new issuer or name whose certificates are all known is listed only. PagerDuty: a problem a waiver accepts is over while it does (`problemStanding`: a health finding with a waiver, an audit rule waived, a known certificate's CA or ISSUER), so its incident is resolved. The summary ends with "Accepted risks · waivers.json": how many of the file's waivers are for the command, the items accepted, those ending within 14 days ("ends in 9 days"), those expired and counting again, those whose item the run could not read — health: a finding of an area whose lookup failed (carry.mjs `failedAreas`); audit: a rule not known tonight; ct: a domain whose read was not complete — as "Not checked this run (kept: its item could not be read)", never as "can go", and the waivers of a domain the run checked that matched nothing (fixed, or no longer reported: the waiver can go). `options.waivers` is the file's base name; a baseline with another (or none) adds a note. Every change tag is at most 9 characters (LAPSED, not WAIVER-EXPIRED), so the tag column of the summary is the same in both tools.
- **Notifications** (`tools/ds/notify.mjs`, pure apart from the injected fetch; the CLI's --notify ported, with PagerDuty, ntfy and the signature it has too, §7). Options on every command, checked before anything is sent (`notifyRoutes`; a `NotifyConfigError` is exit 2 and never repeats a URL):
  - `--notify URL` (repeatable; without it the URLs of `DOMAINSCOPE_NOTIFY_URL`, separated by whitespace) posts the changes that count when any does (every run with `--notify-always`); `--notify-bad URL` (repeatable; else `DOMAINSCOPE_NOTIFY_BAD_URL`) posts only the changes that count and are bad, the pager route, and never a heartbeat. A URL on both is posted to once, on the --notify route. `--notify-format FMT` (NOTIFY_FORMATS: auto, slack, teams, discord, telegram, googlechat, json, pagerduty, ntfy) names the format of every URL; auto follows each (`detectNotifyFormat`: the CLI's table, plus events.pagerduty.com / events.eu.pagerduty.com → pagerduty and ntfy.sh → ntfy). With no URL set, `--notify-format`, `--notify-always` and `--fail-on-notify-error` change nothing, so a scheduled job passes them whether or not its secrets are set. A URL on the command line with nothing to send (no `--baseline`, no `--notify-always`) is a warning; the environment's are not.
  - URLs: https:// only, but to this machine (localhost, 127.0.0.0/8, [::1]) — the CLI only warns; a Telegram URL needs `/bot…/sendMessage` and `chat_id`, a PagerDuty one `routing_key`. A URL is a credential: never printed or written (stdout, stderr, `--json`, `--md`); messages name its host only (`notifyHost`), and every error text or answer is redacted (`redactUrl`: the CLI's redact_url, plus the ntfy token, the signing secret and an ntfy topic). `user:password@` goes as Basic authentication.
  - Messages (`notificationMessage`, `buildRequest`): the title (`DomainScope COMMAND: N changes since <baseline run>`, "bad changes" on the --notify-bad route; first run, no changes, finished), a line per change carried (`- TAG text`, at most 20, then how many more), the footer (the run's time, its targets, how many changes are listed only) and the Actions run's link (`runUrl`: `$GITHUB_SERVER_URL/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs/$GITHUB_RUN_ID`). Chat formats as the CLI's — Slack `{text}` (`& < >` escaped), Discord `{content, allowed_mentions: {parse: []}}`, Teams one Adaptive Card of TextRuns, Google Chat `{text}` (`<` → `‹`), Telegram `{chat_id, text, link_preview_options}` (`chat_id` moved from the query; a number when safe, else text) —, cut to NOTIFY_TEXT_LIMITS (slack 3,500, teams 3,500, discord 1,800, telegram 3,900, googlechat 3,500, json 3,500), every line at 400 characters (`fitLines`, never inside a surrogate pair). `json`: `{ tool, version, command, title, text, startedAt, finishedAt, run, baseline: { file, missing, finishedAt }, counts: { changes, counted, bad }, changes: [{ tag, tone, counts, target, item, text, before, after }] (≤ 500; the --notify-bad route's: the counted bad ones), changesTotal }`, signed when `DOMAINSCOPE_NOTIFY_SECRET` is set (surrounding whitespace ignored): `X-DomainScope-Timestamp` (Unix seconds, the injected clock) and `X-DomainScope-Signature: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, timestamp + "." + body)>` (`signBody`). `ntfy`: the lines as plain text, at most 4,000 bytes (`NTFY_MAX_BYTES`), headers `Title` (RFC 2047 when not ASCII), `Priority` 4 when a change carried is bad (else 3), `Tags: warning`, `Click` (the run's link) and `Authorization: Bearer $DOMAINSCOPE_NTFY_TOKEN` (refused unless printable ASCII without spaces; not for a URL with user info).
  - PagerDuty (`pagerDutyPlan`, `pagerDutyRequests`; Events API v2 at the URL without `routing_key`, which goes into each event): a `trigger` per counted change with tone bad, one per `dedupKey` = the first 32 hex characters of SHA-256 of `command|target|item|tag` (no item: empty) — `{ routing_key, event_action: 'trigger', dedup_key, payload: { summary (≤ 1,024: `TAG text`), source: 'domainscope:<command>', severity, component: target, group: command, custom_details: { tag, item, before, after, run } }, client: 'DomainScope', client_url? }`; severity (`eventSeverity(change, command)`) `critical` for REGISTRAR, NS, DS, LOCK, EXPIRED, UNTRUSTED (CRITICAL_TAGS), for the same problems as today's commands report them (CRITICAL_ITEMS, by item: health `rdap.expired`, `rdap.hold`, `rdap.pending-delete`, `dnssec.broken`; drift `NS`, the name servers; audit `registrar`, `transferLock`, `status.critical`, `dnssec`, `expiryDays`, `nsExpiryDays`, and a domain added that fails one of them; watch's STATUS of `server hold`, `client hold`, `pending delete`, `redemption period`, `pending transfer` and `registration`, the registry losing the domain), for ct's REVOKED (the certificate in use) and tls's (a revoked certificate still served), for a tls endpoint that turned EXPIRED or UNTRUSTED (`after`) and for a change whose `after` says critical (a critical takeover risk), `error` otherwise. The report keeps the keys triggered and not resolved (`notify.open: [{ key, target, item, tag, since, state?, over? }]`, at most 500, PAGERDUTY_MAX_OPEN, the oldest dropped; `openKeysOf` drops a malformed entry, and a `state` that is not a short text or a number; a run without a PagerDuty URL carries them as they are). `state` (`tools/ds/states.mjs pagedState`) is the level the item was paged at — the change's `after` for health (a finding's severity, the score), drift (a record set's status, the name servers' match), renew (the verdict) and dane (an endpoint's status); none for a host, a certificate or a rule, which are bad or not. The next run sends `{ routing_key, event_action: 'resolve', dedup_key }` for each open key whose problem is over (`problemOver`): its target is no longer in the run, or the run's report shows the item better than it was paged at (`states.mjs problemStanding`, per command) — health: the finding's worst severity, read or carried, below its `state`, or no longer reported where its lookups answered (a lookup error once the lookup answers; the score above its `state`, read with no lookup failed); subdomains: the host's answer — FAILED once it answers, whatever it says, DANGLING once not dangling, GONE once it resolves, EXPOSED once it is behind a proxy again or not direct, RECOVERED (answering with no address) once it resolves —, a host out of an `--exact` file being over; ct: the certificate superseded by a newer one for every name (renewed), the issuer gone from a complete read; drift: the record set's DRIFT_SEVERITY below its `state` (FAILED: checked again), one out of the file being over, the name servers' match better; renew: the verdict better (FAILED, or paged at `unknown`: checked again); dane: the endpoint's DANE_SEVERITY below its `state`, one no longer checked being over (not known while an MX lookup failed: the mail hosts come from it); audit: the rule passes (one not checked this run counts as last checked, `last`), a rule out of the policy being over, a domain added once none of its rules fails; tls: a certificate's key (EXPIRING, EXPIRED, RENEW-NOW, MOVED-UP, CA-NOTICE, REVOKED: the item is its SHA-256) once no endpoint serves that certificate any more — an endpoint that served it last time and could not be read says nothing, an IPv6 address the machine cannot reach never counts —, a host's (item null) UNTRUSTED, MISMATCH, NOT-LIVE, HTTP and REDIRECT once none of the addresses read for it has the problem (`TLS_PROBLEMS` `read`: UNTRUSTED where the leaf has not expired, NOT-LIVE only in a run that read CT, HTTP where GET / answered and REDIRECT where port 80 did, so a run in which none answered says nothing; an address that failed is not waited for — a dead pool member would keep the incident open for ever —: back with the problem it is RECOVERED with a bad status, paged on its own; nothing read says nothing), an endpoint's (`address|port`) FAILED once a handshake completes there and WORSE / RECOVERED once its status is OK, the name no longer resolving (GONE) once it resolves again, an address no longer asked being over, a CERT never known fixed, and a DNS lookup that failed or a host --max-endpoints left out (`carried`) saying nothing; takeover: a risk once the report no longer lists it or lists it at a lesser severity than it was paged at (`state`, the change's `after`), one carried over a lookup that failed saying nothing, and a domain watched for the first time (NEW) once none of its risks is at medium severity or above; watch: a transfer lock removed (LOCK, the item its status) once the registry lists a transfer prohibition again, a hold (STATUS, the item the status) once it is gone, the registry losing the domain (STATUS `registration`) once it holds it again, an expiry not renewed (EXPIRY) once the report no longer marks it (`soon`), a lame server (LAME, its address) once it answers with authority or is no longer a server, a record set out of sync (SYNC, its key) once the servers are compared on it again and agree (a mismatch carried, not compared this run, stays open); a registration not read this run or name servers not asked say nothing; another registrar, other name servers or DS records and a record changed (REGISTRAR, NS, DS, RECORD) are events: nothing a later report says shows them wanted, so they stay open until someone resolves them in PagerDuty. A key without its `state` is over only once its item is fully good. Never because another change came by: a failed lookup, a record set or endpoint not checked (`error`, `skipped`), a host a discovery run did not look up again, a certificate no longer listed, a rule not known say nothing, so the key stays open (an origin still exposed after a night of SERVFAIL is still paged). A problem that stays as it was keeps its key open; a key triggered again keeps its `since` and `state`. At most 50 events a run per URL (PAGERDUTY_MAX_EVENTS), triggers first: the triggers cut are not sent (a warning), the resolves cut stay open with `over` and go out with the next run. The keys a run leaves open are those delivered (`keysOpenAfter(plan, { triggered, resolved })`; `pagerDutyPlan`'s `open` assumes every event went out): a trigger taken by any PagerDuty URL opens its key, a resolve closes it once every PagerDuty URL took it, and a key whose resolve was not delivered stays as it was.
  - Delivery (`deliver`, `sendNotifications`): after the summary, before the `--md` and `--json` reports; one route after the other, each stopping at its first request that fails. POST, 10 s timeout per attempt (NOTIFY_TIMEOUT_MS), one retry after 2 s or a 429's Retry-After (≤ 10 s) for network errors, 5xx and 429 (a 4xx is the webhook's answer), `redirect: 'manual'` (a redirect is a failure: a redirected POST would arrive as a GET), User-Agent `domainscope-ds/<version>`. stderr: `notification sent (FORMAT, HOST[, --notify-bad])` (PagerDuty: N triggered, N resolved; not with `-q`) or `error: notification failed (FORMAT, HOST): <redacted reason>` — the answer's reason (`responseDetail`) and status text redacted before they are cut at 200 characters, and an answer cut at the 512 bytes read without what it ends with that begins a secret, so no part of a secret echoed across a cut is printed. When the `--json` file is also the baseline and a route that carried changes that count (or PagerDuty events) failed, the file keeps the previous report ("kept the previous baseline in FILE (this report is not written there): the N changes will be reported again on the next run"), so the next run sends them again — on every route; when PagerDuty got events that run, the kept report's `notify.open` is replaced by the keys open after it (`withOpenKeys`, written whole through a temporary file; "…; the PagerDuty incidents still open are noted in it"), so an incident opened on such a night is resolved once its problem is over. `--fail-on-notify-error`: exit 5 when a notification was not delivered (3 wins over 5, 5 over 4). Ctrl-C while posting: exit 130, nothing written (neither the `--md` nor the `--json` report).
- **History** (`--history DIR`, `tools/ds/history.mjs` over `lib/monitor.js historyLines`, §5.98; every command): after the reports, one JSON line per target of the run appended to `DIR/YYYY-MM.jsonl` (the month of the run's end, UTC): `{ v: 1, at, command, target, ok, score?, grade?, minDaysLeft?, counts: { bad, info }, changes: [{ tag, tone, item }] (≤ 20), run? }` — whether the target's check completed (`checkCompleted`), Domain Health's score and grade, the soonest expiry of the certificates the run saw (tls: served; ct: the current ones), the changes that count with a bad tone and the rest, the changes' tags, tones and items (the ones that count first), the GitHub Actions run (`runUrl`) when it ran in one; a target of the baseline the run no longer checks gets a line for its changes (`gone: true`). An item names what moved (a finding or rule id, a host, an RRset key, an issuer, a certificate's CT id or SHA-256, an endpoint's `address|port`, a takeover risk's key); nothing else of the report is kept: no change's words, no value before or after. Whole or not at all, like `--json`: the month's file is read, the lines added after it (a last line without its newline ends first) and the result written to a temporary file renamed over it, so a stopped run leaves it as it was; one writer at a time (the template runs its checks one after the other). Then the month files older than 13 months are deleted (this month and the twelve before it stay; nothing else in DIR is touched). DIR is created with the first line when its parent exists; a DIR that is a file, or one where no file can be created, is exit 2 before anything is sent; a history that cannot be written is an error line and exit 3 (the reports are written). The history is a log, not a baseline: a night whose notification failed and kept the previous `--json` report is logged too (its changes come again the next night). stderr: `history: N lines added to FILE`, `history: NAME deleted (older than 13 months)` (not with `-q`).
- **Nightly template** (`docs/examples/nightly-domainscope.yml`, `docs/examples/README.md`): a scheduled workflow for a private repository with a `domains.txt`. It checks out that repository and DomainScope (`ref:` to be pinned to a commit SHA, or a release tag once there is one; its actions are pinned to commit SHAs with their versions in comments, as in the repository's own workflows), both with `persist-credentials: false` so no token sits in `.git/config` while the checks run (the commit step hands the token to its `git pull` / `git push` alone through `-c http.<server>/.extraheader`; the issue step's gh reads `GH_TOKEN`), runs `health`, `ct`, `takeover` and `watch`, and `[ -f tls-hosts.txt ] && ds tls tls --list tls-hosts.txt --ct results/ct.json` after the ct line, so the served-certificate monitor runs once the repository has a `tls-hosts.txt` and reads the ct report that line just wrote (subdomains, an exact host list, the takeover watch over the hosts subdomain discovery found, the change watch with `--names watch-hosts.txt --authoritative` — `--from-subdomains results/subdomains.json`, after the subdomains line —, drift, renew, the policy audit — exit 4 while a rule fails, so the issue stays open until every rule passes — and the tls line with `--ari --revocation --http` instead are commented out) with `results/NAME.json` as both `--baseline` and `--json`, `--md results/NAME.md`, `--history results/history` (the Monitoring view's trends; the commit step keeps it with the reports), `--fail-on-change` and `--fail-on-notify-error` (exit 4 = changed; 5 = a notification was not delivered: `changed` and `failed` with `NAME:notify`, so the issue still opens — also on a night whose only undelivered event was a PagerDuty resolve, which lists no change — and the job fails, and the kept NAME.json makes the next night send the changes again; any other non-zero = failed), commits `results/`, then keeps one issue labelled `domainscope` through the gh CLI (created, or edited and commented, when something counts; closed on a night with none on which every check completed; left open with a comment on a night a check did not complete, which compared nothing) and fails the job when a check did not complete. Each check runs under `timeout -s INT` for at most `CHECK_MINUTES` (20), and all of them within `RUN_MINUTES` (45) of the job's `timeout-minutes` (60), so a slow night is a failed check (124) and the commit and issue steps still run. The template and its README say that more than about 10 domains exhaust Cert Spotter's quota and offer `--sources crtsh`. Its header says: use it in a PRIVATE repository, never commit inventories or zone files unless you mean to, no secret is needed (the GITHUB_TOKEN with `contents: write` and `issues: write` only); alerts are optional Actions secrets, read by the checks step alone as its environment — `DOMAINSCOPE_NOTIFY_URL`, `DOMAINSCOPE_NOTIFY_BAD_URL`, `DOMAINSCOPE_NOTIFY_SECRET`, `DOMAINSCOPE_NTFY_TOKEN` (an unset secret is empty: nothing is sent).
- **Tests:** `tests/js/ds-waivers.test.js` — `--waivers`: the option, the file, health over four nights (accepted, then LAPSED and exit 4), a waiver added after a run without one (WAIVED, exit 0), a night the MX lookup fails (kept, never "can go"), audit's exit 4 and the waived status, RDAP down (kept) and a waiver ending while it is still down (expired, exit 4), a CT night with crt.sh down (kept), the diffs of every kind, the summary, the tag column, PagerDuty's standing; `tests/js/ds-history.test.js` — `--history` on the command line, the directory checked before the run, a run's lines appended to its month (a rollover starts the next file; a last line without its newline), month files past 13 months deleted and nothing else, the write whole or not at all (no temporary file left), and runs of `main()` over the fake DoH: a first run, a run with changes, a history that cannot be written (exit 3, the reports written), a file as the directory (exit 2, nothing sent). `tests/js/ds-runner.test.js` — the command line, every diff, baseline validation and notes, the renderers, what a run carries (health areas over three nights, CT over an outage and a partial read, a host's last answer), offline runs of `main()` with an injected fetch (the fake DoH of `tests/js/ds-fake-doh.mjs`: the Zone File e2e suite's fake live zone of the Cloudflare export fixture;
